pinnedClauses.title: Public feedback portal
pinnedClauses.gap: Gap: owner-configured workspace identity and a changed portal description have no passing assertion.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** An installed Penny serves its public feedback board at `/`, with search, status, board, category and sort parameters, server rendering and customer-safe reads; `/portal/feedback` serves the same board as a compatibility address. The board's home identifies the workspace by the owner's company name and logo (INT-007) and gives the owner's configured one-line portal description; public feedback, roadmap and updates follow REQ-001, ROAD-006 and REL-010. **Acceptance.** 1. `/` and `/portal/feedback` serve the same board, with the same search, status, board, category and sort parameters. 2. `/portal` and `/portal/` answer `302` to `/` with the same query, and `/` does not redirect a filtered board request to a landing page. 3. Portal navigation, board filters, the submission page's way back, sign-in's "Back to feedback" and the operator's "Open public board" link use `/`, and existing links to either address keep working. 4. At both addresses the home identifies the workspace by the owner's company name and logo and shows the owner's configured one-line description, and a changed description shows on the next load. 5. The home makes no vendor, pricing, testimonial or metric claims and exposes no operator-only data.

pinnedClauses.title: Public product landing
pinnedClauses.gap: The run site's built landing page at both widths with no cross-origin request, cookie or workspace read; no test reads the built site yet.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Penny's public product page is the run site's home: `/` of run-penny.com, built from `src/site`, not a route of an installation. It is rendered on the server as the finished page, and its copy names only capabilities whose clauses are `done` in the Status table and shows no pricing, testimonials, customer logos, metrics or integrations Penny does not ship; drawn labels use the portal's own status and sort vocabulary. **Acceptance.** 1. The header has Penny's coin mark and name and links to the documentation at `/docs`, the public board, the source repository and `/signin`. 2. A hero has the page's one heading, a supporting line and links to `/docs/install` and `/docs`. 3. Sections, each with a decorative paper-collage drawing of Penny's own screens, cover the moderated public board, evidence-based decisions, closing the loop with followers, private commercial context, and self-hosted ownership the owner may change with their own agents. 4. A closing call to action repeats the two links, and the footer repeats the navigation. 5. The public board, roadmap and updates remain the portal (REQ-001, ROAD-006, REL-010). 6. The page reads no workspace or operator data, and its fonts, styles, script and drawings are the site's own. 7. The optional footer credit, "Powered by Penny · runeditrun.com", is visible by default and `showPoweredByCredit` in `src/ext/config.ts` turns it off; the credit is a plain link. 8. Motion is optional and plays once on load; it never loops, is off under reduced motion, and never hides content: without script, with reduced motion and after motion ends, every section is fully visible.

pinnedClauses.title: Public documentation
pinnedClauses.gap: Gap: manifest navigation order; build/development rendering and rejection of unlisted Markdown, broken links and forbidden image paths; full header/footer and page-navigation semantics; client navigation and HTML escaping; nested-unknown-slug 404/article exclusion; and workspace/session/cookie isolation lack sentence-complete running assertions.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Penny's delta on Base's on-site docs duty: the public paths `/docs` and `/docs/<slug>` serve Penny's first-party documentation, the install, portal, decision-loop, email, data and customization guides, from the deployment itself. The pages are the Markdown files that `docs/site.json` lists as published, in the sections and order it gives, which is the only navigation. **Acceptance.** 1. Pages are served as HTML rendered from the Markdown ahead of time, in a build and in development; no request and no browser renders Markdown, and a page loads only its own content. 2. A page has its title as its one top-level heading, under the same header as the product landing (HOME-002): Penny's coin mark and name linking to `/`, then links to the docs (marked as the current section), the public board at `/portal`, the source repository and `/signin`, of which a phone keeps the mark, the name and sign-in; the landing's footer repeats them. 3. A page has a section menu, an on-this-page list, previous and next links, tables in labeled scrollable regions and an Edit-on-GitHub link; after the page loads, moving between docs pages is client-side navigation. 4. Every Markdown file at the repository root, under `docs/` and as a top-level `<directory>/README.md` is either published or listed in the manifest as GitHub-only with a reason, and an unlisted file fails verification. 5. A broken internal link or anchor, an image outside `docs/media/` or an absolute build-machine path fails the build. 6. Raw HTML in the Markdown is shown as text, never rendered. 7. The documentation reads no workspace record and no requester or operator identity or session. 8. An unknown or nested slug answers a `404` with no article.

pinnedClauses.title: Roles
pinnedClauses.gap: Current operators share product access, and workspace clock settings admit Owners and Admins (OPS-008) while other configuration remains owner-only. No journey yet signs in one operator per role: the Viewer, Contributor, Product manager and Admin refusals, unchanged state on refusal and next-request role change lack passing assertions.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Penny's five operator roles, each checked in the business transaction like current authority, with a role change applying to the next request. Contributor and Viewer seats are unlimited, and operators invited before the full roles system ships become Product managers. *Policy: `operator.roles.v1`; default: the five roles below.* | Role | Rights | | --- | --- | | Owner | Everything, including installation configuration, ownership handover (OPS-002), integrations, export and erasure. | | Admin | All product work plus settings (including branding, INT-007, and sender identity, NOTIFY-013), boards, integrations, automation rules and the roles below Owner. | | Product manager | All product work on evidence, requests, moderation (including editing published content, REQ-038, and removing it, REQ-041), decisions, roadmap and releases. | | Contributor | The seat for support, sales and success staff: capture evidence, record proxy votes (CAP-014), comment internally and read product records; no moderation, publication, commitment, settings or commercial fields unless granted (ROLE-001). | | Viewer | Read-only. | **Acceptance.** A base and browser journey signs in one operator per role and attempts every guarded action through its route and its UI: 1. A Viewer is refused every write. 2. A Contributor captures evidence, records a proxy vote and comments internally but is refused moderation, publication, commitment, settings and every commercial field. 3. A Product manager is refused settings, integrations and roles. 4. An Admin is refused ownership handover, export and erasure. 5. A role change takes effect on the operator's next request.

pinnedClauses.title: Management
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Operators are invited and removed in settings. **Acceptance.** 1. The operator configured at setup can be removed only by themselves. 2. *Policy: `operator.management.v1`; default: any operator may invite or remove any other operator.*

pinnedClauses.title: Overview
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** The operator home lists decisions that are ready or review due, evidence that is unreviewed, roadmap items that are Planned or In progress, and releases published in the last 30 days with their outcome totals. **Acceptance.** 1. Every figure links to the records it counts, and a section with no records names what is absent and links to the action that creates one.

pinnedClauses.title: First-run setup
pinnedClauses.gap: A signed-in operator who is not the owner never being sent to /setup, setup completion staying out of archives, an installation with an active owner being treated as finished, and local rer dev opening signed in as the owner with mail suppressed have no passing assertion.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** The signed-in owner whose setup is unfinished completes it at `/setup`, and every `/app` document and client-side app navigation sends that owner there first. **Acceptance.** 1. Finishing setup opens the app, and later visits to `/setup` go to the app. 2. A signed-out visitor to `/setup` is sent to sign-in and back, and a signed-in operator who is not the owner is never sent there. 3. Setup completion is installation state recorded once by the owner under the same-origin and authority checks of the business transaction; it is not portable domain data and does not transfer in an archive. 4. An installation that already has an active owner is treated as finished. 5. After `rer setup`, local `rer dev` opens automatically signed in as the owner and returns them to `/setup` until it is finished; local development has no outbox and silently suppresses mail. 6. Setup cannot finish until the owner has chosen the workspace timezone and seen the requester quiet hours (OPS-008) and entered the company name (INT-007) and the business postal address (NOTIFY-014).

pinnedClauses.title: Global search
pinnedClauses.gap: Search across every other named field ships; product, component and feature names are not yet searched (src/core/features/workspace/list-repository.ts), and the 500 ms first page has no seeded run at the seed.json limits (D-3).
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Operators can search request titles and descriptions, evidence wording, decision questions and rationales, roadmap item titles and summaries, release titles and bodies, requester display names and email addresses, account names, and product, component and feature names (PRIO-001). **Acceptance.** 1. Each named field is searchable, and a result links to its record. 2. Searching one product, one component and one feature, each by its full name and by a partial name, returns it with a link to its record and in the same ranking as other results. 3. Product, component and feature results pass the same permission filtering as every other searched record: an operator who cannot open one does not see its name. 4. The first page of results returns within 500ms.

pinnedClauses.title: Capture
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Every portal submission creates exactly one evidence item in the same transaction (REQ-003). **Acceptance.** 1. An operator can also record an evidence item, whose source is one of sales call, support conversation, interview, email, or a free-text label the operator supplies.

pinnedClauses.title: Provenance
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Every evidence item stores its source, its original wording, the observed time, and the operator or portal submission that created it. Observed times follow the precision rules in [docs/contract-mechanism.md](docs/contract-mechanism.md#observed-time-precision). **Acceptance.** 1. The submitting requester or named speaker and the account are nullable, are set only from what the recorder supplies, and are never inferred.

pinnedClauses.title: Review lifecycle
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** New evidence is unreviewed. **Acceptance.** 1. An operator can link it to a request or to a candidate bet in a decision brief (DEC-002), create a request or a decision from it, or mark it reviewed with a reason, and can return any reviewed item to unreviewed. 2. Linking alone does not mark it reviewed.

pinnedClauses.title: Non-destructive linking
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** One evidence item can be linked to any number of candidate bets, and each link is recorded as supporting or contradicting that bet. **Acceptance.** 1. Linking, unlinking, tagging, merging a request, and committing a decision never alter or remove an evidence item or any of its versions; only an operator deleting it does.

pinnedClauses.title: Account context
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** An account has a name, an internal owner, optional commercial fields for revenue, renewal date, and health, its requesters, its evidence in observed-time order, and its linked requests and decisions. **Acceptance.** 1. Evidence recorded against an account appears on that account, and on every request and decision the same transaction linked it to, when that transaction commits.

pinnedClauses.title: Private commercial data
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** No field of an account (EVID-005), no evidence source attribution, and no internal note (REQ-032) is ever public. **Acceptance.** 1. None of them appears in a portal response, on a public page, in page metadata, in a sitemap, or in the subject or body of a requester notification.

pinnedClauses.title: Duplicate suggestions
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** When an operator records evidence or a requester types a request title, Penny returns within 500ms up to 5 existing requests ranked by term overlap between the typed title and stored request titles and descriptions, and names the matched terms for each. **Acceptance.** 1. A requester is shown published requests only. 2. Matching is lexical and deterministic and keeps working when no model is configured; AI-001 adds meaning-based suggestions beside it. 3. Penny never links or merges without an explicit operator or requester action, or an auto-link or auto-merge rule an owner enabled (AI-002, AI-003).

pinnedClauses.title: Evidence attachments
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator can attach files to an evidence item within the limits in `seed.json` under BASE-INPUT-003. **Acceptance.** 1. An evidence attachment is readable only by an operator session and is never served from a public path, whatever the publication state of a linked request.

pinnedClauses.title: Tags
pinnedClauses.gap: Tags filtering every operator list, surviving a request merge and appearing in the export have no passing assertion; tag privacy is asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Operators create, rename, merge, and delete tags and apply them to evidence items and requests. **Acceptance.** 1. A tag is operator-only, filterable in every operator list, survives a request merge, and is included in the export.

pinnedClauses.title: Versions
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Editing an evidence item's wording writes a new version and leaves every earlier version readable to operators. **Acceptance.** 1. The item's own ID never changes.

pinnedClauses.title: Public portal
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** The portal serves published requests, a request detail page with its discussion, the public roadmap, and published releases. **Acceptance.** 1. *Policy: `request.visibility.v1`; default: any visitor may read all four without signing in.*

pinnedClauses.title: Requester identity
pinnedClauses.gap: The requester's chosen display name in a portal response has no passing assertion, and the check that no email address or account appears reads the public request list while it holds no published request, so it checks an empty list; submissions under a valid host-signed identity, with and without outbound mail, and the refusal of invalid or new host identities without mail are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Submitting, voting, commenting, following, subscribing, and recording an outcome each require either an email address verified under REQ-023 (by emailed link, or by Google or GitHub sign-in under REQ-039) or a host-signed identity under REQ-031 (from a parent frame, the widget, or WIDGET-008's sign-in redirect). **Acceptance.** 1. A portal response shows the requester's chosen display name and never their email address or account.

pinnedClauses.title: Submission
pinnedClauses.gap: The unreviewed evidence item created in the same transaction as the request, and requester edits held for moderation, have no passing assertion in this clause's evidence; the held submission and comment are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A requester submits a title, a problem description, an optional free-text proposed solution, an optional free-text impact statement, a board (REQ-018), a category where the board uses them (REQ-034), and optional attachments; on a board with vote subscriptions on, the form states before submission that the author will get updates (NOTIFY-011). **Acceptance.** 1. The submission atomically creates one unreviewed evidence item and one request awaiting moderation; the request is not public until an operator publishes it, except on a board whose owner turned on auto-publish (REQ-033). 2. *Policy: `request.moderation.v1`; default: each board's moderation setting in settings (REQ-033); on a board without auto-publish an operator reviews every requester submission, edit, and comment before it becomes public.*

pinnedClauses.title: Duplicate prevention
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Before a requester submits, the portal shows the suggestions from EVID-007 with a vote control and a follow control on each. **Acceptance.** 1. Choosing one applies that vote or follow and discards the draft, creating no request, evidence item, or moderation item.

pinnedClauses.title: Publication
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator publishes a moderated request by approving its public title, description, board, category (REQ-034), requester display name, and each attachment separately (REQ-011). **Acceptance.** 1. The published record contains only the approved fields.

pinnedClauses.title: Voting
pinnedClauses.gap: Refusing a vote outside Open, Under review, Planned or In progress, and the author's vote recorded at submission counting once, have no passing assertion; one vote per identity and the distinct-voter total are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A requester identity has at most one vote on a request and can remove it. **Acceptance.** 1. The vote total is the count of distinct current voters, and a vote is accepted only while the request's public status is Open, Under review, Planned, or In progress (REQ-016). 2. The author's vote recorded at submission is NOTIFY-011's and counts once like any other. 3. *Policy: `request.vote-eligibility.v1`; default: any verified requester may vote and every vote counts once.*

pinnedClauses.title: Discussion
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Verified requesters and operators can comment on a published request. Threaded replies and images in comments are REQ-037. **Acceptance.** 1. A requester comment is held under `request.moderation.v1` and becomes public only when an operator approves it; an operator comment is public when posted.

pinnedClauses.title: Merge
pinnedClauses.gap: Moving the duplicate's evidence links, approved attachments and followers, keeping its title and source as merge history, and merging a duplicate into the end of its chain have no passing assertion; the 301, moved comments and collapsed votes are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator can merge a duplicate request into the canonical request, which is the one that survives. **Acceptance.** 1. The operation atomically moves the duplicate's evidence links, approved attachments, comments, and followers, collapses the combined votes so each identity counts once, keeps the duplicate's title and source as merge history, and answers the duplicate's public URL with a 301 to the canonical request. 2. Merging a request that is itself a duplicate merges it into the canonical request at the end of its chain.

pinnedClauses.title: Unmerge
pinnedClauses.gap: Restoring the duplicate's votes, followers and evidence links, leaving post-merge additions on the canonical request and recording the reversal have no passing assertion; the duplicate's comment and status update reappearing are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator can reverse a merge. **Acceptance.** 1. Penny restores the duplicate request's own content, votes, comments, followers, and evidence links, leaves anything added to the canonical request after the merge on the canonical request, and records the reversal.

pinnedClauses.title: Follow and consent
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A verified requester can follow and unfollow a published request. **Acceptance.** 1. Submitting and voting present an unticked "Email me updates" control and grant no email permission on their own, except that on a board whose owner turned on vote subscriptions (NOTIFY-008) the vote control says that voting subscribes and the vote itself follows, and submitting subscribes the author (NOTIFY-011). 2. Following, or ticking that control, stores a timestamped permission record for the verified address, which is what makes the identity eligible under REL-004.

pinnedClauses.title: Portal attachments
pinnedClauses.gap: Rejecting a file with a reason without rejecting the request, and the declared content type and inline disposition of a published image, have no passing assertion; approval, the 404 before it and the served bytes are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A file submitted with a request is operator-only until an operator approves that file for publication. Supersedes `BASE-INPUT-003` for published image attachments only: while both the parent request and the file are published, `GET /api/public/attachments/:id` serves an image type in `seed.json → limits.uploadTypes` with an inline disposition so it renders on the request page, instead of the download disposition. **Acceptance.** 1. Rejecting a file records a reason for operators and does not reject the request. 2. While both the parent request and the file are published, `GET /api/public/attachments/:id` serves it with its declared content type and, for the image types in `seed.json → limits.uploadTypes`, an inline disposition. 3. In every other state that path returns 404.

pinnedClauses.title: Portal search and browse
pinnedClauses.gap: Category filtering, newest and recency-weighted last-14-day trending are implemented alongside search, board, status and existing sorts. Gap: the 500 ms first page has no seeded run at the seed.json limits (D-3).
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Visitors can search published request titles and descriptions, browse one board at a time, filter by public status and by category (REQ-034), and sort by vote total, by most recent public activity (the request's latest published comment, status update, or vote), by newest, or by trending, meaning new votes and published comments in the last 14 days with each day's activity weighted by recency and ties broken by vote total. **Acceptance.** 1. The first page returns within 500ms. 2. No result, count, or facet includes an internal board, an unpublished or removed request (REQ-041), or a held or removed comment.

pinnedClauses.title: Submission idempotency
pinnedClauses.gap: No test repeats a submission with its idempotency key to get the original request and evidence result back, sends a changed body under the same key for 409, or checks 30-day key retention and keys holding no personal data.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A public submission accepts an idempotency key. **Acceptance.** 1. Repeating the same submission with that key returns the original request and evidence result and creates no second record of any kind; the same key with a different body returns 409. 2. Keys are retained for 30 days and hold no personal data.

pinnedClauses.title: Identity failure
pinnedClauses.gap: The visitor being offered email verification (REQ-023) after a rejected identity has no passing assertion; the refusal of expired, future-dated and wrongly signed claims at the host-identity exchange with the identity-required error, no writes and no account or identity disclosure is asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A host-signed identity is expired when its signed issue time is more than 24 hours old or more than 5 minutes in the future. **Acceptance.** 1. An identity that is expired, or whose signature does not verify, is rejected for every identity-required action, changes no data, and reveals no account or identity match; the visitor is offered email verification (REQ-023) instead.

pinnedClauses.title: Status updates
pinnedClauses.gap: A status update rendered distinctly from comments, pinned above them and notifying followers under NOTIFY-001 has no passing assertion; posting a pinned update and its text on the request are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator can publish a status update on a published request. **Acceptance.** 1. It is rendered distinctly from comments, can be pinned above them, enters the request history, and notifies followers under NOTIFY-001. 2. Setting a request's status (REQ-036) publishes one.

pinnedClauses.title: Public status
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A published request has exactly one public status: Open, Under review, Planned, In progress, Shipped, or Declined. A declined request is Declined (REQ-017). Otherwise two sources can set it: the direct status an operator sets on the request (REQ-036), including one a migration lands (MIG-008), and the status its approved roadmap mapping projects under ROAD-003. Whichever of the two changed most recently wins: approving a mapping (ROAD-004) and each later transition of the mapped item count as changes of the mapped status at that moment, and a later direct status overrides the mapped one until the mapped item's next transition, the rule DELIV-006 uses for tracker changes. Withdrawing the mapping or dropping its item leaves the direct status, or Open if none was ever set. A request with neither source is Open. The operator request page shows which source the current public status comes from. **Acceptance.** A base test: 1. A request with no mapping reads Open, then Planned after a direct set. 2. Approving a mapping to an In progress item makes it In progress. 3. A later direct set to Planned wins until the item moves to Shipped, which then wins. 4. Withdrawing the mapping returns the last direct status. 5. Declining wins over both, and reversing the decline restores the status this rule gives. 6. Every public payload agrees within 5 seconds.

pinnedClauses.title: Decline
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator can decline a published request. A decline without a public reason is rejected. Declining sets the public status to Declined, adds the reason to the request history as a status update (REQ-015), and refuses new votes and requester comments while leaving existing ones visible and counted. Reversing a decline restores the request's previous public status. Decline and reversal ship through the operator request controls; repeating a decline with another reason preserves the prior direct or mapped status for reversal. **Acceptance.** 1. Through the routes and the customer and operator screens at 1440 and 390, a decline without a public reason is refused. 2. A decline sets Declined and adds its reason to the request history. 3. New votes and comments are refused while existing votes and discussion stay visible and counted. 4. Reversing a repeated decline restores the earlier status.

pinnedClauses.title: Boards
pinnedClauses.gap: Renaming, reordering and archiving boards, moving a request with its votes, comments, followers and evidence links, and the 409 on submission to an archived board have no passing assertion.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Every request belongs to exactly one board. **Acceptance.** 1. Operators create, rename, reorder, and archive boards in settings and can move a request to another board, which keeps its votes, comments, followers, and evidence links. 2. An archived board leaves portal navigation, keeps its published requests reachable at their URLs, and refuses a new submission with 409.

pinnedClauses.title: Internal boards
pinnedClauses.gap: Keeping internal-board requests off the public roadmap, out of releases and out of requester notifications has no passing assertion in this clause's evidence; the request and attachment 404s are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Each board is public or internal. **Acceptance.** 1. A request on an internal board never appears in a portal response, on the public roadmap, in a release, or in a requester notification, whatever its own publication state. 2. Moving a request to an internal board withdraws it from the portal within 5 seconds and its public URL returns 404.

pinnedClauses.title: Requester's own content
pinnedClauses.gap: Gap: Request title and description edit retention, and auto-publish edits with earlier wording retained for operators still lack complete passing assertions. Holding-board own-comment editing and approved-text retention through pending, rejected and approved edits are proved.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A requester can edit the title and description of their own request and the text of their own comment. **Acceptance.** 1. An edit to already-public text re-enters moderation under `request.moderation.v1`, and the previously approved text stays public until the edit is approved or rejected; on an auto-publish board (REQ-033) an unflagged edit is public on submission and the earlier text stays in the request's history for operators.

pinnedClauses.title: Requester withdrawal
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A requester can withdraw their own request. **Acceptance.** 1. A withdrawn request leaves moderation or the portal, its public URL returns 410, and its votes stop counting. 2. Its evidence item survives under EVID-004, marked withdrawn.

pinnedClauses.title: Blocking a requester
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator can block a requester identity. A blocked identity's submissions, votes, comments, follows, and outcome responses are refused with 403; their published requests and comments are hidden from the portal but kept for operators; and their votes stop counting toward totals. Unblocking restores all of it. Block and unblock ship in the private requester directory, and the server checks existing sessions on each participation write. **Acceptance.** 1. Through the routes and the requester and operator screens at 1440 and 390, a blocked identity's submission, vote, comment, follow and outcome response are refused. 2. Its published requests and comments leave the portal and its votes leave the totals, while operators keep them. 3. Unblocking restores visibility, counts and participation. 4. Refusing the audit write rolls back the block or unblock.

pinnedClauses.title: Email verification
pinnedClauses.gap: The verified session expiring after 30 days without use, and a held action discarded after 24 hours without verification, have no passing assertion; held actions applied on verification are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A requester verifies an email address by following a single-use link sent to it; the link expires 30 minutes after it is sent and fails after one use. **Acceptance.** 1. The verified session is a browser-local token created at the requester's first interaction and expiring after 30 days without use, so no portal surface sets a cookie. 2. An identity-required action attempted before verification is held for 24 hours, applied on the first verification of that address, and otherwise discarded, and it creates no vote, public record, or notification while held.

pinnedClauses.title: Requester identity merge
pinnedClauses.gap: The survivor keeping both verified addresses and all requests, comments, follows and permission records, votes collapsing to one, the recorded merge, and no new vote or permission record have no passing assertion; carried mutes and preferences and working old links are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator can merge two requester identities. **Acceptance.** 1. The survivor keeps both verified addresses and all requests, comments, follows, permission records, and suppression state; votes for the same request collapse to one; and the merge is recorded. 2. A merge creates no new vote and no new permission record.

pinnedClauses.title: Requester activity
pinnedClauses.gap: The current moderation state and public status of the requester's own requests in the view have no passing assertion; the view's counts of their requests, votes, follows and comments including held and rejected ones, and unfollow, mute and subscription changes from it, are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A verified requester has one view of their own participation and can manage their updates from it. **Acceptance.** 1. The view lists their own requests with their current moderation state and public status, their votes, their follows, and their own comments including held and rejected ones. 2. From that view they can unfollow, mute, or change their update subscription (REL-012).

pinnedClauses.title: Demand attribution
pinnedClauses.gap: The vote date in the private supporter view, and the first 50 supporters on expansion with Show more revealing 50 more at a time, have no passing assertion (the browser check clicks Show more until it is gone and counts only the full history); the separate vote, linked-evidence and distinct-account figures with no score, the supporter view's names, addresses, accounts, proxy marks and per-account totals, the complete history with no 100-person cap, and the portal showing none of it are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** For any request, operators can see every current voter's display name, verified address, and linked account, and the vote total broken down by account. None of it appears in a portal response. **Acceptance.** 1. The operator view shows the vote total (proxy votes marked, CAP-014), the linked-evidence count, and the distinct-account count as separate figures, and combines them into no score; only a prioritization view an operator builds under PRIO-003 may combine them, with every input shown. 2. The private supporter view shows each current voter's display name, vote date, every verified address and linked account, with native and historical UserVoice proxy marks, and per-account vote totals. 3. The first 50 supporters appear on expansion; Show more reveals 50 more at a time until the complete history is visible, with no 100-person cap. 4. The operator demand payload holds exactly the three separate figures and no score, and the portal shows none of it.

pinnedClauses.title: Portal embedding
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Penny's delta on BASE-PUBLIC-002: the portal is Penny's embeddable surface, and the owner lists its host origins in the `publicOriginAllowlist` setting. **Acceptance.** 1. The portal's permitted host origins are exactly those in `publicOriginAllowlist`.

pinnedClauses.title: Request queue
pinnedClauses.gap: Queue filters and sorts work; the 500 ms first page has no seeded run at the seed.json limits (D-3).
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Operators can list every request, including unpublished ones, filtered by moderation state, board, public status, tag, linked decision, and account, and sorted by vote total, most recent activity, or age. **Acceptance.** 1. The first page returns within 500ms.

pinnedClauses.title: Operator-authored request
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator can create a request from one or more evidence items. **Acceptance.** 1. It skips moderation, records the operator as its author, links the evidence it was created from, and becomes public only through REQ-005.

pinnedClauses.title: Moderation verdicts
pinnedClauses.gap: A rejected item counting toward no public total and staying visible with its reason to its author and operators, and the author notice's consent, suppression, mute and quiet-hours checks, have no passing assertion; the unsubscribe link and the once-only send are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator can approve, edit and then approve, or reject with a reason any request or comment awaiting moderation. **Acceptance.** 1. A rejected item never becomes public, counts toward no public total, stays visible with its reason to its author and to operators, and notifies its author only when the operator chooses to. 2. This private author-only notice requires current verified request-specific email consent and respects suppression, mute, unsubscribe and quiet hours; it does not publish the rejected content or create follower notifications.

pinnedClauses.title: Host identity claims
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A host-signed identity may assert a display name, an email address, and an account identifier and name. **Acceptance.** 1. A valid signature marks that address verified without a further challenge and links the requester to the matching or newly created account; any asserted commercial field is stored operator-only under EVID-006.

pinnedClauses.title: Internal notes
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Operators can add a note to any request. **Acceptance.** 1. A note is rendered distinctly from an operator comment and never appears in a portal response, page metadata, a release, or a notification.

pinnedClauses.title: States and queue
pinnedClauses.gap: The review date in the decision queue has no passing assertion; decisions in every state staying in the queue with their state and owner, and the last action and linked-evidence count, are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A decision is draft until its brief has a question, an owner, at least one candidate bet, and at least one linked evidence item, at which point it is ready; committing makes it committed, and DEC-007 makes a committed decision review due. A question that is blank as [docs/contract-mechanism.md](docs/contract-mechanism.md#blank-decision-questions) defines it does not count. **Acceptance.** 1. The decision queue lists every decision in each state with its owner, last action, review date, and linked-evidence count, and a decision changes row rather than leaving the queue when its state changes.

pinnedClauses.title: Brief
pinnedClauses.gap: Per-bet assumptions, the low, medium or high confidence level, the review date, and the requesters currently eligible under REL-004 through the mapped requests have no passing assertion, and the brief does not carry the eligible requesters yet; the question, accountable owner, candidate bets, linked evidence and accounts, and each bet's counter-evidence count are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A candidate bet is one named option a decision could commit to, and a bet has at most one internal roadmap item. **Acceptance.** 1. A decision brief holds a question, an accountable owner, its linked evidence and accounts, its candidate bets with the counter-evidence and assumptions for each, a confidence level of low, medium, or high, a review date, and the requesters currently eligible under REL-004 through its mapped requests.

pinnedClauses.title: Comparable bets
pinnedClauses.gap: The absence of a stored or displayed combined score and of an automatic ranking has no passing assertion: the bet record and the stored snapshot are checked in a way that allows extra fields, and bets are looked up by id, so their order is unchecked; each bet's metrics holding exactly the five dimension figures is asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Every candidate bet in a brief shows the same dimensions: affected requesters and accounts, the count and most recent observed time of its supporting evidence, its contradicting evidence, urgency, delivery shape, and an observable success measure. **Acceptance.** 1. Penny stores and displays no combined score and no automatic ranking of the bets.

pinnedClauses.title: Commitment
pinnedClauses.gap: The decision.commitment.v1 default that any operator may commit has no passing assertion, since every cited commit runs as the owner; the recorded declined bets and the evidence snapshot of evidence IDs, evidence-version IDs and DEC-003 dimensions, with the evidence itself unchanged, are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Committing requires a selected bet, a rationale, an owner, a confidence level, and a review date, and committing a brief with fewer than two candidate bets additionally requires a recorded reason why no viable alternative exists. **Acceptance.** 1. The operation records the declined bets and an evidence snapshot made of the evidence IDs, evidence-version IDs, and DEC-003 dimensions as they stood at that moment, without altering the evidence itself. 2. *Policy: `decision.commitment.v1`; default: any operator may commit.*

pinnedClauses.title: Commitment effects
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Committing atomically marks the decision committed, creates or updates the selected bet's internal roadmap item as Planned, leaves the declined bets' roadmap items unchanged, and links the decision to that roadmap item. **Acceptance.** 1. Commitment writes no public field itself; whether the new status reaches the portal is decided entirely by ROAD-004 and ROAD-005.

pinnedClauses.title: Revision
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A later change of selected bet or rationale under `decision.commitment.v1` supersedes the prior commitment as a new decision revision, and the original rationale, evidence snapshot, and declined bets stay readable. **Acceptance.** 1. A revision that changes the selected bet returns the superseded bet's roadmap item to Exploring and, where that item was published, withdraws its approval under ROAD-004 and prepares a status update draft under ROAD-007.

pinnedClauses.title: Review due
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A review is complete when an operator records a review note and either a new review date or a revision (DEC-006). **Acceptance.** 1. A committed decision whose review date has passed in `workspaceTimezone` without a complete review becomes review due within 1 hour and its owner is notified under NOTIFY-003. 2. Becoming review due changes no roadmap status, no public status, and no selected bet.

pinnedClauses.title: Outcome evidence
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Post-release evidence reaches the decision it informs without changing what supported the commitment. **Acceptance.** 1. A requester outcome (REL-008) and any evidence recorded against a linked release appear on the decision as post-release evidence within 60 seconds. 2. Neither alters the evidence snapshot that supported the commitment.

pinnedClauses.title: Internal states
pinnedClauses.gap: The activity entry a status change adds to the linked decision has no passing assertion in this clause's evidence; each transition's actor, reason and from and to status, the decision's unchanged state, and backward moves recorded as further transitions are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A roadmap item is Exploring, Planned, In progress, Shipped, or Dropped. **Acceptance.** 1. A status change records the actor, time, and reason and adds an activity entry to the linked decision without changing that decision's state. 2. Moving backward is allowed and is recorded as a further transition.

pinnedClauses.title: Internal record
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A roadmap item keeps its internal planning record beside its customer-safe wording. **Acceptance.** 1. A roadmap item holds its owner, target or release window, linked decision and evidence, account impact, confidence, delivery notes, and its customer-safe title, summary, and status.

pinnedClauses.title: Public projection
pinnedClauses.gap: The absence of account names, revenue, internal dates, confidence, rationale, evidence, declined bets and delivery notes from the projection has no passing assertion in this clause's evidence, whose check of the public item allows extra fields; the projected public status within 5 seconds and a dropped item's withdrawal are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** An approved roadmap item's public status follows its internal status within 5 seconds of a transition: Exploring is shown as Under review; Planned, In progress, and Shipped keep their labels; a Dropped item is withdrawn from the public roadmap. **Acceptance.** 1. The projection exposes only the approved title, summary, board, and public status; account names, revenue, internal dates, confidence, rationale, evidence, declined bets, and delivery notes are never projected.

pinnedClauses.title: Approval is publication
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A roadmap item and each of its request mappings are internal until an operator approves their customer-safe fields, and that approval alone is what puts them on the public roadmap and on the mapped requests. **Acceptance.** 1. A published request has at most one approved mapping; approving a second is rejected. 2. Withdrawing approval removes the projection from the portal within 5 seconds, makes its public roadmap URL return 404, and deletes no internal record. 3. *Policy: `roadmap.publication.v1`; default: an operator approves every public mapping explicitly.*

pinnedClauses.title: Commitment mapping
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** The roadmap item DEC-005 creates or updates is internal unless it already carries an approval under ROAD-004. **Acceptance.** 1. An already-approved item projects its new Planned status under ROAD-003; an unapproved item and its mappings stay private, and commitment never grants an approval.

pinnedClauses.title: Public roadmap
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A public roadmap whose source is approved roadmap items groups them under Under review, Planned, In progress, and Shipped and links each to its public request or release. A public roadmap whose source is request statuses follows ROAD-014. **Acceptance.** 1. It exposes no unapproved item and no count that includes one.

pinnedClauses.title: Status update draft
pinnedClauses.gap: The draft's absence of internal rationale, commercial context, declined bets and outcome prompts has no passing assertion in this clause's evidence, whose check of the draft allows extra fields, and no cited case reads the portal before the draft is published; a draft prepared for each approved status change with the safe title, problem and new public status, unpublished until an operator publishes it, and no draft for an unapproved item are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Every status change of a roadmap item that carries an approval under ROAD-004, and every request decline under REQ-017, prepares a draft customer-safe update naming the new public status and the problem it addresses. **Acceptance.** 1. The draft carries no internal rationale, commercial context, declined bet, or outcome prompt, and is invisible on the portal until an operator publishes it.

pinnedClauses.title: Status update publication
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Publishing that draft adds it to the history of every approved mapped request and queues one notification per update version for each requester eligible under REL-004 who follows one of those requests, deduplicated by identity and subject to the coalescing in NOTIFY-002. **Acceptance.** 1. Republishing the same version queues nothing further.

pinnedClauses.title: Draft and targets
pinnedClauses.gap: A saved draft holding its publication date, optional setup or usage link and outcome-prompt wording has no passing assertion; the title, type, tag, body, author and target are entered and saved.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A targeted release draft has one or more targets, each linking one roadmap item in any state to its decision and its approved public request mappings, or one published request directly (REL-019); a draft with no target is an announcement (REL-018). **Acceptance.** 1. The draft also holds a customer-safe title, a type of New, Improved, or Fixed, one or more subject tags drawn from EVID-009, a body, a publication date, an optional setup or usage link, an author, and, for a targeted release, the wording of the outcome prompt shown with the REL-008 response.

pinnedClauses.title: Publication
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator can publish a targeted draft only when it has a title, a body, at least one target, and every linked roadmap item at Shipped; publishing with any linked item in another state is rejected. Announcements publish under REL-018 and request targets under REL-019. **Acceptance.** 1. Publication makes one versioned update visible on the portal and durably records the complete recipient snapshot (REL-004) before it queues any delivery.

pinnedClauses.title: Published wording
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Published release wording is never overwritten. **Acceptance.** 1. A correction creates a new version, keeps the earlier version readable by operators, and marks which version the portal shows. 2. A correction changes the portal only; sending it to recipients requires an operator to send it as a new delivery version.

pinnedClauses.title: Recipient eligibility and snapshot
pinnedClauses.gap: The snapshot staying unchanged after a later merge, relink or preference change, and the release.recipient-eligibility.v1 default (which actions grant a permission record, that voting elsewhere and an operator-entered address grant none, and NOTIFY-009's one-snapshot addition) have no passing assertion; export and restore of the snapshot tables, an identity merge fenced while a send is in flight, and follower erasure are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A recipient is eligible when they hold a verified address and a current permission record, and each eligible identity appears exactly once in the snapshot however many target contexts it has. **Acceptance.** 1. At publication Penny snapshots every release target and each recipient's linked request or evidence context, and a later merge, relink, or preference change does not alter that snapshot. 2. *Policy: `release.recipient-eligibility.v1`; default: a permission record comes only from following a request (REQ-010), subscribing to updates (REL-012), voting on a board with vote subscriptions on (NOTIFY-008), submitting a request on such a board (NOTIFY-011) or an owner-selected migration carry-over (MIG-007, which makes its address eligible for email without verifying it); voting elsewhere and an operator-entered address grant nothing, and an operator's per-update choice to email captured contacts (NOTIFY-009) adds them to that one snapshot without a permission record.*

pinnedClauses.title: Customer-safe delivery
pinnedClauses.gap: The owner's brand header (INT-008) in release email and the remaining acceptance-point-1 email privacy obligations are unproved; private context staying out of the public updates is asserted. Live verified-domain, reply and inbox qualification remains held in R-6.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Release email and release portal content carry only the published release fields and the recipient's own request context. **Acceptance.** 1. Recipient lists, other requesters, account context, commercial impact, decision rationale, confidence, and declined bets never appear in either. 2. Release email carries the owner's brand header (INT-008), sender identity (NOTIFY-013) and postal address (NOTIFY-014).

pinnedClauses.title: Acceptance and retry
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Publication queues each eligible delivery within 60 seconds of its permitted send time (NOTIFY-002), with the release scheduling and ordering rules in [docs/contract-mechanism.md](docs/contract-mechanism.md#release-scheduling). **Acceptance.** 1. A failure returned before provider acceptance is retried up to 5 times with exponential backoff over 1 hour and then marked failed. 2. After acceptance Penny never resends automatically. 3. A result the provider leaves ambiguous, or a send interrupted before its outcome is known, is marked unknown and shown to operators, and Penny never replays it automatically with either provider (RULINGS.md RL-3): Resend suppresses a duplicate for its delivery key (REL-007), while SendGrid's delivery key is correlation only. 4. The published update stays visible on the portal in every failure state.

pinnedClauses.title: Idempotent delivery and provider events
pinnedClauses.gap: Resend idempotency key and signed event dedupe ship; SendGrid has no provider duplicate suppression, so its delivery key is correlation only (RL-3).
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Every release version and recipient has one durable delivery key that Penny passes to the mail provider as an idempotency key, and the accepted provider message ID is stored against it. **Acceptance.** 1. Resend receives each delivery key as its `Idempotency-Key` and suppresses a duplicate within 24 hours. 2. SendGrid receives each delivery key as a provider idempotency key in the same way, so a duplicate send for that key is suppressed. 3. `/api/public/mail/events` accepts only signed provider callbacks and deduplicates their event IDs, which are retained for 30 days; signed event receipts are retained without automatic deletion, consistent with BASE-DATA-002.

pinnedClauses.title: Outcome response
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A requester in a release's publication snapshot can answer Adopted, Partly adopted, or Not yet for each of its targets, whether or not they have muted or unsubscribed from email. **Acceptance.** 1. Penny stores one current response per release, requester, and target; changing it records a revision and updates the aggregates without exposing the requester on any public surface. 2. Repeating the same response records no revision.

pinnedClauses.title: Outcome coverage
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Operators can see, per target and for the whole release, the count of each response and the coverage, meaning current responses divided by snapshot recipients, and can see the individual responses. **Acceptance.** 1. Each current response links through its snapshotted target and recipient context back to the applicable request or evidence, roadmap item, and decision.

pinnedClauses.title: Empty feed
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** The public updates surface tells the truth when nothing has been released. **Acceptance.** 1. With no release published, the public updates surface states that there are no updates yet and renders no draft, example, or placeholder entry.

pinnedClauses.title: Bounces and complaints
pinnedClauses.gap: A soft bounce marking one delivery failed and suppressing nothing, a spam complaint's suppression, and suppression removing no vote, request, comment or portal access have no passing assertion; hard-bounce suppression is asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A hard bounce or a spam complaint suppresses the address: no further Penny email reaches it until the requester verifies it again, and its permission records are marked suppressed rather than deleted. **Acceptance.** 1. A soft bounce marks that one delivery failed and suppresses nothing. 2. Suppression removes no vote, request, comment, or portal access.

pinnedClauses.title: Update subscription
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A verified requester can subscribe to every published release from the public updates surface and unsubscribe there or from any notification's unsubscribe link. **Acceptance.** 1. Subscribing stores a timestamped permission record for that address; unsubscribing withdraws it without removing votes, requests, or follows.

pinnedClauses.title: Delivery states
pinnedClauses.gap: An out-of-order provider event never moving a delivery backward and never counting a result twice has no passing assertion.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A delivery moves through queued, then accepted, then delivered, and can terminate at failed, suppressed, or unknown. **Acceptance.** 1. An out-of-order provider event never moves a delivery backward along that order and never counts a result twice.

pinnedClauses.title: Requester updates
pinnedClauses.gap: Notifying voters on vote-subscription boards (NOTIFY-008) as followers has no passing assertion; the subscribed author's notice is asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A follower of a published request is notified when an operator publishes a status update on it (REQ-015), including a status set under REQ-036, declines it (REQ-017), publishes a status update mapped to it (ROAD-008), posts a public reply on it, approves a requester comment on it (REQ-007) or receives an auto-published one (REQ-033), unless they have muted that request or their address is suppressed. **Acceptance.** 1. Voters on vote-subscription boards (NOTIFY-008) and subscribed authors (NOTIFY-011) are notified as followers, and a merge notifies under NOTIFY-012. 2. Held or rejected comments, unpublished requests, internal boards, internal notes, and an internal roadmap transition with no published update notify nobody, and republishing the same update version notifies nobody again.

pinnedClauses.title: Preferences, timing, and unsubscribe
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A notification's permitted send time is the first moment after it is queued at which the requester's preferences and the quiet hours below allow it. *Policy: `requester.notification.v1`; default: hold requester email during the requester quiet hours the owner sets under OPS-008 (by default 20:00 inclusive to 08:00 exclusive in `workspaceTimezone`; the owner may turn them off), and coalesce updates for the same requester and request in a fixed 1-minute window starting with the first pending event into one message, with later events never extending that boundary.* The deployment timezone input and the release ordering rule are in [docs/contract-mechanism.md](docs/contract-mechanism.md#notification-timing). **Acceptance.** 1. Every requester notification carries a one-click unsubscribe link that works without signing in. 2. A requester can mute one request or all requester email; the preference is checked immediately before each send and removes no vote, evidence, or portal access. 3. An eligible notification sends as soon as its window and quiet hours allow, and a wakeup that comes earlier sends nothing. 4. A missed wakeup is recovered within a minute under the same delivery claims, and a repeated wakeup or recovery run never sends a notification twice.

pinnedClauses.title: Decision review
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A decision owner receives one email and one in-app notification, which stays in their notification list until dismissed, the first time a decision becomes review due. **Acceptance.** 1. Operator email carries no quiet hours and queues within 60 seconds of the decision becoming review due. 2. No repeat is sent until the review date changes or the operator completes the review and schedules another.

pinnedClauses.title: No mail loops
pinnedClauses.gap: Sign-in and verification mail going out from MAIL_FROM or a NOTIFY-013 sender, with Auto-Submitted: auto-generated and no reply-to, has no passing assertion; a follower's status notification's sender, header and absent reply-to, and the refusal of its reply at every door, are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Notifications are sent from a no-reply address, and Penny reads no mail at any address it sends from. The only inbound-mail route is CAP-009's dedicated capture address, which accepts mail only from operators and allowlisted senders and never from Penny's own notification addresses. **Acceptance.** 1. A reply to any notification creates no evidence item, comment, request, or other record. 2. Every notification, sign-in and verification message goes out from the deployment's `MAIL_FROM` or a NOTIFY-013 tested sender, carries `Auto-Submitted: auto-generated`, and has no reply-to unless the owner sets a monitored one under NOTIFY-013. 3. The Worker accepts inbound mail only through CAP-009’s dedicated platform-invoked email handler; no HTTP route accepts a posted mail message. 4. CAP-009’s handler refuses Penny’s own sender addresses, configured reply-to and notification replies, retaining only non-personal refusal counts; CAP-009 enforces reciprocal capture/reply-to exclusion, and NOTIFY-013 retains its other obligations. 5. A follower's status notification has its sender, no reply-to and the `Auto-Submitted` header; its reply, posted as a raw message, an Inbound Parse form and a JSON inbound webhook to the provider event route and each plausible capture path, is refused, and no table changes except the per-IP request counters every HTTP request charges.

pinnedClauses.title: Notification failure
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Requester status-update email and operator decision-review email each use a durable recipient-and-event key and retry, suppress, and expose failure exactly as REL-006, REL-011, and REL-013 describe. **Acceptance.** 1. The in-app or portal record of the same event stays available when the email fails.

pinnedClauses.title: Export contents
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Penny's delta on Base export: the export names every Penny record kind. **Acceptance.** 1. The export contains every durable record as JSON, including every operator, requester, identity merge, account, board, tag, request, moderation decision and reason, merge history, vote, comment, note, follower, block, evidence item and version, decision and revision, roadmap item and transition, release, release version and target, delivery with its key and provider message ID, outcome and revision, subscription, suppressed address, notification and preference, custom field, and audit entry, plus every attachment as its original file.

pinnedClauses.title: Public/private boundary
pinnedClauses.gap: The absence of operator-only field names and values from a public payload has no passing assertion over a non-empty response: both cited checks read the public request list while it holds no published request (the non-empty public-surface scan in tests/base/penny-evidence.test.ts is not cited here); the refusal of invalid signed claims without writes or identity disclosure is asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Operator-only data never travels in a public response, rendered or not. **Acceptance.** 1. No operator-only field name and no operator-only value appears anywhere in a public response payload, including in fields the portal does not render.

pinnedClauses.title: Erasure outranks history
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Penny's delta on Base erasure: where a clause here says a record is preserved, versioned, immutable, or never overwritten, erasure under BASE-DATA-003 takes precedence: the record is deleted or anonymized and the surviving audit entry keeps an anonymized reference. **Acceptance.** 1. Unmerging (REQ-009) and revision history never recreate erased data.

pinnedClauses.title: Custom fields
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Operators define custom fields in settings on each entity listed in `seed.json → customFields`, and can read and edit their values wherever that entity is shown. **Acceptance.** 1. A custom field is operator-only and is never projected to a public surface.

pinnedClauses.title: Permitted originals
pinnedClauses.gap: The deployment pinning the source installation and permitted source principals, and model output being unable to set identity or grants, have no passing assertion; separate original text, revision and time fields and nullable source identity are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Equal native operators select native evidence/requests and exact Orbit `rer-delegation/1` evidence targets with a recorded purpose/use basis and all-operator authorization. **Acceptance.** 1. The deployment pins the source installation and permitted source principals. 2. The adapter only reads selected targets; original text, source revision, supplied record time and retrieval time remain separate. 3. Requester/account links come only from native records; Orbit identity remains source-local and nullable. 4. Model output cannot set identity or grants.

pinnedClauses.title: Contestable learning
pinnedClauses.gap: Every option carrying the DEC-003 dimensions computed from originals, invalidation by native or source corrections with versioned operator contests, and the absence of automatic ranking, customer contact or publication have no passing assertion in this clause's evidence; validated spans, the clarification and the no-build option are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A configured model prepares an evidence comparison, exact validated spans, contradictions, uncertainty, a distinguishing clarification when evidence is thin, and a usable internal implementation brief. **Acceptance.** 1. Every option has the DEC-003 dimensions computed from originals, including a materially different no-build/process/support/onboarding option. 2. Native/source corrections invalidate current derived work; operator contests are versioned. 3. There is no automatic ranking, customer contact or publication.

pinnedClauses.title: Accountable pre-action choice
pinnedClauses.gap: The committed snapshot retaining the interpretation, original evidence, compared options, owner and full predeclared protocol, and missing protocol fields as explicit nulls that prevent commitment, have no passing assertion in this clause's evidence; commitment and its attributed audit are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator selects an option, rationale, confidence and review date. Commitment is a decision record, not execution or an observed customer outcome. **Acceptance.** 1. The immutable snapshot retains the exact interpretation, original evidence, comparable selected/declined options and owner, plus the predeclared cohort, denominator, baseline, window, measure, data source, comparison, limits, stop rule and budget. 2. Missing protocol fields are explicit nulls and prevent commitment.

pinnedClauses.title: Bounded recurring work
pinnedClauses.gap: Expiry, budget, correction-version and erasure-epoch checks before external work and in the result transaction, the absence of any implicit contact, production or publication effect, and interrupted or ambiguous calls keeping their uncertainty and reserved budget without retry have no passing assertion in this clause's evidence; durable runs, unchanged-input deduplication, in-flight pause and revoke, and pause, resume, revoke and disconnect are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Scheduled Worker events refresh selected sources and advance the authorized evidence comparison/internal brief. **Acceptance.** 1. Every run has a durable event/claim, source revision cursor and budget reservation; unchanged inputs produce no new artifact/card/model call. 2. Source, purpose, native authority, expiry, budget, correction version and erasure epoch are checked before external work and in the result transaction. 3. No implicit contact, production or publication effect exists. 4. Pause one/all, resume within a valid grant, revoke and disconnect are native operator controls. 5. Interrupted/ambiguous calls retain visible uncertainty and reserved budget rather than automatic retries.

pinnedClauses.title: Privacy closure
pinnedClauses.gap: Running claims becoming uncertain after a restore has no passing assertion: no run is in flight at export and nothing reads an uncertain claim after the restore; same-source erasure across duplicate connections, hash fences under a fresh connection, revocation purging copies and derived work, and a restore that leaves no investigation active and refuses a restored run with learning_scope_changed are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Person/native contribution erasure deletes dependent interpretations, corrections, commitment snapshots and provenance copies. DATA-003 erasure precedence remains operative. **Acceptance.** 1. Same-source external-person erasure covers duplicate connections. 2. Stable provider/installation/event and person hashes fence replay even under a fresh local source connection. 3. Source revocation purges copies and derived work; in-flight results cannot survive a changed scope or erasure epoch. 4. Archives carry this history and opaque fences, never credentials; restored sources/grants remain held and running claims become uncertain.

pinnedClauses.title: Configuration and proof boundary
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Absent source, model or enforcing RPC transport visibly refuses work. **Acceptance.** 1. Installation-controlled configuration declares a model, token prices/output bound and source read cost. 2. The run reserves its ceiling before work, refunds known unused cost and separates metered cost from uncertain reservations.

pinnedClauses.title: Saved records
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A current native operator previews saved feedback boards, posts/status, individual votes/comments, explicitly supplied merge chains (saved post API mergeHistory with complete posts, or owner relationship sidecars) and private tags. **Acceptance.** 1. Every mapped request receives one exact-provenance evidence item. 2. Historical contributors have a non-authorizing provenance representation; imports cannot grant verified identity, consent, authority, an outreach audience or commercial context.

pinnedClauses.title: Review and mapping
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Exact originals and explicit status/visibility choices bind the reviewed fingerprint. **Acceptance.** 1. Unsupported fields, missing references and aggregate-only data are named before apply. 2. Rejected mapping prevents application; no row is silently dropped or guessed. 3. Publication/moderation remains a distinct native decision.

pinnedClauses.title: Durable custody
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Native D1 changes, original custody, provenance and checkpoints commit atomically under current session/installation authority and maintenance fences. **Acceptance.** 1. Identical sources repeat without duplication; changed identities conflict. 2. Restart resumes the persisted plan rather than acquiring the source again. 3. Imports never send or enqueue external effects.

pinnedClauses.title: Safe reversal
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Undo/rollback removes only owned effects under full native value, revision, relationship and cardinality fences. **Acceptance.** 1. Later native work or shared dependencies cause a visible conflict without collateral deletion. 2. Reversal is durable and restartable; ordinary reversal retains originals.

pinnedClauses.title: Privacy precedence
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Erasure purges affected retained originals/creation copies and records opaque target fences. **Acceptance.** 1. Old imports cannot recreate erased effects. 2. Historical identity and import metadata participate in product archive and erasure classification; installation credentials remain non-portable.

pinnedClauses.title: Ideas aggregates
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Saved Ideas CSV rows become unpublished, unreviewed requests with one exact-provenance evidence item under explicit source-key, status and visibility mappings. **Acceptance.** 1. Count, company, score, formula, owner and custom fields remain private source material, with aggregate columns named in preview, numeric totals and source-row coverage for textual company data. 2. Counts never manufacture individual voters, commenters, followers, accounts or commercial records. 3. Unknown headings and missing required headings are refused by name; an idea ID or URL must be supplied, never invented from a title or row number.

pinnedClauses.title: Move-in receipt
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Preview, apply and reversal expose a private operator receipt with per-kind source/read/applied/skipped counts and reasons, destination counts, named omissions and unresolved relationships, non-authorizing identity treatment, and job-created mail and notification counts (zero). **Acceptance.** 1. Reversal names removed effects and conflicts preserving later native work, and reports retained originals. 2. Receipt contents, attribution and commercial/source fields remain outside public projections.

pinnedClauses.title: UserVoice saved source
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Saved UserVoice ideas-only and Ideas & Voters CSV exports, read by the headings UserVoice documents, become unpublished, unreviewed requests with one exact-provenance evidence item keyed by Idea ID, under explicit status, board and forum mappings. **Acceptance.** 1. Each idea and UserVoice User ID pair becomes one historical, non-authorizing vote attribution with its original link date; repeated rows for extra accounts or captured feedback fold into it and stay in the private original. 2. A supporter is marked proxy only from the documented feedback-capturer columns, the mark is shown in preview, receipt and the operator request page, and it never upgrades the supporter. 3. A Subscribed value creates no follow or permission unless the owner selects MIG-007 carry-over. 4. Names and email addresses never match, merge or link people; account, company, revenue, subscription and contact columns create no account, follow, consent, verified address or outreach audience. 5. Each file declares its export scope; an undeclared scope is refused, a filtered one shows a partial-history warning, and claimed vote counts beyond the supplied supporters are named aggregate-only and create nothing. 6. Unknown headings, unmapped statuses or forums, unzoned timestamps and spreadsheet workbooks are refused by name before any write.

pinnedClauses.title: Signed first owner
pinnedClauses.area: Optional installation ownership and visual editing
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Penny's delta on native Base bootstrap: a trusted configured issuer, public signing key ring, installation ID and exact application audience can admit the first owner. **Acceptance.** 1. Expiry, signature, audience, replay, concurrent second claim and any installed owner refuse authority. 2. The original setup token remains compatible. 3. Claims cannot supply trusted configuration or take over an existing workspace; raw credentials stay out of storage/archives.

pinnedClauses.title: Owner editor
pinnedClauses.gap: Compiled data-only edits applying after the destination hydrates with native navigation and privacy preserved, and the management service's own admission of its owner and frame origin, have no passing assertion; the short owner-only lease and the refusal of other operators and foreign origins are asserted.
pinnedClauses.area: Optional installation ownership and visual editing
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** The optional maintained editor receives only a short lease and validated management origin/installation ID after current native owner admission. **Acceptance.** 1. Equal product operators remain equal for product work; this does not grant owner configuration. 2. Compiled data-only edits apply after the rendered destination hydrates and preserve native navigation/privacy. 3. The management service independently admits its owner and registered frame origin.

pinnedClauses.title: Scoped keys
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** A current native operator may issue a named optional-expiry REST key. Its random value is revealed once; only its hash persists. Route-selected scopes are `requests:read`, `requests:write`, `comments:read`, `comments:write`, `status:read`, `status:write`, `releases:read`, `releases:write` and `votes:write`. The first eight admit their documented resource reads and writes; `votes:write` authorizes customer lookup at `GET /api/v1/proxy-vote-contacts` and recording an attributed customer proxy vote at `POST /api/v1/requests/:slug/proxy-votes`, without verification or email permission. Bearers never grant operator HTML, generated-function, export or owner configuration authority. **Acceptance.** 1. A current token with `votes:write` records a proxy vote. 2. A token without that scope is refused the same vote write and changes no vote or permission record. 3. Revocation refuses the next write.

pinnedClauses.title: Current custody
pinnedClauses.gap: Credentials staying out of portable archives, and a restore honouring none, have no passing assertion; usage metadata written before authority is returned with storage failure refusing, revocation, expiry and issuer removal fencing requests and business writes, and a bearer key refused at export are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Penny's delta on server-side authorisation for scoped keys: revocation, expiry and issuer authority changes fence every API request and its business transaction in the same native database. **Acceptance.** 1. Authorization writes safe usage metadata durably before returning authority; storage failure refuses. 2. Credentials are installation custody and are not a portable identity backup.

pinnedClauses.title: Native publication
pinnedClauses.gap: That imported or restored history creates no new publication or integration effect has no passing assertion: the cited upgrade case snapshots its tables after the import and compares them only across migrations, and no cited case restores an archive; prior history, including imported feedback, staying unchanged across each new migration is asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** API writes reuse native validation, moderation, explicit customer-safe approval, consent, maintenance and immutable snapshots. Tracker synchronization follows the Delivery sync clauses (DELIV-001–DELIV-010), never an API side effect. **Acceptance.** 1. Imported/restored history creates no new publication or integration effect.

pinnedClauses.title: Explicit integration effects
pinnedClauses.gap: Gap: Selected public event kinds, immutable destinations, atomic business-write/event-target capture, held restored history and portable safe integration history with nonportable credentials lack complete passing assertions.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Operators select approved public request/comment/status/release events and immutable destinations. **Acceptance.** 1. Native writes and event targets commit together. 2. Imported/restored history cannot create live outbound effects. 3. Product archives carry safe event/attempt/receipt history; installation credentials are nonportable.

pinnedClauses.title: Enforcing transport
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Webhook/Slack dispatch uses the maintained Base delivery service through an installation-owned enforcing RPC transport. **Acceptance.** 1. Missing transport disables outbound integrations.

pinnedClauses.title: Durable uncertainty
pinnedClauses.gap: Gap: Durable attempt identity, finite retry, ambiguity/reconciliation and revoked/private/blocked send fencing lack complete passing assertions.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Attempt identity, finite retry, ambiguity and explicit reconciliation survive restart. **Acceptance.** 1. An ambiguous effect does not resend under another identity. 2. Revoked configuration and private/blocked content cannot start a send.

pinnedClauses.title: Signed inbound notes
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Original bounded bytes verify before parsing; current native authority, replay identity, internal note and processed receipt commit together. **Acceptance.** 1. Notes do not publish content or grant identity or consent.

pinnedClauses.title: Deliberate tracker issues
