pinnedClauses.gap: Gap: Complete Linear/Jira create and link from requests/decisions, entered-only wording and uncertain-outcome reconciliation lack passing assertions.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Operators create or link a selected Linear or Jira issue from a request or decision. Ongoing state mapping, GitHub, Vector, Azure DevOps, ClickUp and Asana are DELIV-001–DELIV-010. **Acceptance.** 1. Only entered wording is sent. 2. Native durable commands retain uncertain outcomes for explicit known-issue reconciliation and never create a duplicate automatically.

pinnedClauses.title: Private tracker receipts
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Provider-specific raw-byte authentication, configured identity, durable replay and original source order guard state receipts in the same D1 transaction. **Acceptance.** 1. Older or conflicting events cannot regress state. 2. Linked state remains private evidence until an operator separately chooses Penny status or publication, except for the tracker states an admin maps under DELIV-006.

pinnedClauses.title: Owner portal branding
pinnedClauses.gap: The accent, description and Penny mark controls ship. Uploaded logos and favicons, their same-origin versioned serving and upload refusals, the website link and theme selection remain unproved.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Owners and Admins (OPS-001) set the portal's brand in settings, as Canny's Branding settings do on every plan: a company name (required at first-run setup, OPS-005, and editable later; it replaces the build-time `publicLandingConfig.ownerName` everywhere an installation names itself), a square logo (PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG sanitized to drop scripts and external references) and a favicon (ICO, PNG or SVG), each within `seed.json → limits` upload limits, an optional link back to the company website (an `https` URL), a readable public accent, the portal description, a light, dark or follow-the-system theme for the portal and widget, and whether Penny's own vector mark shows. **Acceptance.** A browser journey at 1440 and 390 pixels: 1. The owner uploads a PNG logo and an ICO favicon and sets the name "Acme" and dark theme; the portal header shows the logo and "Acme" in dark theme. 2. The logo and favicon are stored in the installation's R2 and served from its own origin at stable versioned paths: the document's icon link is the uploaded favicon, served from the same origin, and the portal makes no request to another origin. 3. A PDF, an oversize PNG and an SVG with a script are refused before storage. 4. The accent, description, theme, website link and Penny mark controls save and apply to the next page load.

pinnedClauses.title: Brand on every customer surface
pinnedClauses.gap: The company name is collected at setup and used by sender identity (OPS-005, NOTIFY-013); applying it throughout the portal in place of publicLandingConfig.ownerName, the website link, the logo on the widget, the changelog, the sign-in page and email, and the neutral default icon remain unproved.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** The brand reaches every customer-facing surface: the portal header (logo and name, linking to the company website when set, else to the board), the browser tab's icon and title on every portal page, the widget launcher and panel (WIDGET-001, WIDGET-003), the changelog page and feeds (REL-015, REL-016), the SSO sign-in page (WIDGET-008), and every requester and release email (NOTIFY-001, REL-005), whose header carries the logo and company name and whose sender name follows NOTIFY-013. A change applies to the next page load and the next message composed. **Acceptance.** A browser journey at 1440 and 390 pixels: 1. The company name replaces `publicLandingConfig.ownerName` everywhere the installation names itself. 2. The portal header links to the company website when set, else to the board. 3. The widget panel and the changelog page show the logo. 4. A status email to a follower carries "Acme" and the logo from the installation's origin. 5. Without a logo the header shows the name alone and the tab shows a neutral default icon, never a customer's.

pinnedClauses.title: Branding permissions and portability
pinnedClauses.gap: Admin branding controls remain unproved: the 403 refusals of branding writes by other roles and the archive round trip of logo bytes and branding settings have no passing assertion.
pinnedClauses.text: **Requirement.** Only Owners and Admins change the brand, and the brand travels with the installation's data. **Acceptance.** 1. Product managers, Contributors and Viewers are refused branding writes. 2. Branding (name, files, colors, theme, link) participates in product archives (DATA-001): an archive export and restore keeps the logo bytes and settings.

pinnedClauses.title: Workspace timezone and requester quiet hours
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-ROLE-001 **Requirement.** First-run setup (OPS-005) asks the owner for the workspace timezone, an IANA timezone pre-selected from the owner's browser (or from the `WORKSPACE_TIMEZONE` deployment input when it is set), and refuses Finish without one. The choice is stored as installation state that Owners and Admins change later in settings; once stored it is the `workspaceTimezone` every clause uses (NOTIFY-002, DEC-007, REL-014), and no installation that has recorded a choice falls back to a built-in default. An installation that finished setup before this ships shows its owner a one-time prompt, on their next sign-in, to confirm or change the current timezone. Settings also hold the requester quiet hours, shown beside the timezone at setup: off, or a start and an end hour in the workspace timezone (default 20:00 to 08:00). Operator email never has quiet hours (NOTIFY-003). A change applies at the next send check, and turning quiet hours off makes every held requester message due at once. In Admin settings, Owners and Admins set the workspace timezone and requester business hours through the quiet-hours schedule. Changes take effect for clocks and SLAs from the change, including the next queued requester send check and calendar-based decision review check. **Acceptance.** A base and browser journey: 1. Setup refuses Finish without a timezone. 2. Setup under an `America/New_York` browser timezone stores `America/New_York`. 3. With the default quiet hours, a status update published at 21:00 Eastern sends at 08:00 Eastern and one published at 14:00 Eastern sends within NOTIFY-002's coalescing window. 4. With quiet hours off, an update published at 23:00 Eastern sends within the coalescing window. 5. Changing the timezone in settings moves the next quiet period. 6. The confirmation prompt appears once for an installation set up before the change. 7. An Owner and an Admin each save the timezone and quiet-hours schedule in Admin, an ordinary operator is refused, and changing the timezone changes a calendar review's next due check while turning quiet hours off releases queued requester mail without delaying operator mail.

pinnedClauses.title: Custom roles and restricted commercial fields
pinnedClauses.gap: A base test signs in under a role without commercial permission and reads requests, accounts, prioritization views, CSV exports and Ask Penny answers through their routes: no revenue, opportunity or health value appears; granting the permission reveals them on the next request; each role change is in the audit log (ROLE-004).
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-ROLE-001 **Requirement.** Admins define custom roles from a fixed permission set (capture evidence and proxy votes, moderate, publish, commit decisions, manage roadmap, manage releases, manage integrations, manage automation, view commercial fields, export, erase) and assign them to operators. Commercial fields (revenue, MRR/ARR, opportunity amounts, health) are hidden from roles without "view commercial fields" in every screen, API response, export, agent answer and notification, including AI-006 draft context and publication checks. **Acceptance.** A base test signs in under a role without commercial permission and reads requests, accounts, prioritization views, CSV exports and Ask Penny answers through their routes: 1. No revenue, opportunity or health value appears. 2. Granting the permission reveals them on the next request. 3. Each role change is in the audit log (ROLE-004).

pinnedClauses.title: Operator single sign-on
pinnedClauses.gap: Today only the optional IDENTITY_PROVIDER dependency is declared; sign-in remains email links. A browser journey against SAML and OIDC test identity providers at the network edge: a first sign-in creates a Contributor, a group claim maps another user to Admin, an enforced domain refuses an email link, and an IdP-side deactivation ends access at the next session check.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-SIGNIN-001 · *Register:* R-14 **Requirement.** Penny's delta on Base standards-based SSO: operators sign in with SAML 2.0 or OIDC from Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace or Auth (the sibling identity provider, https://github.com/just-every/run-auth). The owner can enforce SSO for a verified email domain (email links then refuse that domain), provision operators just in time with a default role, and map IdP groups to roles. **Acceptance.** A browser journey against SAML and OIDC test identity providers at the network edge: 1. A first sign-in creates a Contributor. 2. A group claim maps another user to Admin. 3. An enforced domain refuses an email link. 4. An IdP-side deactivation ends access at the next session check. 5. An address on an SSO-enforced domain that signs in through REQ-039 stays only a requester, and REQ-039's unverified fallback link obeys the domain's email-link refusal.

pinnedClauses.title: SCIM provisioning
pinnedClauses.gap: Okta and Entra SCIM request fixtures through the public endpoint create, patch and deactivate a user; the deactivated user's session and API key are refused on their next request, as they are after OPS-002 removal.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Later · *Cites:* BASE-SIGNIN-001 · *Register:* R-15 **Requirement.** SCIM 2.0 Users and Groups endpoints let Okta and Entra create operators, change their role by group membership and deactivate them; deactivation revokes cookies, links, generated functions and keys exactly as OPS-002 removal does. **Acceptance.** 1. Okta and Entra SCIM request fixtures through the public endpoint create, patch and deactivate a user. 2. The deactivated user's session and API key are refused on their next request, as they are after OPS-002 removal.

pinnedClauses.title: Audit log
pinnedClauses.gap: Durable actor audits are recorded and archived today; there is no audit screen or export. Perform each listed action (including REQ-038 and REQ-041 edits, removals, restores and permanent deletes and INT-007 and NOTIFY-013 changes), then read and export the log through the UI and API; erase an operator and see their entries anonymized while the events remain.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-AUDIT-001, BASE-OPS-005 **Requirement.** Penny's delta on Base audit: Owners and Admins read, filter (actor, action, subject, date) and export as CSV or JSON an audit log of every privileged action: publication, moderation verdict, edit (REQ-038), removal, restore and permanent delete (REQ-041) of published content, branding and sender changes (INT-007, NOTIFY-013), merge and unmerge, commitment, role and member change, integration connect and disconnect, automation rule change, export, erasure and every agent action, with the person or agent responsible. **Acceptance.** 1. Perform each listed action, then read and export the log through the UI and API. 2. Entries contain no customer wording or commercial values. 3. Erase an operator and see their entries anonymized while the events remain (DATA-003).

pinnedClauses.title: Saved views and filters
pinnedClauses.gap: A browser test saves a filtered, sorted view, then a second operator opens the shared view and gets the same result set; a private view is not listed for them.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Every operator list (inbox, requests, features, evidence, accounts, roadmap, releases) filters on any field, custom field, tag, theme, segment, owner and date, chooses its columns and sort, and saves the result as a private or shared view. **Acceptance.** 1. A browser test saves a filtered, sorted view, then a second operator opens the shared view and gets the same result set. 2. A private view is not listed for them.

pinnedClauses.title: Person view
pinnedClauses.gap: Voter lists and account requesters ship today; no per-person page exists. A fixture requester with two posts, three votes, a comment, captured Zendesk evidence and an account: the profile lists each with a link to its record; a role without commercial permission sees no ARR or MRR; the profile path answers 404 to a portal visitor and appears in no public payload.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Every requester and captured contact has an operator profile: display name, verified and carried-over addresses (MIG-007), company or account with its ARR and MRR (ROLE-001), segment membership (SEG-006), custom fields (DATA-004), every request they submitted, voted on (with importance, REQ-035, and proxy marks), followed or commented on, the evidence captured about them with its source links (CAP-002), their permission records and suppression state, and their outcome responses (REL-008). It is reachable from global search (OPS-004), request voter lists (REQ-026) and account pages (EVID-005), and offers merge (REQ-024), block (REQ-022), export and erasure (DATA-003). **Acceptance.** 1. A fixture requester with two posts, three votes, a comment, captured Zendesk evidence and an account: the profile lists each with a link to its record. 2. A role without commercial permission sees no ARR or MRR. 3. The profile path answers 404 to a portal visitor and appears in no public payload.

pinnedClauses.title: Feedback inbox
pinnedClauses.gap: Today the unreviewed evidence list does this for portal and manually recorded evidence only. A browser journey at 1440 and 390 pixels: items from three connector fixtures arrive, are triaged by keyboard (link, create, dismiss with reason, snooze), each linked request shows the item with its source link, and the overview counts match the inbox.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Every item captured from any channel (portal, widget, connectors, email, Slack, browser extension, API) lands once as unreviewed evidence (EVID-001) in one inbox that shows its source, customer, account, segment attributes, excerpt and suggested links (AI-002). From the inbox an operator links it to a request, creates a request (REQ-029), adds it to a decision, assigns an owner (TRIAGE-001), tags it, snoozes it until a date or marks it reviewed with a reason, by keyboard and in bulk (TRIAGE-005). The inbox filters by source, connector, owner, segment, theme, age and state. **Acceptance.** A browser journey at 1440 and 390 pixels: 1. Items from three connector fixtures arrive, are triaged by keyboard (link, create, dismiss with reason, snooze), each linked request shows the item with its source link, and the overview counts match the inbox.

pinnedClauses.title: Source provenance and link-back
pinnedClauses.gap: EVID-002 provenance ships today for manually recorded sources without deep links or source sync. A connector fixture test captures a record, edits it at the source and deletes it at the source: Penny shows changed and removed states, purges the excerpt at the window, and the deep link opens the original record.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** A captured item stores its connector, the source record's ID, a deep link to the original (ticket, conversation, call timestamp, Slack permalink, email message ID or page URL), the verbatim excerpt the operator or rule selected, the author or speaker as the source names them, the capturing person or rule and the source's own time. When the source record changes, the captured version stays and Penny shows that the source changed; when it is deleted or access is revoked at the source, the item is marked source-removed and its excerpt is purged after the owner's policy window. **Acceptance.** 1. A connector fixture test captures a record, edits it at the source and deletes it at the source: Penny shows changed and removed states, purges the excerpt at the window, and the deep link opens the original record.

pinnedClauses.title: Zendesk
pinnedClauses.gap: Zendesk OAuth, API and webhook fixtures at the network edge: install, link, create and proxy-vote from the sidebar; tag-triggered capture creates one item per ticket however often the webhook replays; the status appears in the sidebar; uninstalling revokes and deletes the tokens.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1, D-2 · *Register:* R-5, R-8 **Requirement.** A Zendesk app in the ticket sidebar lets an agent search requests, link the ticket to one, create a new request, record a proxy vote for the ticket's requester (CAP-014) and see the request's public status without leaving Zendesk. Tickets with a configured tag or in a configured view are captured automatically. The ticket requester and organization map to a Penny requester and account by email and organization ID. When a linked request changes status, the sidebar shows it and offers the drafted reply (NOTIFY-007). **Acceptance.** 1. Zendesk OAuth, API and webhook fixtures at the network edge: install, link, create and proxy-vote from the sidebar. 2. Tag-triggered capture creates one item per ticket however often the webhook replays. 3. The status appears in the sidebar. 4. Uninstalling revokes and deletes the tokens.

pinnedClauses.title: Intercom
pinnedClauses.gap: Intercom API and webhook fixtures run CAP-003's journey and show company attributes arriving as private segment attributes.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1, D-2 **Requirement.** An Intercom Inbox app (Canvas Kit) offers CAP-003's actions inside a conversation; conversations with a configured tag or topic are captured; Intercom contacts and companies map to requesters and accounts with their custom attributes (plan, MRR) feeding segments (SEG-006); NOTIFY-007 replies can go back through the conversation. **Acceptance.** 1. Intercom API and webhook fixtures run CAP-003's journey and show company attributes arriving as private segment attributes.

pinnedClauses.title: HappyToHelp
pinnedClauses.gap: A journey against a running HappyToHelp test installation links a ticket, captures one by tag and receives the drafted status reply on that ticket.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1, D-2 **Requirement.** HappyToHelp, the sibling help desk (https://github.com/just-every/run-happytohelp), gets CAP-003's sidebar, tag capture and close-the-loop replies through its public API. Neither product keeps the other's records beyond the linked excerpt and IDs. **Acceptance.** 1. A journey against a running HappyToHelp test installation links a ticket, captures one by tag and receives the drafted status reply on that ticket.

pinnedClauses.title: Help Scout
pinnedClauses.gap: Help Scout API fixtures: link, create, tag capture and mapping, each once per conversation.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1, D-2 **Requirement.** A Help Scout sidebar app and tag-based capture with customer and company mapping, on CAP-003's terms. **Acceptance.** Help Scout API fixtures: 1. Link, create, tag capture and mapping, each once per conversation.

pinnedClauses.title: Gong
pinnedClauses.gap: Gong API fixtures: filtered calls are ingested, proposals carry exact transcript spans and timestamps, accounts map through Gong's CRM association, and the fixture records no request for an out-of-filter call.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** For calls matching configured filters (workspace, tracker, deal stage, participants), Penny reads the transcript and call metadata, and the extraction agent (AI-004) proposes the feature-request moments as inbox items with the verbatim span, speaker, a timestamped deep link and the deal and account Gong associates. Calls outside the filters are never read. **Acceptance.** Gong API fixtures: 1. Filtered calls are ingested, proposals carry exact transcript spans and timestamps, accounts map through Gong's CRM association, and the fixture records no request for an out-of-filter call.

pinnedClauses.title: Call recorders, recordings and transcripts
pinnedClauses.gap: Fathom, Zoom, Google Meet, Fireflies, Grain and tl;dv fixtures each ingest one filtered call with timestamped spans and ignore an out-of-filter call; a VTT upload produces a searchable transcript whose highlight becomes evidence with a timestamp link; an audio upload shows progress, reserved and metered cost, and a visible failure when the provider fails.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** Fathom, Zoom cloud recording, Google Meet (Workspace recordings and transcripts), Fireflies, Grain and tl;dv connectors work on CAP-007's terms. An operator can also upload a recording or a VTT, SRT or text transcript; audio is transcribed by the owner-configured transcription provider as a bounded background job with LEARN-006's cost rules. Transcripts are searchable, and a highlighted passage becomes evidence linked to its timestamp. **Acceptance.** 1. Fathom, Zoom, Google Meet, Fireflies, Grain and tl;dv fixtures each ingest one filtered call with timestamped spans and ignore an out-of-filter call. 2. A VTT upload produces a searchable transcript whose highlight becomes evidence with a timestamp link. 3. An audio upload shows progress, reserved and metered cost, and a visible failure when the provider fails.

pinnedClauses.title: Email capture
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-2 · *Register:* R-3 **Requirement.** Each installation has a dedicated capture address on the owner's domain (Cloudflare Email Routing or the configured mail provider's inbound parse). Operators forward or BCC customer emails to it. Penny accepts only mail from operator addresses or allowlisted domains with DMARC alignment, recovers the original sender from the forwarded message, keeps attachments within `seed.json` limits and creates one inbox item per message ID. Notification reply addresses never reach this route, and it refuses mail from Penny's own sender addresses (`MAIL_FROM` and any NOTIFY-013 sender), as NOTIFY-004 requires. **Acceptance.** Inbound-mail fixtures: 1. Forwarded Gmail and Outlook messages each create one item attributed to the original sender. 2. A replayed message ID, an unaligned sender, mail from Penny's own sender address and a reply to a Penny notification create nothing.

pinnedClauses.title: Slack and Nook
pinnedClauses.gap: Signed Slack Events and Interactivity fixtures: the shortcut and the reaction each capture a message once, a bad signature is refused, and a Slack Connect channel maps to its account; the same capture runs against a Nook test installation.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 · *Register:* R-8 **Requirement.** A Slack app adds a "Send to Penny" message shortcut and an emoji-reaction trigger in selected channels, including Slack Connect channels shared with customers. The message and its thread permalink become an inbox item, the Slack user who triggered it is the capturer, and a Slack Connect workspace maps to an account. Nook, the sibling team chat (https://github.com/just-every/run-nook), offers the same actions. Outbound Slack posts are NOTIFY-006 and INT-001. **Acceptance.** Signed Slack Events and Interactivity fixtures: 1. The shortcut and the reaction each capture a message once, a bad signature is refused, and a Slack Connect channel maps to its account. 2. The same capture runs against a Nook test installation.

pinnedClauses.title: Microsoft Teams
pinnedClauses.gap: Bot Framework fixtures with token validation capture a message once and refuse an unsigned request.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** A Teams message action captures a message and its link into the inbox; channel notifications follow NOTIFY-006. **Acceptance.** 1. Bot Framework fixtures with token validation capture a message once and refuse an unsigned request.

pinnedClauses.title: Browser extension
pinnedClauses.gap: A Playwright extension journey on a fixture page creates an inbox item with the URL, excerpt and screenshot attachment; a signed-out extension is refused.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 · *Register:* R-8 **Requirement.** A Chrome and Edge extension (Manifest V3), signed in with the operator's Penny session, captures selected text or a screenshot from any page (a CRM record, a review site, a community thread) with its URL, picks the customer and the request, and can record a proxy vote. **Acceptance.** 1. A Playwright extension journey on a fixture page creates an inbox item with the URL, excerpt and screenshot attachment. 2. A signed-out extension is refused.

pinnedClauses.title: CRM record panels
pinnedClauses.gap: HubSpot and Salesforce fixtures render the panel for a record's company, capture feedback tied to an opportunity amount and attribute a proxy vote to the right customer.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** A HubSpot CRM card and a Salesforce Lightning component on contact, company or account and deal or opportunity records show that account's requests and their statuses, and let sales capture feedback or a proxy vote tied to the opportunity (SEG-002). Orbit gets the same panel through its extension point. **Acceptance.** 1. HubSpot and Salesforce fixtures render the panel for a record's company, capture feedback tied to an opportunity amount and attribute a proxy vote to the right customer.

pinnedClauses.title: Proxy votes
pinnedClauses.gap: UserVoice-imported supporters keeping their historical proxy marks (IMP-008) have no passing assertion in this clause's evidence (tests/base/feedback-import-uservoice.test.ts asserts them and is not cited here), and the CSV export is checked for the source text and the customer but never the recorder; counting once per customer, the proxy mark with who recorded it, collapse with the customer's own later vote, no verified identity, consent or permission record, public appearance only inside the vote total, and recording from the inbox, the request page and the Zendesk sidebar fixture are asserted.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Register:* R-5 **Requirement.** An operator records a vote on behalf of a customer (an existing requester, a connector contact, or a new unverified contact) with the source that justifies it. **Acceptance.** 1. A proxy vote counts once per customer in demand (REQ-026, SEG-007), is marked proxy with who recorded it, and collapses with that customer's own later vote. 2. It grants no verified identity or email consent (REQ-010), and appears publicly only inside the vote total. 3. Native proxy recording works from the inbox, the request page and the private Zendesk sidebar at the connector edge, proved with a network-edge fixture. 4. Supporters imported from UserVoice (IMP-008) retain their historical proxy marks. 5. A base test records proxy votes from the inbox, the request page and a Zendesk sidebar fixture: each counts once, collapses with the customer's own later vote, creates no permission record, and appears in the CSV export with its recorder.

pinnedClauses.title: Automation platforms
pinnedClauses.gap: Scoped keys and outbound events ship today; no packaged app exists. A Zapier CLI test against a running installation fires each trigger once per event and runs each action within its key's scopes; an out-of-scope action is refused.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 · *Register:* R-8 **Requirement.** Zapier and Make apps offer triggers (new request, status change, new evidence, release published) and actions (create evidence, create request, record proxy vote, find request) over the scoped REST API (API-001) and signed webhooks (INT-001); Crank, the sibling automation seed (https://github.com/just-every/run-crank), uses the same surface. Owners install the app definitions Penny publishes against their own installation; a public directory listing is a register row. **Acceptance.** 1. A Zapier CLI test against a running installation fires each trigger once per event. 2. It runs each action within its key's scopes. 3. An out-of-scope action is refused.

pinnedClauses.title: Connector health
pinnedClauses.gap: Delivery and tracker-receipt states are shown today for outbound integrations only. A clock-advanced fixture with an expired token and a rate limit shows the connector failing with its reason once an hour passes without a successful sync (or after the owner's shorter setting), notifies the owner once, and after reconnect resumes from its cursor without duplicate items.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Each connector shows the connected account, scope, last successful sync, items captured, backlog and its last failure with the reason and a fix (reconnect, grant scope). A connector with no successful sync for 1 hour (the owner may set 15 minutes to 24 hours per connector in its settings) is failing: it notifies the owner once per failure episode (NOTIFY-006) and appears on the overview until a sync succeeds. Disconnecting revokes and deletes its tokens and stops capture; captured evidence stays. **Acceptance.** 1. A clock-advanced fixture with an expired token and a rate limit shows the connector failing with its reason once an hour passes without a successful sync (and after the owner's shorter setting when set), notifies the owner once, and after reconnect resumes from its cursor without duplicate items.

pinnedClauses.title: Capture scope, minimization and consent
pinnedClauses.gap: Purpose-bound selected-record acquisition ships today for Orbit and native records (LEARN-001). Connector fixtures assert that no request is made for out-of-scope records, that redaction precedes the write, and that captured people hold no permission record (NOTIFY-009 sends create none either).
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Connectors read only the configured scope (channels, tags, views, call filters, record types), store the selected excerpt rather than the whole record unless the operator chooses otherwise, apply redaction (AI-008) before storage, keep any source person nullable and non-authorizing (EVID-002), and never create an email permission record for a captured person (REQ-010); a captured contact is emailed only when an operator chooses so for one update under NOTIFY-009. **Acceptance.** 1. Connector fixtures assert that no request is made for out-of-scope records, that redaction precedes the write, and that captured people hold no permission record.

pinnedClauses.title: Submission forms and polls
pinnedClauses.gap: A conditional question renders and validates on the portal and the widget at both widths; poll answers aggregate per request and by segment and stay operator-only.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Owners configure the portal and widget submission form per board: custom questions (text, single or multiple choice, number, rating), required and conditional fields, and a short poll attached to a request or a release ("How important is this to you?"). Answers are evidence linked to the request and filterable by segment. General surveys and NPS stay in Pencil, the sibling forms seed (https://github.com/just-every/run-pencil). **Acceptance.** 1. A conditional question renders and validates on the portal and the widget at both widths. 2. Poll answers aggregate per request and by segment and stay operator-only.

pinnedClauses.title: Freshdesk
pinnedClauses.gap: Freshdesk API and webhook fixtures run CAP-003's journey: install, link, create and proxy-vote from the sidebar; tag-triggered capture creates one item per ticket however often the webhook replays; company fields arrive as private attributes; a shipped request drafts one reply on the linked ticket; uninstalling revokes and deletes the API key.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1, D-2 **Requirement.** A Freshdesk app (Freshworks developer kit) in the ticket sidebar offers CAP-003's actions: search, link the ticket to a request, create a request, record a proxy vote for the ticket's requester and see the request's public status. Tickets with a configured tag, or matched by a configured Freshdesk automation rule that calls Penny's signed webhook, are captured automatically. Freshdesk contacts and companies map to requesters and accounts by email and company ID, with their configured custom fields arriving as private segment attributes (SEG-006). NOTIFY-007 drafts the status reply on the ticket as a reply or a private note. **Acceptance.** Freshdesk API and webhook fixtures run CAP-003's journey: 1. Install, link, create and proxy-vote from the sidebar. 2. Tag-triggered capture creates one item per ticket however often the webhook replays. 3. Company fields arrive as private attributes. 4. A shipped request drafts one reply on the linked ticket. 5. Uninstalling revokes and deletes the API key.

pinnedClauses.title: Review sites and app stores
pinnedClauses.gap: Recorded fixtures from G2, Capterra, TrustRadius, Trustpilot, Product Hunt, the App Store and Google Play produce one inbox item per review however often the feed is re-read, each with its rating, date and a deep link that opens that review; an edited fixture review shows changed;
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** The owner connects the product's listings on G2, Capterra, TrustRadius, Trustpilot, Product Hunt, the Apple App Store and Google Play. Penny reads new reviews on a schedule (default daily, never less often than Google Play's one-week review window allows) as accountable background work (TRIAGE-006), through the site's own vendor interface where it offers one (App Store Connect customer reviews, the Google Play Developer reply-to-reviews API, the Trustpilot Business API, the G2 API, the Product Hunt API) and otherwise from the listing's public review page within that site's terms. Each review lands once in the inbox, keyed by site and review ID, with the reviewer as the site names them (nullable and non-authorizing), rating, title, text, date, app version and country where given, and a deep link to the review. An edited review shows CAP-002's changed state and a removed one becomes source-removed. The extraction agent (AI-004) proposes requests from review text. A reviewer has no email permission and is never emailed (NOTIFY-009 skips them). **Acceptance.** 1. Recorded fixtures from each of the seven sites produce one inbox item per review however often the feed is re-read, each with its rating, date and a deep link that opens that review. 2. An edited fixture review shows changed. 3. AI-004 proposals from a review carry byte-exact spans.

pinnedClauses.title: Discord
pinnedClauses.gap: Signed interaction and gateway fixtures: the command and the reaction each capture a message once with its jump link, a bad signature is refused, and a message in an unselected channel is never read.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** A Discord app adds a "Send to Penny" message command and an emoji-reaction trigger in selected channels of the customer's community server. The message and its jump link become an inbox item, the Discord member who triggered it is the capturer and the author is the source person (nullable, non-authorizing). Interactions are verified by their Ed25519 signature before parsing. **Acceptance.** Signed interaction and gateway fixtures: 1. The command and the reaction each capture a message once with its jump link, a bad signature is refused, and a message in an unselected channel is never read.

pinnedClauses.title: Survey responses
pinnedClauses.gap: Typeform, SurveyMonkey, Google Forms and Pencil fixtures produce one inbox item per response with its link and mapped attributes; a replayed webhook creates nothing; a bad Typeform signature is refused; an unmapped question's answer is absent from D1 and the archive.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** Typeform, SurveyMonkey, Google Forms and Pencil connectors bring in responses to the forms the owner selects. The owner maps which open-text questions become evidence and which answers become private attributes; each new response lands once as an inbox item with a link to the response, and a respondent email or hidden field maps to a requester and account (nullable, never verified identity or consent). Typeform and SurveyMonkey deliver by signed webhook and Google Forms by scheduled read of the Forms API. Unmapped questions are not stored. **Acceptance.** 1. Fixtures from each tool produce one inbox item per response with its link and mapped attributes. 2. A replayed webhook creates nothing. 3. A bad Typeform signature is refused. 4. An unmapped question's answer is absent from D1 and the archive.

pinnedClauses.title: In-app feedback widget
pinnedClauses.gap: Allow-listed iframe embedding of the portal (REQ-027) ships today. A browser test on a fixture host page at both widths: an identified user submits, votes and follows, and on an auto-publish board sees their post listed at once; the page URL appears only in private evidence; the documented CSP directives suffice; no third-party cookie is set.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-PUBLIC-001 **Requirement.** A JavaScript snippet and npm package embed Penny in the customer's own product as a launcher, modal or side panel: identified users submit, search, vote, comment and follow without leaving the product, and the current page URL and any metadata the host passes are attached as private context. It follows the board's moderation setting (REQ-003, REQ-033) so an identified user's post on an auto-publish board shows at once, keeps the portal's privacy, and shows the owner's brand (INT-008) in the host's colors or the brand accent, as the owner chooses. **Acceptance.** A browser test on a fixture host page at both widths: 1. An identified user submits, votes and follows, and on an auto-publish board sees their post listed at once. 2. The page URL appears only in private evidence. 3. The documented CSP directives suffice.

pinnedClauses.title: SSO identify
pinnedClauses.gap: REQ-031 host identity ships for the portal today, by postMessage from an allow-listed parent frame only. Host-identity tests extended to JWT and to the widget origin: a valid token identifies the user and links the account with private attributes; expired, future-dated and forged tokens are refused and change nothing.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** The customer's server signs a user token (JWT with HS256 or RS256, or REQ-031's host identity) carrying user ID, email, name, company ID and name, and optional attributes such as plan, role and MRR in USD. The widget and portal accept it without email verification, from the widget's identify call, from REQ-031's allow-listed parent frame, or on the standalone portal through WIDGET-008's sign-in redirect, apply REQ-014's expiry and store the attributes operator-only for segments (SEG-006). **Acceptance.** 1. Host-identity tests extended to JWT and to the widget origin: a valid token identifies the user and links the account with private attributes. 2. Expired, future-dated and forged tokens are refused and change nothing.

pinnedClauses.title: Changelog widget and announcements
pinnedClauses.gap: A browser test: the unread count falls after viewing; a segment-targeted announcement shows only to matching identified users; an unpublished release never appears.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** The same snippet shows a "What's new" panel with an unread badge of published releases, targeted and announcements alike (REL-018), optional in-app announcements of a release to a segment, and reactions; each entry opens its release. **Acceptance.** A browser test: 1. The unread count falls after viewing. 2. A segment-targeted announcement shows only to matching identified users. 3. An unpublished release never appears.

pinnedClauses.title: Mobile SDKs
pinnedClauses.gap: SDK sample apps run XCTest and Espresso UI tests against a test installation: identified submit, vote and changelog read, and a queued offline submission sent once on reconnect.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Register:* R-17 **Requirement.** iOS (Swift Package), Android (Kotlin, Maven Central) and React Native SDKs give the customer's app native feedback, voting and changelog screens with SSO identify, offline queueing of submissions and status-change hooks for the host app's own push. **Acceptance.** SDK sample apps run XCTest and Espresso UI tests against a test installation: 1. Identified submit, vote and changelog read, and a queued offline submission sent once on reconnect.

pinnedClauses.title: Moment capture
pinnedClauses.gap: A fixture host triggers two moments; their answers arrive as evidence tagged with the moment; the widget sends nothing to Penny until a call is made.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** The host product opens a short Penny prompt at a deliberate moment (`penny.capture({moment: 'cancellation'})`: cancellation, downgrade, failed search, feature-flag exit), and the answer becomes evidence tagged with that moment. There is no passive tracking, session replay or keystroke capture. **Acceptance.** 1. A fixture host triggers two moments. 2. Their answers arrive as evidence tagged with the moment. 3. The widget sends nothing to Penny until a call is made.

pinnedClauses.title: Portal domain and audiences
pinnedClauses.gap: A browser test: a segment member sees the restricted board while a non-member and a signed-out visitor get 404 and no count; on an SSO-required portal, a signed-out request to a request page, the board, the public API, the feed and an attachment returns no request content (WIDGET-008's redirect or the sign-in page for documents, 401 for the rest), and REQ-023's link and REQ-039's buttons are absent; a custom hostname configured through the deployment path serves the portal (its TLS receipt is R-7).
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Register:* R-7 **Requirement.** The owner can serve the portal at a custom domain (such as feedback.example.com through Cloudflare custom hostnames), require SSO identify for the whole portal (WIDGET-008), and restrict a board to identified users in a segment (an Enterprise beta board) or to employees signed in through ROLE-002. A restricted board never appears to anyone else, in counts, search or the sitemap. Internal boards (REQ-019) remain operator-only. **Acceptance.** 1. A segment member sees the restricted board while a non-member and a signed-out visitor get 404 and no count. 2. On an SSO-required portal, every portal document (board, request, roadmap, changelog, activity) answers a not-yet-identified visitor with WIDGET-008's redirect to the owner's login URL, or, when no login URL is set, a sign-in page showing only the company name and logo (INT-007) and a note that the portal is for the company's customers. 3. On an SSO-required portal, every public API read, feed, sitemap and attachment answers 401 with no request, comment, release or count in the body. 4. Every response of an SSO-required portal carries `noindex`. 5. On an SSO-required portal, REQ-023's emailed link and REQ-039's provider buttons are absent, and their start and callback routes refuse without issuing state or a session. 6. A browser test: a signed-out request to a request page, the board, the public API, the feed and an attachment returns no request content (a redirect or the sign-in page for documents, 401 for the rest). 7. A custom hostname configured through the deployment path serves the portal.

pinnedClauses.title: Localized portal and widget
pinnedClauses.gap: A browser test renders the portal and widget in Spanish once through Accept-Language and once through an identify locale, with no English interface string left; a catalog missing a key fails the build; a status email to a requester identified with es arrives in Spanish.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** The portal, widget, mobile SDK screens and requester email are available in English (default), Spanish, French, German, Brazilian Portuguese and Japanese, and in any further locale the owner adds as a message catalog. The locale comes from SSO identify (WIDGET-002), then the browser's Accept-Language, then the owner's default; dates and numbers follow it. Customer wording is shown as written; operators can read a machine translation of a post or comment under AI-010, labeled as translated, and the original stays authoritative. **Acceptance.** 1. A browser test renders the portal and widget in Spanish once through Accept-Language and once through an identify locale, with no English interface string left. 2. A catalog missing a key fails the build. 3. A status email to a requester identified with `es` arrives in Spanish.

pinnedClauses.title: SSO sign-in redirect
pinnedClauses.gap: Today host identity reaches the portal only by postMessage from an allow-listed parent frame (src/core/features/auth/ui/host-identity-bridge.tsx); there is no login URL, redirect or state. At both widths against a fixture host: a signed-out visitor to /portal/feedback/<request> on an SSO-required portal is redirected to the login URL; with SSO required and no token the request page response carries no request content.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** As Canny's SSO redirect does, the owner sets a login URL on their own site (an `https` URL) in settings, beside WIDGET-002's signing key, and the portal signs visitors in through the owner's product. An unidentified visitor to any page of an SSO-required portal (WIDGET-006), or a visitor on any portal who chooses "Sign in with <company name>" (offered beside REQ-023 and REQ-039 when a login URL is set), is answered with a 302 to the login URL carrying a `redirect` parameter: Penny's callback path on the portal's own origin with a `state` value. **Acceptance.** A browser journey against a fixture host at both widths: 1. The state is signed by the installation, single-use, expires 10 minutes after issue and binds the return path, which must be a same-origin portal path; any other return path is replaced by the board home. 2. A signed-out visitor to `/portal/feedback/<request>` on an SSO-required portal is redirected to the login URL. 3. With SSO required and no token, the response for the request page carries no request content. 4. No redirect leaves the portal's origin except to the configured login URL.

pinnedClauses.title: SSO return and refusals
pinnedClauses.gap: There is no login URL, callback or state today. At both widths against a fixture host: the visitor returns with a valid token and lands on the request identified, with no cookie and no token left in the address bar; a vote chosen before sign-in is applied once after return; an expired token, a forged token, a reused state, a tampered return path and a return path on another origin are each refused and change nothing.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *From:* WIDGET-008 **Requirement.** The owner's server authenticates the user in its own product and sends the browser to the callback with a WIDGET-002 token in the URL fragment or a form POST, never the query string, so the token reaches no request log. The callback verifies the token's signature and REQ-014's expiry and the state's signature, expiry and single use; consumes the state; establishes REQ-023's browser-local session for the identified requester (no cookie), linking the account and private attributes as WIDGET-002 does; removes the token from the address bar and history; applies any action held before sign-in (REQ-023); and lands the visitor on the page they asked for. A visitor already signed in to the owner's product passes through with no prompt. **Acceptance.** A browser journey against a fixture host at both widths: 1. The fixture host returns a valid token, and the visitor lands on the request they asked for, identified, with no cookie set and no token left in the address bar. 2. A vote chosen before sign-in on a non-SSO-required portal is applied once after return. 3. An expired token, a forged token, a reused state, a tampered return path and a return path on another origin are each refused with a page that offers to try again, and change nothing. 4. A refusal reveals no identity match (REQ-014).

pinnedClauses.title: Links from email into the owner's product
pinnedClauses.gap: There is no in-app link pattern today. With Open requests in my product on, a status email's request link follows the owner's pattern and the fixture host's widget opens that request; the unsubscribe link works signed out.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *From:* WIDGET-008 **Requirement.** The owner can turn on "Open requests in my product" and set a URL pattern on their own product's origin with `{request}` (the request's public ID) and optional `{board}` placeholders, such as `https://app.example.com/feedback?request={request}`. With it on, every link to a request in requester email (NOTIFY-001, NOTIFY-008, NOTIFY-010, NOTIFY-011, NOTIFY-012) and release email (REL-005) uses the pattern, and the widget (WIDGET-001) opens that request when the host page passes it (`penny.open({request})`), already identified. With it off, those links go to the portal, and on an SSO-required portal they pass through WIDGET-008's redirect. **Acceptance.** A browser journey against a fixture host at both widths: 1. With "Open requests in my product" on, a status email's request link follows the owner's pattern. 2. The fixture host's widget opens that request, already identified. 3. With it off, the request links go to the portal. 4. Unsubscribe and mute links always go to Penny and work without signing in (NOTIFY-002): the unsubscribe link in the same email works signed out.

pinnedClauses.title: Semantic duplicate detection
pinnedClauses.gap: The duplicates-v1 evaluation meets the AI-001 bars (precision ≥ 0.90, recall ≥ 0.85, top-five ≥ 0.90, paraphrase recall ≥ lexical + 0.15); requester suggestions contain only published requests; with the model disabled, lexical suggestions still return within EVID-007's limit.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-4 **Requirement.** Alongside EVID-007's lexical suggestions, Penny ranks existing requests by meaning (embeddings over titles, descriptions and linked evidence) for a requester typing a title, for each inbox item and for an operator viewing a request, and names the passages that matched. Requesters see published requests only. When the model is unavailable the lexical suggestions still appear. **Acceptance.** 1. The `duplicates-v1` evaluation (AI-011) reports, at the suggestion threshold, precision of at least 0.90 and recall of at least 0.85, the true duplicate among the top five suggestions for at least 0.90 of positive pairs, and recall on the paraphrase subset at least 0.15 above the lexical EVID-007 baseline measured on the same set. 2. Requester suggestions contain only published requests. 3. With the model disabled, lexical suggestions still return within EVID-007's limit.

pinnedClauses.title: Auto-link suggestions
pinnedClauses.gap: The links-v1 evaluation meets the AI-002 bars; an inbox journey accepts and rejects suggestions; an auto-link rule on one fixture source links only above its threshold, marks and can undo each link, and changes no public payload.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-4 **Requirement.** Each new inbox item gets up to three suggested requests and one suggested theme, each with a confidence and a reason; the operator accepts or rejects in one action, and a rejected suggestion is not offered again. An owner may enable a rule that links automatically above a confidence threshold for chosen sources; auto-links are marked, reversible, and never publish, vote or notify. **Acceptance.** 1. The `links-v1` evaluation (AI-011) reports the labeled request among the three suggestions for at least 0.85 of items that have one, no suggestion above the threshold for at least 0.80 of items labeled none, and auto-link precision of at least 0.97 at the default threshold. 2. An inbox journey accepts and rejects suggestions. 3. An auto-link rule on one fixture source links only above its threshold, marks and can undo each link, and changes no public payload.

pinnedClauses.title: Duplicate sweep and merge proposals
pinnedClauses.gap: Reversible explicit merge (REQ-008, REQ-009) ships today. The merges-v1 evaluation with its 0.80 coverage and 0.85 precision sweep bar and zero wrongful automatic merges on the labelled fixture, the sweep and its proposals, and the evaluation-gated, off-by-default, one-board auto-merge rule that logs each merge for REQ-009 to restore are not built.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-4 **Requirement.** On demand or weekly, Penny sweeps open requests for likely duplicates and lists merge proposals with a suggested canonical request and the evidence; accepting runs REQ-008's merge. An optional auto-merge rule (*Policy: `request.auto-merge.v1`; default: off*) can be enabled only after a passing evaluation (AI-012), merges only above its threshold and only within one board, logs each merge, and can be undone by REQ-009. **Acceptance.** 1. The `merges-v1` evaluation (AI-011) reports sweep proposals covering at least 0.80 of labeled duplicate pairs with precision of at least 0.85. 2. On that labelled fixture, `request.auto-merge.v1` at its default threshold makes zero wrongful merges and none across boards; the report publishes the wrongful-merge rate of automatic merges against the 0.5% target, which does not gate. 3. The auto-merge rule is off on a new installation, and enabling it for a model and prompt version with no passing evaluation is refused with the reason. 4. A sweep over the fixture backlog lists proposals with a suggested canonical request and the evidence. 5. Accepting a proposal collapses votes as REQ-008 requires. 6. The auto-merge rule logs each merge, never merges across boards, and REQ-009 restores it.

pinnedClauses.title: Request extraction from conversations
pinnedClauses.gap: Selected Orbit and native evidence produce cited learning options today, not requests. The extraction-v1 evaluation meets the AI-004 bars; fixture conversations yield proposals whose spans match their source byte for byte; auto-creation produces unpublished requests only; re-running the same conversation creates nothing new.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-4 **Requirement.** From connected tickets, chats, calls, emails and Slack threads in scope, the extraction agent proposes candidate requests or links: a problem statement, the verbatim spans, the customer and the closest existing request. Proposals land in the inbox as suggestions; an owner may let a source create unpublished requests automatically, and REQ-005 still governs publication. **Acceptance.** 1. The `extraction-v1` evaluation (AI-011) reports span-level precision of at least 0.85 and recall of at least 0.80 against labeled request moments. 2. Fixture conversations yield proposals whose spans match their source byte for byte. 3. Auto-creation produces unpublished requests only. 4. Re-running the same conversation creates nothing new.

pinnedClauses.title: Themes and adaptive taxonomy
pinnedClauses.gap: The themes-v1 evaluation meets the AI-005 macro-F1 bars; a fixture corpus gets an initial taxonomy; new feedback is classified in the next run; an operator split reclassifies with history; themes filter the inbox and the request queue; a captured item on a board with no default owner, classified into a theme that has one, takes the theme's owner (TRIAGE-001). Native themes do not exist yet.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-4 · *Register:* R-13 **Requirement.** Penny keeps a hierarchical taxonomy (area, theme, sub-theme) over all evidence and requests, classifies new feedback continuously, proposes new themes as volume emerges, and lets operators rename, merge, split, pin or retire themes; operator edits win and reclassification keeps history. Themes filter every list and appear in reports (MEAS-004). Each theme can have a default owner applied on capture (TRIAGE-001). **Acceptance.** 1. The `themes-v1` evaluation (AI-011) reports agreement with the adjudicated labels of macro-F1 at least 0.80 at area and theme level and at least 0.70 at sub-theme level. 2. Where the set records the agreement between two human labelers, the report publishes Cohen's kappa against 90% of that agreement. 3. A fixture corpus gets an initial taxonomy, and new feedback is classified in the next run. 4. An operator split reclassifies with history. 5. Themes filter the inbox and the request queue. 6. A captured item on a board with no default owner, classified into a theme that has one, takes the theme's owner (TRIAGE-001).

pinnedClauses.title: Summaries and reply drafts
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-2, D-4 **Requirement.** For a request, decision or account, Penny drafts a cited summary of its evidence and discussion; for comments and inbox items it drafts a reply or status-update wording that is edited and then sent through the reply door (D-2). A draft carrying a private value (an account name, revenue, an internal note) is flagged before publication (EVID-006). Drafting reads only records available to the current operator; the prompt obeys AI-010’s data-processing setting. Unresolvable citations are dropped with a visible notice and never displayed as cited. Unlinked inbox drafts remain editable until linked to a published request. **Acceptance.** 1. Every citation in a fixture summary resolves to a stored record; unknown citations are dropped and disclosed. 2. A draft containing a private account name is flagged and its publication refused until edited. 3. Nothing is sent without an explicit send of the edited wording. 4. A revoked session refuses a draft completed in flight.

pinnedClauses.title: Spam and abuse flags
pinnedClauses.gap: The spam-v1 evaluation meets the AI-007 bars; a fixture spam batch is flagged with reasons and stays in moderation (held on an auto-publish board); a false positive is approved normally.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-4 **Requirement.** Portal and widget submissions and comments that look like spam, abuse or exposed personal data are flagged in moderation with a reason; on an auto-publish board (REQ-033) a flag holds the item instead of publishing it. A flag never deletes or publishes anything. **Acceptance.** 1. The `spam-v1` evaluation (AI-011) reports precision of at least 0.95 and recall of at least 0.90 for spam and abuse, and recall of at least 0.95 for exposed personal data. 2. A fixture spam batch is flagged with reasons and stays in moderation. 3. A false positive is approved normally.

pinnedClauses.title: Sensitive-data redaction
pinnedClauses.gap: Deterministic owner rules cover operator evidence, CAP-009 email capture, native portal submissions, saved Canny/UserVoice imports and Orbit/native learning acquisition before storage, and owner-confirmed reapplication rewrites editable wording and copies; AI-010 is not used for redaction, and AI-011 still inherits the minimal runner. Gap: Optional model detection is not built. Rule reapplication does not rewrite the preserved or fingerprinted places explicitly counted as blocked in preview: saved-import plans/originals/provenance and their owned native rows; learning scope/originals/interpretations/corrections/commitments; decision and approved/published/status/notification history; pending verification payloads; canonical request addresses; signed/outbound/tracker envelopes; audit reason copies; archive/restore staging. These require DATA-003 erasure/copy resolution or an owner ruling. Binary attachment originals are not rewritten. No transcript store exists; CAP-008 inherits transcript capture and redaction.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-4 **Requirement.** Owner-configured rules (US Social Security numbers, payment card numbers, phone numbers, email addresses, credential shapes and custom patterns), with optional model detection, redact captured excerpts and transcripts before storage; redactions are marked, and the unredacted original stays only in the source system. **Acceptance.** 1. The `redaction-v1` evaluation (AI-011) reports recall of at least 0.99 for Social Security and payment card numbers and at least 0.95 for the other default kinds, with precision of at least 0.90. 2. A fixture ticket containing an SSN and a card number is stored redacted in D1, search and the archive. 3. A new rule applies to new captures and, on request, re-applies to stored ones.

pinnedClauses.title: Ask Penny
pinnedClauses.gap: Main’s missing judgment is retained pending acceptance of the replayed cited-answer, commercial-permission and chosen-Slack assertions. A question over a fixture corpus returns an answer whose every citation resolves; a role without commercial permission receives no revenue figures; a Slack answer posts only where the asker chose.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-4 **Requirement.** Operators ask questions in Penny, Slack or Teams ("What are Enterprise accounts saying about SSO this quarter?") and get an answer that cites the evidence, requests and accounts it used, limited to what the asker's role may see. **Acceptance.** 1. A question over a fixture corpus returns an answer whose every citation resolves. 2. A role without commercial permission receives no revenue figures. 3. A Slack answer posts only where the asker chose.

pinnedClauses.title: Model configuration and cost
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** The owner chooses the model provider and model for each AI capability (default: Claude through Penny’s enforcing model port), a monthly USD budget and data-processing settings. Every AI run reserves and reports cost as LEARN-006 does; an absent or exhausted model visibly refuses AI work while every non-AI path keeps working. Settings choose OpenAI or Anthropic and a catalog model per capability, a UTC-calendar-month USD cap (initially $0), and whether permitted private context may be sent. By default private notes, account names and commercial fields are withheld where prompts are built. Keys, allowed models and prices remain installation bindings, never D1 or the screen. Learning keeps its investigation ceiling inside the installation cap; ambiguous calls keep their reservation and are never automatically retried. **Acceptance.** 1. Exhausting a fixture budget refuses new AI runs with a visible reason while lexical suggestions, manual capture and triage keep working. 2. The cost report matches metered fixture usage.

pinnedClauses.title: Measured AI quality
pinnedClauses.gap: Each named set exists with its documented size and label mix; the evaluation command reports every figure for each set and exits non-zero on a deliberately degraded fixture model; the lexical baseline run needs no model. Only redaction-v1 (210 synthetic excerpts) and a minimal runner exist.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Every AI capability that suggests, links, merges, classifies, extracts, flags or redacts is measured against a named, versioned, labeled fixture set held in the repository: `duplicates-v1` (at least 300 request pairs, at least 30% of them hard negatives that share key terms but differ in need, and paraphrase positives with no shared terms), `links-v1` (at least 200 inbox items labeled with their request or none, and their theme), `merges-v1` (a backlog of at least 500 requests across at least three boards with labeled duplicate clusters), `extraction-v1` (at least 50 tickets, calls, emails and threads with labeled request spans), `themes-v1` (at least 400 items with a three-level taxonomy, adjudicated), `spam-v1` (at least 300 submissions and comments labeled spam, abuse, personal data or clean) and `redaction-v1` (at least 200 excerpts with labeled sensitive spans). One evaluation command runs a capability over its set through the configured model adapter, with the model chosen per run. **Acceptance.** 1. Each named set exists with its documented size and label mix. 2. The evaluation command writes a report naming the set version and hash, model and prompt version, counts, precision, recall, F1 or agreement, the confusion matrix and cost, and whether each bar in the capability's clause is met. 3. It exits non-zero when a bar is not met, including on a deliberately degraded fixture model. 4. The lexical baseline (EVID-007) is evaluated on `duplicates-v1` without a model, so every report has a floor to beat; the baseline run needs no model. 5. Each model evaluation is recorded as a dated receipt in CHANGELOG.md.

pinnedClauses.title: Evaluation gates automatic rules
pinnedClauses.gap: Settings show no evaluation, and no automatic rule is gated on a passing evaluation; enabling auto-merge for a model with no passing evaluation must be refused with the reason, a passing evaluation must allow it, and accept and reject decisions must export as a private labeled set.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *From:* AI-011 **Requirement.** In the product, settings show the latest evaluation for the configured model on each capability, and an auto-link (AI-002), auto-merge (AI-003), automatic theme assignment (AI-005) or automatic request creation (AI-004) rule cannot be enabled for a model and prompt version whose recorded evaluation is missing or below its bar; changing either one turns such rules off until a passing evaluation is recorded. Operators' accept and reject decisions can be exported as a private labeled set to run the same evaluation on the owner's own data; it is never committed to the repository. **Acceptance.** 1. Settings show the latest evaluation for the configured model on each capability. 2. Enabling auto-merge for a model with no passing evaluation is refused with the reason, and a passing evaluation allows it. 3. Changing the model or prompt version turns such rules off until a passing evaluation is recorded. 4. Operators' accept and reject decisions export as a private labeled set that the evaluation command runs on.

pinnedClauses.title: HubSpot
pinnedClauses.gap: HubSpot API fixtures map companies, contacts and deals; a webhook update changes segment membership within 5 minutes and a property changed without a webhook arrives at the next 6-hour (or owner-set) refresh; nothing is written to HubSpot by default.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** An OAuth connection syncs HubSpot companies and contacts (domain, lifecycle stage, owner and configured properties such as ARR, MRR, plan and renewal date) and deals (amount, stage, close date) into Penny accounts and requesters by HubSpot ID and email, through webhooks, applied within 5 minutes of arrival, plus a scheduled full refresh every 6 hours (the owner may set 1 to 24 hours in the connector's settings). Write-back of a "Penny requests" property and timeline events is off unless the owner enables it. **Acceptance.** 1. HubSpot API fixtures map companies, contacts and deals. 2. A webhook update changes segment membership within 5 minutes and a property changed without a webhook arrives at the next scheduled refresh. 3. Nothing is written to HubSpot by default.

pinnedClauses.title: Salesforce
pinnedClauses.gap: Salesforce REST fixtures with sandbox OAuth: mapping, opportunity-linked evidence summing open amounts in USD, and closed-lost opportunities excluded from revenue at stake.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** A Salesforce connected app syncs Accounts, Contacts, Opportunities (amount, stage, close date, type) and configured fields; feedback can be tied to an opportunity, so revenue at stake is the sum of open opportunity amounts; an optional Penny Requests related list is written back when enabled. **Acceptance.** 1. Salesforce REST fixtures with sandbox OAuth: mapping, opportunity-linked evidence summing open amounts in USD, and closed-lost opportunities excluded from revenue at stake.

pinnedClauses.title: Orbit
pinnedClauses.gap: Today Penny reads only selected Orbit evidence records for learning (LEARN-001). A journey against an Orbit test installation shows Orbit account attributes as Penny segment attributes and Orbit deals in revenue at stake.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** Orbit, the sibling CRM (https://github.com/just-every/run-orbit), syncs accounts, contacts and deals on SEG-001's terms through its public API. **Acceptance.** 1. A journey against an Orbit test installation shows Orbit account attributes as Penny segment attributes and Orbit deals in revenue at stake.

pinnedClauses.title: Billing revenue
pinnedClauses.gap: Stripe API fixtures compute MRR from subscriptions with discounts and several items, flag churned customers and convert a non-USD subscription with its recorded rate.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** Stripe Billing, and Nectar, the sibling billing seed (https://github.com/just-every/run-nectar), sync each customer's MRR, plan and subscription status by customer ID or email domain, in USD; a non-USD subscription records its conversion rate and date. **Acceptance.** 1. Stripe API fixtures compute MRR from subscriptions with discounts and several items, flag churned customers and convert a non-USD subscription with its recorded rate.

pinnedClauses.title: Product and success attributes
pinnedClauses.gap: Signed Segment webhook fixtures set traits that move an account into a segment; a Buoy health change does the same.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** Segment identify and group traits, and Buoy, the sibling customer-success seed (https://github.com/just-every/run-buoy), supply user and company attributes such as plan, seats, health and last active. **Acceptance.** 1. Signed Segment webhook fixtures set traits that move an account into a segment. 2. A Buoy health change does the same.

pinnedClauses.title: Dynamic segments
pinnedClauses.gap: A base test changes an attribute and sees the account enter and leave a segment within 5 minutes; request, inbox and report filters agree on membership; no segment name or attribute appears in any public payload (DATA-002).
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Operators save segments as rules over any account or requester attribute (plan is Enterprise and ARR at least $50,000; health at risk; churned in the last 90 days). Membership is recomputed within 5 minutes of a changed attribute reaching Penny (SEG-001's webhook and refresh timing), and every operator list, prioritization view, roadmap view, report and agent scope filters by segment. Segments and attributes are operator-only. **Acceptance.** 1. A base test changes an attribute and sees the account enter and leave a segment within 5 minutes. 2. Request, inbox and report filters agree on membership. 3. No segment name or attribute appears in any public payload (DATA-002).

pinnedClauses.title: Customer-value demand
pinnedClauses.gap: REQ-026 ships private per-account vote totals and separate vote, linked-evidence and distinct-account counts, with all verified address/account associations and complete supporter history expandable 50 people at a time. Private account revenue is available on account records (EVID-005). PRIO-001 ships private feature demand that counts each person and account once with recorded account revenue and evidence. CAP-014 native proxy support ships from the inbox, request page and Zendesk edge. Aggregated ARR/MRR, opportunity and churn value figures beside request and feature counts, theme demand, and segment/date filtering remain required.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** For every request, feature and theme, operators see as separate figures: voters (including proxy votes), accounts, the ARR and MRR of requesting accounts, open opportunity amounts citing it, churned ARR that cited it, and evidence count, each filterable by segment and date range, in USD, counting each account once. The value figures appear beside REQ-026's separate vote, evidence and account figures and are combined into no score. **Acceptance.** 1. A fixture with several voters from one account counts that account's ARR once. 2. Opportunity and churn figures reconcile with fixture CRM data and appear beside REQ-026's separate counts. 3. Each figure filters by segment and date range, for requests, features and themes. 4. None of them appears publicly.

pinnedClauses.title: Auto-publish for identified requesters
pinnedClauses.gap: With auto-publish on, a verified requester's post and comment are public on submission and a widget-identified user's post is listed at once; an AI-007-flagged post and a hold-rule match are held with their reason; a PDF post is held while an image post publishes with its image; a takedown (REQ-041's removal) removes the post from every public read within 5 seconds and its URL answers 404; with the model unavailable, posts publish marked not screened, or are held when the board chooses hold; with the setting off, REQ-003's holding applies unchanged.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Owners and Admins choose each public board's moderation in settings: hold everything (REQ-003's holding) or auto-publish. On an auto-publish board, a submission (REQ-003), comment (REQ-007) or edit (REQ-020) from a requester verified under REQ-023 or identified through host or SSO identity (REQ-031, WIDGET-002) is public on submission in the requester's own wording, with the public status Open, unless it is held: flagged by AI-007, matched by a hold rule (TRIAGE-003), from a requester an operator set to always-moderate, or carrying a file other than an image within `seed.json` upload limits. A held item enters moderation with its reason and follows REQ-030. Image attachments on an unheld post publish with it; this supersedes REQ-011's separate file approval on auto-publish boards only, and every other file stays held under REQ-011. An operator can take down an auto-published post or comment at any time with a reason; this is REQ-041's removal, which works on every board: it leaves the portal within 5 seconds, its URL answers 404, it counts toward no public total and its author can see the reason. Operators edit auto-published wording under REQ-038. A blocked requester is still refused (REQ-022), duplicate suggestions still appear before submission (REQ-004), and each submission still creates its evidence item (EVID-001). When AI-007 cannot run (AI-010), the board's choice applies: publish and mark the item "not screened" for operator review (default), or hold. New public boards default to auto-publish; boards that exist when this ships keep holding until the owner chooses. *Policy: `request.moderation.v1` reads this setting.* **Acceptance.** A base and browser journey: 1. With auto-publish on, a verified requester's post and comment are public on submission and a widget-identified user's post is listed at once. 2. A post flagged by an AI-007 fixture, and one matched by a hold rule, are held with their reason. 3. A post with a PDF is held while an image post publishes with its image. 4. A takedown removes the post from every public read within 5 seconds and its URL answers 404. 5. With the model unavailable, posts publish marked not screened, or are held when the board chooses hold. 6. With the setting off, REQ-003's holding applies unchanged.

pinnedClauses.title: Public categories
pinnedClauses.gap: Board categories/subcategories, rename/order/archive/merge, required submission, moderation and later assignment, visible-only counts/filtering, canonical merge custody, CSV/API/archive and roadmap cards are implemented; route and 1440/390 browser journeys pass. Gap: incumbent category imports, category automation rules and a standalone SDK interface remain missing.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Operators define categories on each board, with one optional level of subcategories, and rename, reorder, merge and archive them. Each board's setting makes a category off, optional or required on submission. A requester picks one category when submitting from the portal, widget or SDK (REQ-003, WIDGET-001, WIDGET-004); an operator can change it when publishing (REQ-005) or later. Categories are public: the portal shows each published request's category, filters by category (REQ-012) and shows per-category counts that include only published requests visible on that board, never unpublished, held, internal, withdrawn or removed (REQ-041) ones. Categories are distinct from operator-only tags (EVID-009) and themes (AI-005), and nothing moves between them implicitly. A merge keeps the canonical request's category (REQ-008). Automation rules can match and set a category (TRIAGE-003), and categories are in the CSV export, the API and the archive (DATA-001, DATA-005, DATA-006). Canny categories and subcategories (MIG-001), Aha! categories (MIG-003) and UserVoice categories (MIG-004) land here. **Acceptance.** A browser journey at both widths: 1. A requester picks a category on submit, and a board with categories required refuses a submission without one. 2. The board's category filter returns only matching published requests. 3. Category counts exclude an unpublished and a held request. 4. Merging two requests in different categories keeps the canonical's. 5. A Canny API fixture's categories and subcategories arrive as categories on their boards, and no tag or public payload changes as a result.

pinnedClauses.title: Vote importance
pinnedClauses.gap: Board-configured three/four labels, optional choose/change/clear, private per-request importance counts, native and Zendesk source-stated proxy importance, CSV and Canny saved votePriority mapping/receipt/replay/undo ship. Importance counts can now sort saved PRIO-003 views. Remaining: SEG-007 commercial-value figures by importance, complete PRIO-003 inputs and MIG-002 Productboard portal-card importance import.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** A board's setting can ask each voter how important the request is to them (default labels Nice to have, Important and Must have; the owner may rename them or use four levels). Choosing is optional and can be changed or cleared. Operators see each request's votes broken down by importance, and with SEG-007's value figures (such as the ARR of Must-have voters); prioritization views (PRIO-003) can use the breakdown. The portal shows only the vote total. Proxy votes (CAP-014) record importance as the source states it; Canny's `votePriority` (MIG-009) and Productboard's portal-card importance (MIG-002) import into it. Completion requires SEG-007’s customer-value figures by importance, PRIO-003’s use of the breakdown and MIG-002’s Productboard importance import; this clause is done only when those dependencies and its native and Canny acceptance are complete. **Acceptance.** 1. A voter picks Must have and later changes it to Important, and the operator breakdown follows. 2. The public request payload carries no importance value. 3. A proxy vote records its importance. 4.
