A Canny fixture vote with each `votePriority` value lands with the matching importance and the receipt counts each.

pinnedClauses.title: Set a request's status
pinnedClauses.gap: Six direct statuses, optional comments, public month/quarter ETA, internal statuses, templates and unchanged-save deduplication are proved through the API and browser at 1440/390. Vote/author subscriptions (NOTIFY-008/011), captured-contact sends and bulk status actions remain separate gaps.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** On any published request an operator changes the status in one action, as Canny's status picker does: one of REQ-016's six public statuses directly, or an internal status (PRIO-002), which sets its mapped public status. The change takes an optional public comment, prefilled from the owner's template for that public status (one per status in settings, editable per change, blank by default), and an optional public ETA of a month or a quarter, which the request shows and the status roadmap (ROAD-014) shows beside it and which can be changed or cleared. Saving publishes one status update (REQ-015) carrying the new status and any comment into the request history, and the public status follows within 5 seconds under REQ-016. It notifies once per change each follower, vote-subscribed voter (NOTIFY-008) and subscribed author (NOTIFY-011) under NOTIFY-001 and NOTIFY-002, and NOTIFY-009's captured contacts when ticked; a change with no comment still sends a status-change message naming the new status. Declined still requires a public reason (REQ-017). Saving the same status again with no comment and no ETA change publishes and sends nothing. A bulk status change (TRIAGE-005) sends one message per request and recipient, coalesced under NOTIFY-002. The request ETA is set by the operator and never derived from an internal target date (ROAD-012). **Acceptance.** A base and browser journey: 1. Setting Planned with no comment on a published request that has no roadmap item shows Planned in every public payload within 5 seconds and emails each vote-subscribed voter and follower once. 2. The request appears in the status roadmap's Planned column with its ETA. 3. An internal status mapped to In progress shows In progress publicly and its own name only to operators. 4. The template prefills and the published comment is the edited wording. 5. Saving the same status again sends nothing. 6. Declined without a reason is refused.

pinnedClauses.title: Comment replies and images
pinnedClauses.gap: At both widths: a requester's reply to an operator comment is held, then shown under its parent once approved; an operator's reply is public at once and notifies followers once; a comment image on a holding board stays hidden until approved and on an auto-publish board publishes with the comment; a reply to a rejected comment is refused; a Canny fixture reply lands under its parent with its image.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Portal comments take one level of threaded replies: a verified requester or an operator replies to a published top-level comment, and replies show under it in time order. A requester's reply is moderated like any comment (REQ-007, REQ-030, REQ-033); an operator's reply is a public reply under NOTIFY-001, and a requester's reply, once public, notifies the parent comment's author once when they hold a permission for the request. Comments and replies can carry images within `seed.json` upload limits: on a holding board each image is approved with its comment under REQ-011, and on an auto-publish board an unheld comment's images publish with it (REQ-033). A held, rejected or removed (REQ-041) parent hides its replies from the portal, and a reply to it is refused. Imported replies and comment images (MIG-009, MIG-004, MIG-005) land in the same thread with their original dates under the import's publication choice (IMP-002); Canny internal comments land as internal notes (REQ-032). **Acceptance.** A browser journey at both widths: 1. A requester's reply to an operator comment is held, then shown under its parent once approved. 2. An operator's reply is public at once and notifies followers once. 3. A comment image on a holding board stays hidden until approved and on an auto-publish board publishes with the comment. 4. A reply to a rejected comment is refused. 5. A Canny fixture reply lands under its parent with its image.

pinnedClauses.title: Edit published wording
pinnedClauses.gap: Before publication, edit-then-approve under REQ-030 ships today; there is no route to edit published content (src/core/features/requests/operator-routes.ts). On a holding board and an auto-publish board: a retitled published request shows the new title in the request page, board list, search and API within 5 seconds while the old title appears only in the operator history; an edited operator comment shows the new wording marked Edited and keeps the old for operators; editing a status update leaves its status and ETA.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** As Canny's Edit Post does, a Product manager, Admin or Owner (OPS-001) can, on any board and whatever its moderation setting (REQ-033), edit a published request's public wording: the title, description and category (REQ-034), and an approved attachment's publication (withdrawing it under REQ-011). They can also edit the text of a published requester comment, operator comment or status update (REQ-015, REQ-036). **Acceptance.** A base and browser journey on a holding board and an auto-publish board: 1. An operator retitles a published request, and within 5 seconds the new title is in the request page, board list, search, category facets, status roadmap, feeds, widget and API, while the old title appears only in the operator history with its editor and time. 2. The request keeps its ID and public URL, and every earlier version stays readable to operators (as EVID-010 keeps evidence versions). 3. The requester's own later edits (REQ-020) start from the operator's wording, and the evidence item the submission created keeps the requester's original wording (EVID-004). 4. Editing an operator comment shows the new wording marked "Edited" on the portal and keeps the old for operators. 5. Editing a status update changes neither the request's status nor its ETA.

pinnedClauses.title: Remove and restore published content
pinnedClauses.gap: There is no route to remove or restore published content (src/core/features/requests/operator-routes.ts). A removed published request answers 404 and leaves the vote total, category counts, search and the status roadmap column within 5 seconds, and restoring it brings each back; a removed requester comment leaves the portal and its author's activity view shows the reason; removing a status update leaves the status unchanged; permanent delete keeps the evidence item.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *From:* REQ-038 **Requirement.** As Canny's delete does, a Product manager, Admin or Owner can remove a published request or comment, with a reason, on any board; this is REQ-033's takedown, available on every board. Removal is reversible: an operator restores it with its earlier state, votes and follows. An Owner or Admin can delete a removed request permanently, which deletes its public content, votes, comments and follows, keeps its evidence item and leaves an audit entry with no customer wording (DATA-003); a merge (REQ-008) is offered instead when the removal names a duplicate. **Acceptance.** A base and browser journey on a holding board and an auto-publish board: 1. Removing a published request makes its URL answer 404 and drops it from the vote total, category counts, search, sitemap, feeds, the status roadmap column (ROAD-014) and widget lists within 5 seconds; its votes, comments and followers are kept for operators, and the evidence item survives (EVID-004). 2. Restoring it brings each back with its earlier state, votes and follows. 3. Removing a requester comment hides it from the portal within 5 seconds, a removed parent hides its replies (REQ-037), and its author's activity view (REQ-025) shows the reason. 4. Removing an operator comment or a status update removes only its text from the portal and leaves the request's status unchanged. 5. An Owner or Admin permanently deletes a removed request: its public content, votes, comments and follows are gone, its evidence item stays, and the audit entry holds no customer wording. 6. Removing a request whose reason names a duplicate offers a merge instead.

pinnedClauses.title: Notice and accountability for edits and removals
pinnedClauses.gap: No action sends mail except one author notice when ticked; a Contributor is refused each action with 403; each action has one audit entry. None of this exists while edits and removals of published content are unbuilt.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *From:* REQ-038 · *Cites:* BASE-ROLE-001 **Requirement.** Edits and removals of published content send no mail by default and are accountable. A removal offers one private notice to the author with its reason, under REQ-030's rules for a rejection notice (current consent, suppression, mute, unsubscribe and quiet hours); editing a status update never re-sends it, and sending a corrected wording to recipients requires a new status update. No follower or voter is notified of an edit or a removal. Bulk removal is TRIAGE-005. **Acceptance.** 1. None of REQ-038's or REQ-041's actions sends mail, except one author notice for a removal when ticked. 2. No follower or voter is notified of an edit or a removal, and editing a status update never re-sends it. 3. Each edit, removal, restore and permanent delete has one audit entry (ROLE-004) with the actor, subject and reason and no customer wording. 4. A Contributor and a Viewer are refused each action.

pinnedClauses.title: Social sign-in for requesters
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Register:* R-4 **Requirement.** Beside REQ-023's emailed link, the owner can turn on "Continue with Google" and "Continue with GitHub" for requesters (each off by default, with the owner's own OAuth client credentials held as installation custody). A provider address verified by that provider (Google's `email_verified`, GitHub's primary verified email) becomes a REQ-023-verified address without a further email, the visitor gets REQ-023's browser-local session with no cookie, and an action held for verification (a vote, a follow, a comment or a submission) is applied on completion exactly as REQ-023 applies it. Sign-in grants no email permission (REQ-010) and no operator authority, and an address an SSO-enforced operator domain covers (ROLE-002) is still only a requester. An unverified provider address falls back to REQ-023's emailed link. On an SSO-required portal (WIDGET-006) only WIDGET-008 applies. **Acceptance.** A browser journey against Google and GitHub OAuth fixtures at the network edge: 1. A signed-out visitor votes, chooses Continue with Google, and returns to the request with the vote applied and no cookie set. 2. A GitHub account with no verified email is sent to the emailed link. 3. A forged or replayed OAuth state is refused and changes nothing. 4. With both providers off, neither button appears.

pinnedClauses.title: Board participation and display settings
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Each public board has settings, as Canny's board settings do: who may post (requesters, or operators only, which makes a vote-and-comment board on which the portal and widget offer no submit form and an API or widget submission is refused with 403), whether requester comments are allowed, whether vote totals show publicly (when hidden, vote totals leave every public read and the API, the board may still sort by them, and operators still see them), whether voters' display names are listed publicly on a request (off by default; when on, the vote control states it before voting), and whether requester names show publicly or every requester reads as "Anonymous" (operators always see who). A setting change applies to every public read within 5 seconds and removes no record. **Acceptance.** A browser journey: 1. On an operators-only board the submit form is absent and a widget or API submission answers 403, while voting and commenting work. 2. Hiding vote totals removes them from the board, request page and public API. 3. Turning on the voter list shows display names only, and the vote control states it. 4. An anonymized board shows "Anonymous" on every public read while the operator page shows the requester.

pinnedClauses.title: Canny board settings in migration
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *From:* REQ-040 · *Rules:* D-5 **Requirement.** For Canny migration (MIG-001), only the board visibility (`isPrivate`) and historical comment visibility (`privateComments`) exposed by [Canny’s API reference](https://developers.canny.io/api-reference) are mapped automatically. Posting permission, vote-count visibility, voter visibility and anonymity are not exposed by that API: for each board, the migration shows a reviewed board-settings mapping for those four settings, with the Canny dashboard values entered or confirmed by the owner before apply. Requester comment participation is also an explicit owner choice: `privateComments` governs historical comment visibility, not permission to comment. The preview distinguishes source API fields from owner-confirmed settings, retains the reviewed mapping with the originals and imports no setting it cannot verify. **Acceptance.** 1. A Canny API fixture maps `isPrivate` and `privateComments` without inventing API fields. 2. For each board the owner enters or confirms posting permission, vote-count visibility, voter visibility and anonymity from the Canny dashboard and explicitly reviews comment participation; a board confirmed as posting off and votes hidden lands with both settings. 3. The preview shows the source of each mapped setting, a changed mapping requires a fresh preview, and an unverified setting is not imported. 4. Replay changes nothing; undo removes the imported settings, while a later native edit refuses reversal rather than overwriting it.

pinnedClauses.title: Request owner
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Every request and inbox item can have one accountable owner; boards have a default owner applied on capture (themes take theirs under AI-005); each operator has a queue of the items, requests and requester comments awaiting them. **Acceptance.** 1. A captured item takes its board's default owner. 2. Reassignment moves it between queues. 3. A queue lists only the operator's own items.

pinnedClauses.title: Aging and reminders
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Untriaged inbox items, unanswered requester comments and requests with no public response past owner-set ages (default 7 days) are flagged on the overview and remind their owner once per age step; snoozed items return on their date. Requests whose public status has stayed Under review, Planned or In progress past an owner-set age (default 28 days, settable per status) are flagged stale on the overview and in the request queue (REQ-028) and remind their owner once per age step, as Canny's stale posts do; a status change (REQ-036) or a mapped roadmap transition clears the flag. **Acceptance.** 1. A clock-advanced test sends one reminder per age step, returns a snoozed item on its date, flags a request left in Planned for 28 days as stale with one reminder, clears the flag when its status changes, and the overview's aging and stale counts link to their records.

pinnedClauses.title: Automation rules
pinnedClauses.gap: A rule dry-runs against a fixture inbox, then applies once per item with one audit entry each; a hold rule keeps a matching auto-publish submission in moderation with the rule as its reason; the rule editor offers no publication, vote, customer-notification or commitment action.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Admins define ordered rules: when an item or request matches conditions (source, connector, board, tag, theme, segment, keyword, account attribute), assign an owner, add tags, set the board or category (REQ-034), link to a request, set a custom field or score input, hold an item for moderation on an auto-publish board (REQ-033), or post to a Slack or Teams channel. A rule previews its matches before saving, runs once per item and logs each action. Rules cannot publish, vote, notify a customer or commit. **Acceptance.** 1. A rule dry-runs against a fixture inbox, then applies once per item with one audit entry each. 2. A hold rule keeps a matching auto-publish submission in moderation with the rule named as its reason. 3. The rule editor offers no publication, vote, customer-notification or commitment action.

pinnedClauses.title: Mentions and internal discussion
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Internal notes (REQ-032) support selected operator @mentions and one level of threaded replies. A mention creates one durable in-app notice per note and active recipient by default; saving again or dismissing the notice does not duplicate it. NOTIFY-006 carries channel preferences and email, chat, push and digest delivery of mention notices. **Acceptance.** 1. A selected mention notifies its operator once, including after an idempotent save and dismissal. 2. A reply appears under its parent. 3. A removed operator cannot receive a new mention. 4. The note and its replies never appear in a public payload. 5. Archive/restore and erasure preserve their custody, and a reply restores after its parent.

pinnedClauses.title: Bulk actions
pinnedClauses.gap: Inbox-item batches, move board, set status, link, mark reviewed, REQ-041 bulk removal with one reason and propose merge remain unimplemented, as do per-record authorization of each verb, the eligible and refused preview and rechecked-authority commit and undo (RL-101); the tag and assignment batch is Owner/Admin only today.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-ROLE-001 **Requirement.** Operators select many inbox items or requests and tag, assign, move board, set status (REQ-036), link, mark reviewed, remove published requests with one reason (REQ-041) or propose merge in one action, see a summary of what changed and can undo the batch. One batch authorization rule applies (RULINGS.md RL-101): each selected record and verb is authorized with the same current operator, board and feature permission as its individual action (OPS-001 roles, ROLE-001 custom permissions, REQ-036 status, REQ-041 reasoned removal); tag, assign and review may be delegated, while merge, move, status and reasoned removal need their own rights, and selecting many records never widens them. **Acceptance.** 1. Tagging and assigning 200 fixture items writes one audited batch; undo restores every item. 2. Each selected record is authorized as its individual action would be, and an operator without the right for a verb has those records refused. 3. The preview shows the eligible selection and the refused records without revealing hidden data. 4. Commit and undo each run as one attributed batch with rechecked authority and unchanged-state fences.

pinnedClauses.title: Accountable background work
pinnedClauses.gap: Learning runs and mail drains meet this today. For each worker type, a kill-and-restart test resumes without duplicates and shows the failure state until resolved.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Every automatic action (connector sync, rule, agent run, scheduled publication, delivery sync, reminder) has an accountable owner, a due condition, durable progress, visible failure and an explicit stop or resolved state. A repeated or restarted run never duplicates a customer message, a request or a tracker issue. **Acceptance.** 1. For each worker type, a kill-and-restart test resumes without duplicates and shows the failure state until resolved.

pinnedClauses.title: Product hierarchy
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Products contain components, components contain features, and requests link to features (many requests to one feature), so demand, value and evidence roll up; roadmap items (ROAD-002) attach to features. The hierarchy is operator-only except through an approved roadmap item. **Acceptance.** 1. A base test rolls three requests from two accounts up to one feature, counting each account once. 2. Moving the feature to another component keeps every link.

pinnedClauses.title: Configurable statuses and fields
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Operators define internal request statuses (Needs info, Researching) each mapped to one of REQ-016's six public statuses; setting one on a request (REQ-036) sets the request's direct public status to its mapping, and changing a status's mapping moves every request holding it, publishing no update and notifying nobody. Custom fields (DATA-004) on requests, features and accounts. The portal shows only the mapped public status, unless the owner chooses to show a custom status's own name publicly in place of its mapped label. **Acceptance.** 1. A custom status mapped to Under review shows Under review in every public payload and the custom name only to operators, and shows its own name publicly once the owner chooses so. 2. A Canny fixture's custom status names arrive as internal statuses each mapped to the public status the owner chose in the migration preview (MIG-008).

pinnedClauses.title: Prioritization views and formulas
pinnedClauses.gap: Saved private/shared request and feature views show native voters, accounts, evidence and importance inputs; RICE, value/effort, manual segment demand and weighted sums sort only the view. Missing inputs stay unscored. Remaining: SEG-007 commercial/segment/date columns, custom-field columns, PRIO-004 scorecard inputs and PRIO-005 delivery-sourced effort.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Operators build saved, shareable views of requests or features with columns from demand (SEG-007), custom fields, scorecards (PRIO-004) and effort (PRIO-005), and an optional formula (presets RICE, value over effort, weighted segment demand, or a custom weighted sum) whose inputs and weights are visible on every row. A formula only sorts: it is never stored on a decision and never changes roadmap or public status. This supersedes REQ-026's "combines them into no score" inside these views only. **Acceptance.** 1. A RICE view sorts fixture features with every component visible. 2. Changing a weight re-sorts. 3. The decision brief and every public payload show no score.

pinnedClauses.title: Scorecards
pinnedClauses.gap: Two operators' inputs are both visible on a card; the weighted rank is computed; changing the criteria keeps earlier scores readable.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Operators define scorecards (named criteria with 1–5 or 1–10 scales and weights) and score ideas individually; each card shows every scorer's inputs and the weighted result, and rankings from scorecards filter by segment. **Acceptance.** 1. Two operators' inputs are both visible on a card. 2. The weighted rank is computed. 3. Changing the criteria keeps earlier scores readable.

pinnedClauses.title: Effort from delivery
pinnedClauses.gap: A Linear, a ClickUp and an Asana fixture estimate each appear as effort on the linked feature with their source; a manual override is marked as such.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Effort comes from the linked Vector, Linear, Jira, GitHub, Azure DevOps, ClickUp or Asana estimate (points, estimate, size or estimated time) or a manual field, with its source shown. **Acceptance.** 1. A Linear fixture estimate appears as effort on the linked feature. 2. A manual override is marked as such.

pinnedClauses.title: Objectives
pinnedClauses.gap: Features linked to an objective appear grouped under it on a roadmap view and filter a prioritization view; a key result reads its value from an Amplitude fixture; a Productboard fixture's objectives land with their feature links.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Operators define objectives with an owner, a timeframe and optional key results with a target, and link features, roadmap items and decisions to them. Prioritization views (PRIO-003) and roadmaps (ROAD-009) filter and group by objective, and a key result can read its current value from a measurement source (MEAS-001–MEAS-003). Objectives are operator-only unless shown on a public roadmap's approved wording (ROAD-004). Productboard objectives migrate here (MIG-002). **Acceptance.** 1. Features linked to an objective appear grouped under it on a roadmap view and filter a prioritization view. 2. A key result reads its value from an Amplitude fixture. 3. A Productboard fixture's objectives land with their feature links.

pinnedClauses.title: Roadmap views
pinnedClauses.gap: A browser journey switches the three views with the same filters and gets the same items; moving an item records a ROAD-001 transition.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Internal roadmaps show as a board by status, Now/Next/Later columns or a timeline by month or quarter from target and release windows; views filter by product, component, owner, theme and segment and can be saved and shared with operators. **Acceptance.** 1. A browser journey switches the three views with the same filters and gets the same items. 2. Moving an item records a ROAD-001 transition.

pinnedClauses.title: Several and audience roadmaps
pinnedClauses.gap: Two public roadmaps each show only their own approved items; an audience roadmap answers 404 to non-members.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Owners publish more than one public roadmap (by product or audience) and can restrict one to a WIDGET-006 audience; each projects only approved items (ROAD-004). **Acceptance.** 1. Two public roadmaps each show only their own approved items. 2. An audience roadmap answers 404 to non-members.

pinnedClauses.title: Release planning and dependencies
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Operators group roadmap items into planned releases with dates and record dependencies between items (blocks, blocked by); a slipped dependency flags its dependents and any public ETA (ROAD-012). Sprint and capacity planning stay in the delivery tool. Plans, dependencies and warnings stay operator-only and publish nothing. **Acceptance.** 1. A slipped dependency flags each dependent item and its ETA. 2. The release plan lists its items with their states.

pinnedClauses.title: Public ETA
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** An approved roadmap item may show a coarse public ETA (a month or a quarter), approved separately like its other customer-safe fields; changing or removing it prepares a status-update draft (ROAD-007). A request's own ETA is set with its status (REQ-036). Internal target dates never appear publicly. **Acceptance.** 1. The ETA appears only after approval. 2. Changing it drafts an update. 3. An internal target date is absent from every public payload.

pinnedClauses.title: Roadmap sharing and export
pinnedClauses.gap: An export contains only fields the exporter's role may see; the shared link refuses a signed-out visitor.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Operators share a read-only internal roadmap with signed-in Viewers and export a roadmap view as PDF, PNG or CSV for leadership reviews; exports respect role field restrictions (ROLE-001). **Acceptance.** 1. An export contains only fields the exporter's role may see. 2. The shared link refuses a signed-out visitor.

pinnedClauses.title: Status roadmap
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Each public roadmap (ROAD-006, ROAD-010) has a source the owner chooses: approved roadmap items (ROAD-006) or request statuses, which is how Canny builds its public roadmap. A status roadmap lists the published requests on the boards the owner selects, in columns by public status (REQ-016): Under review, Planned, In progress and Shipped by default; the owner can hide a column, rename its heading and limit Shipped to the last 30, 90 or 365 days or show all. Each card shows the request's title, board, category (REQ-034), vote total and public ETA (REQ-036) and links to the request. A status change moves the card within 5 seconds. Open and Declined requests, and unpublished, held, internal (REQ-019), withdrawn and removed (REQ-041) requests, never appear, and no count includes them. A request mapped to an approved roadmap item appears once, in the column of its public status. A new installation's first public roadmap uses request statuses; a roadmap that exists when this ships keeps approved items until the owner chooses. A migration rebuilds the source's public roadmap as a status roadmap (MIG-011). The preview binds the settings before and after apply, refuses stale approval, and supports replay and undo of unchanged imported settings; later native edits refuse undo rather than being overwritten. **Acceptance.** A browser journey at both widths: 1. A request set to Planned appears in the Planned column within 5 seconds with its ETA and moves to Shipped when set. 2. An Open, an unpublished and an internal-board request never appear and no column count includes them. 3. A hidden column and a Shipped limit apply. 4. A mapped request appears once. 5. Switching the source to approved items shows ROAD-006's projection unchanged.

pinnedClauses.title: Scheduled publication
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Register:* R-16 **Requirement.** A release (REL-002), an announcement (REL-018) or a status update (ROAD-008) can be scheduled for a time in `workspaceTimezone`. Penny retains the UTC instant and the entered IANA timezone, shows the schedule and lets an operator cancel it before publication. At that time Penny checks the same current publication conditions as Publish now: REL-002's for roadmap targets, ROAD-008's for status updates, REL-018's for announcements and REL-019's for request targets. If they fail, the entry stays a draft and its author receives a durable in-app failure notice. Scheduled publication is audited and repeated Cron runs publish the version only once. **Acceptance.** 1. A clock-advanced test publishes a scheduled release and status update once at their times, never before. 2. Cancellation prevents publication. 3. A release whose target is no longer Shipped and a status update whose approval is stale stay draft and notify their authors. 4. The browser journey schedules and cancels through the release and status-update controls at both widths.

pinnedClauses.title: Rich changelog
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Release bodies support Markdown with inline images from the release's approved attachments and video embeds from approved hosts, public labels (New, Improved, Fixed and owner-defined labels), and a changelog page filterable by label and product. Raw HTML is shown as text. **Acceptance.** 1. An inline image renders from an approved attachment. 2. The label filter returns only matching releases. 3. Raw HTML in a body is not rendered.

pinnedClauses.title: Changelog distribution
pinnedClauses.gap: Subscriber email ships today. The feeds validate and list only published versions; a segment send reaches exactly the intersection of consent and segment.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Besides email to subscribers (REL-012), the changelog has RSS and Atom feeds, a segment-targeted email send that reaches only consented recipients in the segment, and the widget (WIDGET-003). **Acceptance.** 1. The feeds validate and list only published versions. 2. A segment send reaches exactly the intersection of consent and segment.

pinnedClauses.title: Release notes from delivered work
pinnedClauses.gap: A Linear fixture completion drafts a release containing only approved wording and marked items.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** When linked delivery work completes (DELIV-006), Penny drafts a release from the shipped requests' approved public wording and the tracker items the operator marks public; the draft waits for approval. **Acceptance.** 1. A Linear fixture completion drafts a release containing only approved wording and marked items.

pinnedClauses.title: Announcements
pinnedClauses.gap: Today every release needs a roadmap target; REL-014 supplies scheduling for the entry types this clause will add. An entry with no target publishes, appears on the changelog page, both feeds and the widget, and emails each updates subscriber once and nobody else; with Notify subscribers unticked it emails nobody; it shows no outcome prompt.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** An operator writes, labels (REL-015) and publishes a changelog entry with no target, as Canny's changelog allows: an announcement, for a fix, a small improvement nobody requested, or a pricing or policy notice. It needs a title, a body, a type or label and a publication date, publishes now or on schedule (REL-014) with no roadmap-state check, and has no outcome prompt (REL-008, REL-009) because it has no target. It appears on the changelog page, its feeds (REL-016) and the changelog widget (WIDGET-003). Its recipient snapshot (REL-004) is the updates subscribers (REL-012), narrowed by any segment send the operator chooses (REL-016); each receives it once under REL-006, REL-007 and NOTIFY-002, and unticking "Notify subscribers" (ticked by default) publishes it with no email. Corrections follow REL-003. Announcements inherit REL-014’s scheduling, cancellation, current-condition checks and durable author failure notices. **Acceptance.** A base and browser journey: 1. An entry with no target publishes, appears on the changelog page, both feeds and the widget, and emails each updates subscriber once and nobody else. 2. With Notify subscribers unticked it emails nobody. 3. It shows no outcome prompt.

pinnedClauses.title: Request targets on any release
pinnedClauses.gap: Today every release needs a roadmap target. A release whose roadmap target is Planned is still refused; a release with an Open request target is refused unless Mark linked requests Shipped is ticked, which makes the request Shipped and adds its subscribed voters to the snapshot once each.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *From:* REL-018 **Requirement.** An operator can link published requests to any release as request targets without a roadmap item: publication requires each linked request to be Shipped (REQ-016), unless the operator ticks "Mark linked requests Shipped", which sets each one through REQ-036 in the same transaction; each linked request's followers, vote-subscribed voters and subscribed author join the snapshot once, with that request as their context, and see its outcome prompt. Corrections follow REL-003. Request targets inherit REL-014’s scheduling, cancellation, current-condition checks and durable author failure notices. A release with a roadmap target still enforces REL-002. **Acceptance.** A base and browser journey: 1. A release whose roadmap target is Planned is still refused. 2. A release with an Open request target is refused unless Mark linked requests Shipped is ticked, which makes the request Shipped and adds its subscribed voters to the snapshot once each.

pinnedClauses.title: Vector
pinnedClauses.gap: A journey against a Vector test installation creates an issue, maps its state change to the roadmap item and shows Penny's demand inside Vector.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** Create or link a Vector issue or project from a request, feature or roadmap item; Vector state changes flow back under DELIV-006; Vector shows the linked demand (DELIV-007); a finished Vector cycle or release can draft a Penny release (REL-017). **Acceptance.** 1. A journey against a Vector test installation creates an issue, maps its state change to the roadmap item and shows Penny's demand inside Vector.

pinnedClauses.title: Linear
pinnedClauses.gap: Deliberate create and link, and signed private state receipts, ship today. Linear fixtures: create, link, state mapping, and the attachment updated when votes change.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** Extends INT-005 and INT-006: create or link Linear issues and projects; Linear webhooks map workflow states to roadmap states (DELIV-006); Penny keeps a Linear attachment with demand on the issue (DELIV-007); estimates feed PRIO-005. **Acceptance.** Linear fixtures: 1. Create, link, state mapping, and the attachment updated when votes change.

pinnedClauses.title: Jira Cloud
pinnedClauses.gap: Deliberate create and link, and signed state receipts, ship today. Jira fixtures: create, link, status-category mapping, and panel content restricted for a role without commercial permission.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 · *Register:* R-8 **Requirement.** DELIV-002's behavior for Jira Cloud issues and epics, plus a Jira issue panel showing linked requests, voters, ARR band and segments, limited by ROLE-001. **Acceptance.** Jira fixtures: 1. Create, link, status-category mapping, and panel content restricted for a role without commercial permission.

pinnedClauses.title: GitHub
pinnedClauses.gap: Signed GitHub webhook fixtures: an issue closed by a merged pull request proposes Shipped; a bad signature is refused.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** A GitHub App creates or links issues and follows issue state, merged pull requests that close them and GitHub Projects status fields, mapping them to roadmap states. **Acceptance.** Signed GitHub webhook fixtures: 1. An issue closed by a merged pull request proposes Shipped. 2. A bad signature is refused.

pinnedClauses.title: Azure DevOps Services
pinnedClauses.gap: Azure DevOps fixtures create a work item and map its state change.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** Create or link Azure DevOps work items and map their states. **Acceptance.** 1. Azure DevOps fixtures create a work item and map its state change.

pinnedClauses.title: Status mapping and close the loop
pinnedClauses.gap: A Linear fixture Done moves the item to Shipped, the public status to Shipped and creates a draft; with auto-update on, each follower and NOTIFY-008 voter gets one notification and a replayed webhook sends nothing more; the same mapping runs for ClickUp and Asana fixtures (DELIV-009, DELIV-010).
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** For each connected tracker (DELIV-001–DELIV-005, DELIV-009, DELIV-010) an admin maps tracker states to roadmap states (In Progress to In progress, Done to Shipped). A mapped change updates the roadmap item with a ROAD-001 transition; for an approved item the public status follows (ROAD-003) and a follower update is drafted (ROAD-007). *Policy: `roadmap.auto-update.v1`; default: off.* When the owner turns it on, mapped changes publish their update from a template that carries only approved wording and follows NOTIFY-002. A manual change wins until the next tracker change, and origin marking prevents loops. This supersedes INT-006's "private until an operator chooses" for mapped states only. **Acceptance.** 1. A Linear fixture Done moves the item to Shipped, the public status to Shipped and creates a draft. 2. With auto-update on, each follower gets one notification and a replayed webhook sends nothing more.

pinnedClauses.title: Demand in the tracker
pinnedClauses.gap: A new vote updates the tracker attachment once; with commercial permission off, no revenue band is sent.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Linked tracker issues show Penny's demand (requests, voters, accounts, ARR band, top segments) with a link back, refreshed as it changes; commercial fields are omitted when the integration's role may not see them. **Acceptance.** 1. A new vote updates the tracker attachment once. 2. With commercial permission off, no revenue band is sent.

pinnedClauses.title: Sync health and reconciliation
pinnedClauses.gap: Held and uncertain tracker commands with known-issue reconciliation ship today. A drift fixture is shown and resolved by resync; an ambiguous create is reconciled to the known issue without a duplicate.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Each tracker connection shows its last event, drift between Penny and tracker state, failures and held effects; operators reconcile ambiguous creates (INT-003) and resync. **Acceptance.** 1. A drift fixture is shown and resolved by resync. 2. An ambiguous create is reconciled to the known issue without a duplicate.

pinnedClauses.title: ClickUp
pinnedClauses.gap: ClickUp API and webhook fixtures create a task from a request, link an existing one and map a status change to Shipped with its ROAD-001 transition and follower draft; the task's demand field updates once when a vote arrives; a bad signature is refused and a replayed webhook changes nothing.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** A ClickUp OAuth app creates or links ClickUp tasks (and lists) from a request, feature or roadmap item on DELIV-002's terms. ClickUp webhooks, verified by their HMAC signature, map task statuses to roadmap states under DELIV-006; Penny keeps demand on the task as a linked custom field and a link back (DELIV-007); sprint points or the time estimate feed effort (PRIO-005). **Acceptance.** 1. ClickUp API and webhook fixtures create a task from a request, link an existing one and map a status change to Shipped with its ROAD-001 transition and follower draft. 2. The task's demand field updates once when a vote arrives. 3. A bad signature is refused and a replayed webhook changes nothing.

pinnedClauses.title: Asana
pinnedClauses.gap: Asana API and webhook fixtures complete the X-Hook-Secret handshake, create and link a task and map its completion to Shipped with its follower draft; the task's demand field updates once when a vote arrives; a bad signature is refused and a replayed event changes nothing.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** An Asana OAuth app creates or links Asana tasks and projects on DELIV-002's terms. Asana webhooks (established with the X-Hook-Secret handshake and verified by X-Hook-Signature) map completion, sections or a status custom field to roadmap states under DELIV-006; demand appears on the task as a linked custom field and a link back (DELIV-007); estimated time feeds effort (PRIO-005). **Acceptance.** 1. Asana API and webhook fixtures complete the handshake, create and link a task and map its completion to Shipped with its follower draft. 2. The task's demand field updates once when a vote arrives. 3. A bad signature is refused and a replayed event changes nothing.

pinnedClauses.title: Operator notifications and digests
pinnedClauses.gap: Decision-review mail (NOTIFY-003) and installation-wide Slack and webhook posts of public events ship today. A preference-matrix test delivers each event, a TRIAGE-004 mention among them, once on each chosen channel and nowhere else; a digest coalesces a day's events into one message.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Each operator chooses, per event (new inbox item on my boards, mention, assignment, aging reminder, decision review due, connector failure, release published, demand threshold reached) and per channel (in-app, email, Slack, Teams, mobile push), immediate or daily or weekly digest. Defaults are quiet: mentions, assignments and review due only. The mention event carries TRIAGE-004's mention notices, whose durable in-app notice stays the default (inherited from TRIAGE-004). **Acceptance.** 1. A preference-matrix test delivers each event, a TRIAGE-004 mention among them, once on each chosen channel and nowhere else. 2. A digest coalesces a day's events into one message.

pinnedClauses.title: Close the loop through the original channel
pinnedClauses.gap: Zendesk and Freshdesk fixtures: a shipped request drafts one reply per linked ticket; nothing is sent until it is explicitly sent (D-2).
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-2 **Requirement.** When a request linked to a ticket or conversation changes public status or ships, Penny drafts a reply on that Zendesk, Freshdesk, Intercom, Help Scout or HappyToHelp thread (or a note to the CRM owner for sales-captured feedback), ready for the support team to send. Email to requesters still requires NOTIFY-001's consent. **Acceptance.** Zendesk and Freshdesk fixtures: 1. A shipped request drafts one reply per linked ticket. 2. Nothing is sent until the draft is explicitly sent (D-2).

pinnedClauses.title: Vote subscriptions
pinnedClauses.gap: Disclosed votes create versioned, board-scoped permission; postal admission, stale-disclosure refusal, status delivery/unsubscribe, vote removal, explicit-follow retention, off-setting retention and reasoned bulk withdrawal are implemented. API/provider-fixture and 1440/390 journeys pass. Gap: Admin-role configuration remains unproved; live provider and inbox acceptance is R-6.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Register:* R-6 **Requirement.** Owners and Admins turn on, per board in settings, "Voting subscribes to updates", which is how Canny closes the loop with voters. On such a board the vote control tells the voter, before they vote, that voting subscribes them to updates on that request and how to stop; the vote then follows the request (REQ-010) and stores a timestamped permission record with its origin (vote), board and setting version, so status updates (REQ-015, ROAD-008), decline (REQ-017) and the release that ships it (REL-004) reach that voter under NOTIFY-001 and NOTIFY-002. Every such email says why it was sent ("You voted for …") and carries the one-click unsubscribe (NOTIFY-002), which withdraws the permission, and the owner's postal address (NOTIFY-014, CAN-SPAM); the setting cannot be turned on until that address is recorded. Removing the vote withdraws a vote-origin permission unless the voter also followed or ticked "Email me updates". Turning the setting off stops new vote subscriptions and keeps existing ones; the owner may also withdraw every vote-origin permission on that board, with a recorded reason. Proxy votes (CAP-014) and historical imported votes never subscribe (MIG-007 is the only import path). The author's subscription on submission is NOTIFY-011. New boards default to on; boards that exist when this ships keep it off until the owner chooses. **Acceptance.** A base and browser journey: 1. With the setting on, the vote control states the subscription, and a vote creates one permission record with origin vote. 2. A published status update emails that voter once. 3. The email's unsubscribe link withdraws the permission and the next update sends nothing. 4. Removing a vote withdraws its permission while a voter who also followed keeps theirs. 5. With the setting off a vote creates no record. 6. A supporter recorded through CAP-014’s native proxy controls on a vote-subscription board creates no permission record and receives no status-update email unless independently subscribed.

pinnedClauses.title: Notify captured contacts
pinnedClauses.gap: With "Also email people linked through captured evidence" ticked, a captured contact linked through Zendesk evidence gets one email, a contact who is also a follower gets one in total, and a suppressed or previously unsubscribed contact gets none; unticked, no captured contact is emailed; neither creates a permission record; the audit entry records the choice and the count.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** When an operator publishes a status update (REQ-015, ROAD-008), declines a request (REQ-017) or publishes a release (REL-002), they can tick "Also email people linked through captured evidence", as Canny's "Notify users tracked internally" does. Before sending, Penny shows the count and list of contacts with a deliverable address linked to the request through captured evidence (CAP-001–CAP-022) or a proxy vote (CAP-014). Each receives one message per update version, deduplicated with followers and voters; the message says why it was sent, carries only customer-safe wording (REL-005), one-click unsubscribe and the owner's postal address (NOTIFY-014; the box cannot be ticked until it is recorded). Suppression (REL-011), a mute and any earlier unsubscribe from Penny email are respected, and an unsubscribe here stops every later NOTIFY-009 message to that address. Ticking it creates no permission record: each send is the operator's recorded choice, with its recipient count, in the audit log (ROLE-004). A board's setting can make the box ticked by default; it starts unticked. **Acceptance.** A base test: 1. With the box ticked, a captured contact linked through Zendesk evidence gets one email, a contact who is also a follower gets one email in total, and a suppressed or previously unsubscribed contact gets none. 2. With the box unticked no captured contact is emailed. 3. Neither case creates a permission record. 4. The audit entry records the choice and the count.

pinnedClauses.title: Weekly requester digest
pinnedClauses.gap: Mail-edge fixture only: the weekly summary flow, portability and the owner and requester choices are asserted at the mail edge. No hosted mailbox receipt; real-provider mailbox proof for live digest delivery and unsubscribe is R-6.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Register:* R-6 **Requirement.** The owner can enable a weekly email to requesters who opt in (a "Weekly summary" choice on the activity view, REQ-025, and the updates surface, REL-012) and to voters subscribed under NOTIFY-008: status changes, new public replies and approved comments on the requests they follow or voted for, and releases published that week. A week with nothing for a requester sends nothing. It carries one-click unsubscribe and respects quiet hours, suppression and mutes (NOTIFY-002, REL-011). **Acceptance.** 1. A clock-advanced test sends one digest per opted-in requester per week containing only their requests' public changes, sends nothing for an empty week, and the unsubscribe link stops the next digest.

pinnedClauses.title: The author's vote and subscription
pinnedClauses.gap: Verified submissions record the author vote and disclosed submission permission; publication notifies once, replies/status/release/rejection use the durable permission path, removing the vote retains it, and withdrawal/unsubscribe revoke it. Held-verification and board-off cases pass through routes; 1440/390 journeys pass. Gap: a separate SDK disclosure journey remains unproved; live inbox acceptance is R-6.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Register:* R-6 **Requirement.** Submitting a request records the author's vote on it, as Canny makes a post's author its first supporter; the vote counts in the vote total (REQ-006) once the request is published, and the author can remove it like any vote. On a board with vote subscriptions on (NOTIFY-008), submitting also subscribes the author: the submit form on the portal, widget and SDK (REQ-003, WIDGET-001, WIDGET-004) says before submission that they will get updates on their request and how to stop, and submission stores one timestamped permission record with origin `submission`, its board and the setting version. Through it, the publication of their held request (one "Your request is now public" message), public operator replies, approved comments, status updates (REQ-015, REQ-036, ROAD-008), a decline (REQ-017), a rejection notice an operator chooses to send (REQ-030) and the release that ships it (REL-004) reach them under NOTIFY-001 and NOTIFY-002. Every such email says why it was sent ("You posted …") and carries the one-click unsubscribe, which withdraws the permission, and the owner's postal address (NOTIFY-014). Removing the author's vote keeps the submission permission; withdrawing the request (REQ-021) withdraws it; a blocked author (REQ-022) gets nothing. A submission held for email verification (REQ-023) records the vote and the permission only once the address is verified. On a board with the setting off, the author gets updates only by ticking "Email me updates" (REQ-010). Operator-authored requests (REQ-029) and imported posts record no author vote or permission (MIG-007 is the only import path). **Acceptance.** 1. A base and browser journey on a vote-subscription board: the submit form states the subscription. 2. An author who never ticks Email me updates receives one email for the first public operator reply and one for a status update, and their permission record has origin `submission`. 3. The published request's vote total includes the author's vote once. 4. The unsubscribe link stops the next update. 5. Withdrawing the request withdraws the permission. 6. On a board with the setting off the author receives nothing without ticking, and their vote still counts.

pinnedClauses.title: Merge notice
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** When an operator merges a duplicate into a canonical request (REQ-008), each follower, vote-subscribed voter and subscribed author of the duplicate who is not already on the canonical request receives one message saying their request was merged into it, with its public title and link, under NOTIFY-002 and REL-004 eligibility; REQ-008 has already moved them to follow the canonical request. The merge dialog shows the count and lets the operator untick the notice for that merge. A merge into an unpublished or internal-board canonical request notifies nobody until that request is published on a public board. Unmerging (REQ-009) notifies nobody, and automatic merges (AI-003) send the notice only when the owner turns it on for them. **Acceptance.** A base test: 1. Merging a duplicate with two followers and a vote-subscribed voter, one of whom already follows the canonical request, sends two messages naming and linking the canonical request. 2. With the notice unticked it sends none. 3. Unmerging sends nothing.

pinnedClauses.title: Sender identity
pinnedClauses.gap: Provider-tested sender acceptance and refusal and configured sender and reply-to headers are implemented; real provider clients use HTTP-edge fixtures, and API and 1440/390 browser proof pass. Gap: Admin-role sender settings remain unproved; live verified-domain, reply and inbox acceptance is R-6.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-MAIL-001 · *Register:* R-6 **Requirement.** Owners and Admins set, in settings, how requester and release email presents the business, as Canny's email whitelabeling does: the sender name (default: the INT-007 company name), the from address on a domain verified with the owner's mail provider (Penny sends a test message to the operator and shows the provider's result before saving, and refuses an address the provider rejects), and an optional monitored reply-to address that is never the CAP-009 capture address (without one, replies go to the no-reply address under NOTIFY-004). Every requester and release email (NOTIFY-001, NOTIFY-008–NOTIFY-012, REL-005, REQ-030's rejection notice) uses the sender name and from address. Operator email (NOTIFY-003, NOTIFY-006) uses the same from address. `MAIL_FROM` supplies the deployment address until a tested sender identity is saved. **Acceptance.** A base and browser journey: 1. A status email to a follower has the configured sender name and from address. 2. A from address the provider fixture rejects is refused before saving. 3. With a reply-to set, a reply reaches that address and creates no record (NOTIFY-004). 4. An Owner and an Admin each save the sender identity in settings.

pinnedClauses.title: Postal address and the mail it unlocks
pinnedClauses.gap: Company/postal setup and the legacy prompt, the postal footer and automatic-subscription admission are implemented, with API and 1440/390 browser proof. Gap: refusing the unsupported carry-over, captured-contact and digest choices without a postal address remains unproved.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *From:* NOTIFY-013 **Requirement.** The owner records the business postal address, and every requester and release email carries it in its footer with the one-click unsubscribe, as CAN-SPAM requires. First-run setup (OPS-005) asks for the postal address with the company name and cannot finish without both; an installation set up earlier shows its owner a one-time prompt alongside OPS-008's. Until a postal address is recorded, the paths that email people who did not ask in that moment cannot be turned on or chosen, each refused with the reason: vote subscriptions (NOTIFY-008), author subscriptions (NOTIFY-011), the captured-contact send (NOTIFY-009), the weekly digest (NOTIFY-010) and MIG-007 carry-over; boards created meanwhile start with vote subscriptions off; mail a requester explicitly asked for (a follow, an Email me updates tick, an updates subscription) still sends; and the overview shows the missing address until it is set. Operator email needs no postal address. **Acceptance.** A base and browser journey: 1. Setup refuses Finish without a postal address, and an installation set up earlier shows the one-time prompt. 2. A status email to a follower carries the postal address in its footer with the one-click unsubscribe. 3. On an installation with no postal address, turning on vote subscriptions, choosing MIG-007 carry-over and ticking NOTIFY-009 are refused with the reason, while a follower's status email still sends. 4. Turning on author subscriptions and the weekly digest is refused with the reason, and boards created meanwhile start with vote subscriptions off. 5. The overview shows the missing address until it is set.

pinnedClauses.title: Insight reports

Report totals reconcile with record counts on fixture data; response and resolution times on a fixture with a public comment, a status update, a snooze and a decline equal the hand-computed median and 90th percentile; a scheduled report sends once per period.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Dashboards show feedback volume, votes and evidence over time by source, theme, board, segment and account; top requests by voters, accounts and ARR; new and rising themes; and time to first response and to resolution. Time to first response runs from a request's creation, or an inbox item's capture, to the first operator action its requester can see: a public operator comment, a published status update, or a NOTIFY-007 reply sent on the original thread. Time to resolution runs to the request reaching Shipped or Declined, or to the inbox item being linked to a request or marked reviewed. Both report median and 90th percentile and exclude snoozed time. Each report exports as CSV and can be scheduled to email or Slack. **Acceptance.** 1. Report totals reconcile with record counts on fixture data. 2. Response and resolution times on a fixture with a public comment, a status update, a snooze and a decline equal the hand-computed median and 90th percentile. 3. A scheduled report sends once per period.

Missing or partial usage is shown as unknown, never as success. **Acceptance.** 1. Fixture usage yields adoption with its denominator and baseline. 2. Removing the usage data reports unknown.

pinnedClauses.title: Loop health

Each figure links through an overview drilldown to the records counted. **Acceptance.** 1. Fixture records reconcile all four figures and their linked drilldowns, including first-response ordering, held-comment exclusion, ROAD-008 publication, accepted versus delivered receipts, empty snapshots and distinct risk counting. 2. The overview and drilldowns work at 1440 and 390 widths.

pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-5 · *Register:* R-9 **Requirement.** A live Canny API migration (with the owner's API key) moves every record a Canny customer relies on, each to a named destination, starting with the board structure: boards with their visibility and access settings (REQ-018, REQ-019, WIDGET-006) and their posting, comment, vote-count, voter-list and anonymity settings (REQ-043); categories and subcategories (REQ-034); and tags (EVID-009). The status mapping, the decline reasons and the roadmap rebuild wait in the preview for the owner's approval, and nothing reaches the portal before it. It produces a redirect map (MIG-006), and a delta run during cutover adds only what changed. Historical users never become verified identity or operator authority. MIG-008 to MIG-011 carry the other record kinds on the same terms. **Acceptance.** A recorded Canny API fixture that contains each kind migrates it into its destination: 1. Records are read live through the Canny API with the owner's API key. 2. Boards land with their visibility and access settings, categories and subcategories as categories, and tags as tags. 3. Nothing reaches the portal before the owner approves the preview. 4. The IMP-007 receipt counts each kind (read, applied, skipped with reasons) and names every field left out. 5. A second run adds only the delta. 6. The migration itself queues zero deliveries, sends no mail and creates no notification.

A post in `planned` and one in `complete` read Planned and Shipped on the portal after the owner approves the preview. 2. A closed post lands Declined with its last status-change comment, or the owner's reason, as the public reason. 3. A custom status lands as an internal status mapped to its public status. 4. A custom post field lands as a request field. 5. Status-change history lands as published status updates with Canny's dates and comments.

An internal comment lands as an internal note, and a merged post as merge history.

pinnedClauses.title: Subscription carry-over
pinnedClauses.gap: A Canny fixture voter subscribed to a post, migrated with carry-over, gets the next status email on the mapped request without re-consent and the email names the move; a changelog subscriber gets the next release; an unsubscribed source row is skipped with its reason; the receipt counts carried-over and skipped subscriptions; without carry-over the same voter gets nothing until they accept the re-consent invitation; undo removes the carried records.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-5 **Requirement.** In a migration preview the owner can select carry-over of the subscriptions the source system recorded: Canny post and changelog subscribers, Productboard portal subscribers, Aha! idea subscribers, UserVoice suggestion subscribers (including the Subscribed column of IMP-008's Ideas & Voters export) and Featurebase post and changelog subscribers. Each carried subscription is stored as an imported permission record holding the source system, the source record ID, the subscription date the source supplied, the import job and the owner who selected carry-over; a post subscription follows the mapped request and a changelog subscription becomes an updates subscription (REL-012). It makes that address eligible for request and release email (REL-004) and nothing else: never verified identity, sign-in, a vote, operator authority, a segment or an outreach audience beyond the subscribed request or changelog. Addresses the source marks unsubscribed, bounced or suppressed, and rows without an address, are skipped with their reason. The first Penny email to a carried address says the feedback board has moved and carries one-click unsubscribe; unsubscribe and suppression then work as for any permission (NOTIFY-002, REL-011). The IMP-007 receipt counts carried and skipped subscriptions per kind; undo (IMP-004) removes the records it created, and erasure (DATA-003) deletes them. Without carry-over, MIG-006's re-consent invitation applies and IMP-008's treatment of the Subscribed column is unchanged. **Acceptance.** 1. A Canny fixture voter subscribed to a post, migrated with carry-over, gets the next status email on the mapped request without re-consent, and the email names the move. 2. A changelog subscriber gets the next release. 3. An unsubscribed source row is skipped with its reason. 4. The receipt counts carried-over and skipped subscriptions. 5. Without carry-over the same voter gets nothing until they accept the re-consent invitation. 6. Undo removes the carried records.

pinnedClauses.title: Phone-width web
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-ACCESSIBILITY-001 **Requirement.** Every portal and operator page works at 390 pixels wide with no horizontal scroll and touch-sized controls; every new surface in this contract (inbox, widget, prioritization and roadmap views) joins the same check. **Acceptance.** 1. At 390 pixels, every portal and operator page passes axe and layout checks, with no horizontal scroll and touch-sized controls, and each new surface in this contract (inbox, widget, prioritization and roadmap views) joins the same check.

pinnedClauses.title: Installable app and push
pinnedClauses.gap: A PWA install check passes; a push fixture delivers once; an offline capture syncs once on reconnect.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** The operator app is an installable progressive web app with web push for NOTIFY-006 events and a capture form that queues offline. **Acceptance.** 1. A PWA install check passes. 2. A push fixture delivers once. 3. An offline capture syncs once on reconnect.

pinnedClauses.title: Native operator apps
pinnedClauses.gap: XCTest and Espresso UI tests against a test installation triage an item, and a share-sheet capture creates exactly one inbox item.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Later · *Register:* R-8 **Requirement.** iOS and Android apps let operators triage the inbox, look up requests and accounts, capture from the share sheet (screenshot, text or link), record voice notes transcribed under CAP-008 and receive push notifications. Store distribution uses the owner's or Run Edit Run's developer accounts. **Acceptance.** 1. XCTest and Espresso UI tests against a test installation triage an item. 2. A share-sheet capture creates exactly one inbox item.

pinnedClauses.title: Accessibility
pinnedClauses.gap: Axe runs on the existing journeys today. Axe on every journey page of the portal, widget and operator app at both widths, and keyboard-only submit, vote and triage journeys, lack passing assertions; the VPAT and the screen-reader review are R-1 and R-2.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-ACCESSIBILITY-001 · *Register:* R-1, R-2 **Requirement.** Penny's delta on Base's accessibility bar: it covers the portal, the widget and the operator app, on every journey page at both widths. Penny publishes a VPAT 2.5 (Section 508 edition) for US public-sector and enterprise buyers, stating WCAG 2.1 AA conformance; the VPAT and the human screen-reader review it rests on are register rows. **Acceptance.** 1. Axe reports no serious or critical violation on every journey page of the portal, the widget and the operator app at both widths. 2. Keyboard-only journeys submit, vote and triage at both widths.

pinnedClauses.title: MCP server
pinnedClauses.gap: An MCP conformance client lists the tools and runs search and capture; a call outside the key's scope is refused.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-001, BASE-AGENT-002, BASE-AGENT-004, BASE-AGENT-005 **Requirement.** Penny's delta on the Base agent door: the Model Context Protocol server gives Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and other MCP clients Penny's search, read and capture tools (search requests and evidence, read the roadmap, add feedback, record a proxy vote), authorized by a scoped key or OAuth and limited to that key's role. **Acceptance.** 1. An MCP conformance client lists the tools and runs search and capture. 2. A call outside the key's scope is refused.

pinnedClauses.title: The registry equals this table
pinnedClauses.gap: Declared subset: 27 native tools with schema, scopes and standard/live classes. The wider target table, UI/REST registry unification, embedded jobs and resource family remain incomplete; no risk-based notTools exemptions are claimed.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface · *From:* new · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-001, BASE-AGENT-002, BASE-AGENT-006, BASE-AGENT-013 **Requirement.** Penny's door serves exactly the tools, resource templates, event types and prompts in this section, generated from one action registry that the operator app, the scoped REST API (API-001), DATA-007's MCP server and Penny's own agents all call. Each tool declares input and output schemas, truthful annotations, the risk classes it can carry and the server-side test that decides them. **Acceptance.** 1. `tools/list` and `resources/templates/list` return exactly the names in the tool table and the resource list, in a stable order. 2. The Core clause ids in `tools/list` `_meta`, with the reasons `server/discover` serves for what is not a tool, cover every Core clause, and no reason given is risk. 3. Each tool's classes in `_meta` equal its Risk class cell, and each tool's fixture result validates against its output schema. 4. For capture, link, tag, assign, approve, set status and merge, the operator app's action and the tool on the same fixture leave the same record state and the same audit event type. 5. `/docs/agents` lists every tool with its classes, scopes and error codes, and the test that adds each computed class. 6. The Base harness passes on Penny's fixtures in CI under both of its policies, all autonomous and held.

pinnedClauses.title: Triage through the door
pinnedClauses.gap: Declared internal capture, lexical search/suggestions, review/link/assign, notes and tags are native. Evidence resource readback is implemented; snooze, proxy votes, all queue filters and future commercial-role restrictions are not fully proved.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface · *From:* new · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-003, BASE-AGENT-005, BASE-AGENT-006 **Requirement.** The feedback triager finds, reads and triages through the read tools and the `penny://` resources. Every read returns exactly what the sponsor's current role shows in the operator app, and a record the sponsor cannot open reads exactly like a missing id. Triage calls inside the business are standard. **Acceptance.** 1. `penny.search` with the request queue's filters returns the same records in the same order as the sponsor's operator search, and none outside the grant. 2. Reads as a role without commercial permission (ROLE-001) return no revenue, opportunity or health value, and as a role with it return them. 3. An out-of-scope id and a missing id return the same not-found result. 4. Capture, link, tag, assign, review, snooze, an internal note and a proxy vote on an unpublished request each compute standard and nothing else. 5. Evidence wording, requester comments and imported posts carry the untrusted marker, and wording that asks for a wider action or claims a recipient is internal changes neither the call nor its class.

pinnedClauses.title: Customer-facing calls are external
pinnedClauses.gap: No call computes a risk class today; external calls, their counterparties and recipient counts are not computed.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface · *From:* new · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-006, BASE-AGENT-008 **Requirement.** Penny computes external, with its counterparty and recipient count, for every call that makes wording public or reaches a customer, as "How Penny computes each class" states. Mail an agent's call sends names "<agent> for <person>" as its sender. **Acceptance.** 1. Approving a held request, publishing a status update, posting a public comment, and editing, removing or restoring published wording each compute external with counterparty public. 2. A status change computes external with the recipient count of its followers, vote-subscribed voters, subscribed authors and ticked captured contacts, deduplicated as NOTIFY-001 counts them. 3. Publishing a release computes external with its snapshot recipient count (REL-004); with Notify subscribers unticked it carries counterparty public and no recipients. 4. Moving a request from an internal board to a public one, merging published requests and moving an approved roadmap item compute external; the same calls on internal boards or unapproved items compute standard. 5. Rejecting a held item computes standard without the author notice and external with one known recipient when the notice is ticked. 6. An outreach message (AGENT-003) computes external with counterparty known and its recipient count, and its email names "<agent> for <person>".

pinnedClauses.title: Destructive and sensitive calls
pinnedClauses.gap: No call computes a risk class today; destructive and sensitive calls are not declared.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface · *From:* new · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-006 **Requirement.** Penny computes destructive, with its item count, for what it cannot undo, and sensitive, with the data kinds, for redaction over regulated numbers. **Acceptance.** 1. `penny.published.delete` and `penny.erasure.run` compute destructive with their item counts. 2. Merging two requester identities computes destructive; blocking and unblocking a requester compute standard. 3. Deleting a tag applied to records computes destructive with the number of records it leaves; deleting an unused tag computes standard. 4. `penny.redaction.reapply` computes destructive and sensitive, with the kinds and place counts its preview shows. 5. A refused destructive call's audit row still records its computed classes.

pinnedClauses.title: Access, security, live and gated calls
pinnedClauses.gap: Public-board creation computes live and its held approval is proved. Access, security, gated connector and the remaining live settings families are undeclared; no self-escalation callback or fixture is invented.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface · *From:* new · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-005, BASE-AGENT-006, BASE-AGENT-008 **Requirement.** Penny computes access with its direction for operators, roles and keys; security for credentials and protective settings; live for settings that change what portal and widget visitors see; and gated for a connector's consent step. **Acceptance.** 1. Inviting an operator or widening a role computes access (widens); removing an operator or narrowing a role computes access (narrows). 2. Issuing a scoped key computes access (widens) and security; revoking one computes access (narrows) and security. 3. Changing SSO enforcement or the AI data-processing setting computes security; changing board moderation, auto-publish, participation, branding or the SSO-required portal computes live. 4. Connecting a connector computes gated with the provider and its consent step, and its OAuth consent goes to a person in that provider account; disconnecting computes security. 5. Configuring an outbound integration destination computes external and security. 6. A call that widens the calling agent's own key or its sponsor's role returns `self_escalation` and changes nothing, under any policy.

pinnedClauses.title: Penny's own agents use the same door
pinnedClauses.gap: Penny's learning runs and AI drafting call internal services, not a tool registry, and there is no decision function or Pause agents control.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface · *From:* new · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-002, BASE-AGENT-007, BASE-AGENT-008, BASE-AGENT-011 **Requirement.** AGENT-001 to AGENT-009 and AI-006's drafting call the registry's tools and the Base decision function, so an embedded agent and an outside one get the same decision for the same call (D-6). A draft never sends itself (D-2). **Acceptance.** 1. Each embedded agent's reads and writes appear in the audit as calls to the registry's tools, read as "<agent> for <person>". 2. Under all autonomous, AGENT-003's approved learning step sends its outreach with no person involved; under the held policy it waits for approval and sends exactly the approved messages. 3. AI-006 drafts produce no send; posting the edited wording is a separate `penny.comments.post` call with its own class and decision. 4. Pause agents stops embedded and outside agents alike on their next call within 60 seconds.

pinnedClauses.title: The feedback triager's week
pinnedClauses.gap: The declared internal triage/decision journey passes autonomous and held policies. The wider week including published merge, status, release and erasure remains undeclared.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface · *From:* new · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-007, BASE-AGENT-009, BASE-AGENT-013 **Requirement.** A stranger agent given only the installation's URL runs a seeded week of feedback work through MCP under two company policies: all autonomous, and held. The week triages new inbox items, links duplicates, merges one published pair, sets a request Planned with a comment, publishes a release to the requesters who asked, and erases one requester on request. **Acceptance.** 1. Before setup is answered, the first call returns `policy_unset` with the setup link, and setup lists every class Penny declares with no answer pre-selected. 2. Under all autonomous, the week completes with no person involved: no call waits for approval, none is refused by policy, and the review feed is empty. 3. Under held, the standard calls run and enter the review feed, and the merge, the status change, the release and the erasure each wait for approval and run once the test person approves. 4. Every call's audit row carries its classes, the rule and the policy revision, and no decision differs from the policy in force. 5. Pause agents stops the agent on its next call within 60 seconds, and resume restores it.

pinnedClauses.title: Competing explanations
pinnedClauses.gap: LEARN-002's competing options and contradictions over selected sources ship today. A fixture problem with planted disconfirming evidence: both explanations cite real spans, the planted counter-evidence is surfaced, and rejecting an explanation keeps its evidence and history.
pinnedClauses.area: Agents on the bet, not just the backlog
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-6 **Requirement.** For a problem the PM selects (a theme, a request or a decision question), an agent keeps at least two rival explanations of why customers ask (a missing capability, an onboarding gap, a plan limit), each with supporting and disconfirming excerpts from tickets, calls, votes, churn reasons and accounts that never asked, updates them as evidence arrives, and names the evidence that would tell them apart. The PM chooses scope and budget and can reject an explanation (kept with its reason, evidence untouched). Adding an explanation to a decision brief is a standard step through the decision tools. **Acceptance.** 1. A fixture problem with planted disconfirming evidence: both explanations cite real spans, and the planted counter-evidence is surfaced. 2. Rejecting an explanation keeps its evidence and history.

pinnedClauses.title: Disconfirming evidence search
pinnedClauses.gap: Contradictions within selected sources ship today. With contradicting fixture tickets, proposals attach with spans; accepting links them as contradicting (EVID-004); crossing the threshold raises one review suggestion.
pinnedClauses.area: Agents on the bet, not just the backlog
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-6 **Requirement.** Before a commitment and on its review schedule, an agent searches every connected source in scope for evidence against the leading explanation and the selected bet (customers who churned anyway, workarounds, contrary requests), attaches what it finds as contradicting-evidence proposals on the bet and suggests a review (DEC-007) when contradictions pass the owner's threshold.
