A proposal is a link that is accepted or rejected through the evidence tools; the search itself changes no decision. **Acceptance.** 1. With contradicting fixture tickets, proposals attach with spans. 2. Accepting a proposal links it as contradicting (EVID-004). 3. Crossing the threshold raises one review suggestion.

pinnedClauses.title: Next learning action
pinnedClauses.gap: LEARN-002's distinguishing clarification ships today. The proposal lists only consenting contacts; under the held policy approval sends exactly the approved messages; poll answers return as evidence linked to the explanation.
pinnedClauses.area: Agents on the bet, not just the backlog
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-6 **Requirement.** When explanations are close, the agent proposes the cheapest useful learning step (five interviews with a named segment, a two-question in-app poll under CAP-018, a usage query under MEAS, or a Pencil survey) with its expected information, cost and the customers it would contact; it drafts outreach only to consenting contacts, with booking links through Dial, the sibling scheduling seed (https://github.com/just-every/run-dial). Each learning step is a standard call, and each outreach message an external call to known counterparties with its recipients counted; the company's policy decides both. **Acceptance.** 1. The proposal lists only consenting contacts. 2. Under the held policy, each message waits for approval, and approval sends exactly the approved messages. 3. Poll answers return as evidence linked to the explanation.

pinnedClauses.title: Quiet and lost segments
pinnedClauses.gap: Selected Orbit cancellation evidence ships today. A fixture where loud small-business voters differ from silent Enterprise renewals: the report names the gap with cited records and, under the held policy, no contact happens before approval.
pinnedClauses.area: Agents on the bet, not just the backlog
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-6 **Requirement.** The agent compares who is asking (votes, ticket volume) with who matters (ARR, renewals due in 90 days, churned accounts, accounts whose usage dropped) and reports the selection bias, such as Enterprise renewals this quarter being absent from votes on reporting, with the accounts concerned and proposed research questions. It reads CRM and usage cohorts only within the grant its sponsor gives it, and any contact is an external call the company's policy decides. **Acceptance.** 1. A fixture where loud small-business voters differ from silent Enterprise renewals: the report names the gap with cited records. 2. Under the held policy, no contact happens before approval.

pinnedClauses.title: Bet review after release
pinnedClauses.gap: Review-due decisions, measurement protocols and outcome responses ship today. Three fixture outcomes (adopted, shipped but unused, negative follow-up) produce keep, change and reverse recommendations citing their data; missing usage produces unknown.
pinnedClauses.area: Agents on the bet, not just the backlog
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-6 **Requirement.** At a committed decision's review date after its release, an agent joins the commitment snapshot (DEC-004, LEARN-003's protocol), delivery receipts (DELIV), the release, cohort adoption (MEAS-005), outcome responses (REL-008) and follow-up feedback, and recommends keeping, changing or reversing the bet with the evidence on each side and its confidence; incomplete data is reported as unknown. Recording the review and any revision (DEC-006) goes through the decision tools. **Acceptance.** 1. Three fixture outcomes (adopted, shipped but unused, negative follow-up) produce keep, change and reverse recommendations citing their data. 2. Missing usage produces unknown.

pinnedClauses.title: Promise keeper
pinnedClauses.gap: Status-update drafts from approved roadmap moves ship today. A fixture slipped issue with a public ETA yields one draft and one owner reminder; dismissal records its reason; under the held policy nothing is published before approval. The remaining promise-detection kinds (a Planned reply on a dropped item, a ticket told "soon" whose issue slipped) and their corrections and reminders are not built.
pinnedClauses.area: Agents on the bet, not just the backlog
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-6 **Requirement.** The agent watches public replies, status updates, approved ETAs (ROAD-012), roadmap state and delivery changes for promises at risk (an ETA past due, a Planned reply on a dropped item, a ticket told "soon" whose issue slipped) and prepares source-linked corrections for the accountable owner, reminding them until resolved or dismissed with a reason. Publishing a correction or sending it to a customer is an external call the company's policy decides. **Acceptance.** 1. A fixture slipped issue with a public ETA yields one draft and one owner reminder. 2. Dismissal records its reason. 3. Under the held policy, nothing is published before approval.

pinnedClauses.title: Sales and renewal brief
pinnedClauses.gap: A fixture opportunity's brief cites that account's requests and uses only approved public wording in its suggested customer language.
pinnedClauses.area: Agents on the bet, not just the backlog
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-6 **Requirement.** For an open opportunity or upcoming renewal in Salesforce, HubSpot or Orbit, the agent writes an internal brief for the account team: the requests that account and similar accounts raised, their status and approved public wording, the cited evidence, and what may and may not be promised; it refreshes when status changes. Promises still go through publication. **Acceptance.** 1. A fixture opportunity's brief cites that account's requests. 2. It uses only approved public wording in its suggested customer language.

pinnedClauses.title: Weekly product brief
pinnedClauses.gap: Scheduled bounded learning runs ship today. A scheduled run over a fixture week produces one brief per subscriber with resolvable citations; an unchanged week produces none and no model call.
pinnedClauses.area: Agents on the bet, not just the backlog
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-6 **Requirement.** On a schedule, an agent sends each subscribed PM a cited brief of their area: rising themes, new high-value requesters, decisions due, promises at risk and connector failures, every line linked to its records, within a per-run budget. Unchanged inputs produce no brief and no model call. **Acceptance.** 1. A scheduled run over a fixture week produces one brief per subscriber with resolvable citations. 2. An unchanged week produces none and no model call.

pinnedClauses.title: Agent controls
pinnedClauses.gap: Learning runs meet this today. For each agent, revoking mid-run stops further reads and model calls, erasure removes its derived work, and the audit log shows each action.
pinnedClauses.area: Agents on the bet, not just the backlog
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-007, BASE-AGENT-009 · *Rules:* D-6 **Requirement.** Every agent runs under LEARN-004–LEARN-006's controls extended to every source: a named owner, scope (sources, segments, themes), budget, schedule, pause, resume and revoke, an activity log of reads, model calls, cost and proposals in the audit log (ROLE-004), and erasure closure (LEARN-005). Each customer contact, publication, merge, vote or commitment an agent takes is a call with its own class, decided by the company's policy at the Base chokepoint. **Acceptance.** 1. For each agent, revoking mid-run stops further reads and model calls. 2. Erasure removes its derived work. 3. The audit log shows each action.

pinnedClauses.title: One MCP door per seed
pinnedClauses.gap: Tools/policy/pause/audit/idempotency and evidence resources are declared. Both MCP eras use the same registry. Events, prompts and subscriptions remain undeclared.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** Every seed, hosted or self-hosted, serves one remote MCP endpoint at `/mcp` over Streamable HTTP. It speaks the current revision (2026-07-28) and accepts 2025-11-25 clients through the twelve-month deprecation window. It implements `server / discover`, tools, resources and prompts. Lists are deterministic and carry `ttlMs` and `cacheScope: "private"`. Roots, Sampling and Logging are not served. **Acceptance.** 1. `server / discover` returns the supported versions, capabilities, `serverInfo` and instructions. 2. A 2026-07-28 request works with no handshake, and a 2025-11-25 client completes `initialize` and lists the same tools. 3. An unsupported version returns `UnsupportedProtocolVersion`. 4. Two `tools / list` calls return the same order, with cache fields. 5. A foreign Origin returns 403, and a header and body method mismatch returns `HeaderMismatch`. 6. An oversized body returns 413 with no effect.

pinnedClauses.title: The seed's jobs are tools, through the UI's own actions
pinnedClauses.gap: Declared tools call real native services. Complete Core clause coverage, all native verbs, UI/REST registry unification and embedded-agent use remain incomplete.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** Each Core job a person does in the product is a tool. Where one is not, the Agent surface says why: it runs on a device, it is a person's interactive screen, it belongs to a connector or the import door, or it is an installation fact. Risk is never the reason: a risky job is a tool with its class (BASE-AGENT-006). Tools are named `<seed>.<area>.<verb>` and declare input and output schemas and truthful annotations. Each calls the same server action as the UI, so validation and authorization are written once, and the seed's embedded agents use the same registry. A business refusal returns `isError` with the seed's stable error code. **Acceptance.** 1. The Core clause ids in each tool's `_meta`, with the not-a-tool reasons that `server / discover` serves, cover every Core clause in the contract, and no reason is risk; the harness and `rer check` fail on a gap. 2. Each tool's fixture result validates against its `outputSchema`. 3. Read tools declare `readOnlyHint`; tools that can carry destructive declare `destructiveHint`, and tools that can carry external declare `openWorldHint`. 4. A refusal returns the same error code the UI gets for the same action. 5. The UI action and its tool, on the same fixture, give the same record state and the same audit event type. 6. The seed's embedded agents appear in the audit as calls to the same tools.

pinnedClauses.title: Records are resources
pinnedClauses.gap: Evidence capture/update return resource links; evidence:read and current native authority gate the native evidence projection and untrusted wording history (tests/base/penny-evidence.test.ts: captures source provenance (agent-resources.ts readback helper)). Other primary record resources, role-specific projections and byte-budget proof remain incomplete.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** Each primary record type has a URI template, and tools return `resource_link`s to the records they touch. A read returns exactly the fields the caller's role sees in the UI. File bytes count against any byte budget on the grant. A record the caller cannot open reads as not found, identical to a missing id. Text from customers, imports or files carries an untrusted marker in `_meta`. **Acceptance.** 1. `resources / templates / list` names every record type in the Agent surface. 2. Reads as two roles return exactly what the UI shows each. 3. An out-of-scope id and a missing id give identical responses. 4. A write's `resource_link` reads back the new state. 5. Bytes over budget return `budget_exhausted` and no partial content. 6. Customer-sourced text carries the untrusted marker.

pinnedClauses.title: Business identity and short-lived, audience-bound tokens
pinnedClauses.gap: Signed owner lifecycle, durable owner/team mapping, unknown and changed-email refusal, scoped native credentials and consent revocation are proved. Inactive/excluded sponsor fixtures and multi-sponsor lifecycle are undeclared; Penny has no native operator allow-list beyond current membership.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** The door is an OAuth 2.1 resource server. Its RFC 9728 metadata names the authorization servers this installation trusts. That is the paired Business when Business provisioned it, verified with the owner-claim trust the installation already holds for its import door; otherwise it is the seed's own sign-in. Access tokens are RFC 9068 JWTs with `aud` set to the seed's canonical MCP URI, `sub` the sponsoring person, `act` the agent (RFC 8693) with its specialist, scopes per tool family, and a lifetime of 15 minutes or less (5 by default). The policy scopes rules on the sponsor, agent and specialist the token names. The consent behind the tokens can last longer and is revocable. Tokens travel only in the Authorization header, and there is no passthrough. **Acceptance.** 1. An unauthenticated call returns 401 with `resource_metadata`, and the metadata names the trusted servers and scopes. 2. A Business token for this seed works, and the same token sent to a sibling seed returns 401. 3. An expired token returns 401, and a token with a lifetime over 15 minutes is refused. 4. A read-only token calling a write tool returns 403 `insufficient_scope` with every needed scope in one challenge. 5. A token in a query string is refused and not logged. 6. Revoking consent in the seed or in Business refuses the next call within 60 seconds. 7. After unpairing, Business tokens are refused and the seed's own sign-in still works.

pinnedClauses.title: An agent acts as a person in a role, never more
pinnedClauses.gap: Native current membership, narrow original key scopes and private view ownership are enforced. Access/security tool families are undeclared, so real widening/narrowing and self-escalation fixtures are not claimed.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** Every call is authorized as the sponsoring person's current role and access (BASE-ACCESS-004), intersected with the grant's resources, actions and budget. A grant only narrows. No call widens the calling agent's own authority. A call that would widen its own grant or its sponsor's role, or change the company policy or Pause, is refused with `self_escalation`, whatever the policy says; narrowing its own grant is allowed. Other access and security changes are ordinary actions in the access and security classes. An agent never acts after its sponsor is suspended. Anything an agent reads (records, files, emails, imports, other seeds' results) is data and cannot change its scope, its targets or a call's class. **Acceptance.** 1. For each role fixture, every tool's allow or deny through MCP equals the UI's for the same action. 2. A one-folder, read-only grant holds, and widening through arguments is refused. 3. Downgrading the sponsor changes the next call's result, and suspending the sponsor returns 401. 4. Calls that widen the agent's own grant or its sponsor's role, or change the policy or Pause, return `self_escalation` and change nothing, even under a policy with every class autonomous; dropping a scope from its own grant runs. 5. An injection fixture yields no out-of-grant call and no change of class: record text asking for a wider action, or claiming that a recipient is internal.

pinnedClauses.title: Every action declares its risk class
pinnedClauses.gap: Declared standard/live tool-class pairs pass native journeys and injection checks. The external/money/commitment/accounts/gated/access/security/destructive/sensitive families are not registered or claimed.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** Classes come from the fleet list in RISK-POLICY.md: standard, external, money, commitment, accounts, gated, access, security, destructive, sensitive and live. In the registry, each tool declares the classes it can carry and a server-side classifier that decides them per call from the arguments, current records and, for gated, the provider's answer. The classifier also supplies each class's facts: the measure (items, recipients, amount and currency, people or records), the counterparty (internal, known, new or public), the direction for access, the provider and step for gated, and the data kind for sensitive. A classifier never reads a flag, label or claim supplied by the agent or by record text. A seed cannot add a class; it proposes one for the fleet list. **Acceptance.** 1. Every tool in `tools / list` carries its possible classes in `_meta`, equal to the Agent surface table. 2. For each tool, fixture calls cover every class it can carry, and the computed classes and facts equal the fixture's expected values. 3. An argument or record text asserting a class or a confirmation (`internal: true`, `confirmExternal: true`) leaves the computed classes unchanged. 4. Money calls carry amount and currency, external calls their counterparty and recipient count, access calls their direction, and destructive calls their item count. 5. No tool in `tools / list` declares a class outside the fleet list, and `rer check` fails on one. 6. A refused call's audit row still records its computed classes.

pinnedClauses.title: The company's policy decides, at one chokepoint
pinnedClauses.gap: CORE signed policy, held native approval, unset/removed/blocked states and Pause pass normal conformance. Embedded, provider and queued lifecycle families remain unscoped.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** Every agent door calls one decision function: MCP, the integration API with agent tokens, and the seed's embedded agents. It evaluates the call's classes against the company's policy, as above. The seed ships no dispositions and fills no gap with one: agent access opens only under a complete policy that setup has asked for (RISK-POLICY.md), and before then every agent call returns `policy_unset` with the setup link and changes nothing. *Autonomous* runs the call. *Review* runs it and adds it to the review feed. *Approval* saves a pending action with server-computed facts and returns `input_required`, with a URL-mode elicitation to the seed's approval page and a pending handle. Each person the rule names approves the exact saved revision in a signed-in browser, and changed inputs need a new approval. The retried call returns the result and a receipt. A rejection returns `approval_rejected`, and a lapse past the wait the rule sets returns `approval_expired`. *Blocked* returns `policy_blocked`, naming the class, rule and revision. **Acceptance.** 1. The Base harness runs each tool under each disposition for every class it can carry, and sees it run, run and enter the review feed, wait with no effect, or be refused. 2. Before setup is complete, the setup page lists every class the seed's tools carry with examples and no answer pre-selected, an agent call returns `policy_unset` with the setup link and changes nothing, and an incomplete revision cannot be confirmed; a `*` rule completes it, and a tool an upgrade adds with an unanswered class appears in `tools / list` once that class is answered, while the other tools keep running. 3. Under "money autonomous up to $500, approval up to $10,000, blocked above", calls of $400, $600 and $20,000 run, wait and are refused; a per-day cap sends the call that crosses it to the next rule. 4. A call carrying two classes takes the stricter disposition. 5. An approval shows server-computed facts and an expiry, returns the URL elicitation and a handle, and completes once after the named approver approves; a changed input needs a new approval, and a rejection or lapse leaves no effect. 6. The same call through MCP, the integration API and an embedded agent gets the same decision. 7. A policy change applies to the next call within 60 seconds, and the audit cites the new revision. 8. A policy document with a bad signature or another Business's id is rejected, and the door keeps the last valid revision.

pinnedClauses.title: Truthful attribution
pinnedClauses.gap: Declared effects retain agent-for-person, sponsor and real approver attribution in door and native audit. Outbound content and native Undo are undeclared.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** Every agent act is recorded and shown as `"<agent> for <person>"`, and mail and messages an agent sends outside name it that way as their sender. An approval, a review mark, a confirmation (a warning dialog, a typed-field confirmation, a delivery confirmation), a decision or a signature attributed to a person comes only from that person's signed-in session. When an agent does the equivalent act, the record names the agent, and the act carries its own class; a binding decision or a signature is commitment. Agent doors ignore arguments that stand for a person's confirmation. No tool solves a bot check, or enters a person's own password or 2FA code at an outside service. A provider step that demands a person goes to a person, whatever the policy says; the gated class marks such steps before they run. **Acceptance.** 1. An agent call carrying a person-confirmation flag is classified and decided exactly as without it. 2. Approving, marking reviewed or answering a policy question with an agent or device token returns 403 and changes nothing. 3. A form-mode elicitation "accept" never completes an approval. 4. Where an agent's decision, signature or field confirmation runs without a person, it reads `"<agent> for <person>"` in the record, the activity view, exports and any certificate, never as the person's own act. 5. After a person approves an agent's prepared action, the record shows the person as approver and the agent as preparer. 6. Activity and exports at 1440 and 390 show `"<agent> for <person>"` for every agent act. 7. Mail an agent sends to an outside address names `"<agent> for <person>"` as its sender.

pinnedClauses.title: Every agent action is audited with its class and decision
pinnedClauses.gap: Declared calls, private reads, refusals, policy decisions and replay audit pass with differs_from_policy zero. Embedded-agent, provider and queued audit families remain unscoped.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** Extending BASE-OPS-005, each call that reads private data or changes anything records the agent client, name and specialist, and the run or task id (`traceparent` when sent); the sponsoring person, the grant, the tool and the targets; the classes and their facts, and the policy revision and rule; the decision (autonomous, review, approval, blocked, unset or self_escalation) and the outcome (done, refused, pending or failed); the approval or review id and person, and the idempotency key. For a period, the seed's Agents page shows actions by class and decision with the notable ones, the review feed (Mark reviewed, Flag, and Undo where reversible), pending approvals, steps waiting for a person and setup questions. Business shows the same across seeds. **Acceptance.** 1. One write leaves a complete audit row. 2. Refused, pending, unset and self-escalation calls are audited. 3. The Agents page's counts by class and decision equal the audit rows on a fixture week. 4. The review feed lists exactly the calls decided as review; Mark reviewed records the person, and Undo restores a reversible one. 5. Filtering by agent or class lists only those rows, and export includes every field. 6. Removing the agent keeps its rows and its name. 7. The Agents page works at 1440 and 390 with no serious or critical axe findings.

pinnedClauses.title: Agents can follow changes
pinnedClauses.gap: No event, cursor, subscription or signed-webhook implementation is declared for the agent door.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** The seed emits a typed event for every record change and for every approval, review and policy decision. Each event carries a stable id, a type, the record URI, the actor (a person, or an agent acting for a person) and a time. Events never carry secrets or more than the subscriber may read. Agents can read events three ways: `subscriptions / listen`, an `events.list` tool with a cursor, and signed webhooks from Base `integrations` using the same ids. Every channel delivers at least once and filters by access at delivery. **Acceptance.** 1. A subscribed record changed in the UI produces a notification within 10 seconds. 2. `events.list` returns the same event id the webhook carries. 3. Replaying from a cursor returns the same ids in order. 4. After access is revoked, no channel delivers events about that record. 5. A failed webhook is visible and replays without duplicate effects. 6. `approval.pending`, `approval.decided`, `review.flagged` and `policy.adopted` carry the class and decision and nothing the subscriber may not read.

pinnedClauses.title: Limits are policy, and Pause stops everything
pinnedClauses.gap: CORE Business/local Pause and consent revocation pass. Spend is none; no cost is registered. Mail edges, timed/dual-host/queued lifecycle, resource refresh and company spend reservation remain unscoped.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** Business limits are rules in the company's policy: per-call and per-day thresholds on any class's measure, such as money moved, outside recipients or items destroyed; spend caps on provider cost (models, SMS, email) per seed, specialist or agent, which setup asks with the classes; "no cap" is an answer. Tools with provider cost declare an estimate before they run, and an exhausted cap returns `budget_exhausted` before any partial effect. The seed's capacity limits (request rate, body and byte sizes) protect the installation: they bound rate and size, never daily business volume, are documented and are not policy. A grant carries budgets only when the person granting it sets them. A **Pause agents** control in the seed, and Pause all agents in Business when paired, refuses every agent token within 60 seconds until a person resumes; browser sessions and devices keep working. **Acceptance.** 1. A rate overrun returns 429 with `Retry-After`. 2. A per-day cap of three outside recipients sends the fourth to the rule that applies past the cap. 3. An exhausted spend cap returns `budget_exhausted` with no partial effect and shows the spend. 4. Under the answer "no cap", a spending call runs and its spend shows in usage; a call that spends nothing is unaffected by any cap. 5. The usage view shows calls, decisions by class, money moved and provider spend per agent. 6. Pause and Pause all agents each stop the next call within 60 seconds, and resume restores access. 7. An agent token cannot resume.

pinnedClauses.title: Writes are idempotent and conflict-safe
pinnedClauses.gap: Declared native write replay, changed-policy/current-scope admission and once-only effect checks pass. Full concurrent/provider/queued lifecycle families remain unscoped; native version guards are retained.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** Every mutating tool requires an idempotency key and takes an optional expected revision. The same key with the same arguments returns the first outcome for at least 24 hours; the same key with different arguments returns `idempotency_conflict`; a stale revision returns `revision_conflict` with the current revision. Long work returns a job handle and a status tool, with no dependence on the Tasks extension. **Acceptance.** 1. Two calls with one key give one effect and equal results. 2. A retry with a new JSON-RPC id and the same key, after a dropped stream, returns the recorded outcome. 3. The same key with different arguments returns a conflict and no effect. 4. A stale revision returns a conflict naming the current revision. 5. A job handle used by another person's token reads as not found.

pinnedClauses.title: Manifest, docs and the conformance journey
pinnedClauses.gap: The declared surface and native journey pass the agent-door conformance harness; docs are generated from that declaration. Other record-resource, event, prompt, subscription and wider specialist-week families remain incomplete.
pinnedClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** `server / discover` instructions and an on-site `/docs/agents` page are generated from the action registry. The page lists tools by job, with each tool's classes, the test that adds each computed class, its scopes, resource templates, event types, capacity limits and error codes, and the specialist role. `prompts / list` carries the specialist's jobs. Base ships the conformance journey, a harness that `rer verify` runs against `rer dev` and seeds run in CI. It is an MCP client; a signed-in test person takes a person's steps (setup answers, approvals, review marks, resume) through the URLs the door returns, and the same browser leg runs the UI-parity actions and the page checks at 1440 and 390. It runs every acceptance point of BASE-AGENT-001 to 012 and of the seed's SURFACE clauses under two company policies: *all autonomous* (`*`), and *held* (standard review, every other class the seed declares approval, which the test person grants), plus the single-class variants a point names. A point that names no disposition passes under both. **Acceptance.** 1. The docs list exactly the names in `tools / list` and `resources / templates / list`. 2. Each tool's classes, and the test behind each computed one, are documented. 3. The harness fails on any of: a tool without a schema; an effect under approval or blocked, or before setup is complete; a computed class that differs from its fixture; a flag that changes a class or completes a person's step; a role-parity mismatch; a wrong-audience token being accepted; a duplicate effect on retry. 4. Every acceptance point runs under both policies, every decision matches the policy in force, and under all autonomous no call waits for a person or is refused by policy. 5. A stranger agent given only the seed URL completes the specialist journey through MCP.

mainClauses.title: Public feedback portal
mainClauses.gap: Gap: owner-configured workspace identity and a changed portal description have no passing assertion.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** An installed Penny serves its public feedback board at `/`, with search, status, board, category and sort parameters, server rendering and customer-safe reads; `/portal/feedback` serves the same board as a compatibility address. The board's home identifies the workspace by the owner's company name and logo (INT-007) and gives the owner's configured one-line portal description; public feedback, roadmap and updates follow REQ-001, ROAD-006 and REL-010. **Acceptance.** 1. `/` and `/portal/feedback` serve the same board, with the same search, status, board, category and sort parameters. 2. `/portal` and `/portal/` answer `302` to `/` with the same query, and `/` does not redirect a filtered board request to a landing page. 3. Portal navigation, board filters, the submission page's way back, sign-in's "Back to feedback" and the operator's "Open public board" link use `/`, and existing links to either address keep working. 4. At both addresses the home identifies the workspace by the owner's company name and logo and shows the owner's configured one-line description, and a changed description shows on the next load. 5. The home makes no vendor, pricing, testimonial or metric claims and exposes no operator-only data.

mainClauses.title: Public product landing
mainClauses.gap: The run site's built landing page at both widths with no cross-origin request, cookie or workspace read; no test reads the built site yet.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Penny's public product page is the run site's home: `/` of run-penny.com, built from `src/site`, not a route of an installation. It is rendered on the server as the finished page, and its copy names only capabilities whose clauses are `done` in the Status table and shows no pricing, testimonials, customer logos, metrics or integrations Penny does not ship; drawn labels use the portal's own status and sort vocabulary. **Acceptance.** 1. The header has Penny's coin mark and name and links to the documentation at `/docs`, the public board, the source repository and `/signin`. 2. A hero has the page's one heading, a supporting line and links to `/docs/install` and `/docs`. 3. Sections, each with a decorative paper-collage drawing of Penny's own screens, cover the moderated public board, evidence-based decisions, closing the loop with followers, private commercial context, and self-hosted ownership the owner may change with their own agents. 4. A closing call to action repeats the two links, and the footer repeats the navigation. 5. The public board, roadmap and updates remain the portal (REQ-001, ROAD-006, REL-010). 6. The page reads no workspace or operator data, and its fonts, styles, script and drawings are the site's own. 7. The optional footer credit, "Powered by Penny · runeditrun.com", is visible by default and `showPoweredByCredit` in `src/ext/config.ts` turns it off; the credit is a plain link. 8. Motion is optional and plays once on load; it never loops, is off under reduced motion, and never hides content: without script, with reduced motion and after motion ends, every section is fully visible.

mainClauses.title: Public documentation
mainClauses.gap: Gap: manifest navigation order; build/development rendering and rejection of unlisted Markdown, broken links and forbidden image paths; full header/footer and page-navigation semantics; client navigation and HTML escaping; nested-unknown-slug 404/article exclusion; and workspace/session/cookie isolation lack sentence-complete running assertions.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Penny's delta on Base's on-site docs duty: the public paths `/docs` and `/docs/<slug>` serve Penny's first-party documentation, the install, portal, decision-loop, email, data and customization guides, from the deployment itself. The pages are the Markdown files that `docs/site.json` lists as published, in the sections and order it gives, which is the only navigation. **Acceptance.** 1. Pages are served as HTML rendered from the Markdown ahead of time, in a build and in development; no request and no browser renders Markdown, and a page loads only its own content. 2. A page has its title as its one top-level heading, under the same header as the product landing (HOME-002): Penny's coin mark and name linking to `/`, then links to the docs (marked as the current section), the public board at `/portal`, the source repository and `/signin`, of which a phone keeps the mark, the name and sign-in; the landing's footer repeats them. 3. A page has a section menu, an on-this-page list, previous and next links, tables in labeled scrollable regions and an Edit-on-GitHub link; after the page loads, moving between docs pages is client-side navigation. 4. Every Markdown file at the repository root, under `docs/` and as a top-level `<directory>/README.md` is either published or listed in the manifest as GitHub-only with a reason, and an unlisted file fails verification. 5. A broken internal link or anchor, an image outside `docs/media/` or an absolute build-machine path fails the build. 6. Raw HTML in the Markdown is shown as text, never rendered. 7. The documentation reads no workspace record and no requester or operator identity or session. 8. An unknown or nested slug answers a `404` with no article.

mainClauses.title: Roles
mainClauses.gap: Current operators share product access, and workspace clock settings admit Owners and Admins (OPS-008) while other configuration remains owner-only. No journey yet signs in one operator per role: the Viewer, Contributor, Product manager and Admin refusals, unchanged state on refusal and next-request role change lack passing assertions.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Penny's five operator roles, each checked in the business transaction like current authority, with a role change applying to the next request. Contributor and Viewer seats are unlimited, and operators invited before the full roles system ships become Product managers. *Policy: `operator.roles.v1`; default: the five roles below.* | Role | Rights | | --- | --- | | Owner | Everything, including installation configuration, ownership handover (OPS-002), integrations, export and erasure. | | Admin | All product work plus settings (including branding, INT-007, and sender identity, NOTIFY-013), boards, integrations, automation rules and the roles below Owner. | | Product manager | All product work on evidence, requests, moderation (including editing published content, REQ-038, and removing it, REQ-041), decisions, roadmap and releases. | | Contributor | The seat for support, sales and success staff: capture evidence, record proxy votes (CAP-014), comment internally and read product records; no moderation, publication, commitment, settings or commercial fields unless granted (ROLE-001). | | Viewer | Read-only. | **Acceptance.** A base and browser journey signs in one operator per role and attempts every guarded action through its route and its UI: 1. A Viewer is refused every write. 2. A Contributor captures evidence, records a proxy vote and comments internally but is refused moderation, publication, commitment, settings and every commercial field. 3. A Product manager is refused settings, integrations and roles. 4. An Admin is refused ownership handover, export and erasure. 5. A role change takes effect on the operator's next request.

mainClauses.title: Management
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Operators are invited and removed in settings. **Acceptance.** 1. The operator configured at setup can be removed only by themselves. 2. *Policy: `operator.management.v1`; default: any operator may invite or remove any other operator.*

mainClauses.title: Overview
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** The operator home lists decisions that are ready or review due, evidence that is unreviewed, roadmap items that are Planned or In progress, and releases published in the last 30 days with their outcome totals. **Acceptance.** 1. Every figure links to the records it counts, and a section with no records names what is absent and links to the action that creates one.

mainClauses.title: First-run setup
mainClauses.gap: A signed-in operator who is not the owner never being sent to /setup, setup completion staying out of archives, an installation with an active owner being treated as finished, and local rer dev opening signed in as the owner with mail suppressed have no passing assertion.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** The signed-in owner whose setup is unfinished completes it at `/setup`, and every `/app` document and client-side app navigation sends that owner there first. **Acceptance.** 1. Finishing setup opens the app, and later visits to `/setup` go to the app. 2. A signed-out visitor to `/setup` is sent to sign-in and back, and a signed-in operator who is not the owner is never sent there. 3. Setup completion is installation state recorded once by the owner under the same-origin and authority checks of the business transaction; it is not portable domain data and does not transfer in an archive. 4. An installation that already has an active owner is treated as finished. 5. After `rer setup`, local `rer dev` opens automatically signed in as the owner and returns them to `/setup` until it is finished; local development has no outbox and silently suppresses mail. 6. Setup cannot finish until the owner has chosen the workspace timezone and seen the requester quiet hours (OPS-008) and entered the company name (INT-007) and the business postal address (NOTIFY-014).

mainClauses.title: Global search
mainClauses.gap: Search across every other named field ships; product, component and feature names are not yet searched (src/core/features/workspace/list-repository.ts), and the 500 ms first page has no seeded run at the seed.json limits (D-3).
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Operators can search request titles and descriptions, evidence wording, decision questions and rationales, roadmap item titles and summaries, release titles and bodies, requester display names and email addresses, account names, and product, component and feature names (PRIO-001). **Acceptance.** 1. Each named field is searchable, and a result links to its record. 2. Searching one product, one component and one feature, each by its full name and by a partial name, returns it with a link to its record and in the same ranking as other results. 3. Product, component and feature results pass the same permission filtering as every other searched record: an operator who cannot open one does not see its name. 4. The first page of results returns within 500ms.

mainClauses.title: Capture
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Every portal submission creates exactly one evidence item in the same transaction (REQ-003). **Acceptance.** 1. An operator can also record an evidence item, whose source is one of sales call, support conversation, interview, email, or a free-text label the operator supplies.

mainClauses.title: Provenance
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Every evidence item stores its source, its original wording, the observed time, and the operator or portal submission that created it. Observed times follow the precision rules in [docs/contract-mechanism.md](docs/contract-mechanism.md#observed-time-precision). **Acceptance.** 1. The submitting requester or named speaker and the account are nullable, are set only from what the recorder supplies, and are never inferred.

mainClauses.title: Review lifecycle
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** New evidence is unreviewed. **Acceptance.** 1. An operator can link it to a request or to a candidate bet in a decision brief (DEC-002), create a request or a decision from it, or mark it reviewed with a reason, and can return any reviewed item to unreviewed. 2. Linking alone does not mark it reviewed.

mainClauses.title: Non-destructive linking
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** One evidence item can be linked to any number of candidate bets, and each link is recorded as supporting or contradicting that bet. **Acceptance.** 1. Linking, unlinking, tagging, merging a request, and committing a decision never alter or remove an evidence item or any of its versions; only an operator deleting it does.

mainClauses.title: Account context
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** An account has a name, an internal owner, optional commercial fields for revenue, renewal date, and health, its requesters, its evidence in observed-time order, and its linked requests and decisions. **Acceptance.** 1. Evidence recorded against an account appears on that account, and on every request and decision the same transaction linked it to, when that transaction commits.

mainClauses.title: Private commercial data
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** No field of an account (EVID-005), no evidence source attribution, and no internal note (REQ-032) is ever public. **Acceptance.** 1. None of them appears in a portal response, on a public page, in page metadata, in a sitemap, or in the subject or body of a requester notification.

mainClauses.title: Duplicate suggestions
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** When an operator records evidence or a requester types a request title, Penny returns within 500ms up to 5 existing requests ranked by term overlap between the typed title and stored request titles and descriptions, and names the matched terms for each. **Acceptance.** 1. A requester is shown published requests only. 2. Matching is lexical and deterministic and keeps working when no model is configured; AI-001 adds meaning-based suggestions beside it. 3. Penny never links or merges without an explicit operator or requester action, or an auto-link or auto-merge rule an owner enabled (AI-002, AI-003).

mainClauses.title: Evidence attachments
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator can attach files to an evidence item within the limits in `seed.json` under BASE-INPUT-003. **Acceptance.** 1. An evidence attachment is readable only by an operator session and is never served from a public path, whatever the publication state of a linked request.

mainClauses.title: Tags
mainClauses.gap: Tags filtering every operator list, surviving a request merge and appearing in the export have no passing assertion; tag privacy is asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Operators create, rename, merge, and delete tags and apply them to evidence items and requests. **Acceptance.** 1. A tag is operator-only, filterable in every operator list, survives a request merge, and is included in the export.

mainClauses.title: Versions
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Editing an evidence item's wording writes a new version and leaves every earlier version readable to operators. **Acceptance.** 1. The item's own ID never changes.

mainClauses.title: Public portal
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** The portal serves published requests, a request detail page with its discussion, the public roadmap, and published releases. **Acceptance.** 1. *Policy: `request.visibility.v1`; default: any visitor may read all four without signing in.*

mainClauses.title: Requester identity
mainClauses.gap: The requester's chosen display name in a portal response has no passing assertion, and the check that no email address or account appears reads the public request list while it holds no published request, so it checks an empty list; submissions under a valid host-signed identity, with and without outbound mail, and the refusal of invalid or new host identities without mail are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Submitting, voting, commenting, following, subscribing, and recording an outcome each require either an email address verified under REQ-023 (by emailed link, or by Google or GitHub sign-in under REQ-039) or a host-signed identity under REQ-031 (from a parent frame, the widget, or WIDGET-008's sign-in redirect). **Acceptance.** 1. A portal response shows the requester's chosen display name and never their email address or account.

mainClauses.title: Submission
mainClauses.gap: The unreviewed evidence item created in the same transaction as the request, and requester edits held for moderation, have no passing assertion in this clause's evidence; the held submission and comment are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A requester submits a title, a problem description, an optional free-text proposed solution, an optional free-text impact statement, a board (REQ-018), a category where the board uses them (REQ-034), and optional attachments; on a board with vote subscriptions on, the form states before submission that the author will get updates (NOTIFY-011). **Acceptance.** 1. The submission atomically creates one unreviewed evidence item and one request awaiting moderation; the request is not public until an operator publishes it, except on a board whose owner turned on auto-publish (REQ-033). 2. *Policy: `request.moderation.v1`; default: each board's moderation setting in settings (REQ-033); on a board without auto-publish an operator reviews every requester submission, edit, and comment before it becomes public.*

mainClauses.title: Duplicate prevention
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Before a requester submits, the portal shows the suggestions from EVID-007 with a vote control and a follow control on each. **Acceptance.** 1. Choosing one applies that vote or follow and discards the draft, creating no request, evidence item, or moderation item.

mainClauses.title: Publication
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator publishes a moderated request by approving its public title, description, board, category (REQ-034), requester display name, and each attachment separately (REQ-011). **Acceptance.** 1. The published record contains only the approved fields.

mainClauses.title: Voting
mainClauses.gap: Refusing a vote outside Open, Under review, Planned or In progress, and the author's vote recorded at submission counting once, have no passing assertion; one vote per identity and the distinct-voter total are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A requester identity has at most one vote on a request and can remove it. **Acceptance.** 1. The vote total is the count of distinct current voters, and a vote is accepted only while the request's public status is Open, Under review, Planned, or In progress (REQ-016). 2. The author's vote recorded at submission is NOTIFY-011's and counts once like any other. 3. *Policy: `request.vote-eligibility.v1`; default: any verified requester may vote and every vote counts once.*

mainClauses.title: Discussion
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Verified requesters and operators can comment on a published request. Threaded replies and images in comments are REQ-037. **Acceptance.** 1. A requester comment is held under `request.moderation.v1` and becomes public only when an operator approves it; an operator comment is public when posted.

mainClauses.title: Merge
mainClauses.gap: Moving the duplicate's evidence links, approved attachments and followers, keeping its title and source as merge history, and merging a duplicate into the end of its chain have no passing assertion; the 301, moved comments and collapsed votes are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator can merge a duplicate request into the canonical request, which is the one that survives. **Acceptance.** 1. The operation atomically moves the duplicate's evidence links, approved attachments, comments, and followers, collapses the combined votes so each identity counts once, keeps the duplicate's title and source as merge history, and answers the duplicate's public URL with a 301 to the canonical request. 2. Merging a request that is itself a duplicate merges it into the canonical request at the end of its chain.

mainClauses.title: Unmerge
mainClauses.gap: Restoring the duplicate's votes, followers and evidence links, leaving post-merge additions on the canonical request and recording the reversal have no passing assertion; the duplicate's comment and status update reappearing are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator can reverse a merge. **Acceptance.** 1. Penny restores the duplicate request's own content, votes, comments, followers, and evidence links, leaves anything added to the canonical request after the merge on the canonical request, and records the reversal.

mainClauses.title: Follow and consent
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A verified requester can follow and unfollow a published request. **Acceptance.** 1. Submitting and voting present an unticked "Email me updates" control and grant no email permission on their own, except that on a board whose owner turned on vote subscriptions (NOTIFY-008) the vote control says that voting subscribes and the vote itself follows, and submitting subscribes the author (NOTIFY-011). 2. Following, or ticking that control, stores a timestamped permission record for the verified address, which is what makes the identity eligible under REL-004.

mainClauses.title: Portal attachments
mainClauses.gap: Rejecting a file with a reason without rejecting the request, and the declared content type and inline disposition of a published image, have no passing assertion; approval, the 404 before it and the served bytes are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A file submitted with a request is operator-only until an operator approves that file for publication. Supersedes `BASE-INPUT-003` for published image attachments only: while both the parent request and the file are published, `GET /api/public/attachments/:id` serves an image type in `seed.json → limits.uploadTypes` with an inline disposition so it renders on the request page, instead of the download disposition. **Acceptance.** 1. Rejecting a file records a reason for operators and does not reject the request. 2. While both the parent request and the file are published, `GET /api/public/attachments/:id` serves it with its declared content type and, for the image types in `seed.json → limits.uploadTypes`, an inline disposition. 3. In every other state that path returns 404.

mainClauses.title: Portal search and browse
mainClauses.gap: Category filtering, newest and recency-weighted last-14-day trending are implemented alongside search, board, status and existing sorts. Gap: the 500 ms first page has no seeded run at the seed.json limits (D-3).
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Visitors can search published request titles and descriptions, browse one board at a time, filter by public status and by category (REQ-034), and sort by vote total, by most recent public activity (the request's latest published comment, status update, or vote), by newest, or by trending, meaning new votes and published comments in the last 14 days with each day's activity weighted by recency and ties broken by vote total. **Acceptance.** 1. The first page returns within 500ms. 2. No result, count, or facet includes an internal board, an unpublished or removed request (REQ-041), or a held or removed comment.

mainClauses.title: Submission idempotency
mainClauses.gap: No test repeats a submission with its idempotency key to get the original request and evidence result back, sends a changed body under the same key for 409, or checks 30-day key retention and keys holding no personal data.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A public submission accepts an idempotency key. **Acceptance.** 1. Repeating the same submission with that key returns the original request and evidence result and creates no second record of any kind; the same key with a different body returns 409. 2. Keys are retained for 30 days and hold no personal data.

mainClauses.title: Identity failure
mainClauses.gap: The visitor being offered email verification (REQ-023) after a rejected identity has no passing assertion; the refusal of expired, future-dated and wrongly signed claims at the host-identity exchange with the identity-required error, no writes and no account or identity disclosure is asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A host-signed identity is expired when its signed issue time is more than 24 hours old or more than 5 minutes in the future. **Acceptance.** 1. An identity that is expired, or whose signature does not verify, is rejected for every identity-required action, changes no data, and reveals no account or identity match; the visitor is offered email verification (REQ-023) instead.

mainClauses.title: Status updates
mainClauses.gap: A status update rendered distinctly from comments, pinned above them and notifying followers under NOTIFY-001 has no passing assertion; posting a pinned update and its text on the request are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator can publish a status update on a published request. **Acceptance.** 1. It is rendered distinctly from comments, can be pinned above them, enters the request history, and notifies followers under NOTIFY-001. 2. Setting a request's status (REQ-036) publishes one.

mainClauses.title: Public status
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A published request has exactly one public status: Open, Under review, Planned, In progress, Shipped, or Declined. A declined request is Declined (REQ-017). Otherwise two sources can set it: the direct status an operator sets on the request (REQ-036), including one a migration lands (MIG-008), and the status its approved roadmap mapping projects under ROAD-003. Whichever of the two changed most recently wins: approving a mapping (ROAD-004) and each later transition of the mapped item count as changes of the mapped status at that moment, and a later direct status overrides the mapped one until the mapped item's next transition, the rule DELIV-006 uses for tracker changes. Withdrawing the mapping or dropping its item leaves the direct status, or Open if none was ever set. A request with neither source is Open. The operator request page shows which source the current public status comes from. **Acceptance.** A base test: 1. A request with no mapping reads Open, then Planned after a direct set. 2. Approving a mapping to an In progress item makes it In progress. 3. A later direct set to Planned wins until the item moves to Shipped, which then wins. 4. Withdrawing the mapping returns the last direct status. 5. Declining wins over both, and reversing the decline restores the status this rule gives. 6. Every public payload agrees within 5 seconds.

mainClauses.title: Decline
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator can decline a published request. A decline without a public reason is rejected. Declining sets the public status to Declined, adds the reason to the request history as a status update (REQ-015), and refuses new votes and requester comments while leaving existing ones visible and counted. Reversing a decline restores the request's previous public status. Decline and reversal ship through the operator request controls; repeating a decline with another reason preserves the prior direct or mapped status for reversal. **Acceptance.** 1. Through the routes and the customer and operator screens at 1440 and 390, a decline without a public reason is refused. 2. A decline sets Declined and adds its reason to the request history. 3. New votes and comments are refused while existing votes and discussion stay visible and counted. 4. Reversing a repeated decline restores the earlier status.

mainClauses.title: Boards
mainClauses.gap: Renaming, reordering and archiving boards, moving a request with its votes, comments, followers and evidence links, and the 409 on submission to an archived board have no passing assertion.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Every request belongs to exactly one board. **Acceptance.** 1. Operators create, rename, reorder, and archive boards in settings and can move a request to another board, which keeps its votes, comments, followers, and evidence links. 2. An archived board leaves portal navigation, keeps its published requests reachable at their URLs, and refuses a new submission with 409.

mainClauses.title: Internal boards
mainClauses.gap: Keeping internal-board requests off the public roadmap, out of releases and out of requester notifications has no passing assertion in this clause's evidence; the request and attachment 404s are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Each board is public or internal. **Acceptance.** 1. A request on an internal board never appears in a portal response, on the public roadmap, in a release, or in a requester notification, whatever its own publication state. 2. Moving a request to an internal board withdraws it from the portal within 5 seconds and its public URL returns 404.

mainClauses.title: Requester's own content
mainClauses.gap: Gap: Request title and description edit retention, and auto-publish edits with earlier wording retained for operators still lack complete passing assertions. Holding-board own-comment editing and approved-text retention through pending, rejected and approved edits are proved.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A requester can edit the title and description of their own request and the text of their own comment. **Acceptance.** 1. An edit to already-public text re-enters moderation under `request.moderation.v1`, and the previously approved text stays public until the edit is approved or rejected; on an auto-publish board (REQ-033) an unflagged edit is public on submission and the earlier text stays in the request's history for operators.

mainClauses.title: Requester withdrawal
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A requester can withdraw their own request. **Acceptance.** 1. A withdrawn request leaves moderation or the portal, its public URL returns 410, and its votes stop counting. 2. Its evidence item survives under EVID-004, marked withdrawn.

mainClauses.title: Blocking a requester
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator can block a requester identity. A blocked identity's submissions, votes, comments, follows, and outcome responses are refused with 403; their published requests and comments are hidden from the portal but kept for operators; and their votes stop counting toward totals. Unblocking restores all of it. Block and unblock ship in the private requester directory, and the server checks existing sessions on each participation write. **Acceptance.** 1. Through the routes and the requester and operator screens at 1440 and 390, a blocked identity's submission, vote, comment, follow and outcome response are refused. 2. Its published requests and comments leave the portal and its votes leave the totals, while operators keep them. 3. Unblocking restores visibility, counts and participation. 4. Refusing the audit write rolls back the block or unblock.

mainClauses.title: Email verification
mainClauses.gap: The verified session expiring after 30 days without use, and a held action discarded after 24 hours without verification, have no passing assertion; held actions applied on verification are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A requester verifies an email address by following a single-use link sent to it; the link expires 30 minutes after it is sent and fails after one use. **Acceptance.** 1. The verified session is a browser-local token created at the requester's first interaction and expiring after 30 days without use, so no portal surface sets a cookie. 2. An identity-required action attempted before verification is held for 24 hours, applied on the first verification of that address, and otherwise discarded, and it creates no vote, public record, or notification while held.

mainClauses.title: Requester identity merge
mainClauses.gap: The survivor keeping both verified addresses and all requests, comments, follows and permission records, votes collapsing to one, the recorded merge, and no new vote or permission record have no passing assertion; carried mutes and preferences and working old links are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator can merge two requester identities. **Acceptance.** 1. The survivor keeps both verified addresses and all requests, comments, follows, permission records, and suppression state; votes for the same request collapse to one; and the merge is recorded. 2. A merge creates no new vote and no new permission record.

mainClauses.title: Requester activity
mainClauses.gap: The current moderation state and public status of the requester's own requests in the view have no passing assertion; the view's counts of their requests, votes, follows and comments including held and rejected ones, and unfollow, mute and subscription changes from it, are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A verified requester has one view of their own participation and can manage their updates from it. **Acceptance.** 1. The view lists their own requests with their current moderation state and public status, their votes, their follows, and their own comments including held and rejected ones. 2. From that view they can unfollow, mute, or change their update subscription (REL-012).

mainClauses.title: Demand attribution
mainClauses.gap: The vote date in the private supporter view, and the first 50 supporters on expansion with Show more revealing 50 more at a time, have no passing assertion (the browser check clicks Show more until it is gone and counts only the full history); the separate vote, linked-evidence and distinct-account figures with no score, the supporter view's names, addresses, accounts, proxy marks and per-account totals, the complete history with no 100-person cap, and the portal showing none of it are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** For any request, operators can see every current voter's display name, verified address, and linked account, and the vote total broken down by account. None of it appears in a portal response. **Acceptance.** 1. The operator view shows the vote total (proxy votes marked, CAP-014), the linked-evidence count, and the distinct-account count as separate figures, and combines them into no score; only a prioritization view an operator builds under PRIO-003 may combine them, with every input shown. 2. The private supporter view shows each current voter's display name, vote date, every verified address and linked account, with native and historical UserVoice proxy marks, and per-account vote totals. 3. The first 50 supporters appear on expansion; Show more reveals 50 more at a time until the complete history is visible, with no 100-person cap. 4. The operator demand payload holds exactly the three separate figures and no score, and the portal shows none of it.

mainClauses.title: Portal embedding
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Penny's delta on BASE-PUBLIC-002: the portal is Penny's embeddable surface, and the owner lists its host origins in the `publicOriginAllowlist` setting. **Acceptance.** 1. The portal's permitted host origins are exactly those in `publicOriginAllowlist`.

mainClauses.title: Request queue
mainClauses.gap: Queue filters and sorts work; the 500 ms first page has no seeded run at the seed.json limits (D-3).
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Operators can list every request, including unpublished ones, filtered by moderation state, board, public status, tag, linked decision, and account, and sorted by vote total, most recent activity, or age. **Acceptance.** 1. The first page returns within 500ms.

mainClauses.title: Operator-authored request
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator can create a request from one or more evidence items. **Acceptance.** 1. It skips moderation, records the operator as its author, links the evidence it was created from, and becomes public only through REQ-005.

mainClauses.title: Moderation verdicts
mainClauses.gap: A rejected item counting toward no public total and staying visible with its reason to its author and operators, and the author notice's consent, suppression, mute and quiet-hours checks, have no passing assertion; the unsubscribe link and the once-only send are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator can approve, edit and then approve, or reject with a reason any request or comment awaiting moderation. **Acceptance.** 1. A rejected item never becomes public, counts toward no public total, stays visible with its reason to its author and to operators, and notifies its author only when the operator chooses to. 2. This private author-only notice requires current verified request-specific email consent and respects suppression, mute, unsubscribe and quiet hours; it does not publish the rejected content or create follower notifications.

mainClauses.title: Host identity claims
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A host-signed identity may assert a display name, an email address, and an account identifier and name. **Acceptance.** 1. A valid signature marks that address verified without a further challenge and links the requester to the matching or newly created account; any asserted commercial field is stored operator-only under EVID-006.

mainClauses.title: Internal notes
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Operators can add a note to any request. **Acceptance.** 1. A note is rendered distinctly from an operator comment and never appears in a portal response, page metadata, a release, or a notification.

mainClauses.title: States and queue
mainClauses.gap: The review date in the decision queue has no passing assertion; decisions in every state staying in the queue with their state and owner, and the last action and linked-evidence count, are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A decision is draft until its brief has a question, an owner, at least one candidate bet, and at least one linked evidence item, at which point it is ready; committing makes it committed, and DEC-007 makes a committed decision review due. A question that is blank as [docs/contract-mechanism.md](docs/contract-mechanism.md#blank-decision-questions) defines it does not count. **Acceptance.** 1. The decision queue lists every decision in each state with its owner, last action, review date, and linked-evidence count, and a decision changes row rather than leaving the queue when its state changes.

mainClauses.title: Brief
mainClauses.gap: Per-bet assumptions, the low, medium or high confidence level, the review date, and the requesters currently eligible under REL-004 through the mapped requests have no passing assertion, and the brief does not carry the eligible requesters yet; the question, accountable owner, candidate bets, linked evidence and accounts, and each bet's counter-evidence count are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A candidate bet is one named option a decision could commit to, and a bet has at most one internal roadmap item. **Acceptance.** 1. A decision brief holds a question, an accountable owner, its linked evidence and accounts, its candidate bets with the counter-evidence and assumptions for each, a confidence level of low, medium, or high, a review date, and the requesters currently eligible under REL-004 through its mapped requests.

mainClauses.title: Comparable bets
mainClauses.gap: The absence of a stored or displayed combined score and of an automatic ranking has no passing assertion: the bet record and the stored snapshot are checked in a way that allows extra fields, and bets are looked up by id, so their order is unchecked; each bet's metrics holding exactly the five dimension figures is asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Every candidate bet in a brief shows the same dimensions: affected requesters and accounts, the count and most recent observed time of its supporting evidence, its contradicting evidence, urgency, delivery shape, and an observable success measure. **Acceptance.** 1. Penny stores and displays no combined score and no automatic ranking of the bets.

mainClauses.title: Commitment
mainClauses.gap: The decision.commitment.v1 default that any operator may commit has no passing assertion, since every cited commit runs as the owner; the recorded declined bets and the evidence snapshot of evidence IDs, evidence-version IDs and DEC-003 dimensions, with the evidence itself unchanged, are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Committing requires a selected bet, a rationale, an owner, a confidence level, and a review date, and committing a brief with fewer than two candidate bets additionally requires a recorded reason why no viable alternative exists. **Acceptance.** 1. The operation records the declined bets and an evidence snapshot made of the evidence IDs, evidence-version IDs, and DEC-003 dimensions as they stood at that moment, without altering the evidence itself. 2. *Policy: `decision.commitment.v1`; default: any operator may commit.*

mainClauses.title: Commitment effects
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Committing atomically marks the decision committed, creates or updates the selected bet's internal roadmap item as Planned, leaves the declined bets' roadmap items unchanged, and links the decision to that roadmap item. **Acceptance.** 1. Commitment writes no public field itself; whether the new status reaches the portal is decided entirely by ROAD-004 and ROAD-005.

mainClauses.title: Revision
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A later change of selected bet or rationale under `decision.commitment.v1` supersedes the prior commitment as a new decision revision, and the original rationale, evidence snapshot, and declined bets stay readable. **Acceptance.** 1. A revision that changes the selected bet returns the superseded bet's roadmap item to Exploring and, where that item was published, withdraws its approval under ROAD-004 and prepares a status update draft under ROAD-007.

mainClauses.title: Review due
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A review is complete when an operator records a review note and either a new review date or a revision (DEC-006). **Acceptance.** 1. A committed decision whose review date has passed in `workspaceTimezone` without a complete review becomes review due within 1 hour and its owner is notified under NOTIFY-003. 2. Becoming review due changes no roadmap status, no public status, and no selected bet.

mainClauses.title: Outcome evidence
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Post-release evidence reaches the decision it informs without changing what supported the commitment. **Acceptance.** 1. A requester outcome (REL-008) and any evidence recorded against a linked release appear on the decision as post-release evidence within 60 seconds. 2. Neither alters the evidence snapshot that supported the commitment.

mainClauses.title: Internal states
mainClauses.gap: The activity entry a status change adds to the linked decision has no passing assertion in this clause's evidence; each transition's actor, reason and from and to status, the decision's unchanged state, and backward moves recorded as further transitions are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A roadmap item is Exploring, Planned, In progress, Shipped, or Dropped. **Acceptance.** 1. A status change records the actor, time, and reason and adds an activity entry to the linked decision without changing that decision's state. 2. Moving backward is allowed and is recorded as a further transition.

mainClauses.title: Internal record
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A roadmap item keeps its internal planning record beside its customer-safe wording. **Acceptance.** 1. A roadmap item holds its owner, target or release window, linked decision and evidence, account impact, confidence, delivery notes, and its customer-safe title, summary, and status.

mainClauses.title: Public projection
mainClauses.gap: The absence of account names, revenue, internal dates, confidence, rationale, evidence, declined bets and delivery notes from the projection has no passing assertion in this clause's evidence, whose check of the public item allows extra fields; the projected public status within 5 seconds and a dropped item's withdrawal are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** An approved roadmap item's public status follows its internal status within 5 seconds of a transition: Exploring is shown as Under review; Planned, In progress, and Shipped keep their labels; a Dropped item is withdrawn from the public roadmap. **Acceptance.** 1. The projection exposes only the approved title, summary, board, and public status; account names, revenue, internal dates, confidence, rationale, evidence, declined bets, and delivery notes are never projected.

mainClauses.title: Approval is publication
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A roadmap item and each of its request mappings are internal until an operator approves their customer-safe fields, and that approval alone is what puts them on the public roadmap and on the mapped requests. **Acceptance.** 1. A published request has at most one approved mapping; approving a second is rejected. 2. Withdrawing approval removes the projection from the portal within 5 seconds, makes its public roadmap URL return 404, and deletes no internal record. 3. *Policy: `roadmap.publication.v1`; default: an operator approves every public mapping explicitly.*

mainClauses.title: Commitment mapping
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** The roadmap item DEC-005 creates or updates is internal unless it already carries an approval under ROAD-004. **Acceptance.** 1. An already-approved item projects its new Planned status under ROAD-003; an unapproved item and its mappings stay private, and commitment never grants an approval.

mainClauses.title: Public roadmap
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A public roadmap whose source is approved roadmap items groups them under Under review, Planned, In progress, and Shipped and links each to its public request or release. A public roadmap whose source is request statuses follows ROAD-014. **Acceptance.** 1. It exposes no unapproved item and no count that includes one.

mainClauses.title: Status update draft
mainClauses.gap: The draft's absence of internal rationale, commercial context, declined bets and outcome prompts has no passing assertion in this clause's evidence, whose check of the draft allows extra fields, and no cited case reads the portal before the draft is published; a draft prepared for each approved status change with the safe title, problem and new public status, unpublished until an operator publishes it, and no draft for an unapproved item are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Every status change of a roadmap item that carries an approval under ROAD-004, and every request decline under REQ-017, prepares a draft customer-safe update naming the new public status and the problem it addresses. **Acceptance.** 1. The draft carries no internal rationale, commercial context, declined bet, or outcome prompt, and is invisible on the portal until an operator publishes it.

mainClauses.title: Status update publication
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Publishing that draft adds it to the history of every approved mapped request and queues one notification per update version for each requester eligible under REL-004 who follows one of those requests, deduplicated by identity and subject to the coalescing in NOTIFY-002. **Acceptance.** 1. Republishing the same version queues nothing further.

mainClauses.title: Draft and targets
mainClauses.gap: A saved draft holding its publication date, optional setup or usage link and outcome-prompt wording has no passing assertion; the title, type, tag, body, author and target are entered and saved.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A targeted release draft has one or more targets, each linking one roadmap item in any state to its decision and its approved public request mappings, or one published request directly (REL-019); a draft with no target is an announcement (REL-018). **Acceptance.** 1. The draft also holds a customer-safe title, a type of New, Improved, or Fixed, one or more subject tags drawn from EVID-009, a body, a publication date, an optional setup or usage link, an author, and, for a targeted release, the wording of the outcome prompt shown with the REL-008 response.

mainClauses.title: Publication
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator can publish a targeted draft only when it has a title, a body, at least one target, and every linked roadmap item at Shipped; publishing with any linked item in another state is rejected. Announcements publish under REL-018 and request targets under REL-019. **Acceptance.** 1. Publication makes one versioned update visible on the portal and durably records the complete recipient snapshot (REL-004) before it queues any delivery.

mainClauses.title: Published wording
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Published release wording is never overwritten. **Acceptance.** 1. A correction creates a new version, keeps the earlier version readable by operators, and marks which version the portal shows. 2. A correction changes the portal only; sending it to recipients requires an operator to send it as a new delivery version.

mainClauses.title: Recipient eligibility and snapshot
mainClauses.gap: The snapshot staying unchanged after a later merge, relink or preference change, and the release.recipient-eligibility.v1 default (which actions grant a permission record, that voting elsewhere and an operator-entered address grant none, and NOTIFY-009's one-snapshot addition) have no passing assertion; export and restore of the snapshot tables, an identity merge fenced while a send is in flight, and follower erasure are asserted.
