mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A recipient is eligible when they hold a verified address and a current permission record, and each eligible identity appears exactly once in the snapshot however many target contexts it has. **Acceptance.** 1. At publication Penny snapshots every release target and each recipient's linked request or evidence context, and a later merge, relink, or preference change does not alter that snapshot. 2. *Policy: `release.recipient-eligibility.v1`; default: a permission record comes only from following a request (REQ-010), subscribing to updates (REL-012), voting on a board with vote subscriptions on (NOTIFY-008), submitting a request on such a board (NOTIFY-011) or an owner-selected migration carry-over (MIG-007, which makes its address eligible for email without verifying it); voting elsewhere and an operator-entered address grant nothing, and an operator's per-update choice to email captured contacts (NOTIFY-009) adds them to that one snapshot without a permission record.*

mainClauses.title: Customer-safe delivery
mainClauses.gap: The owner's brand header (INT-008) in release email and the remaining acceptance-point-1 email privacy obligations are unproved; private context staying out of the public updates is asserted. Live verified-domain, reply and inbox qualification remains held in R-6.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Release email and release portal content carry only the published release fields and the recipient's own request context. **Acceptance.** 1. Recipient lists, other requesters, account context, commercial impact, decision rationale, confidence, and declined bets never appear in either. 2. Release email carries the owner's brand header (INT-008), sender identity (NOTIFY-013) and postal address (NOTIFY-014).

mainClauses.title: Acceptance and retry
mainClauses.gap: The published update staying visible on the portal in every failure state has no passing assertion, and an ambiguous or interrupted send held unknown with no replay (point 3, reconciled with RL-3) is asserted for requester status-update mail but not for a release delivery; bounded retry of known failures ending in failed, and a restored queued release held unknown and inert, are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Publication queues each eligible delivery within 60 seconds of its permitted send time (NOTIFY-002), with the release scheduling and ordering rules in [docs/contract-mechanism.md](docs/contract-mechanism.md#release-scheduling). **Acceptance.** 1. A failure returned before provider acceptance is retried up to 5 times with exponential backoff over 1 hour and then marked failed. 2. After acceptance Penny never resends automatically. 3. A result the provider leaves ambiguous, or a send interrupted before its outcome is known, is marked unknown and shown to operators, and Penny never replays it automatically with either provider (RULINGS.md RL-3): Resend suppresses a duplicate for its delivery key (REL-007), while SendGrid's delivery key is correlation only. 4. The published update stays visible on the portal in every failure state.

mainClauses.title: Idempotent delivery and provider events
mainClauses.gap: Resend idempotency key and signed event dedupe ship; SendGrid has no provider duplicate suppression, so its delivery key is correlation only (RL-3).
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Every release version and recipient has one durable delivery key that Penny passes to the mail provider as an idempotency key, and the accepted provider message ID is stored against it. **Acceptance.** 1. Resend receives each delivery key as its `Idempotency-Key` and suppresses a duplicate within 24 hours. 2. SendGrid receives each delivery key as a provider idempotency key in the same way, so a duplicate send for that key is suppressed. 3. `/api/public/mail/events` accepts only signed provider callbacks and deduplicates their event IDs, which are retained for 30 days; signed event receipts are retained without automatic deletion, consistent with BASE-DATA-002.

mainClauses.title: Outcome response
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A requester in a release's publication snapshot can answer Adopted, Partly adopted, or Not yet for each of its targets, whether or not they have muted or unsubscribed from email. **Acceptance.** 1. Penny stores one current response per release, requester, and target; changing it records a revision and updates the aggregates without exposing the requester on any public surface. 2. Repeating the same response records no revision.

mainClauses.title: Outcome coverage
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Operators can see, per target and for the whole release, the count of each response and the coverage, meaning current responses divided by snapshot recipients, and can see the individual responses. **Acceptance.** 1. Each current response links through its snapshotted target and recipient context back to the applicable request or evidence, roadmap item, and decision.

mainClauses.title: Empty feed
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** The public updates surface tells the truth when nothing has been released. **Acceptance.** 1. With no release published, the public updates surface states that there are no updates yet and renders no draft, example, or placeholder entry.

mainClauses.title: Bounces and complaints
mainClauses.gap: A soft bounce marking one delivery failed and suppressing nothing, a spam complaint's suppression, and suppression removing no vote, request, comment or portal access have no passing assertion; hard-bounce suppression is asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A hard bounce or a spam complaint suppresses the address: no further Penny email reaches it until the requester verifies it again, and its permission records are marked suppressed rather than deleted. **Acceptance.** 1. A soft bounce marks that one delivery failed and suppresses nothing. 2. Suppression removes no vote, request, comment, or portal access.

mainClauses.title: Update subscription
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A verified requester can subscribe to every published release from the public updates surface and unsubscribe there or from any notification's unsubscribe link. **Acceptance.** 1. Subscribing stores a timestamped permission record for that address; unsubscribing withdraws it without removing votes, requests, or follows.

mainClauses.title: Delivery states
mainClauses.gap: An out-of-order provider event never moving a delivery backward and never counting a result twice has no passing assertion.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A delivery moves through queued, then accepted, then delivered, and can terminate at failed, suppressed, or unknown. **Acceptance.** 1. An out-of-order provider event never moves a delivery backward along that order and never counts a result twice.

mainClauses.title: Requester updates
mainClauses.gap: Notifying voters on vote-subscription boards (NOTIFY-008) as followers has no passing assertion; the subscribed author's notice is asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A follower of a published request is notified when an operator publishes a status update on it (REQ-015), including a status set under REQ-036, declines it (REQ-017), publishes a status update mapped to it (ROAD-008), posts a public reply on it, approves a requester comment on it (REQ-007) or receives an auto-published one (REQ-033), unless they have muted that request or their address is suppressed. **Acceptance.** 1. Voters on vote-subscription boards (NOTIFY-008) and subscribed authors (NOTIFY-011) are notified as followers, and a merge notifies under NOTIFY-012. 2. Held or rejected comments, unpublished requests, internal boards, internal notes, and an internal roadmap transition with no published update notify nobody, and republishing the same update version notifies nobody again.

mainClauses.title: Preferences, timing, and unsubscribe
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A notification's permitted send time is the first moment after it is queued at which the requester's preferences and the quiet hours below allow it. *Policy: `requester.notification.v1`; default: hold requester email during the requester quiet hours the owner sets under OPS-008 (by default 20:00 inclusive to 08:00 exclusive in `workspaceTimezone`; the owner may turn them off), and coalesce updates for the same requester and request in a fixed 1-minute window starting with the first pending event into one message, with later events never extending that boundary.* The deployment timezone input and the release ordering rule are in [docs/contract-mechanism.md](docs/contract-mechanism.md#notification-timing). **Acceptance.** 1. Every requester notification carries a one-click unsubscribe link that works without signing in. 2. A requester can mute one request or all requester email; the preference is checked immediately before each send and removes no vote, evidence, or portal access. 3. An eligible notification sends as soon as its window and quiet hours allow, and a wakeup that comes earlier sends nothing. 4. A missed wakeup is recovered within a minute under the same delivery claims, and a repeated wakeup or recovery run never sends a notification twice.

mainClauses.title: Decision review
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A decision owner receives one email and one in-app notification, which stays in their notification list until dismissed, the first time a decision becomes review due. **Acceptance.** 1. Operator email carries no quiet hours and queues within 60 seconds of the decision becoming review due. 2. No repeat is sent until the review date changes or the operator completes the review and schedules another.

mainClauses.title: No mail loops
mainClauses.gap: Sign-in and verification mail going out from MAIL_FROM or a NOTIFY-013 sender, with Auto-Submitted: auto-generated and no reply-to, has no passing assertion; a follower's status notification's sender, header and absent reply-to, and the refusal of its reply at every door, are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Notifications are sent from a no-reply address, and Penny reads no mail at any address it sends from. The only inbound-mail route is CAP-009's dedicated capture address, which accepts mail only from operators and allowlisted senders and never from Penny's own notification addresses. **Acceptance.** 1. A reply to any notification creates no evidence item, comment, request, or other record. 2. Every notification, sign-in and verification message goes out from the deployment's `MAIL_FROM` or a NOTIFY-013 tested sender, carries `Auto-Submitted: auto-generated`, and has no reply-to unless the owner sets a monitored one under NOTIFY-013. 3. The Worker accepts inbound mail only through CAP-009’s dedicated platform-invoked email handler; no HTTP route accepts a posted mail message. 4. CAP-009’s handler refuses Penny’s own sender addresses, configured reply-to and notification replies, retaining only non-personal refusal counts; CAP-009 enforces reciprocal capture/reply-to exclusion, and NOTIFY-013 retains its other obligations. 5. A follower's status notification has its sender, no reply-to and the `Auto-Submitted` header; its reply, posted as a raw message, an Inbound Parse form and a JSON inbound webhook to the provider event route and each plausible capture path, is refused, and no table changes except the per-IP request counters every HTTP request charges.

mainClauses.title: Notification failure
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Requester status-update email and operator decision-review email each use a durable recipient-and-event key and retry, suppress, and expose failure exactly as REL-006, REL-011, and REL-013 describe. **Acceptance.** 1. The in-app or portal record of the same event stays available when the email fails.

mainClauses.title: Export contents
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Penny's delta on Base export: the export names every Penny record kind. **Acceptance.** 1. The export contains every durable record as JSON, including every operator, requester, identity merge, account, board, tag, request, moderation decision and reason, merge history, vote, comment, note, follower, block, evidence item and version, decision and revision, roadmap item and transition, release, release version and target, delivery with its key and provider message ID, outcome and revision, subscription, suppressed address, notification and preference, custom field, and audit entry, plus every attachment as its original file.

mainClauses.title: Public/private boundary
mainClauses.gap: The absence of operator-only field names and values from a public payload has no passing assertion over a non-empty response: both cited checks read the public request list while it holds no published request (the non-empty public-surface scan in tests/base/penny-evidence.test.ts is not cited here); the refusal of invalid signed claims without writes or identity disclosure is asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Operator-only data never travels in a public response, rendered or not. **Acceptance.** 1. No operator-only field name and no operator-only value appears anywhere in a public response payload, including in fields the portal does not render.

mainClauses.title: Erasure outranks history
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Penny's delta on Base erasure: where a clause here says a record is preserved, versioned, immutable, or never overwritten, erasure under BASE-DATA-003 takes precedence: the record is deleted or anonymized and the surviving audit entry keeps an anonymized reference. **Acceptance.** 1. Unmerging (REQ-009) and revision history never recreate erased data.

mainClauses.title: Custom fields
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Operators define custom fields in settings on each entity listed in `seed.json → customFields`, and can read and edit their values wherever that entity is shown. **Acceptance.** 1. A custom field is operator-only and is never projected to a public surface.

mainClauses.title: Permitted originals
mainClauses.gap: The deployment pinning the source installation and permitted source principals has no passing assertion. Native runs refuse model-supplied identity and grants at root and option boundaries without changing authority or selected scope; valid output retains native identity derivation and legitimate run accounting. Separate original text, revision and time fields and nullable source identity are asserted. Live Orbit and model qualification and wider source qualification remain unproved.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Equal native operators select native evidence/requests and exact Orbit `rer-delegation/1` evidence targets with a recorded purpose/use basis and all-operator authorization. **Acceptance.** 1. The deployment pins the source installation and permitted source principals. 2. The adapter only reads selected targets; original text, source revision, supplied record time and retrieval time remain separate. 3. Requester/account links come only from native records; Orbit identity remains source-local and nullable. 4. Model output cannot set identity or grants.

mainClauses.title: Contestable learning
mainClauses.gap: Every option carrying the DEC-003 dimensions computed from originals, invalidation by native or source corrections with versioned operator contests, and the absence of automatic ranking, customer contact or publication have no passing assertion in this clause's evidence; validated spans, the clarification and the no-build option are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A configured model prepares an evidence comparison, exact validated spans, contradictions, uncertainty, a distinguishing clarification when evidence is thin, and a usable internal implementation brief. **Acceptance.** 1. Every option has the DEC-003 dimensions computed from originals, including a materially different no-build/process/support/onboarding option. 2. Native/source corrections invalidate current derived work; operator contests are versioned. 3. There is no automatic ranking, customer contact or publication.

mainClauses.title: Accountable pre-action choice
mainClauses.gap: The committed snapshot retaining the interpretation, original evidence, compared options, owner and full predeclared protocol, and missing protocol fields as explicit nulls that prevent commitment, have no passing assertion in this clause's evidence; commitment and its attributed audit are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** An operator selects an option, rationale, confidence and review date. Commitment is a decision record, not execution or an observed customer outcome. **Acceptance.** 1. The immutable snapshot retains the exact interpretation, original evidence, comparable selected/declined options and owner, plus the predeclared cohort, denominator, baseline, window, measure, data source, comparison, limits, stop rule and budget. 2. Missing protocol fields are explicit nulls and prevent commitment.

mainClauses.title: Bounded recurring work
mainClauses.gap: Expiry, budget, correction-version and erasure-epoch checks before external work and in the result transaction, the absence of any implicit contact, production or publication effect, and interrupted or ambiguous calls keeping their uncertainty and reserved budget without retry have no passing assertion in this clause's evidence; durable runs, unchanged-input deduplication, in-flight pause and revoke, and pause, resume, revoke and disconnect are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Scheduled Worker events refresh selected sources and advance the authorized evidence comparison/internal brief. **Acceptance.** 1. Every run has a durable event/claim, source revision cursor and budget reservation; unchanged inputs produce no new artifact/card/model call. 2. Source, purpose, native authority, expiry, budget, correction version and erasure epoch are checked before external work and in the result transaction. 3. No implicit contact, production or publication effect exists. 4. Pause one/all, resume within a valid grant, revoke and disconnect are native operator controls. 5. Interrupted/ambiguous calls retain visible uncertainty and reserved budget rather than automatic retries.

mainClauses.title: Privacy closure
mainClauses.gap: Running claims becoming uncertain after a restore has no passing assertion: no run is in flight at export and nothing reads an uncertain claim after the restore; same-source erasure across duplicate connections, hash fences under a fresh connection, revocation purging copies and derived work, and a restore that leaves no investigation active and refuses a restored run with learning_scope_changed are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Person/native contribution erasure deletes dependent interpretations, corrections, commitment snapshots and provenance copies. DATA-003 erasure precedence remains operative. **Acceptance.** 1. Same-source external-person erasure covers duplicate connections. 2. Stable provider/installation/event and person hashes fence replay even under a fresh local source connection. 3. Source revocation purges copies and derived work; in-flight results cannot survive a changed scope or erasure epoch. 4. Archives carry this history and opaque fences, never credentials; restored sources/grants remain held and running claims become uncertain.

mainClauses.title: Configuration and proof boundary
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Absent source, model or enforcing RPC transport visibly refuses work. **Acceptance.** 1. Installation-controlled configuration declares a model, token prices/output bound and source read cost. 2. The run reserves its ceiling before work, refunds known unused cost and separates metered cost from uncertain reservations.

mainClauses.title: Saved records
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A current native operator previews saved feedback boards, posts/status, individual votes/comments, explicitly supplied merge chains (saved post API mergeHistory with complete posts, or owner relationship sidecars) and private tags. **Acceptance.** 1. Every mapped request receives one exact-provenance evidence item. 2. Historical contributors have a non-authorizing provenance representation; imports cannot grant verified identity, consent, authority, an outreach audience or commercial context.

mainClauses.title: Review and mapping
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Exact originals and explicit status/visibility choices bind the reviewed fingerprint. **Acceptance.** 1. Unsupported fields, missing references and aggregate-only data are named before apply. 2. Rejected mapping prevents application; no row is silently dropped or guessed. 3. Publication/moderation remains a distinct native decision.

mainClauses.title: Durable custody
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Native D1 changes, original custody, provenance and checkpoints commit atomically under current session/installation authority and maintenance fences. **Acceptance.** 1. Identical sources repeat without duplication; changed identities conflict. 2. Restart resumes the persisted plan rather than acquiring the source again. 3. Imports never send or enqueue external effects.

mainClauses.title: Safe reversal
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Undo/rollback removes only owned effects under full native value, revision, relationship and cardinality fences. **Acceptance.** 1. Later native work or shared dependencies cause a visible conflict without collateral deletion. 2. Reversal is durable and restartable; ordinary reversal retains originals.

mainClauses.title: Privacy precedence
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Erasure purges affected retained originals/creation copies and records opaque target fences. **Acceptance.** 1. Old imports cannot recreate erased effects. 2. Historical identity and import metadata participate in product archive and erasure classification; installation credentials remain non-portable.

mainClauses.title: Ideas aggregates
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Saved Ideas CSV rows become unpublished, unreviewed requests with one exact-provenance evidence item under explicit source-key, status and visibility mappings. **Acceptance.** 1. Count, company, score, formula, owner and custom fields remain private source material, with aggregate columns named in preview, numeric totals and source-row coverage for textual company data. 2. Counts never manufacture individual voters, commenters, followers, accounts or commercial records. 3. Unknown headings and missing required headings are refused by name; an idea ID or URL must be supplied, never invented from a title or row number.

mainClauses.title: Move-in receipt
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Preview, apply and reversal expose a private operator receipt with per-kind source/read/applied/skipped counts and reasons, destination counts, named omissions and unresolved relationships, non-authorizing identity treatment, and job-created mail and notification counts (zero). **Acceptance.** 1. Reversal names removed effects and conflicts preserving later native work, and reports retained originals. 2. Receipt contents, attribution and commercial/source fields remain outside public projections.

mainClauses.title: UserVoice saved source
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Saved UserVoice ideas-only and Ideas & Voters CSV exports, read by the headings UserVoice documents, become unpublished, unreviewed requests with one exact-provenance evidence item keyed by Idea ID, under explicit status, board and forum mappings. **Acceptance.** 1. Each idea and UserVoice User ID pair becomes one historical, non-authorizing vote attribution with its original link date; repeated rows for extra accounts or captured feedback fold into it and stay in the private original. 2. A supporter is marked proxy only from the documented feedback-capturer columns, the mark is shown in preview, receipt and the operator request page, and it never upgrades the supporter. 3. A Subscribed value creates no follow or permission unless the owner selects MIG-007 carry-over. 4. Names and email addresses never match, merge or link people; account, company, revenue, subscription and contact columns create no account, follow, consent, verified address or outreach audience. 5. Each file declares its export scope; an undeclared scope is refused, a filtered one shows a partial-history warning, and claimed vote counts beyond the supplied supporters are named aggregate-only and create nothing. 6. Unknown headings, unmapped statuses or forums, unzoned timestamps and spreadsheet workbooks are refused by name before any write.

mainClauses.title: Signed first owner
mainClauses.area: Optional installation ownership and visual editing
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Penny's delta on native Base bootstrap: a trusted configured issuer, public signing key ring, installation ID and exact application audience can admit the first owner. **Acceptance.** 1. Expiry, signature, audience, replay, concurrent second claim and any installed owner refuse authority. 2. The original setup token remains compatible. 3. Claims cannot supply trusted configuration or take over an existing workspace; raw credentials stay out of storage/archives.

mainClauses.title: Owner editor
mainClauses.gap: Compiled data-only edits applying after the destination hydrates with native navigation and privacy preserved, and the management service's own admission of its owner and frame origin, have no passing assertion; the short owner-only lease and the refusal of other operators and foreign origins are asserted.
mainClauses.area: Optional installation ownership and visual editing
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** The optional maintained editor receives only a short lease and validated management origin/installation ID after current native owner admission. **Acceptance.** 1. Equal product operators remain equal for product work; this does not grant owner configuration. 2. Compiled data-only edits apply after the rendered destination hydrates and preserve native navigation/privacy. 3. The management service independently admits its owner and registered frame origin.

mainClauses.title: Scoped keys
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** A current native operator may issue a named optional-expiry REST key. Its random value is revealed once; only its hash persists. Route-selected scopes are `requests:read`, `requests:write`, `comments:read`, `comments:write`, `status:read`, `status:write`, `releases:read`, `releases:write` and `votes:write`. The first eight admit their documented resource reads and writes; `votes:write` authorizes customer lookup at `GET /api/v1/proxy-vote-contacts` and recording an attributed customer proxy vote at `POST /api/v1/requests/:slug/proxy-votes`, without verification or email permission. Bearers never grant operator HTML, generated-function, export or owner configuration authority. **Acceptance.** 1. A current token with `votes:write` records a proxy vote. 2. A token without that scope is refused the same vote write and changes no vote or permission record. 3. Revocation refuses the next write.

mainClauses.title: Current custody
mainClauses.gap: Credentials staying out of portable archives, and a restore honouring none, have no passing assertion; usage metadata written before authority is returned with storage failure refusing, revocation, expiry and issuer removal fencing requests and business writes, and a bearer key refused at export are asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Penny's delta on server-side authorisation for scoped keys: revocation, expiry and issuer authority changes fence every API request and its business transaction in the same native database. **Acceptance.** 1. Authorization writes safe usage metadata durably before returning authority; storage failure refuses. 2. Credentials are installation custody and are not a portable identity backup.

mainClauses.title: Native publication
mainClauses.gap: That imported or restored history creates no new publication or integration effect has no passing assertion: the cited upgrade case snapshots its tables after the import and compares them only across migrations, and no cited case restores an archive; prior history, including imported feedback, staying unchanged across each new migration is asserted.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** API writes reuse native validation, moderation, explicit customer-safe approval, consent, maintenance and immutable snapshots. Tracker synchronization follows the Delivery sync clauses (DELIV-001–DELIV-010), never an API side effect. **Acceptance.** 1. Imported/restored history creates no new publication or integration effect.

mainClauses.title: Explicit integration effects
mainClauses.gap: Gap: Selected public event kinds, immutable destinations, atomic business-write/event-target capture, held restored history and portable safe integration history with nonportable credentials lack complete passing assertions.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Operators select approved public request/comment/status/release events and immutable destinations. **Acceptance.** 1. Native writes and event targets commit together. 2. Imported/restored history cannot create live outbound effects. 3. Product archives carry safe event/attempt/receipt history; installation credentials are nonportable.

mainClauses.title: Enforcing transport
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Webhook/Slack dispatch uses the maintained Base delivery service through an installation-owned enforcing RPC transport. **Acceptance.** 1. Missing transport disables outbound integrations.

mainClauses.title: Durable uncertainty
mainClauses.gap: Gap: Durable attempt identity, finite retry, ambiguity/reconciliation and revoked/private/blocked send fencing lack complete passing assertions.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Attempt identity, finite retry, ambiguity and explicit reconciliation survive restart. **Acceptance.** 1. An ambiguous effect does not resend under another identity. 2. Revoked configuration and private/blocked content cannot start a send.

mainClauses.title: Signed inbound notes
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Original bounded bytes verify before parsing; current native authority, replay identity, internal note and processed receipt commit together. **Acceptance.** 1. Notes do not publish content or grant identity or consent.

mainClauses.title: Deliberate tracker issues
mainClauses.gap: Gap: Complete Linear/Jira create and link from requests/decisions, entered-only wording and uncertain-outcome reconciliation lack passing assertions.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Operators create or link a selected Linear or Jira issue from a request or decision. Ongoing state mapping, GitHub, Vector, Azure DevOps, ClickUp and Asana are DELIV-001–DELIV-010. **Acceptance.** 1. Only entered wording is sent. 2. Native durable commands retain uncertain outcomes for explicit known-issue reconciliation and never create a duplicate automatically.

mainClauses.title: Private tracker receipts
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Provider-specific raw-byte authentication, configured identity, durable replay and original source order guard state receipts in the same D1 transaction. **Acceptance.** 1. Older or conflicting events cannot regress state. 2. Linked state remains private evidence until an operator separately chooses Penny status or publication, except for the tracker states an admin maps under DELIV-006.

mainClauses.title: Owner portal branding
mainClauses.gap: The accent, description and Penny mark controls ship. Uploaded logos and favicons, their same-origin versioned serving and upload refusals, the website link and theme selection remain unproved.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Owners and Admins (OPS-001) set the portal's brand in settings, as Canny's Branding settings do on every plan: a company name (required at first-run setup, OPS-005, and editable later; it replaces the build-time `publicLandingConfig.ownerName` everywhere an installation names itself), a square logo (PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG sanitized to drop scripts and external references) and a favicon (ICO, PNG or SVG), each within `seed.json → limits` upload limits, an optional link back to the company website (an `https` URL), a readable public accent, the portal description, a light, dark or follow-the-system theme for the portal and widget, and whether Penny's own vector mark shows. **Acceptance.** A browser journey at 1440 and 390 pixels: 1. The owner uploads a PNG logo and an ICO favicon and sets the name "Acme" and dark theme; the portal header shows the logo and "Acme" in dark theme. 2. The logo and favicon are stored in the installation's R2 and served from its own origin at stable versioned paths: the document's icon link is the uploaded favicon, served from the same origin, and the portal makes no request to another origin. 3. A PDF, an oversize PNG and an SVG with a script are refused before storage. 4. The accent, description, theme, website link and Penny mark controls save and apply to the next page load.

mainClauses.title: Brand on every customer surface
mainClauses.gap: The company name is collected at setup and used by sender identity (OPS-005, NOTIFY-013); applying it throughout the portal in place of publicLandingConfig.ownerName, the website link, the logo on the widget, the changelog, the sign-in page and email, and the neutral default icon remain unproved.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** The brand reaches every customer-facing surface: the portal header (logo and name, linking to the company website when set, else to the board), the browser tab's icon and title on every portal page, the widget launcher and panel (WIDGET-001, WIDGET-003), the changelog page and feeds (REL-015, REL-016), the SSO sign-in page (WIDGET-008), and every requester and release email (NOTIFY-001, REL-005), whose header carries the logo and company name and whose sender name follows NOTIFY-013. A change applies to the next page load and the next message composed. **Acceptance.** A browser journey at 1440 and 390 pixels: 1. The company name replaces `publicLandingConfig.ownerName` everywhere the installation names itself. 2. The portal header links to the company website when set, else to the board. 3. The widget panel and the changelog page show the logo. 4. A status email to a follower carries "Acme" and the logo from the installation's origin. 5. Without a logo the header shows the name alone and the tab shows a neutral default icon, never a customer's.

mainClauses.title: Branding permissions and portability
mainClauses.gap: Admin branding controls remain unproved: the 403 refusals of branding writes by other roles and the archive round trip of logo bytes and branding settings have no passing assertion.
mainClauses.text: **Requirement.** Only Owners and Admins change the brand, and the brand travels with the installation's data. **Acceptance.** 1. Product managers, Contributors and Viewers are refused branding writes. 2. Branding (name, files, colors, theme, link) participates in product archives (DATA-001): an archive export and restore keeps the logo bytes and settings.

mainClauses.title: Workspace timezone and requester quiet hours
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-ROLE-001 **Requirement.** First-run setup (OPS-005) asks the owner for the workspace timezone, an IANA timezone pre-selected from the owner's browser (or from the `WORKSPACE_TIMEZONE` deployment input when it is set), and refuses Finish without one. The choice is stored as installation state that Owners and Admins change later in settings; once stored it is the `workspaceTimezone` every clause uses (NOTIFY-002, DEC-007, REL-014), and no installation that has recorded a choice falls back to a built-in default. An installation that finished setup before this ships shows its owner a one-time prompt, on their next sign-in, to confirm or change the current timezone. Settings also hold the requester quiet hours, shown beside the timezone at setup: off, or a start and an end hour in the workspace timezone (default 20:00 to 08:00). Operator email never has quiet hours (NOTIFY-003). A change applies at the next send check, and turning quiet hours off makes every held requester message due at once. In Admin settings, Owners and Admins set the workspace timezone and requester business hours through the quiet-hours schedule. Changes take effect for clocks and SLAs from the change, including the next queued requester send check and calendar-based decision review check. **Acceptance.** A base and browser journey: 1. Setup refuses Finish without a timezone. 2. Setup under an `America/New_York` browser timezone stores `America/New_York`. 3. With the default quiet hours, a status update published at 21:00 Eastern sends at 08:00 Eastern and one published at 14:00 Eastern sends within NOTIFY-002's coalescing window. 4. With quiet hours off, an update published at 23:00 Eastern sends within the coalescing window. 5. Changing the timezone in settings moves the next quiet period. 6. The confirmation prompt appears once for an installation set up before the change. 7. An Owner and an Admin each save the timezone and quiet-hours schedule in Admin, an ordinary operator is refused, and changing the timezone changes a calendar review's next due check while turning quiet hours off releases queued requester mail without delaying operator mail.

mainClauses.title: Custom roles and restricted commercial fields
mainClauses.gap: A base test signs in under a role without commercial permission and reads requests, accounts, prioritization views, CSV exports and Ask Penny answers through their routes: no revenue, opportunity or health value appears; granting the permission reveals them on the next request; each role change is in the audit log (ROLE-004).
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-ROLE-001 **Requirement.** Admins define custom roles from a fixed permission set (capture evidence and proxy votes, moderate, publish, commit decisions, manage roadmap, manage releases, manage integrations, manage automation, view commercial fields, export, erase) and assign them to operators. Commercial fields (revenue, MRR/ARR, opportunity amounts, health) are hidden from roles without "view commercial fields" in every screen, API response, export, agent answer and notification, including AI-006 draft context and publication checks. **Acceptance.** A base test signs in under a role without commercial permission and reads requests, accounts, prioritization views, CSV exports and Ask Penny answers through their routes: 1. No revenue, opportunity or health value appears. 2. Granting the permission reveals them on the next request. 3. Each role change is in the audit log (ROLE-004).

mainClauses.title: Operator single sign-on
mainClauses.gap: Today only the optional IDENTITY_PROVIDER dependency is declared; sign-in remains email links. A browser journey against SAML and OIDC test identity providers at the network edge: a first sign-in creates a Contributor, a group claim maps another user to Admin, an enforced domain refuses an email link, and an IdP-side deactivation ends access at the next session check.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-SIGNIN-001 · *Register:* R-14 **Requirement.** Penny's delta on Base standards-based SSO: operators sign in with SAML 2.0 or OIDC from Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace or Auth (the sibling identity provider, https://github.com/just-every/run-auth). The owner can enforce SSO for a verified email domain (email links then refuse that domain), provision operators just in time with a default role, and map IdP groups to roles. **Acceptance.** A browser journey against SAML and OIDC test identity providers at the network edge: 1. A first sign-in creates a Contributor. 2. A group claim maps another user to Admin. 3. An enforced domain refuses an email link. 4. An IdP-side deactivation ends access at the next session check. 5. An address on an SSO-enforced domain that signs in through REQ-039 stays only a requester, and REQ-039's unverified fallback link obeys the domain's email-link refusal.

mainClauses.title: SCIM provisioning
mainClauses.gap: Okta and Entra SCIM request fixtures through the public endpoint create, patch and deactivate a user; the deactivated user's session and API key are refused on their next request, as they are after OPS-002 removal.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Later · *Cites:* BASE-SIGNIN-001 · *Register:* R-15 **Requirement.** SCIM 2.0 Users and Groups endpoints let Okta and Entra create operators, change their role by group membership and deactivate them; deactivation revokes cookies, links, generated functions and keys exactly as OPS-002 removal does. **Acceptance.** 1. Okta and Entra SCIM request fixtures through the public endpoint create, patch and deactivate a user. 2. The deactivated user's session and API key are refused on their next request, as they are after OPS-002 removal.

mainClauses.title: Audit log
mainClauses.gap: Durable actor audits are recorded and archived today; there is no audit screen or export. Perform each listed action (including REQ-038 and REQ-041 edits, removals, restores and permanent deletes and INT-007 and NOTIFY-013 changes), then read and export the log through the UI and API; erase an operator and see their entries anonymized while the events remain.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-AUDIT-001, BASE-OPS-005 **Requirement.** Penny's delta on Base audit: Owners and Admins read, filter (actor, action, subject, date) and export as CSV or JSON an audit log of every privileged action: publication, moderation verdict, edit (REQ-038), removal, restore and permanent delete (REQ-041) of published content, branding and sender changes (INT-007, NOTIFY-013), merge and unmerge, commitment, role and member change, integration connect and disconnect, automation rule change, export, erasure and every agent action, with the person or agent responsible. **Acceptance.** 1. Perform each listed action, then read and export the log through the UI and API. 2. Entries contain no customer wording or commercial values. 3. Erase an operator and see their entries anonymized while the events remain (DATA-003).

mainClauses.title: Saved views and filters
mainClauses.gap: A browser test saves a filtered, sorted view, then a second operator opens the shared view and gets the same result set; a private view is not listed for them.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Every operator list (inbox, requests, features, evidence, accounts, roadmap, releases) filters on any field, custom field, tag, theme, segment, owner and date, chooses its columns and sort, and saves the result as a private or shared view. **Acceptance.** 1. A browser test saves a filtered, sorted view, then a second operator opens the shared view and gets the same result set. 2. A private view is not listed for them.

mainClauses.title: Person view
mainClauses.gap: Voter lists and account requesters ship today; no per-person page exists. A fixture requester with two posts, three votes, a comment, captured Zendesk evidence and an account: the profile lists each with a link to its record; a role without commercial permission sees no ARR or MRR; the profile path answers 404 to a portal visitor and appears in no public payload.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Every requester and captured contact has an operator profile: display name, verified and carried-over addresses (MIG-007), company or account with its ARR and MRR (ROLE-001), segment membership (SEG-006), custom fields (DATA-004), every request they submitted, voted on (with importance, REQ-035, and proxy marks), followed or commented on, the evidence captured about them with its source links (CAP-002), their permission records and suppression state, and their outcome responses (REL-008). It is reachable from global search (OPS-004), request voter lists (REQ-026) and account pages (EVID-005), and offers merge (REQ-024), block (REQ-022), export and erasure (DATA-003). **Acceptance.** 1. A fixture requester with two posts, three votes, a comment, captured Zendesk evidence and an account: the profile lists each with a link to its record. 2. A role without commercial permission sees no ARR or MRR. 3. The profile path answers 404 to a portal visitor and appears in no public payload.

mainClauses.title: Feedback inbox
mainClauses.gap: Today the unreviewed evidence list does this for portal and manually recorded evidence only. A browser journey at 1440 and 390 pixels: items from three connector fixtures arrive, are triaged by keyboard (link, create, dismiss with reason, snooze), each linked request shows the item with its source link, and the overview counts match the inbox.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Every item captured from any channel (portal, widget, connectors, email, Slack, browser extension, API) lands once as unreviewed evidence (EVID-001) in one inbox that shows its source, customer, account, segment attributes, excerpt and suggested links (AI-002). From the inbox an operator links it to a request, creates a request (REQ-029), adds it to a decision, assigns an owner (TRIAGE-001), tags it, snoozes it until a date or marks it reviewed with a reason, by keyboard and in bulk (TRIAGE-005). The inbox filters by source, connector, owner, segment, theme, age and state. **Acceptance.** A browser journey at 1440 and 390 pixels: 1. Items from three connector fixtures arrive, are triaged by keyboard (link, create, dismiss with reason, snooze), each linked request shows the item with its source link, and the overview counts match the inbox.

mainClauses.title: Source provenance and link-back
mainClauses.gap: EVID-002 provenance ships today for manually recorded sources without deep links or source sync. A connector fixture test captures a record, edits it at the source and deletes it at the source: Penny shows changed and removed states, purges the excerpt at the window, and the deep link opens the original record.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** A captured item stores its connector, the source record's ID, a deep link to the original (ticket, conversation, call timestamp, Slack permalink, email message ID or page URL), the verbatim excerpt the operator or rule selected, the author or speaker as the source names them, the capturing person or rule and the source's own time. When the source record changes, the captured version stays and Penny shows that the source changed; when it is deleted or access is revoked at the source, the item is marked source-removed and its excerpt is purged after the owner's policy window. **Acceptance.** 1. A connector fixture test captures a record, edits it at the source and deletes it at the source: Penny shows changed and removed states, purges the excerpt at the window, and the deep link opens the original record.

mainClauses.title: Zendesk
mainClauses.gap: Zendesk OAuth, API and webhook fixtures at the network edge: install, link, create and proxy-vote from the sidebar; tag-triggered capture creates one item per ticket however often the webhook replays; the status appears in the sidebar; uninstalling revokes and deletes the tokens.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1, D-2 · *Register:* R-5, R-8 **Requirement.** A Zendesk app in the ticket sidebar lets an agent search requests, link the ticket to one, create a new request, record a proxy vote for the ticket's requester (CAP-014) and see the request's public status without leaving Zendesk. Tickets with a configured tag or in a configured view are captured automatically. The ticket requester and organization map to a Penny requester and account by email and organization ID. When a linked request changes status, the sidebar shows it and offers the drafted reply (NOTIFY-007). **Acceptance.** 1. Zendesk OAuth, API and webhook fixtures at the network edge: install, link, create and proxy-vote from the sidebar. 2. Tag-triggered capture creates one item per ticket however often the webhook replays. 3. The status appears in the sidebar. 4. Uninstalling revokes and deletes the tokens.

mainClauses.title: Intercom
mainClauses.gap: Intercom API and webhook fixtures run CAP-003's journey and show company attributes arriving as private segment attributes.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1, D-2 **Requirement.** An Intercom Inbox app (Canvas Kit) offers CAP-003's actions inside a conversation; conversations with a configured tag or topic are captured; Intercom contacts and companies map to requesters and accounts with their custom attributes (plan, MRR) feeding segments (SEG-006); NOTIFY-007 replies can go back through the conversation. **Acceptance.** 1. Intercom API and webhook fixtures run CAP-003's journey and show company attributes arriving as private segment attributes.

mainClauses.title: HappyToHelp
mainClauses.gap: A journey against a running HappyToHelp test installation links a ticket, captures one by tag and receives the drafted status reply on that ticket.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1, D-2 **Requirement.** HappyToHelp, the sibling help desk (https://github.com/just-every/run-happytohelp), gets CAP-003's sidebar, tag capture and close-the-loop replies through its public API. Neither product keeps the other's records beyond the linked excerpt and IDs. **Acceptance.** 1. A journey against a running HappyToHelp test installation links a ticket, captures one by tag and receives the drafted status reply on that ticket.

mainClauses.title: Help Scout
mainClauses.gap: Help Scout API fixtures: link, create, tag capture and mapping, each once per conversation.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1, D-2 **Requirement.** A Help Scout sidebar app and tag-based capture with customer and company mapping, on CAP-003's terms. **Acceptance.** Help Scout API fixtures: 1. Link, create, tag capture and mapping, each once per conversation.

mainClauses.title: Gong
mainClauses.gap: Gong API fixtures: filtered calls are ingested, proposals carry exact transcript spans and timestamps, accounts map through Gong's CRM association, and the fixture records no request for an out-of-filter call.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** For calls matching configured filters (workspace, tracker, deal stage, participants), Penny reads the transcript and call metadata, and the extraction agent (AI-004) proposes the feature-request moments as inbox items with the verbatim span, speaker, a timestamped deep link and the deal and account Gong associates. Calls outside the filters are never read. **Acceptance.** Gong API fixtures: 1. Filtered calls are ingested, proposals carry exact transcript spans and timestamps, accounts map through Gong's CRM association, and the fixture records no request for an out-of-filter call.

mainClauses.title: Call recorders, recordings and transcripts
mainClauses.gap: Fathom, Zoom, Google Meet, Fireflies, Grain and tl;dv fixtures each ingest one filtered call with timestamped spans and ignore an out-of-filter call; a VTT upload produces a searchable transcript whose highlight becomes evidence with a timestamp link; an audio upload shows progress, reserved and metered cost, and a visible failure when the provider fails.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** Fathom, Zoom cloud recording, Google Meet (Workspace recordings and transcripts), Fireflies, Grain and tl;dv connectors work on CAP-007's terms. An operator can also upload a recording or a VTT, SRT or text transcript; audio is transcribed by the owner-configured transcription provider as a bounded background job with LEARN-006's cost rules. Transcripts are searchable, and a highlighted passage becomes evidence linked to its timestamp. **Acceptance.** 1. Fathom, Zoom, Google Meet, Fireflies, Grain and tl;dv fixtures each ingest one filtered call with timestamped spans and ignore an out-of-filter call. 2. A VTT upload produces a searchable transcript whose highlight becomes evidence with a timestamp link. 3. An audio upload shows progress, reserved and metered cost, and a visible failure when the provider fails.

mainClauses.title: Email capture
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-2 · *Register:* R-3 **Requirement.** Each installation has a dedicated capture address on the owner's domain (Cloudflare Email Routing or the configured mail provider's inbound parse). Operators forward or BCC customer emails to it. Penny accepts only mail from operator addresses or allowlisted domains with DMARC alignment, recovers the original sender from the forwarded message, keeps attachments within `seed.json` limits and creates one inbox item per message ID. Notification reply addresses never reach this route, and it refuses mail from Penny's own sender addresses (`MAIL_FROM` and any NOTIFY-013 sender), as NOTIFY-004 requires. **Acceptance.** Inbound-mail fixtures: 1. Forwarded Gmail and Outlook messages each create one item attributed to the original sender. 2. A replayed message ID, an unaligned sender, mail from Penny's own sender address and a reply to a Penny notification create nothing.

mainClauses.title: Slack and Nook
mainClauses.gap: Signed Slack Events and Interactivity fixtures: the shortcut and the reaction each capture a message once, a bad signature is refused, and a Slack Connect channel maps to its account; the same capture runs against a Nook test installation.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 · *Register:* R-8 **Requirement.** A Slack app adds a "Send to Penny" message shortcut and an emoji-reaction trigger in selected channels, including Slack Connect channels shared with customers. The message and its thread permalink become an inbox item, the Slack user who triggered it is the capturer, and a Slack Connect workspace maps to an account. Nook, the sibling team chat (https://github.com/just-every/run-nook), offers the same actions. Outbound Slack posts are NOTIFY-006 and INT-001. **Acceptance.** Signed Slack Events and Interactivity fixtures: 1. The shortcut and the reaction each capture a message once, a bad signature is refused, and a Slack Connect channel maps to its account. 2. The same capture runs against a Nook test installation.

mainClauses.title: Microsoft Teams
mainClauses.gap: Bot Framework fixtures with token validation capture a message once and refuse an unsigned request.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** A Teams message action captures a message and its link into the inbox; channel notifications follow NOTIFY-006. **Acceptance.** 1. Bot Framework fixtures with token validation capture a message once and refuse an unsigned request.

mainClauses.title: Browser extension
mainClauses.gap: A Playwright extension journey on a fixture page creates an inbox item with the URL, excerpt and screenshot attachment; a signed-out extension is refused.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 · *Register:* R-8 **Requirement.** A Chrome and Edge extension (Manifest V3), signed in with the operator's Penny session, captures selected text or a screenshot from any page (a CRM record, a review site, a community thread) with its URL, picks the customer and the request, and can record a proxy vote. **Acceptance.** 1. A Playwright extension journey on a fixture page creates an inbox item with the URL, excerpt and screenshot attachment. 2. A signed-out extension is refused.

mainClauses.title: CRM record panels
mainClauses.gap: HubSpot and Salesforce fixtures render the panel for a record's company, capture feedback tied to an opportunity amount and attribute a proxy vote to the right customer.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** A HubSpot CRM card and a Salesforce Lightning component on contact, company or account and deal or opportunity records show that account's requests and their statuses, and let sales capture feedback or a proxy vote tied to the opportunity (SEG-002). Orbit gets the same panel through its extension point. **Acceptance.** 1. HubSpot and Salesforce fixtures render the panel for a record's company, capture feedback tied to an opportunity amount and attribute a proxy vote to the right customer.

mainClauses.title: Proxy votes
mainClauses.gap: UserVoice-imported supporters keeping their historical proxy marks (IMP-008) have no passing assertion in this clause's evidence (tests/base/feedback-import-uservoice.test.ts asserts them and is not cited here), and the CSV export is checked for the source text and the customer but never the recorder; counting once per customer, the proxy mark with who recorded it, collapse with the customer's own later vote, no verified identity, consent or permission record, public appearance only inside the vote total, and recording from the inbox, the request page and the Zendesk sidebar fixture are asserted.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Register:* R-5 **Requirement.** An operator records a vote on behalf of a customer (an existing requester, a connector contact, or a new unverified contact) with the source that justifies it. **Acceptance.** 1. A proxy vote counts once per customer in demand (REQ-026, SEG-007), is marked proxy with who recorded it, and collapses with that customer's own later vote. 2. It grants no verified identity or email consent (REQ-010), and appears publicly only inside the vote total. 3. Native proxy recording works from the inbox, the request page and the private Zendesk sidebar at the connector edge, proved with a network-edge fixture. 4. Supporters imported from UserVoice (IMP-008) retain their historical proxy marks. 5. A base test records proxy votes from the inbox, the request page and a Zendesk sidebar fixture: each counts once, collapses with the customer's own later vote, creates no permission record, and appears in the CSV export with its recorder.

mainClauses.title: Automation platforms
mainClauses.gap: Scoped keys and outbound events ship today; no packaged app exists. A Zapier CLI test against a running installation fires each trigger once per event and runs each action within its key's scopes; an out-of-scope action is refused.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 · *Register:* R-8 **Requirement.** Zapier and Make apps offer triggers (new request, status change, new evidence, release published) and actions (create evidence, create request, record proxy vote, find request) over the scoped REST API (API-001) and signed webhooks (INT-001); Crank, the sibling automation seed (https://github.com/just-every/run-crank), uses the same surface. Owners install the app definitions Penny publishes against their own installation; a public directory listing is a register row. **Acceptance.** 1. A Zapier CLI test against a running installation fires each trigger once per event. 2. It runs each action within its key's scopes. 3. An out-of-scope action is refused.

mainClauses.title: Connector health
mainClauses.gap: Delivery and tracker-receipt states are shown today for outbound integrations only. A clock-advanced fixture with an expired token and a rate limit shows the connector failing with its reason once an hour passes without a successful sync (or after the owner's shorter setting), notifies the owner once, and after reconnect resumes from its cursor without duplicate items.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Each connector shows the connected account, scope, last successful sync, items captured, backlog and its last failure with the reason and a fix (reconnect, grant scope). A connector with no successful sync for 1 hour (the owner may set 15 minutes to 24 hours per connector in its settings) is failing: it notifies the owner once per failure episode (NOTIFY-006) and appears on the overview until a sync succeeds. Disconnecting revokes and deletes its tokens and stops capture; captured evidence stays. **Acceptance.** 1. A clock-advanced fixture with an expired token and a rate limit shows the connector failing with its reason once an hour passes without a successful sync (and after the owner's shorter setting when set), notifies the owner once, and after reconnect resumes from its cursor without duplicate items.

mainClauses.title: Capture scope, minimization and consent
mainClauses.gap: Purpose-bound selected-record acquisition ships today for Orbit and native records (LEARN-001). Connector fixtures assert that no request is made for out-of-scope records, that redaction precedes the write, and that captured people hold no permission record (NOTIFY-009 sends create none either).
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Connectors read only the configured scope (channels, tags, views, call filters, record types), store the selected excerpt rather than the whole record unless the operator chooses otherwise, apply redaction (AI-008) before storage, keep any source person nullable and non-authorizing (EVID-002), and never create an email permission record for a captured person (REQ-010); a captured contact is emailed only when an operator chooses so for one update under NOTIFY-009. **Acceptance.** 1. Connector fixtures assert that no request is made for out-of-scope records, that redaction precedes the write, and that captured people hold no permission record.

mainClauses.title: Submission forms and polls
mainClauses.gap: A conditional question renders and validates on the portal and the widget at both widths; poll answers aggregate per request and by segment and stay operator-only.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Owners configure the portal and widget submission form per board: custom questions (text, single or multiple choice, number, rating), required and conditional fields, and a short poll attached to a request or a release ("How important is this to you?"). Answers are evidence linked to the request and filterable by segment. General surveys and NPS stay in Pencil, the sibling forms seed (https://github.com/just-every/run-pencil). **Acceptance.** 1. A conditional question renders and validates on the portal and the widget at both widths. 2. Poll answers aggregate per request and by segment and stay operator-only.

mainClauses.title: Freshdesk
mainClauses.gap: Freshdesk API and webhook fixtures run CAP-003's journey: install, link, create and proxy-vote from the sidebar; tag-triggered capture creates one item per ticket however often the webhook replays; company fields arrive as private attributes; a shipped request drafts one reply on the linked ticket; uninstalling revokes and deletes the API key.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1, D-2 **Requirement.** A Freshdesk app (Freshworks developer kit) in the ticket sidebar offers CAP-003's actions: search, link the ticket to a request, create a request, record a proxy vote for the ticket's requester and see the request's public status. Tickets with a configured tag, or matched by a configured Freshdesk automation rule that calls Penny's signed webhook, are captured automatically. Freshdesk contacts and companies map to requesters and accounts by email and company ID, with their configured custom fields arriving as private segment attributes (SEG-006). NOTIFY-007 drafts the status reply on the ticket as a reply or a private note. **Acceptance.** Freshdesk API and webhook fixtures run CAP-003's journey: 1. Install, link, create and proxy-vote from the sidebar. 2. Tag-triggered capture creates one item per ticket however often the webhook replays. 3. Company fields arrive as private attributes. 4. A shipped request drafts one reply on the linked ticket. 5. Uninstalling revokes and deletes the API key.

mainClauses.title: Review sites and app stores
mainClauses.gap: Recorded fixtures from G2, Capterra, TrustRadius, Trustpilot, Product Hunt, the App Store and Google Play produce one inbox item per review however often the feed is re-read, each with its rating, date and a deep link that opens that review; an edited fixture review shows changed;
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** The owner connects the product's listings on G2, Capterra, TrustRadius, Trustpilot, Product Hunt, the Apple App Store and Google Play. Penny reads new reviews on a schedule (default daily, never less often than Google Play's one-week review window allows) as accountable background work (TRIAGE-006), through the site's own vendor interface where it offers one (App Store Connect customer reviews, the Google Play Developer reply-to-reviews API, the Trustpilot Business API, the G2 API, the Product Hunt API) and otherwise from the listing's public review page within that site's terms. Each review lands once in the inbox, keyed by site and review ID, with the reviewer as the site names them (nullable and non-authorizing), rating, title, text, date, app version and country where given, and a deep link to the review. An edited review shows CAP-002's changed state and a removed one becomes source-removed. The extraction agent (AI-004) proposes requests from review text. A reviewer has no email permission and is never emailed (NOTIFY-009 skips them). **Acceptance.** 1. Recorded fixtures from each of the seven sites produce one inbox item per review however often the feed is re-read, each with its rating, date and a deep link that opens that review. 2. An edited fixture review shows changed. 3. AI-004 proposals from a review carry byte-exact spans.

mainClauses.title: Discord
mainClauses.gap: Signed interaction and gateway fixtures: the command and the reaction each capture a message once with its jump link, a bad signature is refused, and a message in an unselected channel is never read.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** A Discord app adds a "Send to Penny" message command and an emoji-reaction trigger in selected channels of the customer's community server. The message and its jump link become an inbox item, the Discord member who triggered it is the capturer and the author is the source person (nullable, non-authorizing). Interactions are verified by their Ed25519 signature before parsing. **Acceptance.** Signed interaction and gateway fixtures: 1. The command and the reaction each capture a message once with its jump link, a bad signature is refused, and a message in an unselected channel is never read.

mainClauses.title: Survey responses
mainClauses.gap: Typeform, SurveyMonkey, Google Forms and Pencil fixtures produce one inbox item per response with its link and mapped attributes; a replayed webhook creates nothing; a bad Typeform signature is refused; an unmapped question's answer is absent from D1 and the archive.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** Typeform, SurveyMonkey, Google Forms and Pencil connectors bring in responses to the forms the owner selects. The owner maps which open-text questions become evidence and which answers become private attributes; each new response lands once as an inbox item with a link to the response, and a respondent email or hidden field maps to a requester and account (nullable, never verified identity or consent). Typeform and SurveyMonkey deliver by signed webhook and Google Forms by scheduled read of the Forms API. Unmapped questions are not stored. **Acceptance.** 1. Fixtures from each tool produce one inbox item per response with its link and mapped attributes. 2. A replayed webhook creates nothing. 3. A bad Typeform signature is refused. 4. An unmapped question's answer is absent from D1 and the archive.

mainClauses.title: In-app feedback widget
mainClauses.gap: Allow-listed iframe embedding of the portal (REQ-027) ships today. A browser test on a fixture host page at both widths: an identified user submits, votes and follows, and on an auto-publish board sees their post listed at once; the page URL appears only in private evidence; the documented CSP directives suffice; no third-party cookie is set.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-PUBLIC-001 **Requirement.** A JavaScript snippet and npm package embed Penny in the customer's own product as a launcher, modal or side panel: identified users submit, search, vote, comment and follow without leaving the product, and the current page URL and any metadata the host passes are attached as private context. It follows the board's moderation setting (REQ-003, REQ-033) so an identified user's post on an auto-publish board shows at once, keeps the portal's privacy, and shows the owner's brand (INT-008) in the host's colors or the brand accent, as the owner chooses. **Acceptance.** A browser test on a fixture host page at both widths: 1. An identified user submits, votes and follows, and on an auto-publish board sees their post listed at once. 2. The page URL appears only in private evidence. 3. The documented CSP directives suffice.

mainClauses.title: SSO identify
mainClauses.gap: REQ-031 host identity ships for the portal today, by postMessage from an allow-listed parent frame only. Host-identity tests extended to JWT and to the widget origin: a valid token identifies the user and links the account with private attributes; expired, future-dated and forged tokens are refused and change nothing.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** The customer's server signs a user token (JWT with HS256 or RS256, or REQ-031's host identity) carrying user ID, email, name, company ID and name, and optional attributes such as plan, role and MRR in USD. The widget and portal accept it without email verification, from the widget's identify call, from REQ-031's allow-listed parent frame, or on the standalone portal through WIDGET-008's sign-in redirect, apply REQ-014's expiry and store the attributes operator-only for segments (SEG-006). **Acceptance.** 1. Host-identity tests extended to JWT and to the widget origin: a valid token identifies the user and links the account with private attributes. 2. Expired, future-dated and forged tokens are refused and change nothing.

mainClauses.title: Changelog widget and announcements
mainClauses.gap: A browser test: the unread count falls after viewing; a segment-targeted announcement shows only to matching identified users; an unpublished release never appears.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** The same snippet shows a "What's new" panel with an unread badge of published releases, targeted and announcements alike (REL-018), optional in-app announcements of a release to a segment, and reactions; each entry opens its release. **Acceptance.** A browser test: 1. The unread count falls after viewing. 2. A segment-targeted announcement shows only to matching identified users. 3. An unpublished release never appears.

mainClauses.title: Mobile SDKs
mainClauses.gap: SDK sample apps run XCTest and Espresso UI tests against a test installation: identified submit, vote and changelog read, and a queued offline submission sent once on reconnect.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Register:* R-17 **Requirement.** iOS (Swift Package), Android (Kotlin, Maven Central) and React Native SDKs give the customer's app native feedback, voting and changelog screens with SSO identify, offline queueing of submissions and status-change hooks for the host app's own push. **Acceptance.** SDK sample apps run XCTest and Espresso UI tests against a test installation: 1. Identified submit, vote and changelog read, and a queued offline submission sent once on reconnect.

mainClauses.title: Moment capture
mainClauses.gap: A fixture host triggers two moments; their answers arrive as evidence tagged with the moment; the widget sends nothing to Penny until a call is made.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** The host product opens a short Penny prompt at a deliberate moment (`penny.capture({moment: 'cancellation'})`: cancellation, downgrade, failed search, feature-flag exit), and the answer becomes evidence tagged with that moment. There is no passive tracking, session replay or keystroke capture. **Acceptance.** 1. A fixture host triggers two moments. 2. Their answers arrive as evidence tagged with the moment. 3. The widget sends nothing to Penny until a call is made.

mainClauses.title: Portal domain and audiences
mainClauses.gap: A browser test: a segment member sees the restricted board while a non-member and a signed-out visitor get 404 and no count; on an SSO-required portal, a signed-out request to a request page, the board, the public API, the feed and an attachment returns no request content (WIDGET-008's redirect or the sign-in page for documents, 401 for the rest), and REQ-023's link and REQ-039's buttons are absent; a custom hostname configured through the deployment path serves the portal (its TLS receipt is R-7).
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Register:* R-7 **Requirement.** The owner can serve the portal at a custom domain (such as feedback.example.com through Cloudflare custom hostnames), require SSO identify for the whole portal (WIDGET-008), and restrict a board to identified users in a segment (an Enterprise beta board) or to employees signed in through ROLE-002. A restricted board never appears to anyone else, in counts, search or the sitemap. Internal boards (REQ-019) remain operator-only. **Acceptance.** 1. A segment member sees the restricted board while a non-member and a signed-out visitor get 404 and no count. 2. On an SSO-required portal, every portal document (board, request, roadmap, changelog, activity) answers a not-yet-identified visitor with WIDGET-008's redirect to the owner's login URL, or, when no login URL is set, a sign-in page showing only the company name and logo (INT-007) and a note that the portal is for the company's customers. 3. On an SSO-required portal, every public API read, feed, sitemap and attachment answers 401 with no request, comment, release or count in the body. 4. Every response of an SSO-required portal carries `noindex`. 5. On an SSO-required portal, REQ-023's emailed link and REQ-039's provider buttons are absent, and their start and callback routes refuse without issuing state or a session. 6. A browser test: a signed-out request to a request page, the board, the public API, the feed and an attachment returns no request content (a redirect or the sign-in page for documents, 401 for the rest). 7. A custom hostname configured through the deployment path serves the portal.

mainClauses.title: Localized portal and widget
mainClauses.gap: A browser test renders the portal and widget in Spanish once through Accept-Language and once through an identify locale, with no English interface string left; a catalog missing a key fails the build; a status email to a requester identified with es arrives in Spanish.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** The portal, widget, mobile SDK screens and requester email are available in English (default), Spanish, French, German, Brazilian Portuguese and Japanese, and in any further locale the owner adds as a message catalog. The locale comes from SSO identify (WIDGET-002), then the browser's Accept-Language, then the owner's default; dates and numbers follow it. Customer wording is shown as written; operators can read a machine translation of a post or comment under AI-010, labeled as translated, and the original stays authoritative. **Acceptance.** 1. A browser test renders the portal and widget in Spanish once through Accept-Language and once through an identify locale, with no English interface string left. 2. A catalog missing a key fails the build. 3. A status email to a requester identified with `es` arrives in Spanish.

mainClauses.title: SSO sign-in redirect
mainClauses.gap: Today host identity reaches the portal only by postMessage from an allow-listed parent frame (src/core/features/auth/ui/host-identity-bridge.tsx); there is no login URL, redirect or state. At both widths against a fixture host: a signed-out visitor to /portal/feedback/<request> on an SSO-required portal is redirected to the login URL; with SSO required and no token the request page response carries no request content.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** As Canny's SSO redirect does, the owner sets a login URL on their own site (an `https` URL) in settings, beside WIDGET-002's signing key, and the portal signs visitors in through the owner's product. An unidentified visitor to any page of an SSO-required portal (WIDGET-006), or a visitor on any portal who chooses "Sign in with <company name>" (offered beside REQ-023 and REQ-039 when a login URL is set), is answered with a 302 to the login URL carrying a `redirect` parameter: Penny's callback path on the portal's own origin with a `state` value. **Acceptance.** A browser journey against a fixture host at both widths: 1. The state is signed by the installation, single-use, expires 10 minutes after issue and binds the return path, which must be a same-origin portal path; any other return path is replaced by the board home. 2. A signed-out visitor to `/portal/feedback/<request>` on an SSO-required portal is redirected to the login URL. 3. With SSO required and no token, the response for the request page carries no request content. 4. No redirect leaves the portal's origin except to the configured login URL.

mainClauses.title: SSO return and refusals
mainClauses.gap: There is no login URL, callback or state today. At both widths against a fixture host: the visitor returns with a valid token and lands on the request identified, with no cookie and no token left in the address bar; a vote chosen before sign-in is applied once after return; an expired token, a forged token, a reused state, a tampered return path and a return path on another origin are each refused and change nothing.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *From:* WIDGET-008 **Requirement.** The owner's server authenticates the user in its own product and sends the browser to the callback with a WIDGET-002 token in the URL fragment or a form POST, never the query string, so the token reaches no request log. The callback verifies the token's signature and REQ-014's expiry and the state's signature, expiry and single use; consumes the state; establishes REQ-023's browser-local session for the identified requester (no cookie), linking the account and private attributes as WIDGET-002 does; removes the token from the address bar and history; applies any action held before sign-in (REQ-023); and lands the visitor on the page they asked for. A visitor already signed in to the owner's product passes through with no prompt. **Acceptance.** A browser journey against a fixture host at both widths: 1. The fixture host returns a valid token, and the visitor lands on the request they asked for, identified, with no cookie set and no token left in the address bar. 2. A vote chosen before sign-in on a non-SSO-required portal is applied once after return. 3. An expired token, a forged token, a reused state, a tampered return path and a return path on another origin are each refused with a page that offers to try again, and change nothing. 4. A refusal reveals no identity match (REQ-014).

mainClauses.title: Links from email into the owner's product
mainClauses.gap: There is no in-app link pattern today. With Open requests in my product on, a status email's request link follows the owner's pattern and the fixture host's widget opens that request; the unsubscribe link works signed out.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *From:* WIDGET-008 **Requirement.** The owner can turn on "Open requests in my product" and set a URL pattern on their own product's origin with `{request}` (the request's public ID) and optional `{board}` placeholders, such as `https://app.example.com/feedback?request={request}`.
