With it on, every link to a request in requester email (NOTIFY-001, NOTIFY-008, NOTIFY-010, NOTIFY-011, NOTIFY-012) and release email (REL-005) uses the pattern, and the widget (WIDGET-001) opens that request when the host page passes it (`penny.open({request})`), already identified. With it off, those links go to the portal, and on an SSO-required portal they pass through WIDGET-008's redirect. **Acceptance.** A browser journey against a fixture host at both widths: 1. With "Open requests in my product" on, a status email's request link follows the owner's pattern. 2. The fixture host's widget opens that request, already identified. 3. With it off, the request links go to the portal. 4. Unsubscribe and mute links always go to Penny and work without signing in (NOTIFY-002): the unsubscribe link in the same email works signed out.

mainClauses.title: Semantic duplicate detection
mainClauses.gap: The duplicates-v1 evaluation meets the AI-001 bars (precision ≥ 0.90, recall ≥ 0.85, top-five ≥ 0.90, paraphrase recall ≥ lexical + 0.15); requester suggestions contain only published requests; with the model disabled, lexical suggestions still return within EVID-007's limit.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-4 **Requirement.** Alongside EVID-007's lexical suggestions, Penny ranks existing requests by meaning (embeddings over titles, descriptions and linked evidence) for a requester typing a title, for each inbox item and for an operator viewing a request, and names the passages that matched. Requesters see published requests only. When the model is unavailable the lexical suggestions still appear. **Acceptance.** 1. The `duplicates-v1` evaluation (AI-011) reports, at the suggestion threshold, precision of at least 0.90 and recall of at least 0.85, the true duplicate among the top five suggestions for at least 0.90 of positive pairs, and recall on the paraphrase subset at least 0.15 above the lexical EVID-007 baseline measured on the same set. 2. Requester suggestions contain only published requests. 3. With the model disabled, lexical suggestions still return within EVID-007's limit.

mainClauses.title: Auto-link suggestions
mainClauses.gap: The links-v1 evaluation meets the AI-002 bars; an inbox journey accepts and rejects suggestions; an auto-link rule on one fixture source links only above its threshold, marks and can undo each link, and changes no public payload.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-4 **Requirement.** Each new inbox item gets up to three suggested requests and one suggested theme, each with a confidence and a reason; the operator accepts or rejects in one action, and a rejected suggestion is not offered again. An owner may enable a rule that links automatically above a confidence threshold for chosen sources; auto-links are marked, reversible, and never publish, vote or notify. **Acceptance.** 1. The `links-v1` evaluation (AI-011) reports the labeled request among the three suggestions for at least 0.85 of items that have one, no suggestion above the threshold for at least 0.80 of items labeled none, and auto-link precision of at least 0.97 at the default threshold. 2. An inbox journey accepts and rejects suggestions. 3. An auto-link rule on one fixture source links only above its threshold, marks and can undo each link, and changes no public payload.

mainClauses.title: Duplicate sweep and merge proposals
mainClauses.gap: Reversible explicit merge (REQ-008, REQ-009) ships today. The merges-v1 evaluation with its 0.80 coverage and 0.85 precision sweep bar and zero wrongful automatic merges on the labelled fixture, the sweep and its proposals, and the evaluation-gated, off-by-default, one-board auto-merge rule that logs each merge for REQ-009 to restore are not built.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-4 **Requirement.** On demand or weekly, Penny sweeps open requests for likely duplicates and lists merge proposals with a suggested canonical request and the evidence; accepting runs REQ-008's merge. An optional auto-merge rule (*Policy: `request.auto-merge.v1`; default: off*) can be enabled only after a passing evaluation (AI-012), merges only above its threshold and only within one board, logs each merge, and can be undone by REQ-009. **Acceptance.** 1. The `merges-v1` evaluation (AI-011) reports sweep proposals covering at least 0.80 of labeled duplicate pairs with precision of at least 0.85. 2. On that labelled fixture, `request.auto-merge.v1` at its default threshold makes zero wrongful merges and none across boards; the report publishes the wrongful-merge rate of automatic merges against the 0.5% target, which does not gate. 3. The auto-merge rule is off on a new installation, and enabling it for a model and prompt version with no passing evaluation is refused with the reason. 4. A sweep over the fixture backlog lists proposals with a suggested canonical request and the evidence. 5. Accepting a proposal collapses votes as REQ-008 requires. 6. The auto-merge rule logs each merge, never merges across boards, and REQ-009 restores it.

mainClauses.title: Request extraction from conversations
mainClauses.gap: Selected Orbit and native evidence produce cited learning options today, not requests. The extraction-v1 evaluation meets the AI-004 bars; fixture conversations yield proposals whose spans match their source byte for byte; auto-creation produces unpublished requests only; re-running the same conversation creates nothing new.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-4 **Requirement.** From connected tickets, chats, calls, emails and Slack threads in scope, the extraction agent proposes candidate requests or links: a problem statement, the verbatim spans, the customer and the closest existing request. Proposals land in the inbox as suggestions; an owner may let a source create unpublished requests automatically, and REQ-005 still governs publication. **Acceptance.** 1. The `extraction-v1` evaluation (AI-011) reports span-level precision of at least 0.85 and recall of at least 0.80 against labeled request moments. 2. Fixture conversations yield proposals whose spans match their source byte for byte. 3. Auto-creation produces unpublished requests only. 4. Re-running the same conversation creates nothing new.

mainClauses.title: Themes and adaptive taxonomy
mainClauses.gap: The themes-v1 evaluation meets the AI-005 macro-F1 bars; a fixture corpus gets an initial taxonomy; new feedback is classified in the next run; an operator split reclassifies with history; themes filter the inbox and the request queue; a captured item on a board with no default owner, classified into a theme that has one, takes the theme's owner (TRIAGE-001). Native themes do not exist yet.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-4 · *Register:* R-13 **Requirement.** Penny keeps a hierarchical taxonomy (area, theme, sub-theme) over all evidence and requests, classifies new feedback continuously, proposes new themes as volume emerges, and lets operators rename, merge, split, pin or retire themes; operator edits win and reclassification keeps history. Themes filter every list and appear in reports (MEAS-004). Each theme can have a default owner applied on capture (TRIAGE-001). **Acceptance.** 1. The `themes-v1` evaluation (AI-011) reports agreement with the adjudicated labels of macro-F1 at least 0.80 at area and theme level and at least 0.70 at sub-theme level. 2. Where the set records the agreement between two human labelers, the report publishes Cohen's kappa against 90% of that agreement. 3. A fixture corpus gets an initial taxonomy, and new feedback is classified in the next run. 4. An operator split reclassifies with history. 5. Themes filter the inbox and the request queue. 6. A captured item on a board with no default owner, classified into a theme that has one, takes the theme's owner (TRIAGE-001).

mainClauses.title: Summaries and reply drafts
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-2, D-4 **Requirement.** For a request, decision or account, Penny drafts a cited summary of its evidence and discussion; for comments and inbox items it drafts a reply or status-update wording that is edited and then sent through the reply door (D-2). A draft carrying a private value (an account name, revenue, an internal note) is flagged before publication (EVID-006). Drafting reads only records available to the current operator; the prompt obeys AI-010’s data-processing setting. Unresolvable citations are dropped with a visible notice and never displayed as cited. Unlinked inbox drafts remain editable until linked to a published request. **Acceptance.** 1. Every citation in a fixture summary resolves to a stored record; unknown citations are dropped and disclosed. 2. A draft containing a private account name is flagged and its publication refused until edited. 3. Nothing is sent without an explicit send of the edited wording. 4. A revoked session refuses a draft completed in flight.

mainClauses.title: Spam and abuse flags
mainClauses.gap: The spam-v1 evaluation meets the AI-007 bars; a fixture spam batch is flagged with reasons and stays in moderation (held on an auto-publish board); a false positive is approved normally.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-4 **Requirement.** Portal and widget submissions and comments that look like spam, abuse or exposed personal data are flagged in moderation with a reason; on an auto-publish board (REQ-033) a flag holds the item instead of publishing it. A flag never deletes or publishes anything. **Acceptance.** 1. The `spam-v1` evaluation (AI-011) reports precision of at least 0.95 and recall of at least 0.90 for spam and abuse, and recall of at least 0.95 for exposed personal data. 2. A fixture spam batch is flagged with reasons and stays in moderation. 3. A false positive is approved normally.

mainClauses.title: Sensitive-data redaction
mainClauses.gap: Deterministic owner rules cover operator evidence, CAP-009 email capture, native portal submissions, saved Canny/UserVoice imports and Orbit/native learning acquisition before storage, and owner-confirmed reapplication rewrites editable wording and copies; AI-010 is not used for redaction, and AI-011 still inherits the minimal runner. Gap: Optional model detection is not built. Rule reapplication does not rewrite the preserved or fingerprinted places explicitly counted as blocked in preview: saved-import plans/originals/provenance and their owned native rows; learning scope/originals/interpretations/corrections/commitments; decision and approved/published/status/notification history; pending verification payloads; canonical request addresses; signed/outbound/tracker envelopes; audit reason copies; archive/restore staging. These require DATA-003 erasure/copy resolution or an owner ruling. Binary attachment originals are not rewritten. No transcript store exists; CAP-008 inherits transcript capture and redaction.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-4 **Requirement.** Owner-configured rules (US Social Security numbers, payment card numbers, phone numbers, email addresses, credential shapes and custom patterns), with optional model detection, redact captured excerpts and transcripts before storage; redactions are marked, and the unredacted original stays only in the source system. **Acceptance.** 1. The `redaction-v1` evaluation (AI-011) reports recall of at least 0.99 for Social Security and payment card numbers and at least 0.95 for the other default kinds, with precision of at least 0.90. 2. A fixture ticket containing an SSN and a card number is stored redacted in D1, search and the archive. 3. A new rule applies to new captures and, on request, re-applies to stored ones.

mainClauses.title: Ask Penny
mainClauses.gap: Main’s missing judgment is retained pending acceptance of the replayed cited-answer, commercial-permission and chosen-Slack assertions. A question over a fixture corpus returns an answer whose every citation resolves; a role without commercial permission receives no revenue figures; a Slack answer posts only where the asker chose.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-4 **Requirement.** Operators ask questions in Penny, Slack or Teams ("What are Enterprise accounts saying about SSO this quarter?") and get an answer that cites the evidence, requests and accounts it used, limited to what the asker's role may see. **Acceptance.** 1. A question over a fixture corpus returns an answer whose every citation resolves. 2. A role without commercial permission receives no revenue figures. 3. A Slack answer posts only where the asker chose.

mainClauses.title: Model configuration and cost
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** The owner chooses the model provider and model for each AI capability (default: Claude through Penny’s enforcing model port), a monthly USD budget and data-processing settings. Every AI run reserves and reports cost as LEARN-006 does; an absent or exhausted model visibly refuses AI work while every non-AI path keeps working. Settings choose OpenAI or Anthropic and a catalog model per capability, a UTC-calendar-month USD cap (initially $0), and whether permitted private context may be sent. By default private notes, account names and commercial fields are withheld where prompts are built. Keys, allowed models and prices remain installation bindings, never D1 or the screen. Learning keeps its investigation ceiling inside the installation cap; ambiguous calls keep their reservation and are never automatically retried. **Acceptance.** 1. Exhausting a fixture budget refuses new AI runs with a visible reason while lexical suggestions, manual capture and triage keep working. 2. The cost report matches metered fixture usage.

mainClauses.title: Measured AI quality
mainClauses.gap: Each named set exists with its documented size and label mix; the evaluation command reports every figure for each set and exits non-zero on a deliberately degraded fixture model; the lexical baseline run needs no model. Only redaction-v1 (210 synthetic excerpts) and a minimal runner exist.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Every AI capability that suggests, links, merges, classifies, extracts, flags or redacts is measured against a named, versioned, labeled fixture set held in the repository: `duplicates-v1` (at least 300 request pairs, at least 30% of them hard negatives that share key terms but differ in need, and paraphrase positives with no shared terms), `links-v1` (at least 200 inbox items labeled with their request or none, and their theme), `merges-v1` (a backlog of at least 500 requests across at least three boards with labeled duplicate clusters), `extraction-v1` (at least 50 tickets, calls, emails and threads with labeled request spans), `themes-v1` (at least 400 items with a three-level taxonomy, adjudicated), `spam-v1` (at least 300 submissions and comments labeled spam, abuse, personal data or clean) and `redaction-v1` (at least 200 excerpts with labeled sensitive spans). One evaluation command runs a capability over its set through the configured model adapter, with the model chosen per run. **Acceptance.** 1. Each named set exists with its documented size and label mix. 2. The evaluation command writes a report naming the set version and hash, model and prompt version, counts, precision, recall, F1 or agreement, the confusion matrix and cost, and whether each bar in the capability's clause is met. 3. It exits non-zero when a bar is not met, including on a deliberately degraded fixture model. 4. The lexical baseline (EVID-007) is evaluated on `duplicates-v1` without a model, so every report has a floor to beat; the baseline run needs no model. 5. Each model evaluation is recorded as a dated receipt in CHANGELOG.md.

mainClauses.title: Evaluation gates automatic rules
mainClauses.gap: Settings show no evaluation, and no automatic rule is gated on a passing evaluation; enabling auto-merge for a model with no passing evaluation must be refused with the reason, a passing evaluation must allow it, and accept and reject decisions must export as a private labeled set.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *From:* AI-011 **Requirement.** In the product, settings show the latest evaluation for the configured model on each capability, and an auto-link (AI-002), auto-merge (AI-003), automatic theme assignment (AI-005) or automatic request creation (AI-004) rule cannot be enabled for a model and prompt version whose recorded evaluation is missing or below its bar; changing either one turns such rules off until a passing evaluation is recorded. Operators' accept and reject decisions can be exported as a private labeled set to run the same evaluation on the owner's own data; it is never committed to the repository. **Acceptance.** 1. Settings show the latest evaluation for the configured model on each capability. 2. Enabling auto-merge for a model with no passing evaluation is refused with the reason, and a passing evaluation allows it. 3. Changing the model or prompt version turns such rules off until a passing evaluation is recorded. 4. Operators' accept and reject decisions export as a private labeled set that the evaluation command runs on.

mainClauses.title: HubSpot
mainClauses.gap: HubSpot API fixtures map companies, contacts and deals; a webhook update changes segment membership within 5 minutes and a property changed without a webhook arrives at the next 6-hour (or owner-set) refresh; nothing is written to HubSpot by default.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** An OAuth connection syncs HubSpot companies and contacts (domain, lifecycle stage, owner and configured properties such as ARR, MRR, plan and renewal date) and deals (amount, stage, close date) into Penny accounts and requesters by HubSpot ID and email, through webhooks, applied within 5 minutes of arrival, plus a scheduled full refresh every 6 hours (the owner may set 1 to 24 hours in the connector's settings). Write-back of a "Penny requests" property and timeline events is off unless the owner enables it. **Acceptance.** 1. HubSpot API fixtures map companies, contacts and deals. 2. A webhook update changes segment membership within 5 minutes and a property changed without a webhook arrives at the next scheduled refresh. 3. Nothing is written to HubSpot by default.

mainClauses.title: Salesforce
mainClauses.gap: Salesforce REST fixtures with sandbox OAuth: mapping, opportunity-linked evidence summing open amounts in USD, and closed-lost opportunities excluded from revenue at stake.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** A Salesforce connected app syncs Accounts, Contacts, Opportunities (amount, stage, close date, type) and configured fields; feedback can be tied to an opportunity, so revenue at stake is the sum of open opportunity amounts; an optional Penny Requests related list is written back when enabled. **Acceptance.** 1. Salesforce REST fixtures with sandbox OAuth: mapping, opportunity-linked evidence summing open amounts in USD, and closed-lost opportunities excluded from revenue at stake.

mainClauses.title: Orbit
mainClauses.gap: Today Penny reads only selected Orbit evidence records for learning (LEARN-001). A journey against an Orbit test installation shows Orbit account attributes as Penny segment attributes and Orbit deals in revenue at stake.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** Orbit, the sibling CRM (https://github.com/just-every/run-orbit), syncs accounts, contacts and deals on SEG-001's terms through its public API. **Acceptance.** 1. A journey against an Orbit test installation shows Orbit account attributes as Penny segment attributes and Orbit deals in revenue at stake.

mainClauses.title: Billing revenue
mainClauses.gap: Stripe API fixtures compute MRR from subscriptions with discounts and several items, flag churned customers and convert a non-USD subscription with its recorded rate.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** Stripe Billing, and Nectar, the sibling billing seed (https://github.com/just-every/run-nectar), sync each customer's MRR, plan and subscription status by customer ID or email domain, in USD; a non-USD subscription records its conversion rate and date. **Acceptance.** 1. Stripe API fixtures compute MRR from subscriptions with discounts and several items, flag churned customers and convert a non-USD subscription with its recorded rate.

mainClauses.title: Product and success attributes
mainClauses.gap: Signed Segment webhook fixtures set traits that move an account into a segment; a Buoy health change does the same.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** Segment identify and group traits, and Buoy, the sibling customer-success seed (https://github.com/just-every/run-buoy), supply user and company attributes such as plan, seats, health and last active. **Acceptance.** 1. Signed Segment webhook fixtures set traits that move an account into a segment. 2. A Buoy health change does the same.

mainClauses.title: Dynamic segments
mainClauses.gap: A base test changes an attribute and sees the account enter and leave a segment within 5 minutes; request, inbox and report filters agree on membership; no segment name or attribute appears in any public payload (DATA-002).
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Operators save segments as rules over any account or requester attribute (plan is Enterprise and ARR at least $50,000; health at risk; churned in the last 90 days). Membership is recomputed within 5 minutes of a changed attribute reaching Penny (SEG-001's webhook and refresh timing), and every operator list, prioritization view, roadmap view, report and agent scope filters by segment. Segments and attributes are operator-only. **Acceptance.** 1. A base test changes an attribute and sees the account enter and leave a segment within 5 minutes. 2. Request, inbox and report filters agree on membership. 3. No segment name or attribute appears in any public payload (DATA-002).

mainClauses.title: Customer-value demand
mainClauses.gap: REQ-026 ships private per-account vote totals and separate vote, linked-evidence and distinct-account counts, with all verified address/account associations and complete supporter history expandable 50 people at a time. Private account revenue is available on account records (EVID-005). PRIO-001 ships private feature demand that counts each person and account once with recorded account revenue and evidence. CAP-014 native proxy support ships from the inbox, request page and Zendesk edge. Aggregated ARR/MRR, opportunity and churn value figures beside request and feature counts, theme demand, and segment/date filtering remain required.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** For every request, feature and theme, operators see as separate figures: voters (including proxy votes), accounts, the ARR and MRR of requesting accounts, open opportunity amounts citing it, churned ARR that cited it, and evidence count, each filterable by segment and date range, in USD, counting each account once. The value figures appear beside REQ-026's separate vote, evidence and account figures and are combined into no score. **Acceptance.** 1. A fixture with several voters from one account counts that account's ARR once. 2. Opportunity and churn figures reconcile with fixture CRM data and appear beside REQ-026's separate counts. 3. Each figure filters by segment and date range, for requests, features and themes. 4. None of them appears publicly.

mainClauses.title: Auto-publish for identified requesters
mainClauses.gap: With auto-publish on, a verified requester's post and comment are public on submission and a widget-identified user's post is listed at once; an AI-007-flagged post and a hold-rule match are held with their reason; a PDF post is held while an image post publishes with its image; a takedown (REQ-041's removal) removes the post from every public read within 5 seconds and its URL answers 404; with the model unavailable, posts publish marked not screened, or are held when the board chooses hold; with the setting off, REQ-003's holding applies unchanged.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Owners and Admins choose each public board's moderation in settings: hold everything (REQ-003's holding) or auto-publish. On an auto-publish board, a submission (REQ-003), comment (REQ-007) or edit (REQ-020) from a requester verified under REQ-023 or identified through host or SSO identity (REQ-031, WIDGET-002) is public on submission in the requester's own wording, with the public status Open, unless it is held: flagged by AI-007, matched by a hold rule (TRIAGE-003), from a requester an operator set to always-moderate, or carrying a file other than an image within `seed.json` upload limits. A held item enters moderation with its reason and follows REQ-030. Image attachments on an unheld post publish with it; this supersedes REQ-011's separate file approval on auto-publish boards only, and every other file stays held under REQ-011. An operator can take down an auto-published post or comment at any time with a reason; this is REQ-041's removal, which works on every board: it leaves the portal within 5 seconds, its URL answers 404, it counts toward no public total and its author can see the reason. Operators edit auto-published wording under REQ-038. A blocked requester is still refused (REQ-022), duplicate suggestions still appear before submission (REQ-004), and each submission still creates its evidence item (EVID-001). When AI-007 cannot run (AI-010), the board's choice applies: publish and mark the item "not screened" for operator review (default), or hold. New public boards default to auto-publish; boards that exist when this ships keep holding until the owner chooses. *Policy: `request.moderation.v1` reads this setting.* **Acceptance.** A base and browser journey: 1. With auto-publish on, a verified requester's post and comment are public on submission and a widget-identified user's post is listed at once. 2. A post flagged by an AI-007 fixture, and one matched by a hold rule, are held with their reason. 3. A post with a PDF is held while an image post publishes with its image. 4. A takedown removes the post from every public read within 5 seconds and its URL answers 404. 5. With the model unavailable, posts publish marked not screened, or are held when the board chooses hold. 6. With the setting off, REQ-003's holding applies unchanged.

mainClauses.title: Public categories
mainClauses.gap: Board categories/subcategories, rename/order/archive/merge, required submission, moderation and later assignment, visible-only counts/filtering, canonical merge custody, CSV/API/archive and roadmap cards are implemented; route and 1440/390 browser journeys pass. Gap: incumbent category imports, category automation rules and a standalone SDK interface remain missing.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Operators define categories on each board, with one optional level of subcategories, and rename, reorder, merge and archive them. Each board's setting makes a category off, optional or required on submission. A requester picks one category when submitting from the portal, widget or SDK (REQ-003, WIDGET-001, WIDGET-004); an operator can change it when publishing (REQ-005) or later. Categories are public: the portal shows each published request's category, filters by category (REQ-012) and shows per-category counts that include only published requests visible on that board, never unpublished, held, internal, withdrawn or removed (REQ-041) ones. Categories are distinct from operator-only tags (EVID-009) and themes (AI-005), and nothing moves between them implicitly. A merge keeps the canonical request's category (REQ-008). Automation rules can match and set a category (TRIAGE-003), and categories are in the CSV export, the API and the archive (DATA-001, DATA-005, DATA-006). Canny categories and subcategories (MIG-001), Aha! categories (MIG-003) and UserVoice categories (MIG-004) land here. **Acceptance.** A browser journey at both widths: 1. A requester picks a category on submit, and a board with categories required refuses a submission without one. 2. The board's category filter returns only matching published requests. 3. Category counts exclude an unpublished and a held request. 4. Merging two requests in different categories keeps the canonical's. 5. A Canny API fixture's categories and subcategories arrive as categories on their boards, and no tag or public payload changes as a result.

mainClauses.title: Vote importance
mainClauses.gap: Board-configured three/four labels, optional choose/change/clear, private per-request importance counts, native and Zendesk source-stated proxy importance, CSV and Canny saved votePriority mapping/receipt/replay/undo ship. Importance counts can now sort saved PRIO-003 views. Remaining: SEG-007 commercial-value figures by importance, complete PRIO-003 inputs and MIG-002 Productboard portal-card importance import.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** A board's setting can ask each voter how important the request is to them (default labels Nice to have, Important and Must have; the owner may rename them or use four levels). Choosing is optional and can be changed or cleared. Operators see each request's votes broken down by importance, and with SEG-007's value figures (such as the ARR of Must-have voters); prioritization views (PRIO-003) can use the breakdown. The portal shows only the vote total. Proxy votes (CAP-014) record importance as the source states it; Canny's `votePriority` (MIG-009) and Productboard's portal-card importance (MIG-002) import into it. Completion requires SEG-007’s customer-value figures by importance, PRIO-003’s use of the breakdown and MIG-002’s Productboard importance import; this clause is done only when those dependencies and its native and Canny acceptance are complete. **Acceptance.** 1. A voter picks Must have and later changes it to Important, and the operator breakdown follows. 2. The public request payload carries no importance value. 3. A proxy vote records its importance. 4. A Canny fixture vote with each `votePriority` value lands with the matching importance and the receipt counts each.

mainClauses.title: Set a request's status
mainClauses.gap: Six direct statuses, optional comments, public month/quarter ETA, internal statuses, templates and unchanged-save deduplication are proved through the API and browser at 1440/390. Vote/author subscriptions (NOTIFY-008/011), captured-contact sends and bulk status actions remain separate gaps.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** On any published request an operator changes the status in one action, as Canny's status picker does: one of REQ-016's six public statuses directly, or an internal status (PRIO-002), which sets its mapped public status. The change takes an optional public comment, prefilled from the owner's template for that public status (one per status in settings, editable per change, blank by default), and an optional public ETA of a month or a quarter, which the request shows and the status roadmap (ROAD-014) shows beside it and which can be changed or cleared. Saving publishes one status update (REQ-015) carrying the new status and any comment into the request history, and the public status follows within 5 seconds under REQ-016. It notifies once per change each follower, vote-subscribed voter (NOTIFY-008) and subscribed author (NOTIFY-011) under NOTIFY-001 and NOTIFY-002, and NOTIFY-009's captured contacts when ticked; a change with no comment still sends a status-change message naming the new status. Declined still requires a public reason (REQ-017). Saving the same status again with no comment and no ETA change publishes and sends nothing. A bulk status change (TRIAGE-005) sends one message per request and recipient, coalesced under NOTIFY-002. The request ETA is set by the operator and never derived from an internal target date (ROAD-012). **Acceptance.** A base and browser journey: 1. Setting Planned with no comment on a published request that has no roadmap item shows Planned in every public payload within 5 seconds and emails each vote-subscribed voter and follower once. 2. The request appears in the status roadmap's Planned column with its ETA. 3. An internal status mapped to In progress shows In progress publicly and its own name only to operators. 4. The template prefills and the published comment is the edited wording. 5. Saving the same status again sends nothing. 6. Declined without a reason is refused.

mainClauses.title: Comment replies and images
mainClauses.gap: At both widths: a requester's reply to an operator comment is held, then shown under its parent once approved; an operator's reply is public at once and notifies followers once; a comment image on a holding board stays hidden until approved and on an auto-publish board publishes with the comment; a reply to a rejected comment is refused; a Canny fixture reply lands under its parent with its image.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Portal comments take one level of threaded replies: a verified requester or an operator replies to a published top-level comment, and replies show under it in time order. A requester's reply is moderated like any comment (REQ-007, REQ-030, REQ-033); an operator's reply is a public reply under NOTIFY-001, and a requester's reply, once public, notifies the parent comment's author once when they hold a permission for the request. Comments and replies can carry images within `seed.json` upload limits: on a holding board each image is approved with its comment under REQ-011, and on an auto-publish board an unheld comment's images publish with it (REQ-033). A held, rejected or removed (REQ-041) parent hides its replies from the portal, and a reply to it is refused. Imported replies and comment images (MIG-009, MIG-004, MIG-005) land in the same thread with their original dates under the import's publication choice (IMP-002); Canny internal comments land as internal notes (REQ-032). **Acceptance.** A browser journey at both widths: 1. A requester's reply to an operator comment is held, then shown under its parent once approved. 2. An operator's reply is public at once and notifies followers once. 3. A comment image on a holding board stays hidden until approved and on an auto-publish board publishes with the comment. 4. A reply to a rejected comment is refused. 5. A Canny fixture reply lands under its parent with its image.

mainClauses.title: Edit published wording
mainClauses.gap: Before publication, edit-then-approve under REQ-030 ships today; there is no route to edit published content (src/core/features/requests/operator-routes.ts). On a holding board and an auto-publish board: a retitled published request shows the new title in the request page, board list, search and API within 5 seconds while the old title appears only in the operator history; an edited operator comment shows the new wording marked Edited and keeps the old for operators; editing a status update leaves its status and ETA.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** As Canny's Edit Post does, a Product manager, Admin or Owner (OPS-001) can, on any board and whatever its moderation setting (REQ-033), edit a published request's public wording: the title, description and category (REQ-034), and an approved attachment's publication (withdrawing it under REQ-011). They can also edit the text of a published requester comment, operator comment or status update (REQ-015, REQ-036). **Acceptance.** A base and browser journey on a holding board and an auto-publish board: 1. An operator retitles a published request, and within 5 seconds the new title is in the request page, board list, search, category facets, status roadmap, feeds, widget and API, while the old title appears only in the operator history with its editor and time. 2. The request keeps its ID and public URL, and every earlier version stays readable to operators (as EVID-010 keeps evidence versions). 3. The requester's own later edits (REQ-020) start from the operator's wording, and the evidence item the submission created keeps the requester's original wording (EVID-004). 4. Editing an operator comment shows the new wording marked "Edited" on the portal and keeps the old for operators. 5. Editing a status update changes neither the request's status nor its ETA.

mainClauses.title: Remove and restore published content
mainClauses.gap: There is no route to remove or restore published content (src/core/features/requests/operator-routes.ts). A removed published request answers 404 and leaves the vote total, category counts, search and the status roadmap column within 5 seconds, and restoring it brings each back; a removed requester comment leaves the portal and its author's activity view shows the reason; removing a status update leaves the status unchanged; permanent delete keeps the evidence item.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *From:* REQ-038 **Requirement.** As Canny's delete does, a Product manager, Admin or Owner can remove a published request or comment, with a reason, on any board; this is REQ-033's takedown, available on every board. Removal is reversible: an operator restores it with its earlier state, votes and follows. An Owner or Admin can delete a removed request permanently, which deletes its public content, votes, comments and follows, keeps its evidence item and leaves an audit entry with no customer wording (DATA-003); a merge (REQ-008) is offered instead when the removal names a duplicate. **Acceptance.** A base and browser journey on a holding board and an auto-publish board: 1. Removing a published request makes its URL answer 404 and drops it from the vote total, category counts, search, sitemap, feeds, the status roadmap column (ROAD-014) and widget lists within 5 seconds; its votes, comments and followers are kept for operators, and the evidence item survives (EVID-004). 2. Restoring it brings each back with its earlier state, votes and follows. 3. Removing a requester comment hides it from the portal within 5 seconds, a removed parent hides its replies (REQ-037), and its author's activity view (REQ-025) shows the reason. 4. Removing an operator comment or a status update removes only its text from the portal and leaves the request's status unchanged. 5. An Owner or Admin permanently deletes a removed request: its public content, votes, comments and follows are gone, its evidence item stays, and the audit entry holds no customer wording. 6. Removing a request whose reason names a duplicate offers a merge instead.

mainClauses.title: Notice and accountability for edits and removals
mainClauses.gap: No action sends mail except one author notice when ticked; a Contributor is refused each action with 403; each action has one audit entry. None of this exists while edits and removals of published content are unbuilt.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *From:* REQ-038 · *Cites:* BASE-ROLE-001 **Requirement.** Edits and removals of published content send no mail by default and are accountable. A removal offers one private notice to the author with its reason, under REQ-030's rules for a rejection notice (current consent, suppression, mute, unsubscribe and quiet hours); editing a status update never re-sends it, and sending a corrected wording to recipients requires a new status update. No follower or voter is notified of an edit or a removal. Bulk removal is TRIAGE-005. **Acceptance.** 1. None of REQ-038's or REQ-041's actions sends mail, except one author notice for a removal when ticked. 2. No follower or voter is notified of an edit or a removal, and editing a status update never re-sends it. 3. Each edit, removal, restore and permanent delete has one audit entry (ROLE-004) with the actor, subject and reason and no customer wording. 4. A Contributor and a Viewer are refused each action.

mainClauses.title: Social sign-in for requesters
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Register:* R-4 **Requirement.** Beside REQ-023's emailed link, the owner can turn on "Continue with Google" and "Continue with GitHub" for requesters (each off by default, with the owner's own OAuth client credentials held as installation custody). A provider address verified by that provider (Google's `email_verified`, GitHub's primary verified email) becomes a REQ-023-verified address without a further email, the visitor gets REQ-023's browser-local session with no cookie, and an action held for verification (a vote, a follow, a comment or a submission) is applied on completion exactly as REQ-023 applies it. Sign-in grants no email permission (REQ-010) and no operator authority, and an address an SSO-enforced operator domain covers (ROLE-002) is still only a requester. An unverified provider address falls back to REQ-023's emailed link. On an SSO-required portal (WIDGET-006) only WIDGET-008 applies. **Acceptance.** A browser journey against Google and GitHub OAuth fixtures at the network edge: 1. A signed-out visitor votes, chooses Continue with Google, and returns to the request with the vote applied and no cookie set. 2. A GitHub account with no verified email is sent to the emailed link. 3. A forged or replayed OAuth state is refused and changes nothing. 4. With both providers off, neither button appears.

mainClauses.title: Board participation and display settings
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Each public board has settings, as Canny's board settings do: who may post (requesters, or operators only, which makes a vote-and-comment board on which the portal and widget offer no submit form and an API or widget submission is refused with 403), whether requester comments are allowed, whether vote totals show publicly (when hidden, vote totals leave every public read and the API, the board may still sort by them, and operators still see them), whether voters' display names are listed publicly on a request (off by default; when on, the vote control states it before voting), and whether requester names show publicly or every requester reads as "Anonymous" (operators always see who). A setting change applies to every public read within 5 seconds and removes no record. **Acceptance.** A browser journey: 1. On an operators-only board the submit form is absent and a widget or API submission answers 403, while voting and commenting work. 2. Hiding vote totals removes them from the board, request page and public API. 3. Turning on the voter list shows display names only, and the vote control states it. 4. An anonymized board shows "Anonymous" on every public read while the operator page shows the requester.

mainClauses.title: Canny board settings in migration
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *From:* REQ-040 · *Rules:* D-5 **Requirement.** For Canny migration (MIG-001), only the board visibility (`isPrivate`) and historical comment visibility (`privateComments`) exposed by [Canny’s API reference](https://developers.canny.io/api-reference) are mapped automatically. Posting permission, vote-count visibility, voter visibility and anonymity are not exposed by that API: for each board, the migration shows a reviewed board-settings mapping for those four settings, with the Canny dashboard values entered or confirmed by the owner before apply. Requester comment participation is also an explicit owner choice: `privateComments` governs historical comment visibility, not permission to comment. The preview distinguishes source API fields from owner-confirmed settings, retains the reviewed mapping with the originals and imports no setting it cannot verify. **Acceptance.** 1. A Canny API fixture maps `isPrivate` and `privateComments` without inventing API fields. 2. For each board the owner enters or confirms posting permission, vote-count visibility, voter visibility and anonymity from the Canny dashboard and explicitly reviews comment participation; a board confirmed as posting off and votes hidden lands with both settings. 3. The preview shows the source of each mapped setting, a changed mapping requires a fresh preview, and an unverified setting is not imported. 4. Replay changes nothing; undo removes the imported settings, while a later native edit refuses reversal rather than overwriting it.

mainClauses.title: Request owner
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Every request and inbox item can have one accountable owner; boards have a default owner applied on capture (themes take theirs under AI-005); each operator has a queue of the items, requests and requester comments awaiting them. **Acceptance.** 1. A captured item takes its board's default owner. 2. Reassignment moves it between queues. 3. A queue lists only the operator's own items.

mainClauses.title: Aging and reminders
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Untriaged inbox items, unanswered requester comments and requests with no public response past owner-set ages (default 7 days) are flagged on the overview and remind their owner once per age step; snoozed items return on their date. Requests whose public status has stayed Under review, Planned or In progress past an owner-set age (default 28 days, settable per status) are flagged stale on the overview and in the request queue (REQ-028) and remind their owner once per age step, as Canny's stale posts do; a status change (REQ-036) or a mapped roadmap transition clears the flag. **Acceptance.** 1. A clock-advanced test sends one reminder per age step, returns a snoozed item on its date, flags a request left in Planned for 28 days as stale with one reminder, clears the flag when its status changes, and the overview's aging and stale counts link to their records.

mainClauses.title: Automation rules
mainClauses.gap: A rule dry-runs against a fixture inbox, then applies once per item with one audit entry each; a hold rule keeps a matching auto-publish submission in moderation with the rule as its reason; the rule editor offers no publication, vote, customer-notification or commitment action.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Admins define ordered rules: when an item or request matches conditions (source, connector, board, tag, theme, segment, keyword, account attribute), assign an owner, add tags, set the board or category (REQ-034), link to a request, set a custom field or score input, hold an item for moderation on an auto-publish board (REQ-033), or post to a Slack or Teams channel. A rule previews its matches before saving, runs once per item and logs each action. Rules cannot publish, vote, notify a customer or commit. **Acceptance.** 1. A rule dry-runs against a fixture inbox, then applies once per item with one audit entry each. 2. A hold rule keeps a matching auto-publish submission in moderation with the rule named as its reason. 3. The rule editor offers no publication, vote, customer-notification or commitment action.

mainClauses.title: Mentions and internal discussion
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Internal notes (REQ-032) support selected operator @mentions and one level of threaded replies. A mention creates one durable in-app notice per note and active recipient by default; saving again or dismissing the notice does not duplicate it. NOTIFY-006 carries channel preferences and email, chat, push and digest delivery of mention notices. **Acceptance.** 1. A selected mention notifies its operator once, including after an idempotent save and dismissal. 2. A reply appears under its parent. 3. A removed operator cannot receive a new mention. 4. The note and its replies never appear in a public payload. 5. Archive/restore and erasure preserve their custody, and a reply restores after its parent.

mainClauses.title: Bulk actions
mainClauses.gap: Inbox-item batches, move board, set status, link, mark reviewed, REQ-041 bulk removal with one reason and propose merge remain unimplemented, as do per-record authorization of each verb, the eligible and refused preview and rechecked-authority commit and undo (RL-101); the tag and assignment batch is Owner/Admin only today.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-ROLE-001 **Requirement.** Operators select many inbox items or requests and tag, assign, move board, set status (REQ-036), link, mark reviewed, remove published requests with one reason (REQ-041) or propose merge in one action, see a summary of what changed and can undo the batch. One batch authorization rule applies (RULINGS.md RL-101): each selected record and verb is authorized with the same current operator, board and feature permission as its individual action (OPS-001 roles, ROLE-001 custom permissions, REQ-036 status, REQ-041 reasoned removal); tag, assign and review may be delegated, while merge, move, status and reasoned removal need their own rights, and selecting many records never widens them. **Acceptance.** 1. Tagging and assigning 200 fixture items writes one audited batch; undo restores every item. 2. Each selected record is authorized as its individual action would be, and an operator without the right for a verb has those records refused. 3. The preview shows the eligible selection and the refused records without revealing hidden data. 4. Commit and undo each run as one attributed batch with rechecked authority and unchanged-state fences.

mainClauses.title: Accountable background work
mainClauses.gap: Learning runs and mail drains meet this today. For each worker type, a kill-and-restart test resumes without duplicates and shows the failure state until resolved.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Every automatic action (connector sync, rule, agent run, scheduled publication, delivery sync, reminder) has an accountable owner, a due condition, durable progress, visible failure and an explicit stop or resolved state. A repeated or restarted run never duplicates a customer message, a request or a tracker issue. **Acceptance.** 1. For each worker type, a kill-and-restart test resumes without duplicates and shows the failure state until resolved.

mainClauses.title: Product hierarchy
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Products contain components, components contain features, and requests link to features (many requests to one feature), so demand, value and evidence roll up; roadmap items (ROAD-002) attach to features. The hierarchy is operator-only except through an approved roadmap item. **Acceptance.** 1. A base test rolls three requests from two accounts up to one feature, counting each account once. 2. Moving the feature to another component keeps every link.

mainClauses.title: Configurable statuses and fields
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Operators define internal request statuses (Needs info, Researching) each mapped to one of REQ-016's six public statuses; setting one on a request (REQ-036) sets the request's direct public status to its mapping, and changing a status's mapping moves every request holding it, publishing no update and notifying nobody. Custom fields (DATA-004) on requests, features and accounts. The portal shows only the mapped public status, unless the owner chooses to show a custom status's own name publicly in place of its mapped label. **Acceptance.** 1. A custom status mapped to Under review shows Under review in every public payload and the custom name only to operators, and shows its own name publicly once the owner chooses so. 2. A Canny fixture's custom status names arrive as internal statuses each mapped to the public status the owner chose in the migration preview (MIG-008).

mainClauses.title: Prioritization views and formulas
mainClauses.gap: Saved private/shared request and feature views show native voters, accounts, evidence and importance inputs; RICE, value/effort, manual segment demand and weighted sums sort only the view. Missing inputs stay unscored. Remaining: SEG-007 commercial/segment/date columns, custom-field columns, PRIO-004 scorecard inputs and PRIO-005 delivery-sourced effort.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Operators build saved, shareable views of requests or features with columns from demand (SEG-007), custom fields, scorecards (PRIO-004) and effort (PRIO-005), and an optional formula (presets RICE, value over effort, weighted segment demand, or a custom weighted sum) whose inputs and weights are visible on every row. A formula only sorts: it is never stored on a decision and never changes roadmap or public status. This supersedes REQ-026's "combines them into no score" inside these views only. **Acceptance.** 1. A RICE view sorts fixture features with every component visible. 2. Changing a weight re-sorts. 3. The decision brief and every public payload show no score.

mainClauses.title: Scorecards
mainClauses.gap: Two operators' inputs are both visible on a card; the weighted rank is computed; changing the criteria keeps earlier scores readable.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Operators define scorecards (named criteria with 1–5 or 1–10 scales and weights) and score ideas individually; each card shows every scorer's inputs and the weighted result, and rankings from scorecards filter by segment. **Acceptance.** 1. Two operators' inputs are both visible on a card. 2. The weighted rank is computed. 3. Changing the criteria keeps earlier scores readable.

mainClauses.title: Effort from delivery
mainClauses.gap: A Linear, a ClickUp and an Asana fixture estimate each appear as effort on the linked feature with their source; a manual override is marked as such.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Effort comes from the linked Vector, Linear, Jira, GitHub, Azure DevOps, ClickUp or Asana estimate (points, estimate, size or estimated time) or a manual field, with its source shown. **Acceptance.** 1. A Linear fixture estimate appears as effort on the linked feature. 2. A manual override is marked as such.

mainClauses.title: Objectives
mainClauses.gap: Features linked to an objective appear grouped under it on a roadmap view and filter a prioritization view; a key result reads its value from an Amplitude fixture; a Productboard fixture's objectives land with their feature links.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Operators define objectives with an owner, a timeframe and optional key results with a target, and link features, roadmap items and decisions to them. Prioritization views (PRIO-003) and roadmaps (ROAD-009) filter and group by objective, and a key result can read its current value from a measurement source (MEAS-001–MEAS-003). Objectives are operator-only unless shown on a public roadmap's approved wording (ROAD-004). Productboard objectives migrate here (MIG-002). **Acceptance.** 1. Features linked to an objective appear grouped under it on a roadmap view and filter a prioritization view. 2. A key result reads its value from an Amplitude fixture. 3. A Productboard fixture's objectives land with their feature links.

mainClauses.title: Roadmap views
mainClauses.gap: A browser journey switches the three views with the same filters and gets the same items; moving an item records a ROAD-001 transition.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Internal roadmaps show as a board by status, Now/Next/Later columns or a timeline by month or quarter from target and release windows; views filter by product, component, owner, theme and segment and can be saved and shared with operators. **Acceptance.** 1. A browser journey switches the three views with the same filters and gets the same items. 2. Moving an item records a ROAD-001 transition.

mainClauses.title: Several and audience roadmaps
mainClauses.gap: Two public roadmaps each show only their own approved items; an audience roadmap answers 404 to non-members.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Owners publish more than one public roadmap (by product or audience) and can restrict one to a WIDGET-006 audience; each projects only approved items (ROAD-004). **Acceptance.** 1. Two public roadmaps each show only their own approved items. 2. An audience roadmap answers 404 to non-members.

mainClauses.title: Release planning and dependencies
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Operators group roadmap items into planned releases with dates and record dependencies between items (blocks, blocked by); a slipped dependency flags its dependents and any public ETA (ROAD-012). Sprint and capacity planning stay in the delivery tool. Plans, dependencies and warnings stay operator-only and publish nothing. **Acceptance.** 1. A slipped dependency flags each dependent item and its ETA. 2. The release plan lists its items with their states.

mainClauses.title: Public ETA
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** An approved roadmap item may show a coarse public ETA (a month or a quarter), approved separately like its other customer-safe fields; changing or removing it prepares a status-update draft (ROAD-007). A request's own ETA is set with its status (REQ-036). Internal target dates never appear publicly. **Acceptance.** 1. The ETA appears only after approval. 2. Changing it drafts an update. 3. An internal target date is absent from every public payload.

mainClauses.title: Roadmap sharing and export
mainClauses.gap: An export contains only fields the exporter's role may see; the shared link refuses a signed-out visitor.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Operators share a read-only internal roadmap with signed-in Viewers and export a roadmap view as PDF, PNG or CSV for leadership reviews; exports respect role field restrictions (ROLE-001). **Acceptance.** 1. An export contains only fields the exporter's role may see. 2. The shared link refuses a signed-out visitor.

mainClauses.title: Status roadmap
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Each public roadmap (ROAD-006, ROAD-010) has a source the owner chooses: approved roadmap items (ROAD-006) or request statuses, which is how Canny builds its public roadmap. A status roadmap lists the published requests on the boards the owner selects, in columns by public status (REQ-016): Under review, Planned, In progress and Shipped by default; the owner can hide a column, rename its heading and limit Shipped to the last 30, 90 or 365 days or show all. Each card shows the request's title, board, category (REQ-034), vote total and public ETA (REQ-036) and links to the request. A status change moves the card within 5 seconds. Open and Declined requests, and unpublished, held, internal (REQ-019), withdrawn and removed (REQ-041) requests, never appear, and no count includes them. A request mapped to an approved roadmap item appears once, in the column of its public status. A new installation's first public roadmap uses request statuses; a roadmap that exists when this ships keeps approved items until the owner chooses. A migration rebuilds the source's public roadmap as a status roadmap (MIG-011). The preview binds the settings before and after apply, refuses stale approval, and supports replay and undo of unchanged imported settings; later native edits refuse undo rather than being overwritten. **Acceptance.** A browser journey at both widths: 1. A request set to Planned appears in the Planned column within 5 seconds with its ETA and moves to Shipped when set. 2. An Open, an unpublished and an internal-board request never appear and no column count includes them. 3. A hidden column and a Shipped limit apply. 4. A mapped request appears once. 5. Switching the source to approved items shows ROAD-006's projection unchanged.

mainClauses.title: Scheduled publication
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Register:* R-16 **Requirement.** A release (REL-002), an announcement (REL-018) or a status update (ROAD-008) can be scheduled for a time in `workspaceTimezone`. Penny retains the UTC instant and the entered IANA timezone, shows the schedule and lets an operator cancel it before publication. At that time Penny checks the same current publication conditions as Publish now: REL-002's for roadmap targets, ROAD-008's for status updates, REL-018's for announcements and REL-019's for request targets. If they fail, the entry stays a draft and its author receives a durable in-app failure notice. Scheduled publication is audited and repeated Cron runs publish the version only once. **Acceptance.** 1. A clock-advanced test publishes a scheduled release and status update once at their times, never before. 2. Cancellation prevents publication. 3. A release whose target is no longer Shipped and a status update whose approval is stale stay draft and notify their authors. 4. The browser journey schedules and cancels through the release and status-update controls at both widths.

mainClauses.title: Rich changelog
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Release bodies support Markdown with inline images from the release's approved attachments and video embeds from approved hosts, public labels (New, Improved, Fixed and owner-defined labels), and a changelog page filterable by label and product. Raw HTML is shown as text. **Acceptance.** 1. An inline image renders from an approved attachment. 2. The label filter returns only matching releases. 3. Raw HTML in a body is not rendered.

mainClauses.title: Changelog distribution
mainClauses.gap: Subscriber email ships today. The feeds validate and list only published versions; a segment send reaches exactly the intersection of consent and segment.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Besides email to subscribers (REL-012), the changelog has RSS and Atom feeds, a segment-targeted email send that reaches only consented recipients in the segment, and the widget (WIDGET-003). **Acceptance.** 1. The feeds validate and list only published versions. 2. A segment send reaches exactly the intersection of consent and segment.

mainClauses.title: Release notes from delivered work
mainClauses.gap: A Linear fixture completion drafts a release containing only approved wording and marked items.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** When linked delivery work completes (DELIV-006), Penny drafts a release from the shipped requests' approved public wording and the tracker items the operator marks public; the draft waits for approval. **Acceptance.** 1. A Linear fixture completion drafts a release containing only approved wording and marked items.

mainClauses.title: Announcements
mainClauses.gap: Today every release needs a roadmap target; REL-014 supplies scheduling for the entry types this clause will add. An entry with no target publishes, appears on the changelog page, both feeds and the widget, and emails each updates subscriber once and nobody else; with Notify subscribers unticked it emails nobody; it shows no outcome prompt.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** An operator writes, labels (REL-015) and publishes a changelog entry with no target, as Canny's changelog allows: an announcement, for a fix, a small improvement nobody requested, or a pricing or policy notice. It needs a title, a body, a type or label and a publication date, publishes now or on schedule (REL-014) with no roadmap-state check, and has no outcome prompt (REL-008, REL-009) because it has no target. It appears on the changelog page, its feeds (REL-016) and the changelog widget (WIDGET-003). Its recipient snapshot (REL-004) is the updates subscribers (REL-012), narrowed by any segment send the operator chooses (REL-016); each receives it once under REL-006, REL-007 and NOTIFY-002, and unticking "Notify subscribers" (ticked by default) publishes it with no email. Corrections follow REL-003. Announcements inherit REL-014’s scheduling, cancellation, current-condition checks and durable author failure notices. **Acceptance.** A base and browser journey: 1. An entry with no target publishes, appears on the changelog page, both feeds and the widget, and emails each updates subscriber once and nobody else. 2. With Notify subscribers unticked it emails nobody. 3. It shows no outcome prompt.

mainClauses.title: Request targets on any release
mainClauses.gap: Today every release needs a roadmap target. A release whose roadmap target is Planned is still refused; a release with an Open request target is refused unless Mark linked requests Shipped is ticked, which makes the request Shipped and adds its subscribed voters to the snapshot once each.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *From:* REL-018 **Requirement.** An operator can link published requests to any release as request targets without a roadmap item: publication requires each linked request to be Shipped (REQ-016), unless the operator ticks "Mark linked requests Shipped", which sets each one through REQ-036 in the same transaction; each linked request's followers, vote-subscribed voters and subscribed author join the snapshot once, with that request as their context, and see its outcome prompt. Corrections follow REL-003. Request targets inherit REL-014’s scheduling, cancellation, current-condition checks and durable author failure notices. A release with a roadmap target still enforces REL-002. **Acceptance.** A base and browser journey: 1. A release whose roadmap target is Planned is still refused. 2. A release with an Open request target is refused unless Mark linked requests Shipped is ticked, which makes the request Shipped and adds its subscribed voters to the snapshot once each.

mainClauses.title: Vector
mainClauses.gap: A journey against a Vector test installation creates an issue, maps its state change to the roadmap item and shows Penny's demand inside Vector.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** Create or link a Vector issue or project from a request, feature or roadmap item; Vector state changes flow back under DELIV-006; Vector shows the linked demand (DELIV-007); a finished Vector cycle or release can draft a Penny release (REL-017). **Acceptance.** 1. A journey against a Vector test installation creates an issue, maps its state change to the roadmap item and shows Penny's demand inside Vector.

mainClauses.title: Linear
mainClauses.gap: Deliberate create and link, and signed private state receipts, ship today. Linear fixtures: create, link, state mapping, and the attachment updated when votes change.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** Extends INT-005 and INT-006: create or link Linear issues and projects; Linear webhooks map workflow states to roadmap states (DELIV-006); Penny keeps a Linear attachment with demand on the issue (DELIV-007); estimates feed PRIO-005. **Acceptance.** Linear fixtures: 1. Create, link, state mapping, and the attachment updated when votes change.

mainClauses.title: Jira Cloud
mainClauses.gap: Deliberate create and link, and signed state receipts, ship today. Jira fixtures: create, link, status-category mapping, and panel content restricted for a role without commercial permission.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 · *Register:* R-8 **Requirement.** DELIV-002's behavior for Jira Cloud issues and epics, plus a Jira issue panel showing linked requests, voters, ARR band and segments, limited by ROLE-001. **Acceptance.** Jira fixtures: 1. Create, link, status-category mapping, and panel content restricted for a role without commercial permission.

mainClauses.title: GitHub
mainClauses.gap: Signed GitHub webhook fixtures: an issue closed by a merged pull request proposes Shipped; a bad signature is refused.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** A GitHub App creates or links issues and follows issue state, merged pull requests that close them and GitHub Projects status fields, mapping them to roadmap states. **Acceptance.** Signed GitHub webhook fixtures: 1. An issue closed by a merged pull request proposes Shipped. 2. A bad signature is refused.

mainClauses.title: Azure DevOps Services
mainClauses.gap: Azure DevOps fixtures create a work item and map its state change.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** Create or link Azure DevOps work items and map their states. **Acceptance.** 1. Azure DevOps fixtures create a work item and map its state change.

mainClauses.title: Status mapping and close the loop
mainClauses.gap: A Linear fixture Done moves the item to Shipped, the public status to Shipped and creates a draft; with auto-update on, each follower and NOTIFY-008 voter gets one notification and a replayed webhook sends nothing more; the same mapping runs for ClickUp and Asana fixtures (DELIV-009, DELIV-010).
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** For each connected tracker (DELIV-001–DELIV-005, DELIV-009, DELIV-010) an admin maps tracker states to roadmap states (In Progress to In progress, Done to Shipped). A mapped change updates the roadmap item with a ROAD-001 transition; for an approved item the public status follows (ROAD-003) and a follower update is drafted (ROAD-007). *Policy: `roadmap.auto-update.v1`; default: off.* When the owner turns it on, mapped changes publish their update from a template that carries only approved wording and follows NOTIFY-002. A manual change wins until the next tracker change, and origin marking prevents loops. This supersedes INT-006's "private until an operator chooses" for mapped states only. **Acceptance.** 1. A Linear fixture Done moves the item to Shipped, the public status to Shipped and creates a draft. 2. With auto-update on, each follower gets one notification and a replayed webhook sends nothing more.

mainClauses.title: Demand in the tracker
mainClauses.gap: A new vote updates the tracker attachment once; with commercial permission off, no revenue band is sent.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Linked tracker issues show Penny's demand (requests, voters, accounts, ARR band, top segments) with a link back, refreshed as it changes; commercial fields are omitted when the integration's role may not see them. **Acceptance.** 1. A new vote updates the tracker attachment once. 2. With commercial permission off, no revenue band is sent.

mainClauses.title: Sync health and reconciliation
mainClauses.gap: Held and uncertain tracker commands with known-issue reconciliation ship today. A drift fixture is shown and resolved by resync; an ambiguous create is reconciled to the known issue without a duplicate.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Each tracker connection shows its last event, drift between Penny and tracker state, failures and held effects; operators reconcile ambiguous creates (INT-003) and resync. **Acceptance.** 1. A drift fixture is shown and resolved by resync. 2. An ambiguous create is reconciled to the known issue without a duplicate.

mainClauses.title: ClickUp
mainClauses.gap: ClickUp API and webhook fixtures create a task from a request, link an existing one and map a status change to Shipped with its ROAD-001 transition and follower draft; the task's demand field updates once when a vote arrives; a bad signature is refused and a replayed webhook changes nothing.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** A ClickUp OAuth app creates or links ClickUp tasks (and lists) from a request, feature or roadmap item on DELIV-002's terms. ClickUp webhooks, verified by their HMAC signature, map task statuses to roadmap states under DELIV-006; Penny keeps demand on the task as a linked custom field and a link back (DELIV-007); sprint points or the time estimate feed effort (PRIO-005). **Acceptance.** 1. ClickUp API and webhook fixtures create a task from a request, link an existing one and map a status change to Shipped with its ROAD-001 transition and follower draft. 2. The task's demand field updates once when a vote arrives. 3. A bad signature is refused and a replayed webhook changes nothing.

mainClauses.title: Asana
mainClauses.gap: Asana API and webhook fixtures complete the X-Hook-Secret handshake, create and link a task and map its completion to Shipped with its follower draft; the task's demand field updates once when a vote arrives; a bad signature is refused and a replayed event changes nothing.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** An Asana OAuth app creates or links Asana tasks and projects on DELIV-002's terms. Asana webhooks (established with the X-Hook-Secret handshake and verified by X-Hook-Signature) map completion, sections or a status custom field to roadmap states under DELIV-006; demand appears on the task as a linked custom field and a link back (DELIV-007); estimated time feeds effort (PRIO-005). **Acceptance.** 1. Asana API and webhook fixtures complete the handshake, create and link a task and map its completion to Shipped with its follower draft. 2. The task's demand field updates once when a vote arrives. 3. A bad signature is refused and a replayed event changes nothing.

mainClauses.title: Operator notifications and digests
mainClauses.gap: Decision-review mail (NOTIFY-003) and installation-wide Slack and webhook posts of public events ship today. A preference-matrix test delivers each event, a TRIAGE-004 mention among them, once on each chosen channel and nowhere else; a digest coalesces a day's events into one message.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Each operator chooses, per event (new inbox item on my boards, mention, assignment, aging reminder, decision review due, connector failure, release published, demand threshold reached) and per channel (in-app, email, Slack, Teams, mobile push), immediate or daily or weekly digest. Defaults are quiet: mentions, assignments and review due only. The mention event carries TRIAGE-004's mention notices, whose durable in-app notice stays the default (inherited from TRIAGE-004). **Acceptance.** 1. A preference-matrix test delivers each event, a TRIAGE-004 mention among them, once on each chosen channel and nowhere else. 2. A digest coalesces a day's events into one message.

mainClauses.title: Close the loop through the original channel
mainClauses.gap: Zendesk and Freshdesk fixtures: a shipped request drafts one reply per linked ticket; nothing is sent until it is explicitly sent (D-2).
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-2 **Requirement.** When a request linked to a ticket or conversation changes public status or ships, Penny drafts a reply on that Zendesk, Freshdesk, Intercom, Help Scout or HappyToHelp thread (or a note to the CRM owner for sales-captured feedback), ready for the support team to send. Email to requesters still requires NOTIFY-001's consent. **Acceptance.** Zendesk and Freshdesk fixtures: 1. A shipped request drafts one reply per linked ticket. 2. Nothing is sent until the draft is explicitly sent (D-2).

mainClauses.title: Vote subscriptions
mainClauses.gap: Disclosed votes create versioned, board-scoped permission; postal admission, stale-disclosure refusal, status delivery/unsubscribe, vote removal, explicit-follow retention, off-setting retention and reasoned bulk withdrawal are implemented. API/provider-fixture and 1440/390 journeys pass. Gap: Admin-role configuration remains unproved; live provider and inbox acceptance is R-6.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Register:* R-6 **Requirement.** Owners and Admins turn on, per board in settings, "Voting subscribes to updates", which is how Canny closes the loop with voters. On such a board the vote control tells the voter, before they vote, that voting subscribes them to updates on that request and how to stop; the vote then follows the request (REQ-010) and stores a timestamped permission record with its origin (vote), board and setting version, so status updates (REQ-015, ROAD-008), decline (REQ-017) and the release that ships it (REL-004) reach that voter under NOTIFY-001 and NOTIFY-002. Every such email says why it was sent ("You voted for …") and carries the one-click unsubscribe (NOTIFY-002), which withdraws the permission, and the owner's postal address (NOTIFY-014, CAN-SPAM); the setting cannot be turned on until that address is recorded. Removing the vote withdraws a vote-origin permission unless the voter also followed or ticked "Email me updates". Turning the setting off stops new vote subscriptions and keeps existing ones; the owner may also withdraw every vote-origin permission on that board, with a recorded reason. Proxy votes (CAP-014) and historical imported votes never subscribe (MIG-007 is the only import path). The author's subscription on submission is NOTIFY-011. New boards default to on; boards that exist when this ships keep it off until the owner chooses. **Acceptance.** A base and browser journey: 1. With the setting on, the vote control states the subscription, and a vote creates one permission record with origin vote. 2. A published status update emails that voter once. 3. The email's unsubscribe link withdraws the permission and the next update sends nothing. 4. Removing a vote withdraws its permission while a voter who also followed keeps theirs. 5. With the setting off a vote creates no record. 6. A supporter recorded through CAP-014’s native proxy controls on a vote-subscription board creates no permission record and receives no status-update email unless independently subscribed.

mainClauses.title: Notify captured contacts
mainClauses.gap: With "Also email people linked through captured evidence" ticked, a captured contact linked through Zendesk evidence gets one email, a contact who is also a follower gets one in total, and a suppressed or previously unsubscribed contact gets none; unticked, no captured contact is emailed; neither creates a permission record; the audit entry records the choice and the count.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** When an operator publishes a status update (REQ-015, ROAD-008), declines a request (REQ-017) or publishes a release (REL-002), they can tick "Also email people linked through captured evidence", as Canny's "Notify users tracked internally" does. Before sending, Penny shows the count and list of contacts with a deliverable address linked to the request through captured evidence (CAP-001–CAP-022) or a proxy vote (CAP-014). Each receives one message per update version, deduplicated with followers and voters; the message says why it was sent, carries only customer-safe wording (REL-005), one-click unsubscribe and the owner's postal address (NOTIFY-014; the box cannot be ticked until it is recorded). Suppression (REL-011), a mute and any earlier unsubscribe from Penny email are respected, and an unsubscribe here stops every later NOTIFY-009 message to that address. Ticking it creates no permission record: each send is the operator's recorded choice, with its recipient count, in the audit log (ROLE-004). A board's setting can make the box ticked by default; it starts unticked. **Acceptance.** A base test: 1. With the box ticked, a captured contact linked through Zendesk evidence gets one email, a contact who is also a follower gets one email in total, and a suppressed or previously unsubscribed contact gets none. 2. With the box unticked no captured contact is emailed. 3. Neither case creates a permission record. 4. The audit entry records the choice and the count.

mainClauses.title: Weekly requester digest
mainClauses.gap: Mail-edge fixture only: the weekly summary flow, portability and the owner and requester choices are asserted at the mail edge. No hosted mailbox receipt; real-provider mailbox proof for live digest delivery and unsubscribe is R-6.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Register:* R-6 **Requirement.** The owner can enable a weekly email to requesters who opt in (a "Weekly summary" choice on the activity view, REQ-025, and the updates surface, REL-012) and to voters subscribed under NOTIFY-008: status changes, new public replies and approved comments on the requests they follow or voted for, and releases published that week.
