A week with nothing for a requester sends nothing. It carries one-click unsubscribe and respects quiet hours, suppression and mutes (NOTIFY-002, REL-011). **Acceptance.** 1. A clock-advanced test sends one digest per opted-in requester per week containing only their requests' public changes, sends nothing for an empty week, and the unsubscribe link stops the next digest.

mainClauses.title: The author's vote and subscription
mainClauses.gap: Verified submissions record the author vote and disclosed submission permission; publication notifies once, replies/status/release/rejection use the durable permission path, removing the vote retains it, and withdrawal/unsubscribe revoke it. Held-verification and board-off cases pass through routes; 1440/390 journeys pass. Gap: a separate SDK disclosure journey remains unproved; live inbox acceptance is R-6.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Register:* R-6 **Requirement.** Submitting a request records the author's vote on it, as Canny makes a post's author its first supporter; the vote counts in the vote total (REQ-006) once the request is published, and the author can remove it like any vote. On a board with vote subscriptions on (NOTIFY-008), submitting also subscribes the author: the submit form on the portal, widget and SDK (REQ-003, WIDGET-001, WIDGET-004) says before submission that they will get updates on their request and how to stop, and submission stores one timestamped permission record with origin `submission`, its board and the setting version. Through it, the publication of their held request (one "Your request is now public" message), public operator replies, approved comments, status updates (REQ-015, REQ-036, ROAD-008), a decline (REQ-017), a rejection notice an operator chooses to send (REQ-030) and the release that ships it (REL-004) reach them under NOTIFY-001 and NOTIFY-002. Every such email says why it was sent ("You posted …") and carries the one-click unsubscribe, which withdraws the permission, and the owner's postal address (NOTIFY-014). Removing the author's vote keeps the submission permission; withdrawing the request (REQ-021) withdraws it; a blocked author (REQ-022) gets nothing. A submission held for email verification (REQ-023) records the vote and the permission only once the address is verified. On a board with the setting off, the author gets updates only by ticking "Email me updates" (REQ-010). Operator-authored requests (REQ-029) and imported posts record no author vote or permission (MIG-007 is the only import path). **Acceptance.** 1. A base and browser journey on a vote-subscription board: the submit form states the subscription. 2. An author who never ticks Email me updates receives one email for the first public operator reply and one for a status update, and their permission record has origin `submission`. 3. The published request's vote total includes the author's vote once. 4. The unsubscribe link stops the next update. 5. Withdrawing the request withdraws the permission. 6. On a board with the setting off the author receives nothing without ticking, and their vote still counts.

mainClauses.title: Merge notice
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** When an operator merges a duplicate into a canonical request (REQ-008), each follower, vote-subscribed voter and subscribed author of the duplicate who is not already on the canonical request receives one message saying their request was merged into it, with its public title and link, under NOTIFY-002 and REL-004 eligibility; REQ-008 has already moved them to follow the canonical request. The merge dialog shows the count and lets the operator untick the notice for that merge. A merge into an unpublished or internal-board canonical request notifies nobody until that request is published on a public board. Unmerging (REQ-009) notifies nobody, and automatic merges (AI-003) send the notice only when the owner turns it on for them. **Acceptance.** A base test: 1. Merging a duplicate with two followers and a vote-subscribed voter, one of whom already follows the canonical request, sends two messages naming and linking the canonical request. 2. With the notice unticked it sends none. 3. Unmerging sends nothing.

mainClauses.title: Sender identity
mainClauses.gap: Provider-tested sender acceptance and refusal and configured sender and reply-to headers are implemented; real provider clients use HTTP-edge fixtures, and API and 1440/390 browser proof pass. CAP-009 proves the reciprocal capture-address exclusion through tests/base/notifications.test.ts. Gap: Admin-role sender settings remain unproved; live verified-domain, reply and inbox acceptance is R-6.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-MAIL-001 · *Register:* R-6 **Requirement.** Owners and Admins set, in settings, how requester and release email presents the business, as Canny's email whitelabeling does: the sender name (default: the INT-007 company name), the from address on a domain verified with the owner's mail provider (Penny sends a test message to the operator and shows the provider's result before saving, and refuses an address the provider rejects), and an optional monitored reply-to address that is never the CAP-009 capture address (without one, replies go to the no-reply address under NOTIFY-004). Every requester and release email (NOTIFY-001, NOTIFY-008–NOTIFY-012, REL-005, REQ-030's rejection notice) uses the sender name and from address. Operator email (NOTIFY-003, NOTIFY-006) uses the same from address. `MAIL_FROM` supplies the deployment address until a tested sender identity is saved. **Acceptance.** A base and browser journey: 1. A status email to a follower has the configured sender name and from address. 2. A from address the provider fixture rejects is refused before saving. 3. With a reply-to set, a reply reaches that address and creates no record (NOTIFY-004). 4. An Owner and an Admin each save the sender identity in settings.

mainClauses.title: Postal address and the mail it unlocks
mainClauses.gap: Company/postal setup and the legacy prompt, the postal footer and automatic-subscription admission are implemented, with API and 1440/390 browser proof. Gap: refusing the unsupported carry-over, captured-contact and digest choices without a postal address remains unproved.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *From:* NOTIFY-013 **Requirement.** The owner records the business postal address, and every requester and release email carries it in its footer with the one-click unsubscribe, as CAN-SPAM requires. First-run setup (OPS-005) asks for the postal address with the company name and cannot finish without both; an installation set up earlier shows its owner a one-time prompt alongside OPS-008's. Until a postal address is recorded, the paths that email people who did not ask in that moment cannot be turned on or chosen, each refused with the reason: vote subscriptions (NOTIFY-008), author subscriptions (NOTIFY-011), the captured-contact send (NOTIFY-009), the weekly digest (NOTIFY-010) and MIG-007 carry-over; boards created meanwhile start with vote subscriptions off; mail a requester explicitly asked for (a follow, an Email me updates tick, an updates subscription) still sends; and the overview shows the missing address until it is set. Operator email needs no postal address. **Acceptance.** A base and browser journey: 1. Setup refuses Finish without a postal address, and an installation set up earlier shows the one-time prompt. 2. A status email to a follower carries the postal address in its footer with the one-click unsubscribe. 3. On an installation with no postal address, turning on vote subscriptions, choosing MIG-007 carry-over and ticking NOTIFY-009 are refused with the reason, while a follower's status email still sends. 4. Turning on author subscriptions and the weekly digest is refused with the reason, and boards created meanwhile start with vote subscriptions off. 5. The overview shows the missing address until it is set.

mainClauses.title: Amplitude
mainClauses.gap: Amplitude API fixtures return a feature's event counts over a window and a cohort that becomes a segment.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** Amplitude supplies event and cohort counts for the features linked to roadmap items and releases (MEAS-005), and Amplitude cohorts can become segments. **Acceptance.** 1. Amplitude API fixtures return a feature's event counts over a window and a cohort that becomes a segment.

mainClauses.title: Mixpanel
mainClauses.gap: Mixpanel API fixtures match MEAS-001's journey.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** Mixpanel supplies the same usage counts and cohorts as MEAS-001. **Acceptance.** 1. Mixpanel API fixtures match MEAS-001's journey.

mainClauses.title: PostHog, Segment and Vane
mainClauses.gap: PostHog, Vane and Segment fixtures produce the same feature usage counts for a linked roadmap item.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1 **Requirement.** PostHog and Vane, the sibling web-analytics seed (https://github.com/just-every/run-vane), supply the same usage reads; Segment track events can be forwarded to Penny's usage store for features without another analytics tool. **Acceptance.** 1. PostHog, Vane and Segment fixtures produce the same feature usage counts for a linked roadmap item.

mainClauses.title: Insight reports
mainClauses.gap: Current per-account counts and release outcome totals ship today. Report totals reconcile with record counts on fixture data; response and resolution times on a fixture with a public comment, a status update, a snooze and a decline equal the hand-computed median and 90th percentile; a scheduled report sends once per period.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Dashboards show feedback volume, votes and evidence over time by source, theme, board, segment and account; top requests by voters, accounts and ARR; new and rising themes; and time to first response and to resolution. Time to first response runs from a request's creation, or an inbox item's capture, to the first operator action its requester can see: a public operator comment, a published status update, or a NOTIFY-007 reply sent on the original thread. Time to resolution runs to the request reaching Shipped or Declined, or to the inbox item being linked to a request or marked reviewed. Both report median and 90th percentile and exclude snoozed time. Each report exports as CSV and can be scheduled to email or Slack. **Acceptance.** 1. Report totals reconcile with record counts on fixture data. 2. Response and resolution times on a fixture with a public comment, a status update, a snooze and a decline equal the hand-computed median and 90th percentile. 3. A scheduled report sends once per period.

mainClauses.title: Release adoption
mainClauses.gap: Outcome responses and coverage ship today. Fixture usage yields adoption with its denominator and baseline; removing the usage data reports unknown.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** For a shipped release target with a declared success measure (DEC-003, LEARN-003), Penny reads usage for the requesting accounts and the comparison cohort over the window and shows adoption against baseline beside the outcome responses (REL-008, REL-009). Missing or partial usage is shown as unknown, never as success. **Acceptance.** 1. Fixture usage yields adoption with its denominator and baseline. 2. Removing the usage data reports unknown.

mainClauses.title: Loop health
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** The overview tracks how well the team closes the loop: the share of current canonical requests with an owner; median seconds from capture to the first published public comment or status update, including ROAD-008 updates and ignoring held comments; the share of shipped requests with a nonempty recipient snapshot whose recipients all have delivered receipts (provider acceptance alone is insufficient); and the distinct active items with promises at risk from approved public ETAs past due or ROAD-011 slipped blockers. Each figure links through an overview drilldown to the records counted. **Acceptance.** 1. Fixture records reconcile all four figures and their linked drilldowns, including first-response ordering, held-comment exclusion, ROAD-008 publication, accepted versus delivered receipts, empty snapshots and distinct risk counting. 2. The overview and drilldowns work at 1440 and 390 widths.

mainClauses.title: CSV exports
mainClauses.gap: The complete JSON archive (DATA-001) remains the full backup and ships today. A CSV export of fixture data reconciles its vote totals with its individual voter rows and with record counts.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** Operators export CSV of requests (vote totals and, separately, every individual voter with proxy marks), evidence and notes, features and hierarchy, accounts and requesters with attributes, roadmap items and releases, from any saved view, within their role's field restrictions. **Acceptance.** 1. A CSV export of fixture data reconciles its vote totals with its individual voter rows and with record counts.

mainClauses.title: Complete API and webhooks
mainClauses.gap: Requests, comments, status and releases are covered today, as are proxy-vote customer lookup and recording under votes:write; the remaining record types, full pagination/filter coverage and OpenAPI acceptance remain required. OpenAPI contract tests exercise every resource through the public API; each webhook's signature verifies and replays are rejected.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** The scoped REST API (API-001) covers every operator record type (evidence, requests, votes including proxy votes, comments, notes, accounts, segments, features, decisions, roadmap, releases) with pagination and filters, and signed webhooks fire for each lifecycle event; an OpenAPI document is published under `/docs`. **Acceptance.** 1. OpenAPI contract tests exercise every resource through the public API. 2. Each webhook's signature verifies and replays are rejected.

mainClauses.title: Canny
mainClauses.gap: Saved Canny CSV and API-response files import today (IMP-001, IMP-006), including reviewed board participation and display settings (REQ-043), with stale-preview refusal, before/after custody, replay and conflict-safe undo. Remaining: live API acquisition; categories; and the complete-fixture acceptance of the board structure, preview approval, receipt, delta run and zero deliveries.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-5 · *Register:* R-9 **Requirement.** A live Canny API migration (with the owner's API key) moves every record a Canny customer relies on, each to a named destination, starting with the board structure: boards with their visibility and access settings (REQ-018, REQ-019, WIDGET-006) and their posting, comment, vote-count, voter-list and anonymity settings (REQ-043); categories and subcategories (REQ-034); and tags (EVID-009). The status mapping, the decline reasons and the roadmap rebuild wait in the preview for the owner's approval, and nothing reaches the portal before it. It produces a redirect map (MIG-006), and a delta run during cutover adds only what changed. Historical users never become verified identity or operator authority. MIG-008 to MIG-011 carry the other record kinds on the same terms. **Acceptance.** A recorded Canny API fixture that contains each kind migrates it into its destination: 1. Records are read live through the Canny API with the owner's API key. 2. Boards land with their visibility and access settings, categories and subcategories as categories, and tags as tags. 3. Nothing reaches the portal before the owner approves the preview. 4. The IMP-007 receipt counts each kind (read, applied, skipped with reasons) and names every field left out. 5. A second run adds only the delta. 6. The migration itself queues zero deliveries, sends no mail and creates no notification.

mainClauses.title: Canny posts and statuses
mainClauses.gap: Saved Canny custom statuses import with owner-approved public mappings (PRIO-002). Remaining: live API acquisition of posts, closed-post decline reasons, ETAs, status-change history and custom post fields, and their complete-fixture acceptance.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *From:* MIG-001 · *Rules:* D-5 **Requirement.** The Canny migration moves posts with title, details, images, status (the request's direct status, REQ-036, under the mapping the owner approves in the preview; a closed post lands Declined with its last status-change comment as the public reason, or the reason the owner gives in the preview), owner (mapped to an operator the owner chooses), ETA (the request's ETA, REQ-036, public only where Canny showed it publicly and the owner approves) and status-change history (published status updates in the request history, with Canny's dates and comments); custom status names (PRIO-002 internal statuses, each mapped to a public status the owner chooses); and custom post fields (DATA-004 fields on requests, typed as Canny types them). **Acceptance.** From the recorded Canny API fixture: 1. A post in `planned` and one in `complete` read Planned and Shipped on the portal after the owner approves the preview. 2. A closed post lands Declined with its last status-change comment, or the owner's reason, as the public reason. 3. A custom status lands as an internal status mapped to its public status. 4. A custom post field lands as a request field. 5. Status-change history lands as published status updates with Canny's dates and comments.

mainClauses.title: Canny votes, comments and merges
mainClauses.gap: Saved Canny votes, comments and merge chains import (IMP-001), with votePriority mapped to importance. Remaining: live API acquisition, proxy votes from teammates, reply and image migration, internal comments as notes, and their complete-fixture acceptance.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *From:* MIG-001 · *Rules:* D-5 **Requirement.** The Canny migration moves votes with each voter, vote date, `votePriority` (REQ-035) and the teammate who voted on a customer's behalf (a proxy vote, CAP-014); comments with their replies and images (REQ-037), and internal comments as internal notes (REQ-032); and merged posts as merge history (REQ-008). **Acceptance.** From the recorded Canny API fixture: 1. Each `votePriority` lands as importance. 2. A teammate's vote on a customer's behalf lands as a proxy vote. 3. A reply lands under its comment, with its image. 4. An internal comment lands as an internal note, and a merged post as merge history.

mainClauses.title: Canny users, companies, insights and opportunities
mainClauses.gap: Live API acquisition, insights/Autopilot evidence, custom user and company fields and opportunity links are not built.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *From:* MIG-001 · *Rules:* D-5 **Requirement.** The Canny migration moves users with their custom fields (DATA-004 requester fields) and companies with MRR, creation date and custom fields (DATA-004 account fields feeding SEG-006); insights and Autopilot captures, each as evidence linked to its post with CAP-002 provenance (the source system, such as Intercom, Zendesk or Gong, its link back, the excerpt, the user and company and its priority); and opportunities linked to posts (SEG-002 opportunity links, in USD). **Acceptance.** From the recorded Canny API fixture: 1. An insight lands as evidence with its source link and company. 2. User and company fields land as attributes a segment can use. 3. An opportunity lands linked to its post's request, in USD.

mainClauses.title: Canny subscribers, changelog and roadmap
mainClauses.gap: Saved-Canny status-roadmap reconstruction ships (ROAD-014). Remaining: live API acquisition, subscriber carry-over under MIG-007, and changelog migration with original dates and request targets.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *From:* MIG-001 · *Rules:* D-5 **Requirement.** The Canny migration carries post subscribers and changelog subscribers only under MIG-007, and moves changelog entries with labels, types and publish dates (REL-015), each published as it was in Canny with its original date: an entry with linked posts as a release whose request targets (REL-019) are those posts' requests, one without as an announcement (REL-018), and an unpublished Canny draft as a draft, with an empty recipient snapshot and no outcome prompt for imported releases. Canny's public roadmap is rebuilt as a status roadmap (ROAD-014) over the same boards and statuses. **Acceptance.** From the recorded Canny API fixture: 1. Subscribers land as MIG-007 records when carry-over is selected and as nothing when it is not. 2. A changelog with an unlinked and a linked entry lands both as published with their original dates and labels, the linked one targeting its post's request. 3. Posts in `planned` and `complete` appear in those columns of the rebuilt status roadmap.

mainClauses.title: Productboard
mainClauses.gap: Productboard API and CSV fixtures rebuild the hierarchy, keep every note-to-feature link, land objectives with their feature links (PRIO-006) and importance on each vote (REQ-035), and name each omitted field in the receipt.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-5 · *Register:* R-9 **Requirement.** Productboard's API and CSV exports move notes (insights) with their users and companies, features in their product and component hierarchy (PRIO-001) with statuses and custom fields, portal cards with votes and importance (REQ-035), releases, and objectives with their key results and feature links (PRIO-006), plus portal subscribers under MIG-007; every field Penny cannot hold is named in the receipt. **Acceptance.** 1. Productboard API and CSV fixtures rebuild the hierarchy, keep every note-to-feature link, land objectives with their feature links and importance on each vote, and name each omitted field in the receipt.

mainClauses.title: Aha! Ideas
mainClauses.gap: An Aha! API fixture migrates with proxy votes marked proxy and portal visibility mapped to boards.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-5 · *Register:* R-9 **Requirement.** The Aha! API migration moves ideas, categories (REQ-034), statuses (PRIO-002), idea subscribers under MIG-007, votes including proxy votes (CAP-014), comments, idea-portal visibility, scores and the ideas' users and organizations. **Acceptance.** 1. An Aha! API fixture migrates with proxy votes marked proxy and portal visibility mapped to boards.

mainClauses.title: UserVoice
mainClauses.gap: IMP-008's saved CSV exports ship today. A UserVoice API fixture produces the same requests and supporters as IMP-008 for overlapping data and adds the comments and notes.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-5 · *Register:* R-9 **Requirement.** Beyond IMP-008's saved CSV exports, the UserVoice API moves suggestions, supporters, comments, status updates, forums, categories (REQ-034), internal notes, labels and suggestion subscribers under MIG-007. **Acceptance.** 1. A UserVoice API fixture produces the same requests and supporters as IMP-008 for overlapping data and adds the comments and notes.

mainClauses.title: Featurebase
mainClauses.gap: A Featurebase fixture migrates with counts reconciling to its receipt.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-5 · *Register:* R-9 **Requirement.** The Featurebase API or CSV migration moves posts, boards, statuses (as direct statuses, REQ-036), upvoters, comments with replies (REQ-037), changelog entries (REL-018, with their original dates) and post and changelog subscribers under MIG-007. **Acceptance.** 1. A Featurebase fixture migrates with counts reconciling to its receipt.

mainClauses.title: Cutover kit
mainClauses.gap: Preview receipts and safe reversal ship today. The dry-run receipt equals the apply receipt; each imported post URL answers 301 to its request; the owner chooses carry-over (MIG-007) or re-consent, and a re-consent invitation creates a permission record only on the customer's click; imported boards get vote-subscription, auto-publish and participation settings (REQ-040) matching the source; the cutover checklist names each unset branding (INT-007), SSO login (WIDGET-008) and sender (NOTIFY-013) item.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-5 **Requirement.** Every migration offers a dry run with the IMP-007 receipt, a side-by-side count check, a redirect map from the old portal's post URLs to Penny's request URLs, the widget swap snippet, the owner's choice between subscription carry-over (MIG-007) and a re-consent invitation that only creates permission when a customer accepts it, the vote-subscription and auto-publish settings (NOTIFY-008, REQ-033) set for each imported board to match the source's behavior, and a cutover checklist that shows, before the redirect map goes live, whether the company name, logo and favicon (INT-007), the SSO login URL when the source used SSO (WIDGET-008), and the sender identity and postal address (NOTIFY-013, NOTIFY-014) are set. Reversal follows IMP-004. **Acceptance.** 1. The dry-run receipt equals the apply receipt. 2. Each imported post URL answers 301 to its request. 3. A re-consent invitation creates a permission record only on the customer's click. 4. The cutover checklist names each unset branding, sign-in and sender item.

mainClauses.title: Subscription carry-over
mainClauses.gap: A Canny fixture voter subscribed to a post, migrated with carry-over, gets the next status email on the mapped request without re-consent and the email names the move; a changelog subscriber gets the next release; an unsubscribed source row is skipped with its reason; the receipt counts carried-over and skipped subscriptions; without carry-over the same voter gets nothing until they accept the re-consent invitation; undo removes the carried records.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-5 **Requirement.** In a migration preview the owner can select carry-over of the subscriptions the source system recorded: Canny post and changelog subscribers, Productboard portal subscribers, Aha! idea subscribers, UserVoice suggestion subscribers (including the Subscribed column of IMP-008's Ideas & Voters export) and Featurebase post and changelog subscribers. Each carried subscription is stored as an imported permission record holding the source system, the source record ID, the subscription date the source supplied, the import job and the owner who selected carry-over; a post subscription follows the mapped request and a changelog subscription becomes an updates subscription (REL-012). It makes that address eligible for request and release email (REL-004) and nothing else: never verified identity, sign-in, a vote, operator authority, a segment or an outreach audience beyond the subscribed request or changelog. Addresses the source marks unsubscribed, bounced or suppressed, and rows without an address, are skipped with their reason. The first Penny email to a carried address says the feedback board has moved and carries one-click unsubscribe; unsubscribe and suppression then work as for any permission (NOTIFY-002, REL-011). The IMP-007 receipt counts carried and skipped subscriptions per kind; undo (IMP-004) removes the records it created, and erasure (DATA-003) deletes them. Without carry-over, MIG-006's re-consent invitation applies and IMP-008's treatment of the Subscribed column is unchanged. **Acceptance.** 1. A Canny fixture voter subscribed to a post, migrated with carry-over, gets the next status email on the mapped request without re-consent, and the email names the move. 2. A changelog subscriber gets the next release. 3. An unsubscribed source row is skipped with its reason. 4. The receipt counts carried-over and skipped subscriptions. 5. Without carry-over the same voter gets nothing until they accept the re-consent invitation. 6. Undo removes the carried records.

mainClauses.title: Phone-width web
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-ACCESSIBILITY-001 **Requirement.** Every portal and operator page works at 390 pixels wide with no horizontal scroll and touch-sized controls; every new surface in this contract (inbox, widget, prioritization and roadmap views) joins the same check. **Acceptance.** 1. At 390 pixels, every portal and operator page passes axe and layout checks, with no horizontal scroll and touch-sized controls, and each new surface in this contract (inbox, widget, prioritization and roadmap views) joins the same check.

mainClauses.title: Installable app and push
mainClauses.gap: A PWA install check passes; a push fixture delivers once; an offline capture syncs once on reconnect.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core **Requirement.** The operator app is an installable progressive web app with web push for NOTIFY-006 events and a capture form that queues offline. **Acceptance.** 1. A PWA install check passes. 2. A push fixture delivers once. 3. An offline capture syncs once on reconnect.

mainClauses.title: Native operator apps
mainClauses.gap: XCTest and Espresso UI tests against a test installation triage an item, and a share-sheet capture creates exactly one inbox item.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Later · *Register:* R-8 **Requirement.** iOS and Android apps let operators triage the inbox, look up requests and accounts, capture from the share sheet (screenshot, text or link), record voice notes transcribed under CAP-008 and receive push notifications. Store distribution uses the owner's or Run Edit Run's developer accounts. **Acceptance.** 1. XCTest and Espresso UI tests against a test installation triage an item. 2. A share-sheet capture creates exactly one inbox item.

mainClauses.title: Accessibility
mainClauses.gap: Axe runs on the existing journeys today. Axe on every journey page of the portal, widget and operator app at both widths, and keyboard-only submit, vote and triage journeys, lack passing assertions; the VPAT and the screen-reader review are R-1 and R-2.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-ACCESSIBILITY-001 · *Register:* R-1, R-2 **Requirement.** Penny's delta on Base's accessibility bar: it covers the portal, the widget and the operator app, on every journey page at both widths. Penny publishes a VPAT 2.5 (Section 508 edition) for US public-sector and enterprise buyers, stating WCAG 2.1 AA conformance; the VPAT and the human screen-reader review it rests on are register rows. **Acceptance.** 1. Axe reports no serious or critical violation on every journey page of the portal, the widget and the operator app at both widths. 2. Keyboard-only journeys submit, vote and triage at both widths.

mainClauses.title: MCP server
mainClauses.gap: An MCP conformance client lists the tools and runs search and capture; a call outside the key's scope is refused.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-001, BASE-AGENT-002, BASE-AGENT-004, BASE-AGENT-005 **Requirement.** Penny's delta on the Base agent door: the Model Context Protocol server gives Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and other MCP clients Penny's search, read and capture tools (search requests and evidence, read the roadmap, add feedback, record a proxy vote), authorized by a scoped key or OAuth and limited to that key's role. **Acceptance.** 1. An MCP conformance client lists the tools and runs search and capture. 2. A call outside the key's scope is refused.

mainClauses.title: The registry equals this table
mainClauses.gap: Declared subset: 27 native tools with schema, scopes and standard/live classes. The wider target table, UI/REST registry unification, embedded jobs and resource family remain incomplete; no risk-based notTools exemptions are claimed.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface · *From:* new · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-001, BASE-AGENT-002, BASE-AGENT-006, BASE-AGENT-013 **Requirement.** Penny's door serves exactly the tools, resource templates, event types and prompts in this section, generated from one action registry that the operator app, the scoped REST API (API-001), DATA-007's MCP server and Penny's own agents all call. Each tool declares input and output schemas, truthful annotations, the risk classes it can carry and the server-side test that decides them. **Acceptance.** 1. `tools/list` and `resources/templates/list` return exactly the names in the tool table and the resource list, in a stable order. 2. The Core clause ids in `tools/list` `_meta`, with the reasons `server/discover` serves for what is not a tool, cover every Core clause, and no reason given is risk. 3. Each tool's classes in `_meta` equal its Risk class cell, and each tool's fixture result validates against its output schema. 4. For capture, link, tag, assign, approve, set status and merge, the operator app's action and the tool on the same fixture leave the same record state and the same audit event type. 5. `/docs/agents` lists every tool with its classes, scopes and error codes, and the test that adds each computed class. 6. The Base harness passes on Penny's fixtures in CI under both of its policies, all autonomous and held.

mainClauses.title: Triage through the door
mainClauses.gap: Declared internal capture, lexical search/suggestions, review/link/assign, notes and tags are native. Evidence resource readback is implemented; snooze, proxy votes, all queue filters and future commercial-role restrictions are not fully proved.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface · *From:* new · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-003, BASE-AGENT-005, BASE-AGENT-006 **Requirement.** The feedback triager finds, reads and triages through the read tools and the `penny://` resources. Every read returns exactly what the sponsor's current role shows in the operator app, and a record the sponsor cannot open reads exactly like a missing id. Triage calls inside the business are standard. **Acceptance.** 1. `penny.search` with the request queue's filters returns the same records in the same order as the sponsor's operator search, and none outside the grant. 2. Reads as a role without commercial permission (ROLE-001) return no revenue, opportunity or health value, and as a role with it return them. 3. An out-of-scope id and a missing id return the same not-found result. 4. Capture, link, tag, assign, review, snooze, an internal note and a proxy vote on an unpublished request each compute standard and nothing else. 5. Evidence wording, requester comments and imported posts carry the untrusted marker, and wording that asks for a wider action or claims a recipient is internal changes neither the call nor its class.

mainClauses.title: Customer-facing calls are external
mainClauses.gap: No call computes a risk class today; external calls, their counterparties and recipient counts are not computed.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface · *From:* new · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-006, BASE-AGENT-008 **Requirement.** Penny computes external, with its counterparty and recipient count, for every call that makes wording public or reaches a customer, as "How Penny computes each class" states. Mail an agent's call sends names "<agent> for <person>" as its sender. **Acceptance.** 1. Approving a held request, publishing a status update, posting a public comment, and editing, removing or restoring published wording each compute external with counterparty public. 2. A status change computes external with the recipient count of its followers, vote-subscribed voters, subscribed authors and ticked captured contacts, deduplicated as NOTIFY-001 counts them. 3. Publishing a release computes external with its snapshot recipient count (REL-004); with Notify subscribers unticked it carries counterparty public and no recipients. 4. Moving a request from an internal board to a public one, merging published requests and moving an approved roadmap item compute external; the same calls on internal boards or unapproved items compute standard. 5. Rejecting a held item computes standard without the author notice and external with one known recipient when the notice is ticked. 6. An outreach message (AGENT-003) computes external with counterparty known and its recipient count, and its email names "<agent> for <person>".

mainClauses.title: Destructive and sensitive calls
mainClauses.gap: No call computes a risk class today; destructive and sensitive calls are not declared.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface · *From:* new · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-006 **Requirement.** Penny computes destructive, with its item count, for what it cannot undo, and sensitive, with the data kinds, for redaction over regulated numbers. **Acceptance.** 1. `penny.published.delete` and `penny.erasure.run` compute destructive with their item counts. 2. Merging two requester identities computes destructive; blocking and unblocking a requester compute standard. 3. Deleting a tag applied to records computes destructive with the number of records it leaves; deleting an unused tag computes standard. 4. `penny.redaction.reapply` computes destructive and sensitive, with the kinds and place counts its preview shows. 5. A refused destructive call's audit row still records its computed classes.

mainClauses.title: Access, security, live and gated calls
mainClauses.gap: Public-board creation computes live and its held approval is proved. Access, security, gated connector and the remaining live settings families are undeclared; no self-escalation callback or fixture is invented.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface · *From:* new · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-005, BASE-AGENT-006, BASE-AGENT-008 **Requirement.** Penny computes access with its direction for operators, roles and keys; security for credentials and protective settings; live for settings that change what portal and widget visitors see; and gated for a connector's consent step. **Acceptance.** 1. Inviting an operator or widening a role computes access (widens); removing an operator or narrowing a role computes access (narrows). 2. Issuing a scoped key computes access (widens) and security; revoking one computes access (narrows) and security. 3. Changing SSO enforcement or the AI data-processing setting computes security; changing board moderation, auto-publish, participation, branding or the SSO-required portal computes live. 4. Connecting a connector computes gated with the provider and its consent step, and its OAuth consent goes to a person in that provider account; disconnecting computes security. 5. Configuring an outbound integration destination computes external and security. 6. A call that widens the calling agent's own key or its sponsor's role returns `self_escalation` and changes nothing, under any policy.

mainClauses.title: Penny's own agents use the same door
mainClauses.gap: Penny's learning runs and AI drafting call internal services, not a tool registry, and there is no decision function or Pause agents control.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface · *From:* new · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-002, BASE-AGENT-007, BASE-AGENT-008, BASE-AGENT-011 **Requirement.** AGENT-001 to AGENT-009 and AI-006's drafting call the registry's tools and the Base decision function, so an embedded agent and an outside one get the same decision for the same call (D-6). A draft never sends itself (D-2). **Acceptance.** 1. Each embedded agent's reads and writes appear in the audit as calls to the registry's tools, read as "<agent> for <person>". 2. Under all autonomous, AGENT-003's approved learning step sends its outreach with no person involved; under the held policy it waits for approval and sends exactly the approved messages. 3. AI-006 drafts produce no send; posting the edited wording is a separate `penny.comments.post` call with its own class and decision. 4. Pause agents stops embedded and outside agents alike on their next call within 60 seconds.

mainClauses.title: The feedback triager's week
mainClauses.gap: The declared internal triage/decision journey passes autonomous and held policies. The wider week including published merge, status, release and erasure remains undeclared.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface · *From:* new · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-007, BASE-AGENT-009, BASE-AGENT-013 **Requirement.** A stranger agent given only the installation's URL runs a seeded week of feedback work through MCP under two company policies: all autonomous, and held. The week triages new inbox items, links duplicates, merges one published pair, sets a request Planned with a comment, publishes a release to the requesters who asked, and erases one requester on request. **Acceptance.** 1. Before setup is answered, the first call returns `policy_unset` with the setup link, and setup lists every class Penny declares with no answer pre-selected. 2. Under all autonomous, the week completes with no person involved: no call waits for approval, none is refused by policy, and the review feed is empty. 3. Under held, the standard calls run and enter the review feed, and the merge, the status change, the release and the erasure each wait for approval and run once the test person approves. 4. Every call's audit row carries its classes, the rule and the policy revision, and no decision differs from the policy in force. 5. Pause agents stops the agent on its next call within 60 seconds, and resume restores it.

mainClauses.title: Competing explanations
mainClauses.gap: LEARN-002's competing options and contradictions over selected sources ship today. A fixture problem with planted disconfirming evidence: both explanations cite real spans, the planted counter-evidence is surfaced, and rejecting an explanation keeps its evidence and history.
mainClauses.area: Agents on the bet, not just the backlog
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-6 **Requirement.** For a problem the PM selects (a theme, a request or a decision question), an agent keeps at least two rival explanations of why customers ask (a missing capability, an onboarding gap, a plan limit), each with supporting and disconfirming excerpts from tickets, calls, votes, churn reasons and accounts that never asked, updates them as evidence arrives, and names the evidence that would tell them apart. The PM chooses scope and budget and can reject an explanation (kept with its reason, evidence untouched). Adding an explanation to a decision brief is a standard step through the decision tools. **Acceptance.** 1. A fixture problem with planted disconfirming evidence: both explanations cite real spans, and the planted counter-evidence is surfaced. 2. Rejecting an explanation keeps its evidence and history.

mainClauses.title: Disconfirming evidence search
mainClauses.gap: Contradictions within selected sources ship today. With contradicting fixture tickets, proposals attach with spans; accepting links them as contradicting (EVID-004); crossing the threshold raises one review suggestion.
mainClauses.area: Agents on the bet, not just the backlog
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-6 **Requirement.** Before a commitment and on its review schedule, an agent searches every connected source in scope for evidence against the leading explanation and the selected bet (customers who churned anyway, workarounds, contrary requests), attaches what it finds as contradicting-evidence proposals on the bet and suggests a review (DEC-007) when contradictions pass the owner's threshold. A proposal is a link that is accepted or rejected through the evidence tools; the search itself changes no decision. **Acceptance.** 1. With contradicting fixture tickets, proposals attach with spans. 2. Accepting a proposal links it as contradicting (EVID-004). 3. Crossing the threshold raises one review suggestion.

mainClauses.title: Next learning action
mainClauses.gap: LEARN-002's distinguishing clarification ships today. The proposal lists only consenting contacts; under the held policy approval sends exactly the approved messages; poll answers return as evidence linked to the explanation.
mainClauses.area: Agents on the bet, not just the backlog
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-6 **Requirement.** When explanations are close, the agent proposes the cheapest useful learning step (five interviews with a named segment, a two-question in-app poll under CAP-018, a usage query under MEAS, or a Pencil survey) with its expected information, cost and the customers it would contact; it drafts outreach only to consenting contacts, with booking links through Dial, the sibling scheduling seed (https://github.com/just-every/run-dial). Each learning step is a standard call, and each outreach message an external call to known counterparties with its recipients counted; the company's policy decides both. **Acceptance.** 1. The proposal lists only consenting contacts. 2. Under the held policy, each message waits for approval, and approval sends exactly the approved messages. 3. Poll answers return as evidence linked to the explanation.

mainClauses.title: Quiet and lost segments
mainClauses.gap: Selected Orbit cancellation evidence ships today. A fixture where loud small-business voters differ from silent Enterprise renewals: the report names the gap with cited records and, under the held policy, no contact happens before approval.
mainClauses.area: Agents on the bet, not just the backlog
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-6 **Requirement.** The agent compares who is asking (votes, ticket volume) with who matters (ARR, renewals due in 90 days, churned accounts, accounts whose usage dropped) and reports the selection bias, such as Enterprise renewals this quarter being absent from votes on reporting, with the accounts concerned and proposed research questions. It reads CRM and usage cohorts only within the grant its sponsor gives it, and any contact is an external call the company's policy decides. **Acceptance.** 1. A fixture where loud small-business voters differ from silent Enterprise renewals: the report names the gap with cited records. 2. Under the held policy, no contact happens before approval.

mainClauses.title: Bet review after release
mainClauses.gap: Review-due decisions, measurement protocols and outcome responses ship today. Three fixture outcomes (adopted, shipped but unused, negative follow-up) produce keep, change and reverse recommendations citing their data; missing usage produces unknown.
mainClauses.area: Agents on the bet, not just the backlog
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-6 **Requirement.** At a committed decision's review date after its release, an agent joins the commitment snapshot (DEC-004, LEARN-003's protocol), delivery receipts (DELIV), the release, cohort adoption (MEAS-005), outcome responses (REL-008) and follow-up feedback, and recommends keeping, changing or reversing the bet with the evidence on each side and its confidence; incomplete data is reported as unknown. Recording the review and any revision (DEC-006) goes through the decision tools. **Acceptance.** 1. Three fixture outcomes (adopted, shipped but unused, negative follow-up) produce keep, change and reverse recommendations citing their data. 2. Missing usage produces unknown.

mainClauses.title: Promise keeper
mainClauses.gap: Status-update drafts from approved roadmap moves ship today. A fixture slipped issue with a public ETA yields one draft and one owner reminder; dismissal records its reason; under the held policy nothing is published before approval. The remaining promise-detection kinds (a Planned reply on a dropped item, a ticket told "soon" whose issue slipped) and their corrections and reminders are not built.
mainClauses.area: Agents on the bet, not just the backlog
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-6 **Requirement.** The agent watches public replies, status updates, approved ETAs (ROAD-012), roadmap state and delivery changes for promises at risk (an ETA past due, a Planned reply on a dropped item, a ticket told "soon" whose issue slipped) and prepares source-linked corrections for the accountable owner, reminding them until resolved or dismissed with a reason. Publishing a correction or sending it to a customer is an external call the company's policy decides. **Acceptance.** 1. A fixture slipped issue with a public ETA yields one draft and one owner reminder. 2. Dismissal records its reason. 3. Under the held policy, nothing is published before approval.

mainClauses.title: Sales and renewal brief
mainClauses.gap: A fixture opportunity's brief cites that account's requests and uses only approved public wording in its suggested customer language.
mainClauses.area: Agents on the bet, not just the backlog
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-6 **Requirement.** For an open opportunity or upcoming renewal in Salesforce, HubSpot or Orbit, the agent writes an internal brief for the account team: the requests that account and similar accounts raised, their status and approved public wording, the cited evidence, and what may and may not be promised; it refreshes when status changes. Promises still go through publication. **Acceptance.** 1. A fixture opportunity's brief cites that account's requests. 2. It uses only approved public wording in its suggested customer language.

mainClauses.title: Weekly product brief
mainClauses.gap: Scheduled bounded learning runs ship today. A scheduled run over a fixture week produces one brief per subscriber with resolvable citations; an unchanged week produces none and no model call.
mainClauses.area: Agents on the bet, not just the backlog
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-6 **Requirement.** On a schedule, an agent sends each subscribed PM a cited brief of their area: rising themes, new high-value requesters, decisions due, promises at risk and connector failures, every line linked to its records, within a per-run budget. Unchanged inputs produce no brief and no model call. **Acceptance.** 1. A scheduled run over a fixture week produces one brief per subscriber with resolvable citations. 2. An unchanged week produces none and no model call.

mainClauses.title: Agent controls
mainClauses.gap: Learning runs meet this today. For each agent, revoking mid-run stops further reads and model calls, erasure removes its derived work, and the audit log shows each action.
mainClauses.area: Agents on the bet, not just the backlog
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-007, BASE-AGENT-009 · *Rules:* D-6 **Requirement.** Every agent runs under LEARN-004–LEARN-006's controls extended to every source: a named owner, scope (sources, segments, themes), budget, schedule, pause, resume and revoke, an activity log of reads, model calls, cost and proposals in the audit log (ROLE-004), and erasure closure (LEARN-005). Each customer contact, publication, merge, vote or commitment an agent takes is a call with its own class, decided by the company's policy at the Base chokepoint. **Acceptance.** 1. For each agent, revoking mid-run stops further reads and model calls. 2. Erasure removes its derived work. 3. The audit log shows each action.

mainClauses.title: One MCP door per seed
mainClauses.gap: Tools/policy/pause/audit/idempotency and evidence resources are declared. Both MCP eras use the same registry. Events, prompts and subscriptions remain undeclared.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** Every seed, hosted or self-hosted, serves one remote MCP endpoint at `/mcp` over Streamable HTTP. It speaks the current revision (2026-07-28) and accepts 2025-11-25 clients through the twelve-month deprecation window. It implements `server / discover`, tools, resources and prompts. Lists are deterministic and carry `ttlMs` and `cacheScope: "private"`. Roots, Sampling and Logging are not served. **Acceptance.** 1. `server / discover` returns the supported versions, capabilities, `serverInfo` and instructions. 2. A 2026-07-28 request works with no handshake, and a 2025-11-25 client completes `initialize` and lists the same tools. 3. An unsupported version returns `UnsupportedProtocolVersion`. 4. Two `tools / list` calls return the same order, with cache fields. 5. A foreign Origin returns 403, and a header and body method mismatch returns `HeaderMismatch`. 6. An oversized body returns 413 with no effect.

mainClauses.title: The seed's jobs are tools, through the UI's own actions
mainClauses.gap: Declared tools call real native services. Complete Core clause coverage, all native verbs, UI/REST registry unification and embedded-agent use remain incomplete.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** Each Core job a person does in the product is a tool. Where one is not, the Agent surface says why: it runs on a device, it is a person's interactive screen, it belongs to a connector or the import door, or it is an installation fact. Risk is never the reason: a risky job is a tool with its class (BASE-AGENT-006). Tools are named `<seed>.<area>.<verb>` and declare input and output schemas and truthful annotations. Each calls the same server action as the UI, so validation and authorization are written once, and the seed's embedded agents use the same registry. A business refusal returns `isError` with the seed's stable error code. **Acceptance.** 1. The Core clause ids in each tool's `_meta`, with the not-a-tool reasons that `server / discover` serves, cover every Core clause in the contract, and no reason is risk; the harness and `rer check` fail on a gap. 2. Each tool's fixture result validates against its `outputSchema`. 3. Read tools declare `readOnlyHint`; tools that can carry destructive declare `destructiveHint`, and tools that can carry external declare `openWorldHint`. 4. A refusal returns the same error code the UI gets for the same action. 5. The UI action and its tool, on the same fixture, give the same record state and the same audit event type. 6. The seed's embedded agents appear in the audit as calls to the same tools.

mainClauses.title: Records are resources
mainClauses.gap: Evidence capture/update return resource links; evidence:read and current native authority gate the native evidence projection and untrusted wording history (tests/base/penny-evidence.test.ts: captures source provenance (agent-resources.ts readback helper)). Other primary record resources, role-specific projections and byte-budget proof remain incomplete.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** Each primary record type has a URI template, and tools return `resource_link`s to the records they touch. A read returns exactly the fields the caller's role sees in the UI. File bytes count against any byte budget on the grant. A record the caller cannot open reads as not found, identical to a missing id. Text from customers, imports or files carries an untrusted marker in `_meta`. **Acceptance.** 1. `resources / templates / list` names every record type in the Agent surface. 2. Reads as two roles return exactly what the UI shows each. 3. An out-of-scope id and a missing id give identical responses. 4. A write's `resource_link` reads back the new state. 5. Bytes over budget return `budget_exhausted` and no partial content. 6. Customer-sourced text carries the untrusted marker.

mainClauses.title: Business identity and short-lived, audience-bound tokens
mainClauses.gap: Signed owner lifecycle, durable owner/team mapping, unknown and changed-email refusal, scoped native credentials and consent revocation are proved. Inactive/excluded sponsor fixtures and multi-sponsor lifecycle are undeclared; Penny has no native operator allow-list beyond current membership.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** The door is an OAuth 2.1 resource server. Its RFC 9728 metadata names the authorization servers this installation trusts. That is the paired Business when Business provisioned it, verified with the owner-claim trust the installation already holds for its import door; otherwise it is the seed's own sign-in. Access tokens are RFC 9068 JWTs with `aud` set to the seed's canonical MCP URI, `sub` the sponsoring person, `act` the agent (RFC 8693) with its specialist, scopes per tool family, and a lifetime of 15 minutes or less (5 by default). The policy scopes rules on the sponsor, agent and specialist the token names. The consent behind the tokens can last longer and is revocable. Tokens travel only in the Authorization header, and there is no passthrough. **Acceptance.** 1. An unauthenticated call returns 401 with `resource_metadata`, and the metadata names the trusted servers and scopes. 2. A Business token for this seed works, and the same token sent to a sibling seed returns 401. 3. An expired token returns 401, and a token with a lifetime over 15 minutes is refused. 4. A read-only token calling a write tool returns 403 `insufficient_scope` with every needed scope in one challenge. 5. A token in a query string is refused and not logged. 6. Revoking consent in the seed or in Business refuses the next call within 60 seconds. 7. After unpairing, Business tokens are refused and the seed's own sign-in still works.

mainClauses.title: An agent acts as a person in a role, never more
mainClauses.gap: Native current membership, narrow original key scopes and private view ownership are enforced. Access/security tool families are undeclared, so real widening/narrowing and self-escalation fixtures are not claimed.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** Every call is authorized as the sponsoring person's current role and access (BASE-ACCESS-004), intersected with the grant's resources, actions and budget. A grant only narrows. No call widens the calling agent's own authority. A call that would widen its own grant or its sponsor's role, or change the company policy or Pause, is refused with `self_escalation`, whatever the policy says; narrowing its own grant is allowed. Other access and security changes are ordinary actions in the access and security classes. An agent never acts after its sponsor is suspended. Anything an agent reads (records, files, emails, imports, other seeds' results) is data and cannot change its scope, its targets or a call's class. **Acceptance.** 1. For each role fixture, every tool's allow or deny through MCP equals the UI's for the same action. 2. A one-folder, read-only grant holds, and widening through arguments is refused. 3. Downgrading the sponsor changes the next call's result, and suspending the sponsor returns 401. 4. Calls that widen the agent's own grant or its sponsor's role, or change the policy or Pause, return `self_escalation` and change nothing, even under a policy with every class autonomous; dropping a scope from its own grant runs. 5. An injection fixture yields no out-of-grant call and no change of class: record text asking for a wider action, or claiming that a recipient is internal.

mainClauses.title: Every action declares its risk class
mainClauses.gap: Declared standard/live tool-class pairs pass native journeys and injection checks. The external/money/commitment/accounts/gated/access/security/destructive/sensitive families are not registered or claimed.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** Classes come from the fleet list in RISK-POLICY.md: standard, external, money, commitment, accounts, gated, access, security, destructive, sensitive and live. In the registry, each tool declares the classes it can carry and a server-side classifier that decides them per call from the arguments, current records and, for gated, the provider's answer. The classifier also supplies each class's facts: the measure (items, recipients, amount and currency, people or records), the counterparty (internal, known, new or public), the direction for access, the provider and step for gated, and the data kind for sensitive. A classifier never reads a flag, label or claim supplied by the agent or by record text. A seed cannot add a class; it proposes one for the fleet list. **Acceptance.** 1. Every tool in `tools / list` carries its possible classes in `_meta`, equal to the Agent surface table. 2. For each tool, fixture calls cover every class it can carry, and the computed classes and facts equal the fixture's expected values. 3. An argument or record text asserting a class or a confirmation (`internal: true`, `confirmExternal: true`) leaves the computed classes unchanged. 4. Money calls carry amount and currency, external calls their counterparty and recipient count, access calls their direction, and destructive calls their item count. 5. No tool in `tools / list` declares a class outside the fleet list, and `rer check` fails on one. 6. A refused call's audit row still records its computed classes.

mainClauses.title: The company's policy decides, at one chokepoint
mainClauses.gap: CORE signed policy, held native approval, unset/removed/blocked states and Pause pass normal conformance. Embedded, provider and queued lifecycle families remain unscoped.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** Every agent door calls one decision function: MCP, the integration API with agent tokens, and the seed's embedded agents. It evaluates the call's classes against the company's policy, as above. The seed ships no dispositions and fills no gap with one: agent access opens only under a complete policy that setup has asked for (RISK-POLICY.md), and before then every agent call returns `policy_unset` with the setup link and changes nothing. *Autonomous* runs the call. *Review* runs it and adds it to the review feed. *Approval* saves a pending action with server-computed facts and returns `input_required`, with a URL-mode elicitation to the seed's approval page and a pending handle. Each person the rule names approves the exact saved revision in a signed-in browser, and changed inputs need a new approval. The retried call returns the result and a receipt. A rejection returns `approval_rejected`, and a lapse past the wait the rule sets returns `approval_expired`. *Blocked* returns `policy_blocked`, naming the class, rule and revision. **Acceptance.** 1. The Base harness runs each tool under each disposition for every class it can carry, and sees it run, run and enter the review feed, wait with no effect, or be refused. 2. Before setup is complete, the setup page lists every class the seed's tools carry with examples and no answer pre-selected, an agent call returns `policy_unset` with the setup link and changes nothing, and an incomplete revision cannot be confirmed; a `*` rule completes it, and a tool an upgrade adds with an unanswered class appears in `tools / list` once that class is answered, while the other tools keep running. 3. Under "money autonomous up to $500, approval up to $10,000, blocked above", calls of $400, $600 and $20,000 run, wait and are refused; a per-day cap sends the call that crosses it to the next rule. 4. A call carrying two classes takes the stricter disposition. 5. An approval shows server-computed facts and an expiry, returns the URL elicitation and a handle, and completes once after the named approver approves; a changed input needs a new approval, and a rejection or lapse leaves no effect. 6. The same call through MCP, the integration API and an embedded agent gets the same decision. 7. A policy change applies to the next call within 60 seconds, and the audit cites the new revision. 8. A policy document with a bad signature or another Business's id is rejected, and the door keeps the last valid revision.

mainClauses.title: Truthful attribution
mainClauses.gap: Declared effects retain agent-for-person, sponsor and real approver attribution in door and native audit. Outbound content and native Undo are undeclared.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** Every agent act is recorded and shown as `"<agent> for <person>"`, and mail and messages an agent sends outside name it that way as their sender. An approval, a review mark, a confirmation (a warning dialog, a typed-field confirmation, a delivery confirmation), a decision or a signature attributed to a person comes only from that person's signed-in session. When an agent does the equivalent act, the record names the agent, and the act carries its own class; a binding decision or a signature is commitment. Agent doors ignore arguments that stand for a person's confirmation. No tool solves a bot check, or enters a person's own password or 2FA code at an outside service. A provider step that demands a person goes to a person, whatever the policy says; the gated class marks such steps before they run. **Acceptance.** 1. An agent call carrying a person-confirmation flag is classified and decided exactly as without it. 2. Approving, marking reviewed or answering a policy question with an agent or device token returns 403 and changes nothing. 3. A form-mode elicitation "accept" never completes an approval. 4. Where an agent's decision, signature or field confirmation runs without a person, it reads `"<agent> for <person>"` in the record, the activity view, exports and any certificate, never as the person's own act. 5. After a person approves an agent's prepared action, the record shows the person as approver and the agent as preparer. 6. Activity and exports at 1440 and 390 show `"<agent> for <person>"` for every agent act. 7. Mail an agent sends to an outside address names `"<agent> for <person>"` as its sender.

mainClauses.title: Every agent action is audited with its class and decision
mainClauses.gap: Declared calls, private reads, refusals, policy decisions and replay audit pass with differs_from_policy zero. Embedded-agent, provider and queued audit families remain unscoped.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** Extending BASE-OPS-005, each call that reads private data or changes anything records the agent client, name and specialist, and the run or task id (`traceparent` when sent); the sponsoring person, the grant, the tool and the targets; the classes and their facts, and the policy revision and rule; the decision (autonomous, review, approval, blocked, unset or self_escalation) and the outcome (done, refused, pending or failed); the approval or review id and person, and the idempotency key. For a period, the seed's Agents page shows actions by class and decision with the notable ones, the review feed (Mark reviewed, Flag, and Undo where reversible), pending approvals, steps waiting for a person and setup questions. Business shows the same across seeds. **Acceptance.** 1. One write leaves a complete audit row. 2. Refused, pending, unset and self-escalation calls are audited. 3. The Agents page's counts by class and decision equal the audit rows on a fixture week. 4. The review feed lists exactly the calls decided as review; Mark reviewed records the person, and Undo restores a reversible one. 5. Filtering by agent or class lists only those rows, and export includes every field. 6. Removing the agent keeps its rows and its name. 7. The Agents page works at 1440 and 390 with no serious or critical axe findings.

mainClauses.title: Agents can follow changes
mainClauses.gap: No event, cursor, subscription or signed-webhook implementation is declared for the agent door.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** The seed emits a typed event for every record change and for every approval, review and policy decision. Each event carries a stable id, a type, the record URI, the actor (a person, or an agent acting for a person) and a time. Events never carry secrets or more than the subscriber may read. Agents can read events three ways: `subscriptions / listen`, an `events.list` tool with a cursor, and signed webhooks from Base `integrations` using the same ids. Every channel delivers at least once and filters by access at delivery. **Acceptance.** 1. A subscribed record changed in the UI produces a notification within 10 seconds. 2. `events.list` returns the same event id the webhook carries. 3. Replaying from a cursor returns the same ids in order. 4. After access is revoked, no channel delivers events about that record. 5. A failed webhook is visible and replays without duplicate effects. 6. `approval.pending`, `approval.decided`, `review.flagged` and `policy.adopted` carry the class and decision and nothing the subscriber may not read.

mainClauses.title: Limits are policy, and Pause stops everything
mainClauses.gap: CORE Business/local Pause and consent revocation pass. Spend is none; no cost is registered. Mail edges, timed/dual-host/queued lifecycle, resource refresh and company spend reservation remain unscoped.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** Business limits are rules in the company's policy: per-call and per-day thresholds on any class's measure, such as money moved, outside recipients or items destroyed; spend caps on provider cost (models, SMS, email) per seed, specialist or agent, which setup asks with the classes; "no cap" is an answer. Tools with provider cost declare an estimate before they run, and an exhausted cap returns `budget_exhausted` before any partial effect. The seed's capacity limits (request rate, body and byte sizes) protect the installation: they bound rate and size, never daily business volume, are documented and are not policy. A grant carries budgets only when the person granting it sets them. A **Pause agents** control in the seed, and Pause all agents in Business when paired, refuses every agent token within 60 seconds until a person resumes; browser sessions and devices keep working. **Acceptance.** 1. A rate overrun returns 429 with `Retry-After`. 2. A per-day cap of three outside recipients sends the fourth to the rule that applies past the cap. 3. An exhausted spend cap returns `budget_exhausted` with no partial effect and shows the spend. 4. Under the answer "no cap", a spending call runs and its spend shows in usage; a call that spends nothing is unaffected by any cap. 5. The usage view shows calls, decisions by class, money moved and provider spend per agent. 6. Pause and Pause all agents each stop the next call within 60 seconds, and resume restores access. 7. An agent token cannot resume.

mainClauses.title: Writes are idempotent and conflict-safe
mainClauses.gap: Declared native write replay, changed-policy/current-scope admission and once-only effect checks pass. Full concurrent/provider/queued lifecycle families remain unscoped; native version guards are retained.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** Every mutating tool requires an idempotency key and takes an optional expected revision. The same key with the same arguments returns the first outcome for at least 24 hours; the same key with different arguments returns `idempotency_conflict`; a stale revision returns `revision_conflict` with the current revision. Long work returns a job handle and a status tool, with no dependence on the Tasks extension. **Acceptance.** 1. Two calls with one key give one effect and equal results. 2. A retry with a new JSON-RPC id and the same key, after a dropped stream, returns the recorded outcome. 3. The same key with different arguments returns a conflict and no effect. 4. A stale revision returns a conflict naming the current revision. 5. A job handle used by another person's token reads as not found.

mainClauses.title: Manifest, docs and the conformance journey
mainClauses.gap: The declared surface and native journey pass the agent-door conformance harness; docs are generated from that declaration. Other record-resource, event, prompt, subscription and wider specialist-week families remain incomplete.
mainClauses.text: *Tier:* Agent surface **Requirement.** `server / discover` instructions and an on-site `/docs/agents` page are generated from the action registry. The page lists tools by job, with each tool's classes, the test that adds each computed class, its scopes, resource templates, event types, capacity limits and error codes, and the specialist role. `prompts / list` carries the specialist's jobs. Base ships the conformance journey, a harness that `rer verify` runs against `rer dev` and seeds run in CI. It is an MCP client; a signed-in test person takes a person's steps (setup answers, approvals, review marks, resume) through the URLs the door returns, and the same browser leg runs the UI-parity actions and the page checks at 1440 and 390. It runs every acceptance point of BASE-AGENT-001 to 012 and of the seed's SURFACE clauses under two company policies: *all autonomous* (`*`), and *held* (standard review, every other class the seed declares approval, which the test person grants), plus the single-class variants a point names. A point that names no disposition passes under both. **Acceptance.** 1. The docs list exactly the names in `tools / list` and `resources / templates / list`. 2. Each tool's classes, and the test behind each computed one, are documented. 3. The harness fails on any of: a tool without a schema; an effect under approval or blocked, or before setup is complete; a computed class that differs from its fixture; a flag that changes a class or completes a person's step; a role-parity mismatch; a wrong-audience token being accepted; a duplicate effect on retry. 4. Every acceptance point runs under both policies, every decision matches the policy in force, and under all autonomous no call waits for a person or is refused by policy. 5. A stranger agent given only the seed URL completes the specialist journey through MCP.
